body:
## Fallo principal

Un usuario **sin permisos de administrador podía crear otro usuario administrador**. Se cierra por todos los caminos y se añade el alta de clientes para el equipo comercial.

## Control de roles (compat — el sistema en producción)
- `admin_users`: el rol por defecto pasa a **`company_user`** (mínimo privilegio). Un no-superadmin ya **no puede escalar** por el API genérico de tablas: en vez de solo borrar el campo `admin_role`, se **fija a `company_user`** y se **ancla la fila a su empresa** (antes `add_defaults` reponía `company_admin`).
- Nuevo guardián `guard_privileged_table_write` para las tablas que conceden acceso o definen empresas (`user_roles`, `user_modules`, `companies`, `company_modules`, `platform_modules`): **ni anónimo ni un usuario normal** pueden escribirlas.
- El **auto-registro público** (`/auth/sign-up`) nace siempre como `user`, nunca `admin`.
- **Borrar un usuario** (`/auth/admin/users/{id}`) exige superadmin (antes estaba abierto).

## Routers SQLAlchemy (montados y explotables desde anónimo)
- `POST /admin_users/` exige superadmin (antes creaba un **superadmin sin auth**).
- `users.py` PATCH/DELETE y `roles.py` POST/DELETE exigen superadmin.
- `auth register`: se **reactiva la anti-escalada** (comentada) y se evita el 500 con rol vacío/compat.

## Alta de clientes (onboarding comercial)
- Nuevo permiso `can_onboard_clients` y endpoints `GET /admin/clients/context` y `POST /admin/clients/onboard`: un comercial crea **empresa + su `company_admin`** sin poder crear superadmins.

## Sesiones cruzadas
- El **reseteo de la demo** (única ruta donde un login muta datos ajenos) ya **nunca borra usuarios reales** ni sus filas de identidad por una referencia cruzada a un id de la demo.

## Tests
- Nuevo `tests/test_role_security.py` (7 casos: escalada bloqueada, escritura de tablas de acceso, sign-up, borrado, onboarding).
- Suite completa: **258 pasan**.

body:
Continues the `hexutil.Big` -> uint256 work (#23216, #23220) into `common.Hash` and `eth_getProof`.

- `Hash.Big` -> `Hash.U256`, returned by value so the conversion allocates nothing. `U256ToHash` is the reverse. All three in-tree callers migrated, so `Big` is deleted — say the word if you would rather keep it as exported API.
- `AccProofResult.Balance` and `StorProofResult.Value` -> `*hexutil.U256`.
- `MockClState.ParentClBlockRoot` / `ParentRandao` -> `uint256.Int`.
- getProof key encoding moves from an anonymous closure onto `StorageKeysInfo.EncodeKey`, so the 32-byte-vs-QUANTITY rule lives with the type.

Wire format is unchanged: `hexutil.U256` encodes byte-identically to `hexutil.Big` for every value both can hold, and a hash is never negative. `TestHashU256MatchesBigIntBehaviour` pins value, hex rendering and round-trip against the old `big.Int` conversion.

Writers copy where the source is owned elsewhere (the trie account, the retainer's proof element) and alias only fresh locals.

author: juliaregistrator
body:
- Registering package: SimpleSolvers
- Repository: https://github.com/JuliaGNI/SimpleSolvers.jl
- Created by: @michakraus
- Version: v0.11.0
- Commit: b06ab5434474ddc390b634573c8af2a53b42f480
- Reviewed by: @michakraus
- Reference: https://github.com/JuliaGNI/SimpleSolvers.jl/commit/b06ab5434474ddc390b634573c8af2a53b42f480#commitcomment-196040018
- Description: Simple linear and nonlinear solvers in Julia
- Release notes:
<!-- BEGIN RELEASE NOTES -->
`````
Four independent changes. This is a **breaking** release: `Backtracking` loses a keyword and a constructor, and two solver failure modes that used to pass silently now report themselves. Everything else is additive, and behaviour at default options is otherwise unchanged. Full detail in the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/JuliaGNI/SimpleSolvers.jl/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#0110).

## Breaking

**`Backtracking` loses `α₀` and its positional constructor** ([#174](https://github.com/JuliaGNI/SimpleSolvers.jl/issues/174), [#175](https://github.com/JuliaGNI/SimpleSolvers.jl/pull/175)). The `α₀` keyword, the constant `SimpleSolvers.DEFAULT_ARMIJO_α₀`, and the positional form `Backtracking{T}(α₀, c₁, c₂, p[, τ_ulps])` are removed. The field was stored, printed by `show`, compared by `isapprox` and converted by `change_precision` — but never read by `solve`/`solve_with_status`, so `Backtracking(; α₀ = 10.0)` configured nothing. The trial step now has exactly one source, the `α` argument:

```julia
solve(Backtracking(; α₀ = 3.0), 1.0, params)   # before — α₀ was silently ignored, α = 1 was used
solve(Backtracking(), 3.0, params)             # after
```

Nothing read the field, so the removal itself changes no results.

**A non-finite direction now raises `NonlinearSolverException`** ([#130](https://github.com/JuliaGNI/SimpleSolvers.jl/issues/130), [#179](https://github.com/JuliaGNI/SimpleSolvers.jl/pull/179)). An `Inf` direction used to pass the `isnan` guard; the line search then saw an infinite directional derivative, returned `LINESEARCH_NO_DESCENT`, and the solve made no progress without saying why. It cannot be damped — `nan_recovery!` scales by a factor and `Inf * nan_factor` is `Inf` — so it is now rejected outright. **A caller driving `solve!` in a time-stepping loop will see an exception where it previously saw a step that quietly achieved nothing.** This is the one visible regression risk in the release.

**An overflowed solve no longer reports convergence** ([#130](https://github.com/JuliaGNI/SimpleSolvers.jl/issues/130)). `residual_small` guarded only `isnan(‖F(x₀)‖)`, so an infinite initial residual made the relative term `f_reltol * Inf = Inf` and the gate vacuously true: a residual of `1e10` counted as small, and the solve claimed success wherever it happened to land. Such a solve now correctly reports non-convergence, so code that depended on the false positive will see the failure it always had.

**Internal rename** — `havenan` is now `SimpleSolvers.havenonfinite` and tests all three residuals with `isfinite`. Unexported and internal, so there is no deprecation.

## Added

- **Convenience entry points for `NonlinearProblem`** ([#159](https://github.com/JuliaGNI/SimpleSolvers.jl/issues/159), [#177](https://github.com/JuliaGNI/SimpleSolvers.jl/pull/177)). `NonlinearProblem` was exported but accepted nowhere, so a hand-built problem forced the seven-argument low-level constructor. Now: `NewtonSolver(x, nlp::NonlinearProblem, y = zero(x))` and the same for `PicardSolver` and `DogLegSolver`, hence `NonlinearSolver(method, x, nlp)`; plus `solve!(x, prob, method, args...; kwargs...)`, `solve(x₀, prob, method, ...)` (returns a new array, leaves `x₀` alone) and `solve_with_status!`, which returns the `NonlinearSolverStatus` rather than the solution. Each wrapper call builds a solver, so a loop should still construct one `NonlinearSolver` and reuse it.
- **An opt-in expansion phase for `Backtracking`** ([#174](https://github.com/JuliaGNI/SimpleSolvers.jl/issues/174)). `Backtracking(; expand = true)` lengthens an accepted *first* trial step while each longer trial still satisfies sufficient decrease and strictly improves the merit, tuned by the new `q` and `nexpand` keys. It exists because a shrink-only search pins `α` at the caller's ceiling on a direction whose natural scale is larger: on the SVD problem of GeometricOptimizers#31, a DFP direction wanting `α ≈ 11` cost **49 679** iterations, against **830** with expansion. The decision to expand costs no extra merit evaluation, and `false` is the default — behaviour is unchanged unless you ask for it.
- **Diagnosis and optional stopping for a solve that is not progressing** ([#173](https://github.com/JuliaGNI/SimpleSolvers.jl/issues/173), [#178](https://github.com/JuliaGNI/SimpleSolvers.jl/pull/178)). `max_stalls` catches a *frozen* iterate; this catches the case beside it, where the iterate keeps moving normally while the residual sits on a floor far above the requested tolerance — for which no existing criterion could fire, and which reported only `"Solver took 1000 iterations."`. The report is unconditional and names the residual achieved, the tolerance asked for, and that the iterate did *not* freeze. The stopping criterion is opt-in through two new `Options` fields, `f_stall_window` (default `0`, disabled) and `f_stall_factor` (default `0.5`); a window is a policy, not a test, so it is the caller's to set. No solve stops earlier than it did at default options.

## Fixed

- **`NaN` was only half of it** ([#130](https://github.com/JuliaGNI/SimpleSolvers.jl/issues/130)). Every guard the nonlinear solvers had against a trial iterate leaving the region where the problem is representable tested `isnan`, and `isnan` is false for `Inf` — so the singularity of the issue's own fixture, `5|x-2|³ - 1/|x|`, went undetected. Nothing downstream caught it either: `rfₐ > f_abstol_break` cannot, since `f_abstol_break` defaults to `Inf` and `Inf > Inf` is false. `nan_recovery!`, the dogleg trust-region rejection and the status predicates now all test `isfinite`.
- `iterate_settled` counted an infinite step as a frozen iterate, since `Inf ≤ ‖x‖·x_suctol` holds once `‖x‖` has overflowed too.
- `nan_recovery!` left its cache untouched at `nan_max_iterations = 0`, so the `PicardSolver` step — which reads that cache instead of re-evaluating `F` — tested a stale residual and committed a stale iterate from the *previous* solver step. One trial is now always evaluated, and the damping happens before the trial it is for, so the budget bounds the damping rather than the evaluation. The Picard step additionally refuses to commit a trial whose residual is not finite.
- The fixed-point bracketer's docstring gave the `a = 0` special case as though it were general ([#176](https://github.com/JuliaGNI/SimpleSolvers.jl/pull/176)).

## Compatibility

Julia 1.10 and later. No dependency bounds changed. Downstream trajectories are bit-identical: GeometricIntegrators × GeometricProblems, five integrators over 1000 steps, plus a collisional initial condition with no root.
`````
<!-- END RELEASE NOTES -->

author: yinlianghui
body:
Closes #4419

## The asymmetry

`userActions.delete` reached the record detail header in its **boolean** form but not in its **predicate** form.

| form | row kebab | detail header |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `userActions: { delete: false }` | hidden | hidden — the host lowers the boolean into `schema.showDelete` |
| `userActions: { delete: { visibleWhen: … } }` | hidden on excluded records | **still offered** |

The header ANDed three gates and never evaluated the predicate (`DetailView.tsx:306-307` on `main`):

```
showDelete: gatedSchema.showDelete && objectAllowsDelete && canDeleteRecord
```

So an author upgrading from "nobody may delete this object" to "these records may not be deleted" — the exact reason the object form exists — silently lost a surface. A key whose scope *shrinks* when you add a predicate to it is ADR-0078's silently-inert metadata, which is the framing the ruling adopted.

## The fix — one evaluator, one answer

The predicate is folded in as a **fourth conjunct**, evaluated against the open record through the same helper family the row surfaces already use. No fresh predicate-evaluation code on this path:

- **`userActionPredicates`** from `@object-ui/core` for the parse — the exact import `RelatedList.tsx:1130-1131` makes, and the one `plugin-grid`'s `resolveRowCrudAffordances` feeds the row kebab from. It is THE parser for the boolean/object form.
- **`useRowPredicate`** from `@object-ui/react` for the evaluation. `plugin-grid`'s `evalRowActionVisibility` — the body of `isBuiltinRowActionVisible`, which `RowActionMenu.tsx:348-350` calls — documents itself as mirroring `useRowPredicate(pred, row, { fallback: false, warnOnError: true, label, fields })` *"exactly, boolean short-circuit included"*, and is hook-free **only** because a row loop evaluates a variable number of actions inside one `useMemo`. The header evaluates a fixed arity of one record, so the hook form is that same evaluator without the constraint that shaped the wrapper. (`isBuiltinRowActionVisible` itself is not importable here: `plugin-grid` is not a `plugin-detail` dependency, and `@object-ui/components`' copy is not re-exported from its barrel.)

Posture copied verbatim from `DataTableBuiltinRowActionItem`:

- `visibleWhen` false → the header affordance is **hidden**. Fails CLOSED; declared by `!= null`, not truthiness, so `visibleWhen: false` is a gate rather than "ungated" (the objectui#3492 invariant).
- `disabledWhen` true → the affordance renders **disabled**, not removed — kebab symmetry. Applied to the desktop Edit CTA *and* its `sm:hidden` overflow twin, plus the overflow Delete, so one predicate gets one answer at every breakpoint.
- `objectSchema.fields` is passed to every predicate for the same reason `ObjectGrid` passes `objectFields` to `RowActionMenu`: a relation field must bind as the stored foreign key, not whatever `$expand` substituted on this surface.

The existing gates all remain, so a predicate that holds can never resurrect a button the user may not press. A bare boolean yields **no** predicate, which keeps the boolean form the host's channel rather than growing a second definition of it here.

## Red-first

New file `packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/DetailView.userActionPredicates.test.tsx`, on the card's own fixture (`showcase_invoice`'s real declaration, paid `INV-1011` vs open `INV-1001`).

Reverse verification was done by removing the fix with `git checkout origin/main -- DetailView.tsx` and restoring from a sha256-verified copy (never `git stash`). Exactly the four new-behaviour cases move; the seven must-not-change cases are green in both directions.

**Pre-fix (fix removed), verbatim** — the failing element's opening tag is spelled with a space after the angle bracket, because GitHub strips a bare bracket-plus-letter from a stored body as an HTML tag and swallowed the line on the first write:

```
 × hides the header Delete on a record its `delete.visibleWhen` excludes 200ms
 × renders the header Edit DISABLED when `edit.disabledWhen` holds 1034ms
 × accepts the canonical `{ dialect, source }` envelope 62ms
 × treats a literal `visibleWhen: false` as declared, not ungated 52ms

AssertionError: expected [ 'Share', 'Edit', 'Delete' ] to not include 'Delete'

Error: expect(element).toBeDisabled()
Received element is not disabled:
  < button
  class="… bg-primary text-primary-foreground hover:bg-primary/90 h-10 px-4 py-2 gap-2 hidden sm:inline-flex"
  data-state="closed"
/ >

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  4 failed | 7 passed (11)
```

**Post-fix:**

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  11 passed (11)
```

Must-not-change, green on both sides: predicate-TRUE record keeps Delete and an enabled Edit; an object with no `userActions` is completely ungated; `delete: false` yields no predicate (the boolean stays the host's channel) while the host lowering it to `showDelete: false` still hides Delete; a read-only role keeps Delete hidden even though the predicate holds; `sys_share` is untouched on an excluded record.

## Verification

```
pnpm --filter '@object-ui/plugin-detail^...' build           exit=0   (dependency closure first)
pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-detail/                 81 files, 781 tests passed
pnpm exec tsc --noEmit                        (plugin-detail) exit=0
pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.test.json           (plugin-detail) exit=0
pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail lint                  exit=0 (0 errors; pre-existing warnings)
node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs                         OK (4221 files)
node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs                    OK
node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs                    OK
```

`.d.ts` measured both ways — `dist/index.d.ts` built from `origin/main` and from this branch is **byte-identical** (78 lines, `diff` empty), so no public type surface moves. Changeset: **patch** `@object-ui/plugin-detail`.

## Scope, and one thing the PM should read

Surface is `DetailView.tsx` + its new test + one changeset. Untouched by ruling: `RelatedList.tsx` (already correct, read-only reference), `plugin-grid/**`, selection-bar components (#4420), `console/**`, `content/docs/releases/`.

**Measured, and it does not match the card's repro attribution:** the console record page's header is **not** served by `DetailView`. `plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-details.tsx:257` mounts the inner `detail-view` with `showHeader: schema.showHeader ?? false`, and `app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx` has zero `DetailView` mounts — its header Edit/Share/Delete come from `synthSystemActions` at line 1911, which ANDs `resolveRecordHeaderActionGates(objectDef, …)` (the boolean affordance channel) with the record-level verdict and never parses or evaluates the predicate.

So this PR fixes the `DetailView` header — `RecordDetailDrawer` and every host mounting `detail-view` / `detail` with `showEdit` / `showDelete` — which is exactly the site #4419 names and the ruling scoped. It does **not** close the console page-header path that #4419's browser table screenshotted; that surface is already owned by the open #4213, where the file:line evidence has been posted as [a comment](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/4213#issuecomment-5275474292) rather than as a duplicate issue. No new issue filed.

author: saltypatron
body:
## Summary
Main's deploy is red: the first live extension upgrade after #1063 died at

```
ERROR: cannot drop function ops.ducet_rank(geometry) because other objects depend on it
DETAIL: function ops.ducet_ordered(integer,integer) depends on function ops.ducet_rank(geometry)
```

`ops.ducet_ordered` is `BEGIN ATOMIC`, so the **installed** copy records a real `pg_depend` edge on `ducet_rank`; the file's `DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS ops.ducet_rank` runs while that dependent still exists and the upgrade script aborts. The DROPs only ever worked on first install, when nothing depended on anything yet.

**Fix:** remove both DROPs. Neither function's signature or return shape changes, so `CREATE OR REPLACE` alone is the correct, dependent-safe form — the exact remedy #1004 applied to ten identity/ functions and the failure mode #1006 documented for `band_edges`. Comments at both sites now say why, so the DROPs don't come back.

Merging this un-reds main: the next push regenerates the upgrade script without the DROP and the extension sync completes. ISA gates green.

author: luoringzl
body:
## 目标

为项目级排期增加跨项目依赖、里程碑与 CPM 关键路径能力，让项目计划不再只是单个项目的 start/DDL，而能描述“哪个项目必须先完成、后续项目何时可启动、哪些节点没有浮动时间”。

## 变更

- 新增 `src/planning/project-dependencies.mjs`
  - 项目 dependencies 规范化
  - 支持 FS / SS / FF / SF 四类依赖
  - 支持工作日 lag / lead
  - 缺失前置项目、自依赖、循环依赖检测
  - 稳定拓扑排序
  - 自定义 milestones 与内置资产完成 / 视频完成 / DDL 合并
  - CPM forward / backward pass
  - 最早开始/完成、最晚开始/完成、总浮动时间
  - 关键项目与主关键路径
  - 工作日 deadline late risk
  - 项目 dependency readiness / blockers
  - 不可变 add/remove dependency 与 milestone upsert helpers
- 新增 `tests/project-dependencies.test.mjs`。

## 关键路径语义

项目 duration 优先使用 `plannedDurationDays`；未设置时从 `startDate → DDL` 按公司工作日历推导。关键路径日期、lag 和 deadline risk 都复用 V2.1 工作日历，因此周末、公司休息日和补班日会真实影响项目网络排期。

## 示例验证

测试网络 A→B→D 与 A→C→D：A/B/D 应构成关键路径，C 有 2 个工作日浮动；D 若计划完成晚于自身 DDL 1 个工作日，会进入 deadlineRisks。

## 风险控制

本 PR 先交付纯规划层，不修改现有项目表单或数据库版本。当前 project upsert 已保留未知扩展字段，因此 dependencies / milestones / plannedDurationDays 可先作为向后兼容项目字段存在；UI 与正式字段编辑器后续独立接入。

## 验证

GitHub Actions 执行完整 `npm test`、模板生成与 Windows Setup / Portable 构建。

author: mnehmos
body:
Phase 1 of the multi-user plan (host side). Pairs with `Mnehmos/mnehmos.rpg.mcp` [#82](https://github.com/Mnehmos/mnehmos.rpg.mcp/pull/82), which verifies the header this mints.

## Why

The reference engine has no tenant isolation of its own, so the host has been compensating: `reference-engine-dm.ts` force-overwrites `worldId`/`partyId`/`sessionId` on outbound calls and gates `characterId` against an allowlist of ids the model legitimately learned this turn.

That control is real and carefully built, but it lives *inside the request body*, alongside arguments the model produced. This moves tenant identity out of the payload entirely and into a signed header the model never sees and cannot influence.

## What

**`reference-engine-tenant.ts`** — mints an HMAC-SHA256 token over `accountId`, `campaignId`, `worldId`, `partyId`, `iat`, `exp`. Short TTL (120s), since it is minted per outbound call.

**`reference-engine-client.ts`** — takes the tenant as a **separate argument** to `callTool`, never a field on `args`, and signs it into `x-rpg-tenant`.

It is omitted for tenant-agnostic meta-tools, which the engine serves unscoped, and omitted rather than faked when no secret is configured — failing closed at the engine beats inventing a context it would have to trust blindly.

**adapter / dm** — tenant is derived from the authenticated `accountId`/`campaignId` plus the routing row, which is the only binding between a Lantern account and a set of reference-engine ids. `tenantFor()` keeps that derivation in one place across the nine adapter call sites.

## Risk

**Low for this PR in isolation; the risk is in deploy ordering.**

- Until `REFERENCE_ENGINE_TENANT_SECRET` is set, the host sends **no header** and behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged. This PR is inert without configuration.
- The engine must have `RPG_MCP_TENANT_SECRET` set **before** this ships with a secret configured, or every scoped call returns 401 and campaigns stop responding. Engine PR #82 tolerates an absent header, so the safe order is: merge #82 → set both secrets → merge this.
- The secret must **differ per environment**. Staging and production currently share a transport token; repeating that here would let a staging compromise mint production tenant contexts.
- No change to what the engine does with the header yet — nothing reads it for routing until Phase 2 makes `getDb()` resolve a database per campaign. This PR cannot change which data a call reaches.

Rollback is a revert plus unsetting the secret; no data or schema is touched.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A scoped `callTool` sends `x-rpg-tenant` carrying the authenticated `accountId`/`campaignId`.
- [x] The tenant is a separate argument, never a field on `args`, so model output cannot influence it.
- [x] The service auth token is still sent alongside it — the two answer different questions.
- [x] Tenant-agnostic meta-tool calls (`load_tool_schema`) send **no** tenant header.
- [x] With no secret configured, no header is sent and no unsigned context is invented.
- [x] Two calls for different campaigns produce two distinct tokens; no cross-campaign reuse.
- [x] Token verifies under the engine's algorithm and does not verify under a different secret.
- [x] Existing behaviour unchanged when the secret is unset.

## Verification

- `npm test` — 732 passed, no failures.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — exit 0.
- `npm run build` — clean.

11 new tests, of which the load-bearing ones:

- The signer test **verifies with raw crypto rather than calling the engine's verifier**, which lives in a separate repository. If either side changes the wire format without the other, one of the two suites fails. That is the only cross-repo contract check available short of an integration environment.
- Asserts the token is two base64url segments with no `+`, `/`, or `=`, so it survives an HTTP header round-trip.
- Asserts a token minted with one secret does not verify against another — the staging/production separation depends on it.
- Client tests assert the header is present for scoped calls, carries the right campaign, sits alongside the service auth token, and is **absent** for meta-tool calls and when no secret is configured.

Not covered: a live end-to-end call against a running engine with matching secrets. That is the deploy-time check, and it is why the ordering above matters.

author: sameersheikh3999
body:
Extends the 1-4 wobble experiment with a second scoring scale and the cross-transcript layer needed to judge indicators rather than lessons.

New:
  wobble_eval/binary.py         YES/NO rubric rendering built from the framework's
                                own level descriptors, prompts, three-tier parser,
                                and binary statistics (Gwet's AC1, Cochran's Q,
                                Wilson intervals, confidence calibration)
  wobble_eval/charts_binary.py  ten figures, sharing charts.py's palette
  wobble_eval/multi_binary.py   pooled analysis across transcripts: per-indicator
                                reliability AND discrimination, Holm-corrected,
                                classified HEALTHY / NOISY / UNINFORMATIVE / BROKEN
  run_wobble_binary.py          single-session binary runner
  run_multi_binary.py           directory runner, crash-safe with --resume
  compare_scales.py             1-4 vs binary head to head, compared at the
                                decision level so the coefficients share a baseline
  requirements.txt              pinned to the versions actually run
  report/                       plain-language write-up of the findings

Fixes:
  backend.py    add ~/.local/bin to the claude CLI search path (the native
                installer's default on Windows); without it the Agent SDK
                backend cannot start at all
  charts.py     chart_drift crashed formatting None when a run had too few
                iterations for the ICC rater test to exist
  run_multi.py  the pooled report died on idxmin() over an all-NA alpha column,
                discarding a completed scoring run at the last step

Why AC1 rather than kappa/alpha on the binary scale: with two categories and a skewed split, chance-corrected coefficients collapse toward zero even at high raw agreement. That is the prevalence paradox, a property of the statistic and not of the scorer. All three are reported so the divergence stays visible.

.gitignore now excludes the pooled run outputs for the same reason Transcripts/ is excluded: their evidence columns quote classroom speech verbatim and name individual students.

author: jthiruveedula
body:
**Holding for your review — the main page, so not merging.**
Look at it: `npm run preview` in `site/`, then <http://localhost:4321/genai-data-platform/>

## The gap this fills

The hero's live WebGL scene paints nothing until it mounts. On a cold load, the first thing anyone saw was an empty box. This fills it — and then keeps going, because the film turned out to be worth more as a permanent layer than as a placeholder.

## Division of labour

- **The film is the room:** dense ruled floor, fog, 900 drifting motes, the arc a request travels, dimension lines, and faint bracket frames marking where the live nodes sit.
- **The canvas keeps the ten pipeline nodes** and draws straight over it — its renderer is `alpha:true`, so the film shows through.

Neither duplicates the other: the film carries depth a browser shouldn't rasterise every frame; the canvas carries everything that has to react to a cloud switch or scroll position. **A film could not have replaced the live hero** — it re-tints per cloud and its ten labels track node positions in 3D.

## Two things I got wrong first, both caught by looking

1. The first cut rendered the pipeline nodes *into the film*, which meant either tearing the film down when the live scene mounted (so it would never be seen) or drawing every cube twice.
2. Subtler, visible only on screen: the live `GridHelper` and the film's floor are two grids at slightly different angles — that reads as interference, not depth. The live grid is gone; the film owns the floor.

## Earning its bytes

Poster is in the markup and paints before any script. The **934KB** loop is an upgrade that loads only on a desktop wide enough, only when motion is allowed, and only after the `load` event. It reveals itself on `playing`, so a half-decoded frame never replaces a clean poster.

Seamless by construction — every animated quantity is periodic over the composition's exact duration, so the last frame hands back to the first with no cut and no crossfade hiding one.

## Measured, not assumed

The poster became the LCP element and **made the metric worse**: LCP 3.2s, performance 0.87. Shrinking it to 960 wide (23KB) and preloading it:

| | before this PR | first cut | shipped |
|---|---|---|---|
| LCP | ~2.6s | 3.2s | **2.7s** |
| TBT | 0ms | 270ms | **0ms** |
| CLS | 0 | 0 | **0** |
| Performance | 0.95 | 0.87 | **0.95** |

## Verification

- `npx playwright test` — 129 passed (6 new: poster in the HTML, both layers persist, loop upgrades on desktop-with-motion, phones and reduced-motion get the poster alone, both assets served)
- Lighthouse homepage: a11y 1.0, every error gate passing

author: tugrulguner
body:
Guidance for agents working on intpot lived in `.claude/skills/`, where only Claude Code could read it — and it had drifted away from the code. This moves all of it into files every tool and every human reads, then removes the vendor directory entirely.

## The stale rules

Two claims in `pr-review/SKILL.md` were wrong, both about bugs fixed after the skill was written:

| Claim | Reality |
|---|---|
| "Return type adjustments: CLI → `None`, API → `dict`" | `transforms.py:_target_return_type` returns `None` when the body has no top-level return, and scalar returns get wrapped as `{"result": ...}`. Treating `dict` as unconditional is exactly what made every generated FastAPI handler 500 before #56. |
| "`discover_sources()` silently skips unrecognizable files — this is intentional" | Non-app files are still skipped quietly, but import failures always report to stderr since #59. |

A reviewer applying either rule would have waved through a regression of the bug that produced it. Nobody caught them because the only tool that could read the file was the one being told the wrong thing.

## Where it went

Split by kind, not by vendor:

- **`AGENTS.md`** — what to look for. Architecture contracts, `ToolInfo`/`ParameterInfo` invariants, template rules, return types, error handling, test and style conventions. Corrected, and each rule that came from a real bug now names the bug.
- **`docs/reviewing.md`** — how to do it. Gathering a PR or local diff, reading current state before judging the diff, which tests to run for which directory, verifying claims before making them, severity classification and output format. Assumes nothing beyond a shell, `git`, and `gh`.

## `.claude/` and `CLAUDE.md` are gone

Once the criteria and procedure moved out, what remained was 52 lines of skill frontmatter and a 10-line pointer file — no facts about intpot in any of it. An address label plus a shortcut for typing `/pr-review 69`. That's a thin reason to privilege one vendor in a project whose own `intpot add skills` emits six formats specifically so that none is privileged.

`.claude/`, `.cursor/`, `.windsurf/` and `.clinerules/` are now gitignored, and `test_no_vendor_specific_agent_files_are_tracked` keeps it that way. Anyone who wants a slash-command wrapper can keep one locally.

`intpot add skills` writing `.claude/skills/` into a **user's** project is the product, and is untouched.

## Checks become tests

`tests/test_docs.py`. A test runs for every contributor on every PR whether or not they use an agent; guidance in a skill file runs only when an agent reads it.

- `test_readme_documents_every_cli_flag` — walks the Click command tree and asserts each long flag appears in the README. The class of gap #64 closed by hand.
- `test_docs_reference_only_paths_that_exist` — resolves every backticked path in `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/reviewing.md` and `docs/releasing.md` against git rather than the filesystem, so it doesn't depend on what's lying around in a given checkout.
- `test_no_vendor_specific_agent_files_are_tracked` — as above.

The path test caught a dangling reference in the criteria while they were being written, then caught its own environment dependence in CI.

Precedent is `tests/test_skills_content.py` from #65, which began as a rule in a skill that never fired.

## Pre-commit hook for conflict copies

`.gitignore` covers iCloud/Dropbox conflict copies while untracked, but staging a directory picks them up anyway — that's how `intpot-cli 2.md` reached #65. Uses pre-commit's built-in `language: fail`, no wrapper script. Verified it fires on `docs/cookbook 2.md` and lets normal filenames through.

## Releasing leaves CONTRIBUTING.md

It told contributors to run `uv version` and `git push origin v0.4.2` — neither of which a contributor can do. Now `docs/releasing.md`, labelled for maintainers, with a pointer left behind saying explicitly not to bump or tag in a PR. The roadmap-check step from #68 was carried here rather than duplicated; #68 dropped its copy so the two don't collide. `CONTRIBUTING.md` now points contributors at `docs/reviewing.md` so they can see what a reviewer will apply to their change.

---

`make check` green: 253 passed, up from 193. CI green on 3.11 / 3.12 / 3.13. Not user-facing, hence `skip-changelog`.

author: mckelveygreg
body:
Follow-up to #75. That PR found a latent coupling and — correctly, given the options it had — documented it in a test comment rather than duplicating a magic number across modules. There was a third option: **export the constant.**

## The coupling

`uploadCustomIr`'s `pointerConfirmed` checks `echo[pLsbOff] === (program & 0x7f)`, while the staged value is `INIT_PROGRAM` (`0x7F`). So a destination `program` of `0x7F` would satisfy that comparison against the **un-repointed** stage, and report a copy-on-save-as that never happened — a false durability confirmation.

It is unreachable only because `DeviceSession.writePreset` rejects slots above `MAX_WRITABLE_SLOT` (`0x7d`) first. That guard lives in a **different module**, and `MAX_WRITABLE_SLOT` was module-private, so #75 could only duplicate the literal or write a comment. It chose the comment, which was the right call between those two.

## This change

Exports `MAX_WRITABLE_SLOT` and asserts it in `uploadCustomIr`. No duplication, and the dependency is now expressed in code: if that guard is ever relaxed, this throws loudly instead of silently returning a false confirmation.

**Belt-and-braces on a path unreachable today** — the value is that a cross-module safety dependency stops resting on a comment somebody has to notice.

`npm run check` fully green: 368 tests, dead-code and dupes clean (the export has a real consumer, so `fallow` is satisfied).

Created by Greg-Bot.

author: krishtoautomate
body:
Held back until **every template passed at least 4 smoke tests against a live grid**, per the bar set for this PR. All five now do. | Template | Result | |---|---| | `playwright` | 8 scenarios, 3 parallel workers | | `playwright-python` | 9 tests | | `selenium-python` | 4 tests | | `wdio` | 4 spec files — 110 steps | | `appium-js` | 5 scenarios, 10 steps on a real Android device | Getting there required fixing four defects. Each one meant a template proved nothing. ## 1. `wdio` could not install at all `package.json` asked for `wdio-html-nice-reporter@^3.2.0`. That package's published versions stop at **8.1.7** — there is no 3.x. `npm install` fails with `ETARGET` and no dependency tree is produced. `appium-js` declared `^8.1.7` correctly, so the two templates disagreed on the same dependency. And since `wdio` ships a `pretest` hook that bootstraps `node_modules` on first run, this broke the documented entry command outright — a clone could not run the suite at all. ## 2. `appium-js` could not start a session on the grid The Android capabilities defaulted `deviceName` and `udid` to `'emulator-5554'`: ```ts 'appium:deviceName': process.env.DEVICE_UDID || 'emulator-5554', 'appium:udid': process.env.DEVICE_UDID || 'emulator-5554', ``` So leaving `DEVICE_UDID` unset did not mean *"any free device"* — it meant *"this specific device"*, for hardware that does not exist. The grid replied `No nodes support the capabilities in the request`. Omitting the capabilities instead lets the grid auto-distribute. `appPackage`/`appActivity` now get the same conditional treatment the iOS block already applied to `bundleId`, so a device-level smoke needs no app installed. Confirmed by watching the grid hand out **T810S**, **SM-N960W** and **SM-N986W** across successive runs. ## 3. Two suites asserted against copy that no longer exists The live H1 is `"Real devices, zero lag"`. `wdio` still expected `"From user story to raised defect"`, `"Real Android & iOS devices"`, `"Talk to your device"` — all gone. Its load feature also still asserted a `"See how it works"` button that the smoke feature had **already** dropped, with a comment explaining it collapses below the fold at ≤600px; the fix was never carried across. `selenium-python` had the right phrase in its known-phrase list but compared literally. The H1 wraps with a `
`, so the DOM text is `"Real devices,\nzero lag."` and never matched `"Real devices, zero lag"`. Fixed by collapsing whitespace on both sides — not by pinning another brittle literal, which would just rot again on the next line-break change. ## 4. `appium-js` smoke was one scenario doing four jobs Split into five, so a failure names the capability that broke rather than collapsing every check into one red test. Two round-trip checks added: the session reports a known platform, and it still answers a second command (a single call can be served from session-creation state; a second proves the session is genuinely live and the proxy still forwarding). ## Notes - The `1.59.0` client against a `1.59.1` grid in `playwright-python` did **not** reproduce the parity failure from #3 — Playwright's guid protocol is stable within a minor. Left alone rather than churned. - No `.env`, `.venv` or `node_modules` in the diff; verified against the ignore rules before committing.

author: wangsijie
body:
## Summary

Implements [LOG-14029](https://linear.app/silverhand/issue/LOG-14029/call-the-script-runner-worker-directly-from-core): remove the cloud hop from the script-run path. Cloud is pinned to a single region while the script-runner Worker is on Cloudflare's edge, so every script run currently pays an avoidable cross-region round trip inline in token issuance.

- `runScriptOnCloud` now calls the Worker's `POST /api/script-run` directly when **dev features are enabled and `SCRIPT_RUNNER_ENDPOINT` is set**; otherwise it keeps the existing `POST /api/services/script-run` cloud hop. The gate stays until the direct path is verified and the endpoint is injected in every region.
- `CloudConnectionLibrary.getWorkerAccessToken()` mints the Worker token with the tenant's existing cloud-connection M2M credentials against the regional admin tenant (resource `https://*.logto.workers.dev`, scope `invoke:worker:script-run`), cached separately from the cloud service token. A token minted without the scope (grant alteration not yet deployed) fails loudly and is never cached.
- Worker script failures are reshaped into the exact error body the cloud route produces (including the `name: 'Error'` default for nameless runtime failures), so `parseCloudScriptFailure` / `buildCloudScriptFailureError` and every caller downstream behave identically on both transports, keeping the `denied` signal intact.
- The Worker's request guard requires `tenantId` (it scopes the isolate cache), so it is now threaded from the libraries; `JwtCustomizerLibrary` gains a `tenantId` constructor parameter.
- `jest.setup.js` pins `SCRIPT_RUNNER_ENDPOINT` to empty so a developer shell running a local Worker cannot flip the cloud-hop suites onto the direct path.

Counterpart cloud PR (grants the scope to the tenant application role; no Worker changes needed — all regions mint against the central admin tenant the deployed Worker already trusts): logto-io/cloud#2077.

Note for stacking: #9433 (removing the dev-feature guard) is parked and will be rebased on top of this change; it does not touch `script-runner/cloud.ts`.

## Testing

- Unit tests: new `cloud.worker.test.ts` covers the direct path (success envelope, failure reshaping round-trip through `parseCloudScriptFailure`, transport failures, isTest/tenantId forwarding, fallback selection); `cloud-connection.test.ts` covers worker-token minting, separate caching, and the missing-scope failure.

body:
## What & why **The islanders stop standing still.** Six people on St Peters now keep a day — out at dawn, at their post through the morning, down to the store for their dinner, on the green at dusk, in through their own door at night — and *where any of them is at a given hour is a pure function of `(worldSeed, gameTime)`*, recomputed and never saved. **Backlog item:** M2-23 (NPC daily routines) — phase 1: the engine, the data model, and one honest day each **Pillar(s) served:** P3 A Living Working Coast (above all) · P5 Cozy-with-Teeth **Owning role:** world-content `StPetersInhabitants` said it in its own remarks since #354 — *"anchored, NOT scheduled … nothing here plans a path, ticks, or reads the clock"*. This is the pass that lifts that. --- ## 1. The law that shaped everything: determinism **Nothing ticks. Nothing is saved. There is no save-format change.** `RoutinePlan.SampleAt(hourOfDay)` is one pure, allocation-free function, and it is the whole engine: ``` block = the departure hour most recently passed (wraps midnight) elapsed = hourOfDay − that departure (wraps midnight) walked = elapsed × speed × secondsPerGameHour (metres) position = PointAlong(that block's route, walked) (clamped at both ends ⇒ arrival needs no branch) ``` Consequences, each of which is a test rather than a claim: - the same seed at the same hour, twice, is the same position **bit for bit**; - a **frozen clock freezes the village** — a paused clock *is* the same hour; - nothing integrates, so nothing can drift over a night of standing still; - a villager enabled mid-leg lands **exactly** where the one who has been walking all along is, because "mid-leg" is simply what the function returns for that hour. This is the case that matters: a region loading at 18:06 puts everybody mid-stride on the right leg, with no snap and no history. The precedent was `AmbientFleetPlan` + `AmbientFleetSchedule`, and the split is the same one: `RoutinePlanner` owns geometry, `RoutineSchedule` owns the clock, and the FNV-1a seeding is re-derived (World may not reference Boats — rule 4) with the same process-stable constants, no `UnityEngine.Random` and no `string.GetHashCode`. **Departure jitter is a personality, not noise.** It is seeded from `(worldSeed, routineId, entryIndex)` and the day index is deliberately **not** folded in: the postmistress opens a few minutes past eight the same way every morning, which a player can learn (`npcs-and-routines.md` §2.1 — *"predictability is a feature"*), and there is no discontinuity at midnight in the block that spans it. The amplitude is clamped to under half the tighter of the two gaps a block sits between, so jitter provably cannot reorder a day. --- ## 2. The roster — six days, and every one of them the owner's to edit Six `RoutineDef` assets under `Data/Routines`, one per person, ids `routine.snake_case`. Times are GAME hours; at the pinned 1800 s day one game hour is 75 real seconds, so 1.15 m/s covers ~86 m of island per game hour. `→` marks a walk the player can watch. ### Rose MacIsaac — the Recreation | → down to the green | | 21:30 | **inside the red saltbox** | Home | → home | ### Marguerite LeBlanc — the storekeeper · 1.10 m/s · ±5 min | From | At | Activity | Walk | |---|---|---|---| | 07:00 | behind the store counter | Work | out of her own door — she **lives over the shop** | | 13:00 | the post office doorstep | Errand | → up the lane with the day's mail | | 14:30 | behind the schoolteacher · 1.05 m/s · ±4 min | From | At | Activity | Walk | |---|---|---|---| | 07:30 | the white farmhouse step (she **boards** there) | Home | out | | 08:15 | **inside the schoolhouse** | Work Recreation | → **out the painted dirt west** | | 20:30 | **inside the white farmhouse** | Home | → the length of the island back, in the dusk | ### Junior Poirier — the clam digger · 1.35 m/s · ±7 min | From | At | Activity | Walk | |---|---|---|---| | 06:00 | the sage cottage step | Home | out early | | 06:30 | the head of the flats | Work | → **out the painted dirt west** | | 12:00 | the store counter, slot B | Errand | → the long walk in for his dinner | | 14:30 | the head of the flats | Work | → back out | | 19:00 | the green, slot D | Recreation | → in off the flats | | 21:00 | **inside the sage cottage** (one side of the doorway lane) | Home | → in | ### Basil Samson — the old skipper · 0.95 m/s · ±8 min | From | At | Activity | Walk | |---|---|---|---| | 05:00 | the wharf head, watching the water | Work | → **the length of the island east, 233 m, 3.3 game hours** | | 12:00 | the shoreward end of the planks | Work | → down the pier | | 15:00 | the wharf head | Recreation | → back out | | 18:00 | **inside the sage cottage** (the other side) | Home | → the whole island again, in the dusk | The slowest walk on the island and by far the longest. He walks it on the **painted dirt path east** — the same path the player walks out to the dory — so you meet him on it. ### Aunt Ginny — ⭐ deliberately the smallest day on the island · 1.00 m/s · ±3 min | From | At | Activity | |---|---|---| | 06:30 | the garden, round the cottage's west side | Work | | 10:00 | **her own step, unmoved** | Home | | 19:00 | the green, centre slot | Recreation | | 21:00 | her step | Home | **She is the onboarding gate** — the first conversation, `met_ginny`, and the `FrontedFeeGrant` that stops the clam licence being a soft-lock — so the opening cannot afford her to be somewhere else on the first morning. author: tamnd
body:
A restarted page service comes up behind the sealed rounds, and the rounds loop read the whole of a round's frames for the tenant before handing the first one to the sink. The sink is the ingest, which says stop the moment its 200 ms slice is spent, and the fetch is what spends it. So the poll stopped on the first frame, and stopping inside a round left the cursor on the round, so the next poll paid for the same chunk again for the same one frame.

On server2 that turned into a freeze, because the frame it kept handing over was one apply_frames drops as already covered. applied never moved, so the next poll asked the same question and got the same answer, for forty minutes.

The chain walk never had this: it hands over every frame of a segment and asks about stopping after it, so a stop lands on a segment boundary and the cursor names the next one. The rounds loop now works the same way, with a chunk cursor on top of the round cursor, and it does better than the chain can because a round index carries the lsn bounds of every chunk, so a chunk that ends at or below what the caller has applied is a GET nobody pays for.

zou-log grows `round_chunks` and `read_round_chunk` so a caller never has to materialize a whole round. `CatchUp` counts chunks next to rounds and segments, and the progress line prints the chunk the cursor is on.

Three tests, each of which fails without the cursor fix:

- a stop inside a round comes back to the next chunk, no frame redelivered, and the range GETs a call makes match the chunks it reports
- a round scan skips the chunks below the applied lsn without fetching them
- a poll over sealed rounds advances on every slice, driven through the real ingest with the deadline already spent

The payloads in those tests are xorshift noise on purpose. Constant bytes compress a whole round into one chunk and the test passes without testing anything.

Closes #327

author: timothy-le7
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
## Summary

Audits whether the workbench should support the latest LeRobot (**0.6.1**, released 2026-08-03, while we default to **0.5.1** from 2026-04-07), then **runs the conclusions against a real install** rather than stopping at static analysis. That second step found a shipped defect.

**Recommendation: adopt 0.6.1 as an additional supported version and promote it to default once the image gates pass.** The upgrade is nearly free; the current state carries more risk than the move.

Three artifacts:

- `docs/workbench/lerobot-version-support-audit-20260813.md` — the audit and proposal.
- `npa/scripts/audit_lerobot_release.py` — a static pre-flight that makes the audit reproducible for the *next* release, plus tests.
- A fix for **D6**, below.

## The defect the real run found (D6)

`npa-lerobot:0.6.0` **cannot construct a Diffusion Policy**. LeRobot 0.6.0 moved `diffusers` and `transformers` out of the base install and behind extras, and enforces them with `require_package()` **inside each policy's `__init__`**. Our extras string was never updated, so `lerobot[training,evaluation,pusht,libero]` installs no `diffusers`, the module still *imports* cleanly, and the failure lands at `make_policy()` — at run time, on the real training command.

Reproduced on an **H100 80GB** with the image pulled from the registry:

```
lerobot 0.6.0 | torch 2.11.0+cu130 | cuda available: True | NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3
diffusers in image:    0        <- absent
transformers in image: 1        <- present, but only transitively via [libero]

A. DiffusionPolicy as shipped  -> ImportError: 'diffusers' is required but not installed
B. ACTPolicy as shipped        -> ValueError: You must provide at least one image ...
C. DiffusionPolicy + diffusers -> ValueError: You must provide at least one image ...
```

B is the control: `ValueError` means construction got past dependency checks into ordinary config validation. C returning *the same* error as B is the point — with the extra present, Diffusion behaves exactly like ACT, so the missing extra was the entire defect.

Also reproduced end-to-end through the actual training command on a real 0.6.1 install:

```
--policy.type=act        exit 0   trains and checkpoints
--policy.type=diffusion  exit 1   ImportError in make_policy(): 'diffusers' is required
--policy.type=diffusion  exit 0   trains and checkpoints, after adding lerobot[diffusion]
```

**Scope.** 0.5.1 is unaffected — `diffusers` is a *core* dependency there — which is why the default B300 image, built from a genuine 0.5.1 commit, was never exposed. This hits anyone opting into `--lerobot-version 0.6.0`, and would have hit everyone had 0.6.x been promoted to default. Two details show the extras set was already drifting: the Dockerfiles hand-install `num2words`, which is exactly what the `smolvla` extra supplies, and `libero` is the only reason `transformers` is present at all.

**Fix:** request the extras the policies gate on (`…,libero,diffusion,smolvla`) in the manifest and Dockerfile, and teach the pre-flight to resolve the extras graph (`diffusion` → `diffusers-dep` → `diffusers`) and cross-check it against the `require_package` gates it finds in each policy module. Against the pre-fix manifest it now reports:

```
LeRobot 0.6.0
  [FAIL] policy-extras: --policy.type=diffusion needs diffusers (add extra 'diffusion')
LeRobot 0.5.1
  [PASS] policy-extras: lerobot[pusht,libero] constructs ['act', 'diffusion', 'smolvla']
```

## Why adopting 0.6.1 is cheap

Checked against the published wheels, then executed against a real 0.6.1 install (Python 3.12.13, torch 2.9.0):

| Claim | Executed result |
|---|---|
| 19/19 bindings resolve | all 19 **import** for real |
| `env_eval_freq` replaces `eval_freq` | `lerobot-train --help` offers `--env_eval_freq`, no longer `--eval_freq` |
| `--policy.path` still works | accepted — parsing reaches a Hub lookup, while a bogus `--policy.x` is rejected. Absent from `--help` only because draccus resolves the path alias pre-parse, which is easy to misread as a break |
| adapters need no migration | a dataset written by `npa/adapter/sim_to_lerobot.py` loads under 0.6.1 `LeRobotDataset`, video decoded, expected keys present |
| the workbench train path works | `lerobot-train --policy.type=act` runs real steps and checkpoints |

Plus: 0.6.1's only breaking change (`lerobot.types` → `lerobot.lerobot_types`) is unreferenced here; signature changes are additive; `CODEBASE_VERSION` is still `v3.0` and 0.6.x made `info.json` parsing forward-compatible; the validated B300 torch stack already satisfies 0.6.1's bounds; and none of 0.6.0's other breaks apply (we never pass `--dataset.vcodec`, never use `sac`, never write `subtask_index`).

## Other findings, independent of the upgrade

- **`npa-lerobot-policy:0.1.1` is a current pin shipping a dependency set upstream declares unusable.** It installs `lerobot[pusht]==0.5.1`, then force-upgrades torch 2.12.1 / torchvision 0.27.1 / diffusers ≥0.38 — all three outside 0.5.1's declared bounds. Because the upgrade is a second `pip` call, nothing re-resolves and the build succeeds silently. This is the mechanical root cause of the torch/torchcodec ABI mismatch already noted in `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **The manifest's torch pins are dead data** — `torch_install_pins()` has no production caller.
- **0.6.0 has no hardware-validated image.** The bare tag exists and runs (it is what D6 was reproduced on), but has no recorded digest and no hardware gate — which is how a defect of D6's size sat in it unnoticed.
- **The stated reason for the 0.5.1 default is stale** — it cites GR00T N1.5 parity, but `npa-groot` clones Isaac-GR00T directly and ships N1.7.
- **Genesis and the sim2real trainer are capped at LeRobot 0.4.4 by their interpreters**, not by choice: LeRobot has required Python ≥3.12 since 0.5.0, `npa-base` is 3.11 and the CUDA-12 Genesis base is 3.10. The one genuinely invasive item, and not recorded anywhere.

## Verification

- [x] Real install: `lerobot[training,evaluation,pusht]==0.6.1` on the dev VM (Python 3.12.13, torch 2.9.0) — 19/19 imports, CLI flags, adapter dataset round-trip with video decode, real ACT training run.
- [x] Real GPU: shipped `npa-lerobot:0.6.0` on an H100 80GB (driver 580.126.09, CUDA 13.0), via a `batch/v1` Job. Job and the temporary pull secret were deleted afterwards; the dev VM venv was removed.
- [x] `make test` → 8847 passed, 37 skipped. The 2 failures in `tests/workflows/test_bdd100k_pipeline.py` are pre-existing and environmental (they shell out to the `npa` console script, absent from PATH in this sandbox); confirmed identical on `origin/main` in a clean worktree.
- [x] Guardrails → 1685 passed. `audit_workbench_image_tags.py` → clean. Skills index → 3 passed.
- [x] New/updated tests: `npa/tests/scripts/test_audit_lerobot_release.py` → 18 passed, each driving a synthetic wheel broken in exactly one way, including four covering the extras graph and the `require_package` gates. `npa/tests/test_lerobot_version_compat.py` → 6 passed.
- [x] `ruff check` clean on all changed Python.
- [x] Public-repo hygiene: no customer names, VM IPs, private endpoints, project IDs, tenant IDs, registry IDs, bucket names, or secrets.

## Remaining gates before 0.6.1 becomes default

Image-level work that needs a build, matching the precedent set by #191: build `npa-lerobot:0.6.1` (CUDA 12 + B300), run `test_lerobot_env` / `test_lerobot_functional` on real GPU, `validate_blackwell_image.sh` with digest recording, and one `workbench.lerobot.policy_train` run. The CPU rig also surfaced one thing it could not settle: `torchcodec` 0.11.1 failed to load against `torch 2.9.0+cpu` and LeRobot fell back to PyAV. That is a property of the ad-hoc CPU rig, not the workbench images — but it is the same ABI coupling D1 describes, so the GPU gate should confirm torchcodec loads rather than silently falling back.

## Skill Maintenance

- [x] The behavior change here is the extras

author: thomasmichon
body:
## pr-claim-accountability Phase 2 — ADO PR settle-on-merge (the odsp-web case)

Extends the reclaim sweep's `pr`-kind merge check (Phase 1, GitHub) to **ADO**
PRs — the primary real-world manual claim: a dotfiles harness worktree owning an
**odsp-web** ADO PR opened out-of-band. Such a claim now **auto-settles once the
PR completes**, so the never-wedge sweep + finalize self-heal reclaim it without
a manual `claims settle`.

### What changed
- `sweep.pr_merged` is now a **dispatcher** by ref shape:
  - GitHub ref (full URL or `owner/repo#N`) → `_github_pr_merged` (`gh pr view --json state`, `MERGED`).
  - ADO PR URL (`*.visualstudio.com` / `dev.azure.com`) → `_ado_pr_merged` (`az repos pr show --query status`, `completed`).
  - Unrecognized ref / missing tool / auth failure / any error → `None` (spare). Never raises.
- `_ado_pr_view_args` parses both classic `https://<org>.visualstudio.com/.../pullrequest/N`
  and modern `https://dev.azure.com/<org>/.../pullrequest/N` into
  `--id N --org <org-url>` (az resolves the org-wide-unique PR id; the repo/project
  in the URL isn't needed).

### Boundary / design
The low-level sweep can't call the `@ado-data` sub-agent, and we want no heavy
dependency. It reaches ADO through the operator's ambient **`az login`** (the
azure-devops extension) — the CLI the harness **already uses** for ADO — best-effort:
unauthenticated / not-visible → nonzero exit → spare, exactly like the GitHub
`gh` path. Conservative: **only** a definitive `completed` reclaims; `active`
(still owed), `abandoned` (closed-unmerged — never silently reclaimed), `notSet`,
or unresolvable → spare.

We project to just the `status` field (not `-o json`) + `errors="replace"` so a PR
title/description carrying **non-UTF-8 (cp1252)** bytes can't crash decoding into a
false spare — found live: PR 2285417's em-dash title broke `-o json`.

### Validation
- **+4 tests** (ADO recognizer both URL forms, `completed`-only merge verdict,
  degrade-safe matrix, github-vs-ado dispatch); 23/23 `test_sweep.py` pass; source
  `ruff`-clean.
- **Live-e2e'd** against real odsp-web ADO PRs: a **merged** PR (both
  `visualstudio.com` and `dev.azure.com` forms) → reclaimed; a live **active** PR,

author: alejandrocoronadon
body:
Closes #870.

## Problem

`forecast_fitted_values()` returns 0 for every in-sample point of a constant
series, instead of the constant:

```python
df = pd.DataFrame({'unique_id': 0, 'ds': range(100), 'y': np.full(100, 7.0)})
sf = StatsForecast(models=[AutoARIMA(allowmean=False)], freq=1)
sf.forecast(h=1, df=df, fitted=True)
sf.forecast_fitted_values()['AutoARIMA']   # all 0.0, should be 7.0
```

When AutoARIMA selects a zero-mean model for a constant series, the residuals
equal the series, so `fitted_arima`'s `x - residuals` is all zeros. The
out-of-sample forecast is already correct because `forecast_arima` special-cases
a constant series with `is_constant(x)`; `fitted_arima` did not.

## Fix

Add the same `is_constant(x)` branch to `fitted_arima`, returning the constant.

## Verification

With the fix, fitted values equal the constant for both `allowmean=False` and
`allowmean=True`, and non-constant series are unchanged (fitted values still
track the series). Added a regression test that fails without the change; the
full `test_arima.py` suite (49 tests) passes.

author: jstar269
body:
## Summary

`sr_guest_sprintf()` assembled guest-controlled flag, width, precision and **length-modifier** bytes into a `conv[]` buffer and passed that buffer to `snprintf()` as the format string, while always supplying a fixed host C argument type. A guest length modifier could therefore name a host variadic type that the supplied argument did not match.

Base `37db86e` (new `main`, includes merged #47) · head `00f77a4`.

The bridge now parses an explicit PSP grammar and renders integers, characters, strings, pointers, `%n`, non-finite floats and `%a`/`%A` **with no host printf call at all**. The remaining floating conversions call `snprintf()` with compile-time literal formats carrying no length modifier, so the host argument type is exactly `double`. `-Werror=format-nonliteral` enforces this mechanically and is wired into `tools/test_guest_printf.py`.

## Evidence: measured, not assumed

Both the ABI and the formatting semantics were established from ground truth rather than from the C standard or the host libc.

**PSP ABI** — proven with the PSPSDK compiler (`psp-gcc` 15.2.0, default `-mabi=eabi`) by inspecting emitted MIPS for variadic `sprintf` calls, plus `_Static_assert` on every type size:

| claim | measured |
|---|---|
| `long` / `size_t` / `ptrdiff_t` / pointer | 4 bytes, one argument word |
| `long long` / `intmax_t` | 8 bytes, `_Alignof` 8 |
| **`long double`** | **8 bytes — identical to `double`** |
| variadic word 0 | `$6`; words 0–5 are `$6..$11` |
| word 6 onward | stack at entry `$sp + 0` (EABI reserves no home area) |
| even-slot rule | 1 int then a `double` → `$8/$9` (`$7` skipped) |
| register→stack transition | 5 ints then `double` → stack+0; 7 ints then `double` → stack+8 |
| variadic `float` | promoted via `__extendsfdf2`, travels in GPRs |

**Formatting semantics** — measured by running the real PSP libc under an emulator across three oracle rounds (145 cells).

## Defects found and fixed by this review

The first commit was correct on the ABI but wrong on six formatting cells and two host-dependence cells:

1. **Unknown conversion consumed an argument.** Measured newlib emits the conversion character alone and consumes nothing, so `%y|%d` hands the **first** argument to `%d`. Consuming shifted every later conversion — a silent cursor desync. *Most serious finding.*
2. **`%p` was a fixed 8-digit form ignoring width/flags.** Measured newlib emits an unconditional `0x` then `%x`-style digits: `%p` of 0 is `0x0`, `%.0p` of 0 is `0x`, and width/precision/zero-fill/left-fill all apply. **Production-relevant** — the census below finds `%p` in use.
3. **Inapplicable length modifiers were refused.** newlib ignores them: `%hf`/`%zf`/`%llf`/`%lLf` print a double, `%Ld` prints one word, `%lp`/`%lc`/`%ls` behave as `%p`/`%c`/`%s`.
4. **Repeated modifiers were refused.** newlib toggles short/char per `h` (short wins when both set), treats ≥2 `l` as 64-bit, and accepts `q` as 64-bit.
5. **`0` flag did not zero-pad `%c`/`%s`.** newlib pads with zeros (`%05c` → `0000A`); glibc uses spaces.
6. **`%n` refused flags/width/precision.** newlib ignores them and still writes. Refusing bought no safety — a guest can always spell a bare `%n`. The real guarantee is the destination span preflight, which is kept and now covered at every end-of-arena alignment for all four write widths.

Plus two host-dependence defects, fixed by rendering the bytes in this file:

- **inf/NaN spelling.** Windows UCRT renders a negative quiet NaN as `nan(ind)`; PSP newlib and glibc use `-nan`.
- **`%a`/`%A`.** UCRT pads the mantissa to full precision and leaves denormals unnormalised; PSP newlib and glibc emit the shortest mantissa with denormals normalised (`0x1p-1074`).

**Result: byte-identical output under glibc and UCRT across all 145 measured cells.**

## Production format census

Aggregate only — no format strings, offsets, addresses or other title-specific constants are reproduced, and nothing from the census is committed.

- 7 320 conversion specs across 17 title binaries.
- Conversions in use: `d s x f X g u c E p F e i`.
- Length modifiers: none (7 299), **`ll` (17)**, **`l` (4)**. No `j`/`z`/`t`/`L`/`q`.
- **Absent:** `%n`, `%a`/`%A`, wide `%lc`/`%ls`.
- Dynamic `*` width present (4); dynamic precision absent.
- Max numeric width **28**, max precision **3**.

So `%p` and `ld`/`lld` are live production paths — the fixes above matter. The never-observed cells are still corrected, but their risk is bounded.

## Semantic table

| cell | status | behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `%p`, incl. NULL and width/flags | MEASURED | `0x` + `%x` digits; `0x0` for NULL |
| `%a`/`%A` shape | MEASURED | shortest mantissa, denormals normalised; rendered in-file |
| inf/NaN spelling, sign, case, zero-pad | MEASURED | `inf`/`nan`, upper for `F E G A`, never zero-padded |
| flags/precision on `%c` `%s` | MEASURED | `0` zero-pads; `-` wins; precision ignored for `%c` |
| `%n` flags/width/precision | MEASURED | ignored, write still performed |
| `%lc` / `%ls` | MEASURED | no wide support; byte-wise, identical to `%c`/`%s` |
| repeated/inapplicable modifiers | MEASURED | newlib toggle model, inapplicable ignored |
| unsupported conversions | MEASURED | emit char alone, **consume nothing** |
| trailing/incomplete `%` | MEASURED | emits nothing further |
| negative `*` width / precision | MEASURED | `-` flag with abs; precision omitted |
| `GP_MAX_WIDTH` / `GP_MAX_PREC` | **PROJECT POLICY, not PSP** | newlib formats `%20000d` fine; bounds are DoS limits, documented as such |
| `%*d` with `INT32_MIN` width | MEASURED | PSP newlib **terminates abnormally**; bridge refuses deterministically |
| `%.0a` return value | UNRESOLVED (newlib bug) | newlib returns 16 for a 17-char result; not replicated |
| retail-title libc identity | UNRESOLVED | oracle is PSPSDK newlib, not the title's own statically linked libc |

## Verification

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| PSP-oracle parity (145 cells) | **144 match, 1 differ** (the `%.0a` newlib return bug) |
| glibc vs UCRT byte comparison | **identical, 0 differing lines** |
| `guest_printf_selftest` | **OK, 156 checks** |
| selftest vs the first commit in this PR (`f583932`) | **40 assertions fail** |
| selftest vs the pre-rewrite bridge (unchanged by #47) | **55 assertions fail** |
| ASan + UBSan, `-fno-sanitize-recover=all`, leak check | clean, exit 0 |
| Differential fuzz vs host libc, 400 000 cases (32-bit int, 64-bit `ll`/`j`/`q` extrema, float, char, string) | **0 mismatches**, under sanitizers |
| `-Wformat=2 -Wformat-nonliteral -Wformat-security -Werror` | clean (pre-rewrite code fails at 4 `snprintf` sites) |
| `-O0` / `-O2` / `-O3`, `-Wall -Wextra -Werror` | clean |
| MSYS2 UCRT64 gcc 16.1.0 | OK |
| `python -m unittest discover -s tools` | **Ran 1171 — OK** (23 skipped) |
| `mingw32-make portable-core-objects` | exit 0 |
| `publish_audit --provenance-self-consistency`, index + worktree | OK (619 files, both content sources) |
| provenance/policy/audit gate tests (#47) | Ran 107 — OK |
| bare `publish_audit` (release boundary) | fails closed: `PROVENANCE_UNVERIFIED` only |
| `provenance_ledger.py --check` | OK (619 entries) |
| `pre-commit run --all-files` | all hooks pass |
| `hst_manager.ps1 -Action Verify` | **[PASS] All verification suites passed** |

Sanitizers cannot detect a varargs type mismatch directly, so the proof of the original defect is behavioral plus the compiler-enforced `-Wformat-nonliteral` gate.

## Boundary red-team

Destination at the final writable guest bytes; format terminator at the last byte; `%s` terminator at the last byte and unterminated source crossing the boundary; `%n` 1/2/4/8-byte writes at exact-fit and one-past-fit alignments (all-or-nothing, no partial store); stack continuation entirely past the arena. All bounded by the checked accessors, ASan-clean, with the PSP-visible return still correct.

## Reba

author: gregnazario
body: ### Description E2E flakes were clustering around indexer lag on a busy localnet (4 Vitest workers), racy test patterns, and keyless JWKS fetches over the public internet. **SDK** - Increase the default `waitForIndexer` timeout from 3s to 10s (`DEFAULT_INDEXER_SYNC_TIMEOUT_SEC`). The timeout error now includes current vs target versions, and callers can pass `timeoutMilliseconds`. - Check the `0x1::account::Account` resource first in `doesAccountExistAtAddress` and skip the indexer `current_objects` query when the resource exists. A slow owned-object query no longer fails discovery for standard accounts; light accounts without a resource still use the fallback. **Tests** - Account derivation / indexer-backed account queries now pass `minimumLedgerVersion` after the relevant transaction, and derivation tests use a longer timeout. - Transaction worker tests use an isolated sender per case, await `push`, stop workers in `afterEach`, and poll for the committed sequence number instead of a 30s sleep. - Keyless e2e installs the federated test JWK from a local `secure_test_jwk.json` fixture instead of fetching GitHub in `beforeEach`. The outdated-JWK case rotates to a different kid locally instead of pulling Auth0 JWKS. The dedicated Auth0 live-install test is unchanged; Firebase remains skipped. - Unit coverage for the new indexer timeout behavior and for skipping `current_objects` when the account resource exists. ### Test Plan - [x] `pnpm check` - [x] `pnpm unit-test` (1714 tests) - [x] Targeted e2e: `account.test.ts` + `transactionWorker.test.ts` (37 passed) - [x] `TMPDIR=/tmp pnpm exec vitest run tests/e2e/api/keyless.test.ts` (25 passed, 1 skipped) - [x] `TMPDIR=/tmp pnpm e2e-test` — 346 passed, 43 skipped ### Related Links Overlaps with (but does not replace) #858 (indexer sync timeout) and #931 (skip owned-object query during account discovery). ### Checklist - [x] Have you ran `pnpm fmt`? - [x] Have you updated the `CHANGELOG.md`?

author: dejeune
body:
<!-- Template from https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/main/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md?-->
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:
1. Consider creating this PR as draft: https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

> ### Branch strategy
>
> - Active development targets `main`.
> - v1 maintenance targets `v1`; forward-port fixes to `main` separately when needed.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

Bundled Claude Code, mise, bun, uv/uvx, ripgrep, and MinGit were shipped as uncompressed binaries or an expanded tree. The macOS arm64 app occupied about 948 MiB after extraction, and several dependencies retained duplicate runtime builds.

After this PR:

Bundled tools use verified Zstd payloads, while Windows MinGit uses a deterministic `tar.zst`. Common tools and MinGit are restored from the local app payload at startup, and Claude Code is restored on first Agent use into a versioned Toolchain cache. Atomic installation, SHA-256 verification, permission restoration, cache repair, and concurrent first-use deduplication keep the runtime fully offline. The packaging filters also remove only verified duplicate dependency builds.

The macOS arm64 app now occupies about 567 MiB after extraction (40.2% smaller), while the DMG is about 286 MiB (11.7% smaller).

<!-- (optional, in `fixes #<issue number>(, fixes #<issue_number>, ...)` format, will close the issue(s) when PR gets merged)*: -->

Fixes #N/A

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The app must keep working in environments where runtime downloads are unavailable. Compressing signed build-time artifacts preserves offline behavior and exact executable bytes while reducing the installed application size.

The following tradeoffs were made:

- First startup restores the common tool payloads, and first Agent use restores Claude Code.
- The versioned Toolchain cache grows after first use, so installed app size is reduced more than app-plus-expanded-cache disk usage.
- DMG savings are smaller because the disk image already applies compression.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Downloading tools on demand was rejected because runtime network access is not reliable.
- Removing tools or replacing runtime dependencies was rejected because it would remove supported functionality.
- Relying only on DMG compression was insufficient because it does not reduce the extracted app size.

Links to places where the discussion took place: N/A

### Breaking changes

None.

### Special notes for your reviewer

- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm format`, `pnpm build:check`, and `pnpm test:lint` pass.
- A signed and notarized macOS arm64 production package was built and inspected.
- Packaged SQLite, Lark SDK, Transformers Node worker initialization, PDF parsing/rendering, and Renderer PDF preview were smoke-tested.
- The restored Claude executable retained its original SHA-256, executable mode, Mach-O signature, and reported version.
- Windows and Linux paths are covered by platform mapping and platform-independent tests; release packages were not built on this macOS host.

### Checklist

This checklist is not enforcing, but it's a reminder of items that could be relevant to every PR.

author: cdubiel08
body:
## What

Flips `external_review.required` to `false` in `.github/ralph-merge-policy.json`. One field, one file.

`attestation.required` is untouched (still `true`) — this loosens the **bot** gate only.

## Why

CodeRabbit's free-OSS quota can file zero reviews on a PR. When that happens, merge-pr.sh gate 5 is unsatisfiable and the `ralph-attestation` status stays PENDING server-side with no operator action that can clear it — the second time this has wedged a PR here. Human decision, authorized by the repo owner on 2026-08-12.

With `required: false` the gate degrades to a `soft_gate` advisory line rather than a PENDING verdict.

## Why the `bot` field stays

merge-pr.sh reads `.external_review.bot` independently of `required`, so the soft-gate line still names the expected reviewer, and re-arming the gate later is a one-token edit. Deleting the whole block would behave identically at runtime (jq defaults) but erase which bot this repo expects.

## Apply decomposition

`.github/**` is a configured `apply.infraPaths` entry, so this PR is infra-touching by construction and carries **no closing keyword** (merge gate 6).

- Ship unit: #1831 — this diff
- Apply unit: #1833 (`ralph:apply`) — the flag being live and verified, dependency-wired as blocked by #1831

The apply unit's proof is that a subsequent PR's `merge-pr.sh --dry-run` no longer emits `MERGE GATE PENDING — external-review`.

## Verification

`bash scripts/__tests__/merge-pr-gates.test.sh` — **129 passed, 0 failed**, and `shellcheck -S error` clean.

The second commit exists because the first version of this claim was false. Every policy fixture in that suite pinned `external_review.required: true`, so the branch this change activates had **zero** coverage — the `--force` and exempt-author cases skip gate 5 by a different predicate (`FORCE`, `EXEMPT`), not by `EXTERNAL_REQUIRED`. Added a `required: false` fixture run against the existing `setup_no_ext` fixture on both the merge and dry-run parity paths, asserting exit 0 / `MERGE GATE PASS`, that the merge is invoked, and the **absence** of the `external-review` verdict token and the `@coderabbitai review` hint. Gates are RUN, not predicted — that applies to the gate's own suite.

Refs #1831
Refs #1833

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

## Adversarial review findings (recorded, not hand-waved)

An internal adversarial review read the two call sites and raised three things worth stating on the record.

**1. What this actually removes.** Gate 5 does not become advisory — it is wholly wrapped in `if [[ "$EXTERNAL_REQUIRED" == "true" && ... ]]` (`scripts/merge-pr.sh:306-355`), so with `false` the block is skipped outright. The commit message's "degrades to a soft_gate" was imprecise; the `soft_gate` at :332 is the `--force` path. More importantly: `scripts/validate-attestation.sh:110-116` still requires the attestation's `review.verdict == "APPROVED"`, and `attest-pr.sh` still refuses to run without a verdict. So what is dropped is the **independent-identity** review requirement — an attested `APPROVED` verdict remains mandatory, but it may now be self-authored. That is the real narrowing and it should be named.

**2. This takes effect on main, not on this PR.** `validate-attestation.yml`'s `validate` job checks out with no `ref:`, so on the `issue_comment` and `pull_request_review` lanes it grades against **main's** policy copy. Those are exactly the lanes that recompute `ralph-attestation` after an attestation comment lands. The flip therefore cannot clear a wedged PR before it is merged — which is precisely the merge-≠-done gap apply unit #1833 models, not a defect in this diff. Filed as #1836 to decide whether that job should pin `ref` to the base sha the way `apply-keywords` deliberately does.

**3. Unrelated doc drift found en route:** CLAUDE.md claims the apply block is not armed in ralph-hero; it is (`apply.enabled: true`). Filed as #1835.

Neither #1835 nor #1836 blocks this change.

author: fufu1209
body:
## Summary

Fixes #45065.

When a custom element class implements an `attributeChangedCallback()`, the browser reads the static `observedAttributes` property from the constructor at definition time (per the [HTML spec](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#concept-element-definition), the *create an element definition* algorithm performs `Get(constructor, "observedAttributes")` when the attribute changed callback is present).

This PR documents that behavior in the **Description** section of the `CustomElementRegistry.define()` page: `observedAttributes` must be a static property/getter, is read at definition time (not at element creation), and if it returns `undefined` no attributes are observed.

## Verification

Verified against the WHATWG HTML spec source:
- If `lifecycleCallbacks["attributeChangedCallback"]` is not null, then `observedAttributesIterable` is the result of `Get(constructor, "observedAttributes")`.
- If the result is not `undefined`, it is converted to a sequence of strings; otherwise `observedAttributes` remains an empty sequence.

This behavior is also what Lit relies on (see [reactive-element.ts](https://github.com/lit/lit/blob/c42ee1e96b8fd61f7256f61d715daef572e76e52/packages/reactive-element/src/reactive-element.ts#L659)).
