author: cewert
body:
# Overview

Adds `npm run measure`: an on-device performance measurement that records what it was taken against, instead of leaving that to whoever ran it to remember.

The procedure in [`home-first-paint-performance.md`](docs/dev/home-first-paint-performance.md) is currently manual — sideload a dev build, hold a console socket, relaunch n times, read numbers off the terminal, type medians into a doc. Every safeguard in it is something to remember, and the project's own audit found recent samples were clear of a leaked demo session only *because each happened to record a count* a reader could check afterwards. That is luck, and it is not available to the next sample.

This is **tiers 1 and 2 of a three-tier design**: tier 1 asserts identity (hard fail), tier 2 records workload and provenance (never asserts). Tier 3 — the paired A/B comparison that prints the workload delta beside the timing delta — is the next piece and is not in this PR; comparison today is still by hand, as [#799](https://github.com/jellyrock/jellyrock/pull/799) does it.

**It caught a real one on its first multi-device run.** Measuring three devices with no `--server`, two were signed into the demo server and so measured **3 rows** where the third measured 10. Read the medians alone and the 512 MB Stick (902 ms) looks nearly twice as fast as the 1 GB Stick 4K (1702 ms). It isn't — it is measuring a third of the workload. The `rows` column is the only thing that makes that visible.

## Changes

- `scripts/measure.js` — a fifth device entry point. Takes the device lock, holds ONE console socket for the session, relaunches n times, appends one line per series to `.device-runs/measure/measurements.jsonl`.
- `scripts/measurements.js` — a **registry** of measurement families, not a Home parser. The app already emits two (Home `latest-rows`, the item grid's `load done` line the genres work reads) and their line shapes disagree, so each family declares a pattern per line. Patterns are grounded on captured device output: the device prefixes every line with roku-log's level and source path, so a pattern written from the doc's idealized form matches nothing.
- `scripts/measurement-guard.js` — tier 1 (`serverUrl` assert plus a series-drift check) and tier 2 (device model, Roku OS, app version, build flags, server identity and version).
- `scripts/measure-args.js` — refuses unknown flags rather than dropping them. `--sever https://…` used to be ignored silently, leaving a confident series that had quietly stopped asserting its server.
- `scripts/run-record.js` — a `measure` run kind, plus `ledgerPath()` and `runProvenance()`. `beginRun` hands back a `dir` under `out/`, which every `build*` rimrafs — a series costing an hour of device time would have been destroyed by the next build, the same defect that moved the run ledger out of `out/` in #803. Its `blocked` advice also stopped asserting "a fixture request failed", which was true while the RTA suite was its only producer and false as soon as this one arrived.
- `scripts/device-lock.js` — its private `fetchDeviceId` generalised into an exported `fetchDeviceInfo`; tier 2 needs the same ECP document the lock already fetches.
- Docs: the `measure` workflow and its preconditions folded into `home-first-paint-performance.md`; the measurements ledger and why it is deliberately **not** joinable with `runs.jsonl` documented in `rta-tests.md`.
- 1254 script tests (+70). The tier-1 gate is mutation-checked — making the URL normalizer one step more eager turns three tests red on exactly the stable-vs-unstable case.

**Verified on hardware** (`.177`, Streaming Stick 4K, Roku OS 15.3.4): a wrong `--server` refuses before taking a sample and folds `blocked`; a correct one produced 3/3 cold samples with full provenance. A review pass landed on top and was re-dogfooded — the sample-window shift is behaviour-neutral on a healthy device (3/3 cold samples before and after).

## Follow-ups

- [`measure-single-device-only`](docs/architecture/tech-debt.md#measure-single-device-only) — the tool drives one device from `ROKU_IP`, so a cross-tier comparison is manual and carries no tier label
- The ODC-precondition refusal is **not verified on hardware** — all three local devices happened to be carrying RTA builds, so the path could not be reached. Filed as a followup in `docs/progress.md` rather than tech-debt: it is a verification gap, not a design gap.

## Issues

Ref #728

## Docs / context updates

- [ ] **Architecture doc** updated if a system's *shape* or *why* changed → `docs/architecture/<topic>.md`
- [x] **`docs/dev/` how-to** updated if a workflow / recipe changed (adding a setting, writing a migration, etc.)
- [ ] **Subdir `CLAUDE.md`** updated if a per-area rule / convention changed
- [x] **`docs/adr/`** ADR added if an architectural / hard-to-reverse / cross-component decision was made (sub-architectural choice → **`docs/decisions.md`** note)
- [x] **`docs/architecture/tech-debt.md`** entry removed if this PR fixes a listed item, or added if this PR introduces new debt or defers a follow-up

### Description of changes

author: miceli583
body:
Card **`t_9a1538d0`**. Same standard as F7–F11: red first, evidence in the PR, feature branch → PR → dev.

## F5 — a substituted wheel was labelled with the system that was asked for

`calcHouses` / `calcHousesFromArmc` read `result.data` and discarded `result.flag`. Inside the polar circles that flag is `−1` for Placidus and Koch, and the cusps in `data` are Porphyry — byte-identical to an explicit `porphyrius` request, asserted to the last digit in the new suite. A caller asking for `placidus` at Tromsø got Porphyry cusps, a response still saying `placidus`, and a warning claiming they "may be unreliable".

Both wrappers now read the flag and return `system` — the system that actually produced the cusps — alongside `requestedSystem`. Chart and composite responses carry `houses.system`; `houses.requestedSystem` appears **only** on a substitution, so its presence is itself the signal. The warning now says what happened: *"placidus house cusps are undefined. These are porphyrius cusps — exact for that system, not unreliable placidus ones."*

## F6 — a degenerate wheel put every body in house 1

Above the polar circle, over a window of sidereal time that widens with latitude (0/360 below the circle → 8/360 at 66.6°N → 122/360 at Longyearbyen → 176/360 at 89°N), Regiomontanus and Campanus cusps collapse and the first forward arc goes negative. `houseFor` read a −0.03° house as a 359.97° one that swallowed the zodiac: all thirteen bodies in house 1.

`houseSpans` now measures which direction closes the circle rather than assuming forward, and `houseFor` places bodies by offset within those spans. A reversed wheel is also announced in `warnings`.

---

## Three decisions the card body did not make

Per the standing instruction to decide and record rather than stop, unless the public contract would change in a way callers depend on. None of these meet that bar — no caller can depend on "every body in house 1".

**1. The card's prescribed fix for F6 is the bug.** *"Normalise arcs into [0,360) in `houseFor`"* is precisely what turns a −0.03° house into a 359.97° one. A second plausible fix — flip the largest arc by −360°, "un-wrap the outlier" — is also wrong, and measurably: at 66.6°N / ARMC 270° it produces two houses of 270.065° that **overlap by 180.13°**. Direction is a property of the whole wheel and cannot be inferred from one arc.

The actual behaviour is that inside these windows the wheel runs **retrograde** — cusps descend, and house *k* runs from cusp *k+1* forward to cusp *k*. Measured across a full sidereal day at 7 latitudes × 7 house systems: every one of **4186** degenerate instants has forward arcs summing to 360 × 11 and backward arcs summing to exactly **360**, worst residual `0.000000000`. The cusps are geometrically exact to 1e-10″; only our direction assumption was wrong. Read backwards, the twelve houses partition the circle exactly once — the same invariant a temperate chart satisfies.

**2. The DoD's house number is wrong.** It says the Moon and Jupiter *"land in house 3"*. They land in house **9**. The "3" came from forward-reading the wide arc — the very assumption F6 is about. Corroborated independently: house numbering reverses with the wheel, mapping *k* → *2 − k* (mod 12), and `whole_sign` — ordered at every latitude — puts that Moon in house 5. 2 − 5 ≡ 9. The DoD's *intent* (bodies distributed across houses, not piled into one) is met and asserted.

**3. F5's "fix the hardcoded 66.5 constant" cannot be done with a constant.** The boundary is not fixed: it tracks the obliquity, moving from **66.532697°** (1800) through **66.562323°** (J2000) to **66.577351°** (≈2333), and is independent of longitude and ARMC. So the constant was not corrected — it was removed from the decision, and the flag is the only source. The suite binary-searches the true boundary at three epochs and across four longitudes specifically to demonstrate that no constant can be right. 66.5° survives only as secondary advice for the systems sweph does *not* substitute, where there is no flag to read.

## One change that came out of the fix, not the finding

`houseFor` existed **twice** — privately in `astrology.ts`, and exported from `overlay.ts` where composite, synastry, transit-to-natal and the event scanner all consume it. F6 was a single defect that would have had to be found and fixed in two places. They are now one function, re-exported, and the suite asserts the overlay path and the chart path agree above the polar circle.

## Red first

Evidence: `.hermes/pm/evidence/t_9a1538d0/red-first.txt`. Method is a file swap — the four changed sources replaced with `git show dev:<f>` while the new tests stay — because `git checkout` would revert the fix too and make the proof theatre.

**Part 1** — `tests/polar-houses.test.ts` against dev's sources: **12 failed | 8 passed (20)**. The 12 are the F5 labelling and boundary cases and the F6 sweep, closure and distribution cases. The 8 that pass on dev pass *correctly* — they assert unchanged behaviour (sub-polar guards, temperate wheels, systems sweph does not substitute), not the fix.

**Part 2** — dev's own characterization test, which was written to assert the bug, breaks on the fix exactly as its comment said it should:

```
AssertionError: bodies are no longer all in house 1 — F6 may be fixed; update this test:
  expected [ 3, 9 ] to deeply equal [ 1 ]
```

`[3, 9]` is the corrected answer. That test now asserts the reversed reading, and a sibling asserts the caller is told the wheel runs backwards.

## The sweep stays in the regression

Point fixtures missed the boundary window once already — an 8/360 window is invisible to twenty sampled instants, which is how the first version of F6 was written from one chart and was wrong. The new suite sweeps ARMC at 0.25° steps (1440 instants) per latitude, with a non-vacuity guard (`degenerate > 1000`) so the sweep cannot silently stop finding anything. My own original 69.65°N fixture turned out to have a forward-running wheel and would have passed against the broken code; it was replaced with genuinely degenerate fixtures, each guarded by an explicit `isDegenerate` assertion so they cannot drift into a harmless window.

## Gates

- **1355 tests, 33 files, all passing** (was 1334 / 32)
- `npm run typecheck` clean; `npx eslint . --max-warnings=0` exit 0
- No accuracy-harness expectation edited
- Docs: `docs/chart-conventions.md` §6.2, §6.3, §7 rewritten; OpenAPI response prose covers `houses.system`, `requestedSystem` and the reversed-wheel warning; `TODO.md` F5/F6 closed against the card

author: dgraziosi
body: Rebased onto current `main` and updated in two glossary passes so this PR can merge. **Locked terms (Danny, 2026-08-12, Obsidian-shaped):** Foundation = the product (what you install). **Vault** = one running instance (`FOUNDATION_DATA` + Postgres); a clone gets their own vault, not yours; Postgres vault, not markdown. **Graph** = the knowledge in that vault — do **not** call the graph “the Vault.” **Blob** = a file on a graph node. **Seldon** = architect of the product. **Chief** = primary writer. **Librarian** = agent from day one (vault health, graph hygiene, applying git updates to the computer). Do **not** say vault-keeping. Do **not** name checkups after Seldon’s Time Vault. ## Librarian pack (this revision) A clone can `compose up`, create Librarian from `prompts/librarian.md`, and paste three routines: | Routine | When | Quiet if | | --- | --- | --- | | `prompts/vault-health.md` | weekdays, morning | green (`GET /health`, real `FOUNDATION_DATA` vault, optional canaries/backup) | | `prompts/graph-hygiene.md` | weekly | green (duplicate titles, zero-edge nodes, type soup — **report only**) | | `prompts/update-foundation.md` | weekdays, late morning | already up to date (`git fetch` / `git pull --ff-only`, `compose up --build -d`, wait for `/health`) | Docs: `docs/VAULT_HEALTH.md`, `docs/GRAPH_HYGIENE.md`, `docs/AGENTS.md` (Librarian created at init). Bootstrap `how_to_extend` names those as operator routines. **No** `get_vault_health` tool. Never force-pull, never `compose down -v`, never delete `FOUNDATION_DATA`. ## Slice 10 blobs Implements redesign slice 10 on top of merged slices 1–9 (including search/undo). After merge, an operator can store a PDF as a blob on a node without putting the file in git or dumping it into MCP JSON. No S3. No embeddings/viewer. Link-validator order, undo/search, and confirm gates are unchanged. **Storage** - `blobs` table: `id`, `sha256` (unique, dedup), `media_type`, `byte_size`, `path`, `created_at` - `path` is exactly `blobs/` relative to `$FOUNDATION_DATA` (rejects `..` and absolute paths; DB check + app checks) - Bytes written to `$FOUNDATION_DATA/blobs/` with dir mode `0700` and file mode `0600` - `FOUNDATION_DATA` is the only durable root (not agent-data) **MCP ingest (no browser)** - `upsert` accepts `payload.storage = "blob"` with exactly one of: `bytes_base64`, `source_path` (move from `$FOUNDATION_DATA/uploads`), or `blob_id` - Size cap **20MB** (decoded). JSON body limit raised to 32MB - Stored payload is `{ storage: "blob", blob_id, media_type }` **Fetch** - `get` returns blob metadata. Body is not dumped as a huge string - HTTP `GET /blobs/:id` with `Authorization: ApiKey` returns the raw bytes **Activity / undo** - Snapshots store `blob_id` + `sha256`, not file bytes - Soft-delete of a node does **not** delete blob bytes **Compose (box ops, this PR)** - Published ports bound to localhost: `127.0.0.1:5432:5432` and `127.0.0.1:${PORT:-8787}:8787` - `db` and `foundation` use `restart: unless-stopped`; `db-init` stays `restart: "no"` - Blob/uploads perms unchanged (`0700` / `1777`) **Bugbot follow-up (already on this branch)** 1. Failed upsert no longer commits blob ingest 2. sha256 dedup race does not abort the transaction 3. Host drop-box: `uploads/` mode `1777`; `blobs/` stays `0700` 4. Omitted payload on update no longer wipes stored JSON / `blob_id` ## Test plan ```bash pnpm install pnpm typecheck DATABASE_URL=postgres://foundation:foundation@127.0.0.1:5432/foundation pnpm test ``` Covers blob ingest/dedup/path-traversal/`get` non-dump/over-cap/soft-delete/failed-upsert rollback, title-only upsert preserving inline payload and blob_id, plus bootstrap `how_to_extend.summary` naming Librarian operator routines (not `get_vault_health`). ### Compose + MCP (after merge / local) ```bash cp .env.example .env # set FOUNDATION_API_KEY to a long random string docker compose up --build ``` Wait until `GET http://127.0.0.1:8787/health` returns `{"ok":true,"service":"foundation","db":"up"}`. Then follow [`docs/AGENTS.md`](docs/AGENTS.md): paste Seldon, create Librarian from `prompts/librarian.md`, attach the three routines. Out of scope: embeddings (slice 11), thin viewer (slice 12), a dedicated blob-upload tool, Momentum copy, offer-letter bytes, write-ACL.

## 요약

문서 두 건. **동작 변경 없음.**

### 1. 미녹음 기본채점의 검사지 근거 (`a9ca59c`)

"미녹음 = 오반응(X·0점)"의 근거가 코드·README 모두 `사용자 확정 2026-08-12`뿐이라, 나중에 보면 임의로 0점을 매기는 것처럼 읽혔다. 실제로는 검사지에 명문이 있다 — **"제한시간 내 읽지 못한 낱말은 0점으로 채점합니다"**. 그 한 줄을 `withUnrecordedDefaults` 주석과 README 표의 근거 칸에 적는다.

### 2. CLAUDE.md 신설 (`045ce17`)

폴더별 README 14개가 이미 충실한데도 매 세션 관례를 어기는 이유는, Claude Code가 자동으로 읽는 파일이 CLAUDE.md뿐이라 그 문서들을 **찾아내야만** 알 수 있어서다. README를 복제하지 않고 **라우터 + 다른 문서에 없는 규칙만** 담는다.

| 규칙 | 왜 필요한가 |
|---|---|
| 임상 규칙 주석의 출처 표기(`담당자 확정` / `사용자 확정` / `확인 대기`) | 코드 15곳이 이미 일관되게 지키는데 규칙 자체는 어디에도 없었다. 어겨서 교정 커밋 `92047ce`가 나갔다 |
| 검사지 절대 기준의 유일한 예외(시행 절차는 담당자 회신 우선) | `lib/survey-flow.ts`가 검사지와 달라 보이는 것을 버그로 오인해 되돌리는 것을 막는다 |
| 코드와 그 폴더 README·주석을 같은 커밋에서 고칠 것 | 드리프트 교정 전용 커밋 2건(`3f5b1f1`, `92047ce`) |
| 커밋 전 typecheck·lint·test·build 전부 | `build`가 타입 에러를 못 잡는 함정(`ignoreBuildErrors`)과 함께 |

**뺀 것**: 아키텍처·문항표·셋업·배포·PII는 README에 있어 복제하면 두 벌이 어긋난다. 작업 디렉터리·`gh` 계정 같은 개인 환경 사실도 저장소 문서가 아니라 제외.

- `npm run lint` 통과(무출력)

클라이언트 지시(2026-08-13): *"영어 다 변화 안 되는 거 왜 수정 안 함? 그냥 영어 기능 제거하자."*

## 왜 고치는 대신 걷는가

영어로 바꿔도 **화면 절반이 한국어로 남는다.**

- `api/client.js`가 `data.detail ?? t(...)`라 **서버 오류 문구(한국어 전용 22건)가 항상 i18n을 이긴다** — 프론트 22곳의 영어 폴백은 한 번도 발화한 적이 없다
- **문항·해설·선지 1,012건이 전량 한국어**(시드에 `_en` 계열 필드 0건)
- 코스명·섹션명·유닛명·개념 칩도 서버 시드라 한국어

오류 문구는 한 줄이면 닫히지만 **콘텐츠는 저작**이라 오늘 안에 불가능하다.
반쪽 영어 화면을 심사에 내는 것보다 **한국어 전용이 낫다**는 판단이다.

## 지운 것 — 통로 둘뿐

1. 헤더의 `LocaleSwitcher` 마운트
2. `detectLocale`의 저장값·navigator 감지 → **항상 ko**

⚠️ 2번이 중요하다. 종전에는 **심사위원 노트북이 영어 설정이면 아무것도 안 눌러도 영어로 열렸다.** 개발 중 스위처를 눌러 localStorage에 `en`이 남은 사용자도 이제 ko로 온다.

## 남긴 것 — 지우면 앱이 죽거나 안전망이 사라진다

| 남긴 것 | 이유 |
|---|---|
| `i18n/` 골격 전체 | `t()` 호출이 수백 곳. 걷으면 전 화면이 **키 문자열**로 렌더된다 |
| en 리소스 3파일 | 지우면 **키 패리티 계약이 통째로 죽는다** — en 복원 시 유일한 안전망 |
| `LocaleSwitcher.jsx` | 스모크가 **직접 마운트**해 en 실렌더를 대조한다(`GuestSaveBanner` 관례) |
| `setLocale` | 화면 통로가 아니라 그 스모크의 프로그램 진입점 |

## 곁가지 1줄이 실제 결함을 드러냈다

스토어 초기 locale을 `detectLocale()` 재호출 대신 `getCurrentLocale()`에서 받게 했다 — **같은 사실의 소유자가 둘이면** 훅 경로와 스토어 밖 경로가 다른 언어로 갈린다.

zustand 5가 SSR에서 `getInitialState()`를 읽으므로 `boardVisual`의 en 실렌더가 실제로 그 틈에 걸려 있었다(원 주석의 *"실측: 절반만 en이 됐다"*가 정확히 이 지점). ko 고정을 넣자 그 시나리오가 **조용히 ko를 렌더하며** 붉어져 드러났다.

## 계약

`i18n.smoke` 시나리오 5 신설 — ⓐ src 어디에도 전환 통로가 없다(정적 스캔) ⓑ navigator가 en-US이고 저장값이 en이어도 ko로 연다. **되돌리면 각각 하나만 운다**(변이 2종 확인).

## ⚠️ 프로세스 발견 — 규정 문서가 틀렸다

`TEAM_PROCESS §2.6.1`이 *"프론트 T2는 `node_modules` 심링크와 포트 배정이 **필수**"*라고 적어 두었는데, **심링크로 하면 react가 두 인스턴스로 잡혀 전 스모크가 죽는다**(`Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useCallback')` — 실측). APFS 클론 복사를 써야 한다. 별도로 대장에 내린다.

`ci.sh` FRONT_TESTS **28종 + board** 전건 초록.

author: watson1978
body:
**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**: 
Fixes #

**What this PR does / why we need it**: 
When `workers > 1`, `out_file` (with `append`) and `out_secondary_file` take an inter-worker lock per output path, and `get_lock_path` derives one lock file per path: `/tmp/fluentd-lock-*/fluentd-<sanitized path>.lock`. A lock file is never removed while fluentd is running; the only cleanup is `cleanup_lock_dir` at a graceful shutdown.

So the number of lock files grows with the number of unique output paths, and with a date or a tag placeholder in `path` that set is effectively unbounded over time.

This PR folds the paths into a fixed pool of buckets:

```ruby
LOCK_FILE_BUCKETS = 65536

def get_lock_path(name)
  bucket = Zlib.crc32(name.to_s) % LOCK_FILE_BUCKETS
  File.join(@fluentd_lock_dir, "fluentd-bucket-#{bucket}.lock")
end
```

The lock is a `flock`, which is bound to the open file description and released when the file is closed or the process dies. The lock file is not state; it is only an anchor that the workers rendezvous on by name. Mutual exclusion therefore does not need a 1:1 correspondence between a path and a file. It needs exactly one property:

> the same path always maps to the same file, in every worker process.

`crc32 % 65536` preserves that property, so any two workers writing the same path still contend on the same file and still serialize. `acquire_worker_lock` itself (`open` / `flock` / `touch`) is untouched.

What changes is that the number of lock files is now bounded by a constant instead of by the number of unique paths. The accumulation, the mass deletion at shutdown, and the dependence on an external tmp cleaner all disappear structurally rather than being mitigated.


#### Collision semantics

Two unrelated paths can land in the same bucket. The effect on correctness is zero: they are serialized against each other, which is exclusion that is wider than necessary, never exclusion that is lost.

The effect on throughput is a rare latency coupling, and it is worth being explicit about it because `flock` is held for the whole chunk write, not just for opening the file. With `N = 65536` buckets and `k` locks held concurrently across all workers, the probability that some pair of them collides is about `1 - exp(-k(k-1)/2N)`:

| concurrent locks `k` | some pair collides | a given flush collides with another |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | 0.043% | 0.011% |
| 32 | 0.75% | 0.047% |
| 64 | 3.0% | 0.096% |
| 120 | 10.3% | 0.18% |

The right-hand column is the one a single flush actually experiences, and it stays below 0.2% even at 120 concurrent locks. A collision costs the duration of one chunk write, and only for the two paths involved.

**Docs Changes**:
N/A

**Release Note**: 
* plugin base: bound the number of worker lock files by hashing the path into a fixed set of buckets

author: pawspaceind
body:
Staging `/team/analytics` reported **331 bookings, GMV ₹3,24,472, Collected ₹0** — with `₹0 collected` on every service line — while `scripts/staging-seed.sql` holds a `captured` payment for each of those bookings. That number was wrong, not empty.

## Root cause

D1 caps a query at **100 bound parameters**. `lib/company-analytics.ts:6` built `WHERE booking_id IN (?,?,…)` from the booking result set — 331 placeholders — and `safeAll` swallowed the refusal and returned `[]`. GMV (no IN clause) computed fine, so the screen showed a confident zero next to a correct total. The CX ticket read in the same call was lost the same way.

The shape passes every fixture and every young environment, then breaks at exactly 101 rows. It was a class, not a query:

| Read | Where | Fed from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| booking payments + CX tickets | `lib/company-analytics.ts:6` | every booking in the period (**the live defect**) |
| booking invoices + payments | `lib/accounts-business-view.ts:46` | every booking in the ledger |
| grooming subscriptions + signup dates | `lib/customer-business-view.ts:28` | every customer in the view |
| grooming cost attribution | `lib/grooming-cost-attribution.ts:28` | every booking costed |
| customer names on the job feed | `lib/partner-job-feed.ts:71` | every customer in the feed |
| coupons, points, wallet, payouts, refunds, reviews, tickets, LTV | `lib/unit-economics.ts:34,86` | every booking / active customer |
| payroll approval + incentive events | `lib/people-reports.ts:29` | every run and result in range |
| manager roster | `lib/manager-dashboard.ts:37` | every employee under a manager |

## Fix

`lib/d1-chunked-in.ts` — `chunkedIn(ids, read)` splits the ids into chunks that fit inside the cap, runs the caller's own SQL per chunk and concatenates, so the result is identical to the query it replaces. All nine call sites route through it. A sweep test fails if any library builds an IN list from a result set again; the eight files whose lists are fixed vocabularies or per-row (literal statuses, one policy's service codes, one stay's pet ids, the months of a financial year) are listed with the reason they are exempt.

## The blank screens

`/team/marketing` and `/team/performance` are blank for want of data, not function — the marketing module is fully wired (create → approve → snapshot audience → activate → attribution), there has simply never been a campaign, and no rep has ever been mapped to the `sales` team.

`scripts/uat-demo-seed-gen.mjs` → `scripts/uat-demo-seed.sql` (deterministic, `INSERT OR IGNORE`, layered on the existing staging seed, documented in `docs/STAGING_DEPLOY.md`):

- **Sales**: 4 reps as active platform users, mapped to `sales`; 27 leads with assignments, first-response SLA clocks (some met, some breached), recorded calls and WhatsApp touches with real outcomes, conversions linked to the seeded bookings, collected and refunded revenue events, and an active productivity policy. One click on **Generate 30-day report** turns it into a ranked leaderboard.
- **Marketing**: a live campaign with its audience snapshot — 74 members split into eligible / holdout / suppressed, every suppression naming its reason — plus one campaign sitting at the approval gate, and ad-spend rows so the unit-economics CAC line has something real to divide by.

Table shapes are copied verbatim from the module that owns each table, and the seed is proven by executing the real modules over it: the fact run produces four reps with non-zero leads, actions, qualified outcomes, conversions and net-of-refund revenue, and the board ranks them 1–4 by name.

### Tests

- `tests/d1-in-clause-fanout.test.mjs` (6) — a D1 shim that **enforces the 100-parameter cap**, so these fail the way production did; 150 bookings with captured payments; analytics reports full GMV *and* full collected; accounts ledger rows carry their payment status past the first chunk; chunk semantics (ordering, empty list, per-chunk placeholders); the sweep.
- `tests/uat-demo-seed.test.mjs` (5) — loads both seed files into a real database, re-runs the demo seed to prove idempotency, generates the fact run and asserts real per-rep numbers with `net = collected − refunds`, checks the campaign/snapshot/holdout/suppression-reason invariants, and pins the generator as deterministic.

### Note for the merge order

`snapshotCampaignAudience` calls `buildCustomer360`, which on `main` still issues 8 queries per customer and will exceed the Workers subrequest limit on staging's 176 customers. That fix is PR #152 (unmerged) — the marketing snapshot button needs it before it will run against a full database.

### Gates

- `npm run typecheck` — 0 errors
- `npm run lint` — 14 warnings, unchanged from `main`; 0 errors
- `npm test` — 1259/1259 pass

Not merged, per the central merge process.

author: deagleon
body:
The Trello integration now treats the Trello card as the source of the lead: when a card is created on the connected board, Chatwoot parses the phone number from the card text and creates a contact + conversation on the WhatsApp inbox chosen at connect time, mirroring the card's list as the pipeline stage. Cards no longer spawn mirror conversations in a dedicated API inbox, and conversations that start in Chatwoot never become cards.

## How to test

1. Settings → Integrations → Trello: enter API key + token, load boards, select a board and the WhatsApp inbox, connect (in dev the callback URL must be publicly reachable — use an ngrok tunnel).
2. Create a card in Trello containing a phone number (e.g. `João (85) 98765-4321`) → a conversation appears in the chosen WhatsApp inbox, placed on the stage matching the card's list.
3. Move the card to another list in Trello → the conversation's stage updates on the board; dragging the conversation on the board moves the card in Trello.
4. Comment on the card → the comment appears as an internal note on the conversation (nothing is sent to the customer).
5. Delete or close the card → the conversation stays on WhatsApp and is simply unlinked.
6. Disconnect the board → the pipeline and its conversations are kept; reconnecting re-maps existing card-linked conversations.
7. Right-click a conversation (list or board card) → "Move to pipeline" → pick a pipeline and stage (nested submenu now renders correctly).
8. Open a board with many columns → horizontal scrolling works.

## What changed

- New `WhatsappConversationService` + `PhoneParser` (BR formats with structural validation: DDD range, 8-digit landlines, 9-digit mobiles) replace the API-inbox mirror (`ConversationSyncService`).
- Webhook processor: `createCard` → WhatsApp conversation; `commentCard` → internal activity note; card deleted/closed → unlink only (conversation untouched).
- Connect flow: WhatsApp inbox selector stored in hook settings (schema-validated); disconnect unlinks the pipeline instead of archiving it; connect reclaims stale pipelines holding the same board id.
- Removed agent-reply → card-comment sync (`CreateCommentJob`, `HookJob`/`HookListener` wiring).
- Backfill now materializes open cards as WhatsApp conversations and re-stages existing conversations on reconnect.
- `MoveCardJob` clears the conversation link when the card returns 404 (deleted while disconnected).
- Context menu: `scrollable=false` on the pipeline-level submenu so stage options aren't clipped (fix on top of 864dba5ba).
- Board: `w-full min-w-0` on the root so the `overflow-x-auto` container engages with many columns.

author: glane339
body:
## Summary

Adds a developer-only live audio diagnostic path for validating real Windows audio capture through the existing `lights-audio-engine` architecture.

The branch proves the end-to-end path:

`sounddevice / PortAudio → SoundDeviceAudioSource → FrameAssembler → run_engine() → AudioEngine → BeatEvent / BPM diagnostic output`

The live source is implemented as reusable capture infrastructure, while the CLI remains intentionally diagnostic and temporary.

## Major Changes

* Added reusable `SoundDeviceAudioSource` backed by `sounddevice`/PortAudio.
* Preserved the existing `AudioSource`, `FrameAssembler`, and `run_engine()` boundaries.
* Added 960-frame blocking reads aligned with the current 20 ms / 960-sample detector window.
* Added mono passthrough and explicit multichannel downmix handling.
* Added overflow and capture-failure discontinuity handling.
* Added optional observational discontinuity reporting without changing `run_engine()` reset semantics.
* Added a developer CLI for:

  * fresh device enumeration and selection
  * live beat-event output
  * BPM output
  * discontinuity reporting
  * clean Ctrl+C shutdown
* Added deterministic fake-backed tests that do not require physical audio hardware.
* Added architecture and live-hardware validation documentation.

## Validation

Deterministic validation completed successfully:

* Focused live-source/CLI tests: `17 passed`
* Full test suite: `207 passed`
* `ruff format --check .`: clean
* `ruff check .`: clean
* BasedPyright: `0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes`
* `git diff --check`: clean

Independent cross-model review returned **PASS** with no Critical or Important findings.

## Real Hardware Validation

Validated on the Lights laptop using the intended physical path:

`music laptop → AUX splitter → speaker + Lights laptop external Realtek input`

Observed:

* External AUX input enumerated separately from the built-in microphone array.
* 48 kHz mono and stereo capture supported.
* 44.1 kHz rejected by the tested Realtek WASAPI input.
* Successful 10-second and 60-second capture runs.
* Full requested frame counts received.
* Zero observed overflowed reads.
* Zero non-finite samples.
* Representative healthy gain: RMS ~`0.0969`, peak ~`0.4467`.
* Live frames successfully reached `AudioEngine`.
* Live `BeatEvent` and BPM output was produced.
* No discontinuity messages were observed during successful runs.
* Ctrl+C shut down the diagnostic cleanly.

PortAudio's reported `0.022 s` input latency is documented only as driver metadata; this PR does not claim a measured end-to-end latency.

## Detector Findings

The live hardware/capture/integration milestone passed, but the current M1 energy detector is not yet production-quality.

Real-music and controlled testing showed:

* good consecutive beat tracking during strong, regular transient sections;
* missed beats and long detection gaps during other sections;
* half-time BPM estimates when alternate beats were missed;
* unstable higher/lower tempo estimates during controlled testing.

These are treated as detector-quality limitations, not failures of the live capture path.

## Scope / Non-Goals

This PR does not add:

* beat-detector algorithm improvements
* WLED or LedFx control
* DMX / sACN
* scene or preset logic
* networking
* GUI
* automatic reconnect or failover
* persistent device identity
* aggressive latency optimization

Detector improvements belong in a separate follow-up milestone.

## Qué trae

**Módulo WhatsApp (la pieza que pediste de Actib), gateado por env vars — deploy seguro: sin tokens queda inactivo y la app funciona igual que hoy.**

- `lib/whatsapp.js` — WhatsApp Cloud API (Meta): confirmación del pedido (código + link), 🎉 listo, recibo al entregar (con premio del Food Lovers Club), cancelación, mensajes de la cocina y cambios de tiempo.

Closes part of the "still open" list from #2: whether a real model — not the scripted stub — produces findings worth publishing.

## What changed

`src/harness/run.ts` now reads `HALF_SHELL_HARNESS_OLLAMA_MODEL`. When set, it swaps the stub inference server for a real Ollama endpoint while leaving GitHub stubbed, so testing a real model's finding quality still needs no repo, webhook, or GitHub App:

```bash
HALF_SHELL_HARNESS_OLLAMA_MODEL=qwen2.5:7b npm run harness
```

Ollama's own server has to already be running with that model pulled (`ollama serve`, `ollama list` to confirm the tag). `HALF_SHELL_HARNESS_OLLAMA_URL` overrides the endpoint if it's not on `127.0.0.1:11434`.

A CPU-bound local model is far slower than the stub, so both the per-call provider timeout and the total wait for the review to post are widened on this path (10 minutes and 30 minutes respectively) rather than sharing the stub's tight defaults.

## Why the harness and not the production app

The production path (`npm start`) needs a real GitHub App, a webhook tunnel, and a live PR — too much setup just to sanity-check whether a model's output is any good. The harness already has a stub GitHub serving a realistic sample diff (a function that grows a required parameter, with one call site left stale) built for exactly this kind of check. Only the inference leg needed to become swappable.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, and `npm test` (156 tests, 15 files) all pass unchanged — this only touches the harness's manual runner, not the pipeline itself.

Not verified here: an actual run against a real model. That still needs a live Ollama instance, which isn't reachable from this environment.

author: david-noble-at-work
body:
Three file-package items from the Windows remainder (#373 phase 3e), one a **product defect**.

## The defect: Find's scope check missed rooted patterns on Windows

`resolveFindRoot` used `filepath.IsAbs` to decide whether a pattern's base escapes the scoped root. `/etc` is **not** `IsAbs` on Windows (no drive letter), so `Find("/etc/**/*.conf")` took the relative branch and silently walked `<scope>/etc` — the confinement contract violated for exactly the shape it exists to refuse. Any rooted form now takes the absolute branch; `filepath.Rel` errors on the volume mismatch and the outside-scope error reports correctly.

Unix is unchanged (`IsAbs` already catches `/`) — which is also why no Darwin-side mutation can prove this: the existing `TestFind_AbsolutePatternOutsideScope_Errors` is the pin, and **CI's windows leg is where it bites**.

## The two test fixes

- `TestDiscoverRegular_WindowsShapedPath_IsAPath` — fed a literal `D:\` path against a C: temp root (cross-volume → panic, aborting the whole package's binary). Now borrows the fixture root's own volume on Windows; Unix keeps the literal `D:` shape. Same treatment as its git-package twin (#398).
- `TestRegularConvertFrom_Unlinked` — asserted a slash literal against `Abs`, which is OS-native by the #377 ruling; expectation now `filepath.FromSlash`-built.

Expected windows-leg effect: the surviving `makePath` panic clears (plus whatever its binary abort was hiding), and the Find-scope and ConvertFrom failures with it.

Verified: `make vet`, `make lint-all`, full `make test` green; gofmt clean.

author: copilot
body:
The `build` job was failing because the QRServer workflow assumed an npm-based project and unconditionally ran `npm install` in a repository that does not contain a `package.json`. This change makes the workflow handle the repository’s current static-site layout and tightens deploy job token permissions.

- **Build job gating**
  - Only run Node setup and npm commands when `package.json` is present.
  - Skip the npm path entirely for static-only revisions.

- **Static-site validation**
  - Add a minimal fallback validation step for static content:
    - require `index.html` to exist before packaging the deployment artifact

- **Workflow hardening**
  - Add an explicit empty `permissions` block to the deploy job to avoid default `GITHUB_TOKEN` scope expansion.

```yaml
- name: Set up Node.js version
  if: ${{ hashFiles('package.json') != '' }}
  uses: actions/setup-node@v3

- name: npm install, build, and test
  if: ${{ hashFiles('package.json') != '' }}
  run: |
    npm install
    npm run build --if-present
    npm run test --if-present

- name: Validate static site files
  if: ${{ hashFiles('package.json') == '' }}
  run: test -f index.html
```

author: tyshaneoneill
body:
Closes #726.

Notify users whose installed **binary** is behind the store and hand them off to the right store listing.

**Why this is launch-critical now:** v1.6.1 bumped `runtimeVersion` to `1.6.1`. Every binary in the wild — 1.6.0 b34 and 1.5.1 b33, both on runtime `1.6.0` — is now permanently frozen at its last OTA bundle. An OTA can never reach them again. This banner is the only remaining channel that can move those users to the store.

## 1 · Remote config: the PostHog flag `outdated_binary_nudge` + its JSON payload

Chosen over a Supabase config table because it needs **zero new infrastructure** and PostHog already initializes at cold start inside every shipped binary — including the frozen ones. It follows the established payload-as-remote-config idiom from `useTvTimeImportGate`'s `{ pinned }`.

```json
{
  "recommended": "1.6.1",
  "minimum": "0.0.0",
  "snoozeDays": 7,
  "ios":     { "recommended": "1.6.1" },
  "android": { "recommended": "1.6.0" }
}
```

Per-platform blocks override the top-level values, and this is **not** gold-plating: iOS and Android reach their stores on different days, so a single global `recommended` would point Android users at a build Play has not published yet.

## 2 · Version source — `Updates.runtimeVersion`, not the JS bundle version

The brief called for `expo-application`'s `nativeAppVersion` / `nativeBuildVersion`. **Those are not available here**, and the reasons matter:

- `expo-application` is not a dependency, and adding it is self-defeating — a new native module can never reach the frozen binaries this feature exists to serve.
- `expo-constants` does not substitute for it. On iOS `Constants.platform.ios.buildNumber` is genuinely native (`CFBundleVersion` from the embedded Info.plist), but on **Android `Constants.platform.android` is an empty map** — verified in `expo-constants/android/.../ConstantsService.kt`, which exports `"platform" to mapOf("android" to emptyMap())`. There is no native version on Android at all.
- `Constants.expoConfig.version` is the trap: after an OTA it resolves from the **update's manifest**, so it describes the JS bundle, not the app the user installed.

`Updates.runtimeVersion` (expo-updates, already a dependency and already embedded in every shipped binary) is a native build-time constant that an OTA cannot rewrite. It is also the semantically correct key: the nudge exists precisely for users OTA cannot reach, and a binary on the current runtime is by definition reachable and needs no banner.

A consequence worth stating plainly: this cannot distinguish two binaries that share a runtimeVersion (1.6.0 b34 vs 1.5.1 b33 — both nudged together, which is exactly what we want today). If a future release ships a new binary *without* a runtime bump, those users won't be nudged — correctly, since an OTA can still reach them.

## 3 · Tiers and snooze policy

- **`recommended`** — dismissible card. Dismissal snoozes for `snoozeDays` (default 7). Unlike the TV Time banner's bounded-dismissal policy (#687), there is **no permanent cap**: this is the only channel that can move a frozen binary, so it returns after each snooze until the user actually updates, at which point the tier resolves to `none` and it stops on its own. A snooze recorded against an older `recommended` no longer applies, so a new release resurfaces it immediately.
- **`minimum`** — persistent, no dismiss affordance, but **never blocking**; the user scrolls straight past it. This is the lever the 1.4.1 iOS brick taught us to want.

## 4 · Surface

Self-gating `<OutdatedBinaryNudgeCard />` on Home, in the "Coming from TV Time?" card idiom (same layout, icon well, theme tokens, haptics). Renders `null` when up to date — no wrapper, no phantom gap. Placed above the other home cards: for a binary the OTA channel can no longer reach, this is the only message that still matters.

Copy is brand voice, one line plus an `UPDATE` action, no dev-speak: "A new cut is out / Update PocketStubs to get the latest." and "This version has retired / Update PocketStubs to keep everything working."

Store links carry the #800 campaign tags: `?ct=app-update-nudge` (Apple) and `&referrer=utm_source%3Dapp-update-nudge` (Play), so update traffic is separable from the web funnel's `web-organic`.

## 5 · Fails closed-quiet, everywhere

Flag off, flag still loading, missing payload, unparseable version, `runtimeVersion` null, web, or unreadable AsyncStorage all resolve to **no banner, no crash**. Sentry gets **at most one** `captureMessage` per session, and only for the one case that is a genuine config mistake: a payload that exists but carries no usable version (typo'd key, or a build number pasted where a version belongs). A missing payload is silent — that's just an unconfigured flag.

One guard worth calling out: `compareVersions` **rejects bare integers**. `"34"` is the iOS `CFBundleVersion`, not a runtime version; parsed naively it beats `"1.6.0"` and would nudge the entire install base. Covered by test.

Dev/QA escape hatch: `EXPO_PUBLIC_VERSION_NUDGE_OVERRIDE` = `recommended` | `minimum` | `off`, read literally so Metro inlines it (per the `EXPO_PUBLIC_*_OVERRIDE` idiom).

## 6 · Tests — 36 new

`__tests__/lib/app-version-nudge.test.ts` — numeric-not-lexicographic ordering (`1.9.0 < 1.10.0`), zero-padded equality (`1.6` === `1.6.0` === `01.06.01`), longer-tail ordering, unparseable/`null` input, the bare-build-number rejection, per-platform payload override and fall-through, web → null, malformed-payload reported exactly once, tier boundaries (at/above/below each tier, recommended-only config, unknown current version), snooze fail-closed-while-loading, window expiry, version-change reset, no-permanent-dismissal, and storage read/write failure paths.

`__tests__/hooks/use-outdated-binary-nudge.test.tsx` — both tiers, minimum ignoring an active snooze, hidden while the snooze read is outstanding, snooze suppress/resurface, optimistic dismissal + persistence, flag-off firing zero payload reads, re-read on `onFeatureFlags` resolution, already-current and unknown-runtime silence, and the tagged store hand-off.

## Delivery — this must ship TWO ways

**(a) Future binaries** — normal merge to `main`. Baked into the next store build.

**(b) The frozen cohorts (1.6.0 b34 + 1.5.1 b33, runtime `1.6.0`)** — a one-off OTA published from a branch based on **`376545a4`** (#815), with this feature cherry-picked on top:

```
git checkout -b ota/runtime-160-nudge 376545a4
git cherry-pick <this PR's squash-merge sha>
# gates, then publish with --config prd against runtime 1.6.0
```

**Base corrected during review.** An earlier draft of this body named `a510c0fb` as the last runtime-`1.6.0` commit. That was wrong: `376545a4` (#815) is, and `b7d52871` (#818) is the commit that bumped the runtime to `1.6.1`. Basing the OTA on `a510c0fb` would have silently rolled #815's iOS picker fix out of the frozen cohort's JS.

**#815's JS is OTA-safe on a pre-#815 binary — verified, not assumed.** This mattered enough to check, because #815 adds a *native* dependency (`@react-native-documents/picker`) that b33 and b34 do not contain, and that's the exact shape of the 07-07 P0. `lib/pick-document.ts` never imports it statically: `requireNativePicker()` is a runtime `require()` inside a try/catch that returns `null` when the module is absent, and the caller falls back to the legacy picker. The module carries an explicit comment naming this hazard. So the frozen cohort gets #815's JS and degrades to the old picker rather than crashing.

**Cherry-pick viability re-verified on the corrected base.** I built `376545a4` + both commits in a throwaway worktree and deleted it: **zero conflicts**, `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0, and all 48 new tests pass there. Every dependency exists at `376545a4` (`analytics.getFeatureFlagPayload`, `analytics.onFeatureFlags`, `captureMessage`, expo-updates). **No obstacle found.**

One correction to the review's expectation: the diff between the two

author: midorimax
body:
The highlights code deployed within minutes of merging #32; its migration is still sitting in a queued CI run. In that window `RanobeHighlight` does not exist, and the chapter page queries it **for every signed-in reader** — so the story would have gone down for exactly the people who have accounts, while signed-out visitors saw nothing wrong.

This is the failure this app already shipped once, when a new column reached production ahead of its migration and every novel page returned 500. The guard written at the time was scoped to translations and never generalized — which is why the same page grew a second unguarded query a day later.

`lib/degrade.ts` now holds the one definition, and the translation reads use it too. The rule it encodes: **a feature layered on top of content that is already there degrades to the content when its own table is missing.** A reader who came for the story still gets the story, minus the marks.

It warns rather than swallowing. A silently degraded page looks exactly like a page with nothing to show, and that is how this stays broken for a week without anyone noticing.

Covers both new call sites — the chapter reader and `/quotes` — plus the two translation reads.

`tsc --noEmit` clean, 247 tests pass, `next build` succeeds.

## What changed

Adds GLIO-PROTEOGEN M03-03, **Raw-format ingestion and parser**, as the third module in C03 Protein inference/ambiguity control.

- defines strict, versioned M03-03 request/result, policy, compact upstream receipt, source, diagnostic, and admission contracts
- implements bounded, read-once protein-inference raw-source admission for mzML, mzIdentML, strict protein-group/ambiguity/bundle JSON, governed FASTA roles, PSI-MOD OBO, VCF, and GFF3
- closes genuine M01-02, M03-01, and M03-02 lineage/protocol/search-space bindings without embedding raw bytes in JSON contracts
- validates checksums, sizes, decompression, format/version, structural references, source manifests, builds, controlled vocabularies, units, and cross-source coherence
- adds service/plugin, schema-only HTTP, safe directory-backed CLI, docs, traceability, executable evidence, benchmark, and release-evidence wiring

## Safety and ownership

M03-03 emits only metadata-bound validated raw-input summaries, typed diagnostics, and a compact admission receipt supporting the parent `complex_activity` workflow. It does not retain raw bytes, assign peptides, infer proteins/proteoforms/complexes, score activity, own kinase state, fuse omics, or make treatment or clinical claims.

All seven control decisions are checked before request or source traversal. Missing and unsupported evidence remains typed and non-negative. Digests prove deterministic self-consistency and source-byte binding, not issuer authenticity, external biological truth, or parser-execution attestation.

## Validation

- full repository source suite: **2,861 passed**
- candidate-only weighted branch coverage: **95%**
- focused contract/boundary/lifecycle/interface/tooling suite: **181 passed**
- M03-03 contract/boundary/lifecycle hardening: **163 passed**
- Ruff, source MyPy, compile, and diff hygiene: passed
- eval corpus: **8 groups / 77 cases / 77 executable oracles**, all passed
- benchmark: mean about **27.1 ms**, p95 about **30.3 ms**, below 150/250 ms budgets
- independent P0/P1 audit: clean after exact 271-evidence max-shape closure and typed dangling-reference remediation

## Release cadence

The expensive clean-wheel, deterministic distribution, dependency-audit, and SBOM replay is intentionally deferred to the C03 chapter checkpoint after M03-08. The source-level candidate gates and installed schema route wiring are complete here.

GitHub-hosted checks may remain queued without execution because the organization currently has an external Actions billing/spending-limit blocker; this is not a source-test failure.

author: macanderson
body:
## What & why

No code validated a tool call's input against the advertised `input_schema`, so a mistyped argument was misreported as a missing one (`{"query": 42}` → "query is required") or silently defaulted (`"trace": "yes"` → traced nothing) — the model then retried against a refusal naming the wrong defect.

This PR adds one validation seam at dispatch — `ToolRegistry::execute` — in a new sibling module `crates/stella-tools/src/registry/validate.rs`, which checks the model-supplied input against the tool's advertised schema before the tool runs:

- `required` fields present → refusal with the existing `InputError::Missing` wording, byte-identical to what every tool already said;
- declared `type` per property honoured (single word and `["string","null"]` array spellings; `integer` rejects fractional numbers; an integer passes `number`) → `InputError::WrongType`, naming field + expected + got, never misreported as missing;
- `enum` membership and `items.type` per element (index named);
- **unknown keys: documented-ignore**, except for schemas that already advertise `additionalProperties: false` (the `task` tool, foundry-authored tools, opted-in custom manifests), which now get them rejected deterministically. Rationale in the module doc: models pass stray keys constantly, and a new refusal class would fail calls that previously succeeded.

It is a small internal checker over exactly the JSON-Schema subset the catalog uses — no `jsonschema` dependency. MCP (`mcp__`) and custom script tools pass through the same seam; a schema with no `properties`/`required` naturally checks nothing. Refusal text is byte-deterministic (fixed check order, sorted unknown keys, capped value rendering) for loop-detector comparability.

The four witnessed per-tool defects are also fixed at the tool level (belt and braces for direct callers that bypass the registry): `search` query, `verify_done` test_files, `read_file` offset/limit, `bash` trace. `InputError` gained the vocabulary the seam needs (`want` became `String` for type-alternative phrasing, `WrongElementType` carries `want`, new `NotOneOf` and `UnknownField` variants) — `Display` output for existing variants is unchanged byte-for-byte. The `ToolCall::input` doc comment in `stella-protocol` now describes what actually happens.

**Exemplar followed:** the `driver/settlement.rs` split pattern — `registry.rs` is a grandfathered god file closed to growth, so the validator is a sibling module and the wiring in `registry.rs` is minimal. To keep `registry.rs` under its ceiling (now 1737 of 1751), the inline `save_exploration` ledger-augmentation block moved to `crate::exploration::ledger_augmented`, beside the `LEDGER_FILES_KEY` it writes. The validator's error vocabulary follows `input.rs` (#1267) rather than inventing a parallel one.

Closes #3144

## The witness

- [x] This PR includes a witness test (fails on `main`, passes here)

Five witnesses, one per defect plus the seam:

1. `registry::validate::tests::a_mistyped_field_is_refused_at_dispatch_and_the_tool_does_not_run` — **run-verified**: with the dispatch gate disabled and the old `trace` read restored, the test fails with `expected a refusal, got Ok { content: "\n[exit code: 0]" }` — the shell ran the command and wrote the probe file.
2. `read::tests::a_mistyped_offset_or_limit_is_refused_not_defaulted` — **run-verified**: with the old `and_then(as_u64)` reads restored, fails with `a mistyped limit must be an error, got: Ok { … 3/3 lines shown … }` — the mistyped limit silently read the default window.
3. `search::tests::a_mistyped_query_is_refused_as_a_type_mismatch_not_as_missing` — fails on main by the diff: `as_str().unwrap_or_default()` collapses `{"query": 42}` into the blank-query "required" refusal the test forbids.
4. `verify::tests::a_mistyped_test_files_is_refused_as_the_type_problem_it_is` — fails on main by the diff: `filter_map(as_str)` empties a mistyped array/string and returns "missing required field `test_files`", not the asserted type message.
5. `bash::tests::a_mistyped_trace_is_refused_not_silently_untraced` — fails on main by the diff (same silent-default shape as 2; the seam variant of it was run-verified in 1).

Plus direct subset-checker tests in `validate.rs` (type arrays, required-null vs nullable types, enums, item indices, bare MCP-shaped schemas, determinism/capping) and a pin that unknown keys still pass where the schema is open.

## The gate

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p stella-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean)
- [x] `cargo test -p stella-tools` (1029 passed, 0 failed) and `cargo test -p stella-cli` (all green, including the `tool_docs` gate — no schema prose changed, so no `docs/tools/` regeneration needed)
- [x] Docs updated where behavior changed (`ToolCall::input` doc comment; validator module doc records the unknown-keys decision)
- [x] CLA signed
- [x] `Closes #3144` appears both above and as a commit trailer

## Nothing left behind

- [x] There is nothing: everything I noticed is fixed in this PR

## Ground-rule check

- [x] No I/O added to `stella-core`; no new deps

## Anything reviewers should know?

Two deliberate deviations from the issue's letter, both toward the codebase's existing conventions:

- **`null` handling.** The issue asked for "null against any type is a mismatch unless the schema allows it". `input.rs`'s `present` deliberately reads `null` as absence ("every JSON encoder in the wild emits null for no value"), and every tool reads input through that convention — a stricter validator would refuse what the tool itself accepts. So: a required field sent as `null` is refused as `Missing` (unless its type lists `"null"`), and an optional `null` is skipped, exactly as the tool will skip it.
- **`search` uses `optional_str`, not `required_str`.** The blank-query refusal is one string shared by the tool door and `stella search` (the `report` seam); keeping absence on that path preserves the shared wording, while the mistyped case now gets the `WrongType` refusal the issue requires. The dispatch seam reports absence as `Missing` anyway for registry callers.

Validation runs after the `tool.call.requested` hook chain (a `modify` decision must be validated, not the original input) and before the internal-key augmentations (`save_exploration`'s ledger key, `run_script`'s gate threading), so engine-authored internal keys are never judged against the model-facing schema.

## Summary by Sourcery

Validate tool call inputs against their advertised schemas at dispatch and align individual tools and docs with the new error vocabulary.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent mistyped tool arguments from being misreported as missing or silently defaulted for search, read_file, verify_done, and bash tools.

Enhancements:
- Introduce a dispatch-time JSON-schema subset validator for tool inputs, including required fields, type checks, enums, item types, and optional strict handling of unknown keys.
- Extend input error variants to describe type mismatches, bad array element types, enum violations, and unknown fields while keeping existing messages stable.
- Factor save_exploration ledger augmentation into a dedicated helper to keep the registry module small and composable.

Documentation:
- Update ToolCall::input documentation to describe dispatch-time schema validation behavior.

Tests:
- Add witness and validator tests covering dispatch gating, per-tool mistyped inputs, schema subset semantics, unknown key handling, and deterministic, capped error messages.

## Descripción

Seguimiento de #107. El realce que señala la actividad al llegar desde el Hub **se recortaba**.

- **El anillo iba hacia fuera.** La actividad se pinta dentro de un contenedor con `overflow: hidden` —el que revela los botones de editar y borrar al pasar el cursor—, así que el anillo desaparecía entero y del realce solo sobrevivía el fondo, casi invisible en una columna llena. Un `outline` se recorta igual, así que el realce tiene que caber **dentro** de la propia caja (`inset`).
- **Pasa de azul a ámbar.** El azul del panel es el color de los enlaces y del tipo «lab»: el realce se confundía con el contenido en vez de destacar sobre él. Los tres tonos salen a tokens (`--destacado-anillo`, `--destacado-halo`, `--destacado-fondo`) con su variante oscura, porque un pastel sobre el fondo oscuro deslumbra y tapa el texto.
- **Parpadea al llegar.** En una semana de veinte actividades el ojo va al movimiento antes que al color, y la página acaba de dar un salto de scroll.

## Tipo de cambio

- [x] `fix` — corrección de bug (SemVer: PATCH)

## ¿Cómo se probó?

- [x] `npm test` pasa — **626/626**
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` sin errores en `packages/web`
- [ ] Build local — no aplica

⚠️ **Nota de honestidad sobre la autoría y el proceso**: estos cambios no los escribí yo — aparecieron en el worktree mientras trabajaba, y son la corrección de un fallo que sí introduje yo en #107. Los revisé, comprobé que `overflow: hidden` está efectivamente en `SortableActivityItem.module.css` (líneas 45 y 65) y que el diagnóstico es correcto, y los subo tal cual con su CHANGELOG.

⚠️ **Sin revisión visual del resultado final**: cerré el navegador antes de encontrarlos, así que el realce ámbar con parpadeo **no lo he visto en pantalla**. Lo que verifiqué en su día fue la versión azul, que es justo la que este PR corrige.

body:
## What changed

- Isolates each Operational Systems acceptance case in its own error boundary.
- Records execution failures in the case table, matrix JSON, and complete automated-review dataset.
- Continues the remaining cases after a timeout, API error, or renderer failure.
- Keeps the matrix and review downloads available even when no case produces an artifact.

## Root cause

The harness used one global `try/catch` around all 18 cases. A single slow or failed finalize/report-render operation therefore aborted the entire matrix and discarded the exact per-case failure from the downloadable evidence. The first observed finalize took about 95 seconds, making this failure mode material.

## Validation

- Parsed the complete inline script with Node's JavaScript parser.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Confirmed clear/reset behavior removes prior execution failures.

body:
Refs #11 — research spike deliverable.

## Recommendation

**No SEO sprint time before the pilot.** The deciding argument is timeline, not risk: new domains face 3–6 months of suppressed ranking and 6–12 months to meaningful traffic. The pilot needs 10–20 users. Even a perfectly safe, free SEO program could not produce a signup in that window.

Three plans, decisively ranked:

- **A — Direct campus outreach.** ✅ Where every pilot signup comes from. $0, days. Includes a seeding-order note: recruit musicians first so creators arrive to real inventory.
- **B — Legitimate borrowed authority.** 🟡 Real directory listings + an earned campus-paper writeup, capped at ~2h/week. Run for domain age, not conversion.
- **C — Parasitic SEO.** ❌ Rejected on four independent grounds — timeline, Google policy, the fact that parasite pages build the *host's* authority rather than ours, and zero control over an asset that vanishes when the host is flagged.

Includes an explicit "will not do" list and a test for future placements: *would we still want this if every link were `nofollow`?*

## Notes for review

- Filed at `research/outreach-strategy.md`, not the `docs/outreach-strategy.md` path named in the issue — per request during the session. Say the word and I'll move it.
- Industry sources **disagree** on whether algorithmic enforcement of site reputation abuse has shipped. Google's own docs don't confirm it. Flagged in the doc rather than resolved — it doesn't change the recommendation.
- **Pilot campus is assumed to be UT Austin**, inferred rather than documented; `docs/prd.md:33` says only "university communities." Worth confirming.

body:
### ⚡ Bolt: CI Workflow Performance Optimization

#### 💡 What:
Implemented optimizations in the GitHub Actions CI workflow file `.github/workflows/blank.yml`:
1. **Concurrency Controls**: Added `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress: true` to prevent concurrent redundant runs of the workflow on the same branch.
2. **Path-Based Trigger Filtering**: Added `paths-ignore` for non-functional file updates such as `README.md`, `LICENSE`, `.jules/**`, and `.Jules/**` to bypass workflow execution.
3. **Runner Job Timeout**: Applied `timeout-minutes: 5` on the build job to prevent stuck processes from wasting runner minutes.
4. **Security Hardening**: Hardened workflow permissions with `permissions: {contents: read}` and pinned `actions/checkout` to a verified Git commit SHA.
5. **Bolt Journal**: Initialized the performance journal at `.jules/bolt.md`.

#### 🎯 Why:
To reduce execution overhead, eliminate redundant workflow runs, prevent infinite hangs from consuming monthly GitHub Actions minutes, and ensure the pipeline is highly secure and responsive.

#### 📊 Impact:
- **Reduces Runner Overhead**: Bypasses workflow runs entirely on documentation changes.
- **Saves Active Build Minutes**: Automatically cancels outdated builds when new code is pushed.
- **Prevents Infinite Hanging**: Limits runaway jobs to 5 minutes max.

#### 🔬 Measurement:
Syntax validated and verified using `js-yaml` and git status.

author: giswqs
body:
Fixes #64

## Problem

On Windows, a float raster whose nodata is IEEE `NaN` renders as an opaque, colormap-colored rectangle covering the layer's whole bounding box instead of a transparent gap. It reproduces with the bundled sample DEM on the default `maplibre-gl-raster` (deck.gl) engine, in both the browser and the desktop shell, and goes away when Chrome is launched with `--use-angle=gl`.

The pipeline logic was already correct: `pushNodataFilters` pushes `FilterNaN` for every float texture unless nodata is off. The failure was in the shader itself. Windows' default graphics path is ANGLE targeting Direct3D 11 (for Chrome and for Tauri/WebView2), which translates GLSL to HLSL, and the HLSL compiler is free to fold the `isnan()` intrinsic to a constant `false` under fast-math assumptions. The discard then never fires and the NaN pixels fall through the rescale and colormap chain.

## Fix

`FilterNaN` now tests the raw IEEE-754 bit pattern - all-ones exponent with a non-zero mantissa - rather than calling `isnan()`:

```glsl
uint filterNaNBits = floatBitsToUint(color.r);
if ((filterNaNBits & 0x7f800000u) == 0x7f800000u &&
    (filterNaNBits & 0x007fffffu) != 0u) {
  discard;
}
```

`floatBitsToUint` lowers to HLSL `asuint`, a pure reinterpret with no float arithmetic left for the optimizer to remove, so the check survives on every backend. Rewriting the test as `x != x` would not have helped: that is the exact comparison those same fast-math passes drop.

Behavior is unchanged everywhere the old code already worked. The test discards exactly the NaN values, and leaves `±Inf`, `±0`, `FLT_MAX`, and denormals alone, matching `isnan()` semantics.

## Verification

- New `tests/shader-modules.test.ts` reads the two masks back out of the GLSL text and runs them over float32 bit patterns, asserting the predicate agrees with `Number.isNaN` across the exponent range, plus regression guards against `isnan(` and `x != x` returning. Full suite: 28 files, 384 tests passing. `npm run lint` and `npm run build` clean.
- A standalone WebGL2 harness compiled the exact snippet against an `R32F` texture of `[NaN, 1.5, Inf, -0]` and read back the alpha channel: `[0, 255, 255, 255]`, so only the NaN texel is discarded on a real GPU pipeline through ANGLE's shader translator.
- Drove the built package inside GeoLibre with the sample DEM on the `maplibre-gl-raster` engine, in both light and dark themes: the NaN border is transparent with the basemap showing through, and the console is free of shader errors. Inverting the mantissa test to disable the discard reproduced the reported symptom exactly - a solid black bounding-box rectangle - which confirms `FilterNaN` is the module doing the work here.

I do not have a Windows/D3D11 machine, so the ANGLE Direct3D backend itself was not exercised directly. The change removes the intrinsic that backend miscompiles, so it should resolve the report; @mhweber, a confirmation on Windows once this is released would be welcome.

author: yutachaos
body:
## Description

`custom_headers` on `aws_amplify_app` never converges: `GetApp` returns it as a bare JSON array with no top-level key, while `UpdateApp` requires a YAML/JSON document with a top-level `customHeaders` key. No single config value satisfies both, so `terraform plan` shows a diff on this attribute on every run, even immediately after a successful `apply`.

This adds a `DiffSuppressFunc` that unwraps both the keyed and bare forms and compares the underlying header-rule list structurally (via a JSON round-trip through `verify.JSONBytesEqual`, so int/float literal mismatches don't cause false diffs), suppressing the diff when content is actually unchanged while still catching real changes.

Reproduced the failure mode independently, including the "fix" several commenters on #34318 already suspected and tried (matching the config to state's bare-array form via `jsonencode`) — that doesn't converge either, since `UpdateApp` then rejects it outright:
```
Error: updating Amplify App (...): operation error Amplify: UpdateApp,
https response error StatusCode: 400, BadRequestException: Invalid spec,
yaml parsing error: Invalid spec, top level must be key value pairs
```

## AI Usage

This PR was written by an AI coding agent (Claude, via Claude Code) operating under my direction, not autopiloted. Specifics:

- I asked it to investigate a recurring Terraform plan diff we were hitting on `aws_amplify_app.custom_headers` in a separate, private infrastructure repo. It traced the issue to the `GetApp`/`UpdateApp` format asymmetry described above. Its first attempt at a fix in that private repo was actually applying the config in the state's bare-array form (`jsonencode([...])`) — that got deployed and caused a live `UpdateApp` 400 error (the same error shown above), which we had to revert. That failure is what confirmed a config-only fix isn't possible and this needs a provider-side `DiffSuppressFunc`.
- After that, I asked it to implement the `DiffSuppressFunc` fix in a local clone of this repo, as a trial, not for submission. It iterated on it across two rounds of self-directed multi-pass review (each round running parallel checks for correctness/edge cases, consistency with this codebase's existing helpers and conventions, and test coverage; one pass in the second round used a more capable model specifically for the correctness check), applying the fixes those passes surfaced, and verified the result against unit tests it wrote.
- I directed the search for duplicate issues/PRs before submission (found and cross-referenced #34318, closed my own earlier duplicate issue), and directed opening this PR once that search came back clear.
- Across this process I reviewed AI-generated summaries of each round's findings and directed follow-up scrutiny where those summaries flagged risk, and read the final diff before asking for this PR to be opened. I understand the mechanism: `custom_headers` is genuinely unsatisfiable as written today because Amplify's read and write shapes for it differ, so the fix has to compare content structurally rather than relying on a literal string match.

## Rollback Plan

If a change needs to be reverted, we will publish an updated version of the library.

## Changes to Security Controls

None. This only changes how a Terraform plan diff is computed/suppressed for one attribute; it does not change any AWS API calls, permissions, or data handling.

## Relations

Closes #34318

## References

- https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws/issues/34318
- https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/latest/userguide/custom-header-YAML-format.html

## Output from Acceptance Testing

Unit tests only in this PR (`TestSuppressCustomHeadersDiff` in `internal/service/amplify/app_test.go`, 12 subtests covering equivalence across bare/keyed forms, genuine changes, parse failures, empty-value transitions, list ordering, YAML formatting differences, and numeric-literal equivalence). All pass:

```
$ go test ./internal/service/amplify/ -run TestSuppressCustomHeadersDiff -v
--- PASS: TestSuppressCustomHeadersDiff (0.00s)
    (12 subtests, all PASS)
PASS
ok  	github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws/internal/service/amplify	4.85s
```

Acceptance tests (`TestAccAmplifyApp_*`) require AWS credentials I don't have configured for this fork — happy to run them or take feedback if a maintainer can trigger CI.

author: tyevans
body:
Starting a round of research from the course page and then opening the active session showed *a turn is running* with no live output — where a turn started from inside the session view shows both.

## Why

Those are two different channels, and only one was wired on both paths.

- **"A turn is running"** comes from `/turns/current`, answered by `TurnSupervisor`. Every turn goes through the supervisor, so this was right everywhere.
- **What the turn is saying** comes from `TurnActivity` — provisional frames plus a catch-up buffer. Its `begin`/`settle` lifecycle was driven by the HTTP turns route, and an auto-research round does not go through that route. `composition.py` drives rounds with `turns.run(session_id, prompt)`, so no buffer was opened and no frames were published. The frontend then did the only correct thing with what it had: `ActivityFeed` gates on `isBusy && activity.size > 0` and rendered nothing.

Passing a reporter into that one lambda would have fixed the symptom and left the next caller to rediscover it. The lifecycle belongs to the one component every turn passes through.

## What this does

`TurnSupervisor.run` now owns the buffer, behind a new `TurnActivityBuffer` protocol in `application/ports.py`. `TurnActivity` stays in `interfaces/web/` and satisfies it structurally, the way `WebApprovals` satisfies `ApprovalPort`; `build_application(activity=...)` wires it exactly as `approvals=` already was.

Two placements carry the design:

- **`begin` is inside the `is_running` guard**, so a caller that loses the race never touches the winner's buffer. The route's careful comment explaining why the loser must *not* settle a buffer it just opened is deleted along with the race it described.
- **`settle` hangs off a done-callback on the task**, not the awaiter's `finally`.

## A second defect, fixed by the same move

The old route settled from `except BaseException`. Because `run` awaits under `asyncio.shield`, a client disconnecting mid-turn settled a **still-running** turn's buffer as failed — its live content filed as a failed turn's discards — and `_record`'s `setdefault` then opened a second buffer nothing would ever settle. Settling from the turn's own fate makes the awaiter irrelevant, which it already was for the turn.

## Testing

- `test_an_awaiter_going_away_settles_nothing_until_the_turn_itself_ends` and four sibling supervisor tests over a recording buffer.
- `test_a_rounds_turn_opens_an_activity_buffer_like_a_persons_does` — the regression test for the report. Proved red by reverting `composition.py`'s `TurnSupervisor(service, activity=activity)`: `AssertionError: assert UUID(...) in []`, the predicted failure. Green with the fix.
- It asserts against a recording buffer rather than a real `TurnActivity` because `current()` answers `[]` both for a buffer that was opened and is empty and for one never opened — the two cases the fix is about.

All four gates pass: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `pytest` (2194 passed), `npm run verify`.

## Notes for review

- **Clean break:** `turns.run` lost its `on_activity` parameter outright, no shim. The final review caught a caller the design's survey had missed — `tests/integration/test_turn_visibility.py` — fixed in 55f8751, which also records the lesson: when a clean break removes a parameter, the survey is a repo-wide grep and it belongs in the task that makes the break.
- **Wider than auto-research:** turns driven by the topic seeder, dispatcher and stage runner share the supervisor, so they buffer and stream too. Consistent (they are turns) and safe (buffers are per-session), but it is extra stream traffic nothing currently reads. Recorded as a decision in the design doc rather than left as a discovery.
- **Deliberately not done:** `TurnActivity` was not moved into the application layer (it owns an SSE fan-out — transport, and its siblings all sit in `interfaces/web` satisfying application ports); the course page was not given a link to the run's holding session; the driver did not get its own channel.

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-12-turn-activity-ownership-design.md`

author: anvaypatil110
body:
## Why this matters now

`resolve()` **could not fail to find evidence**. BM25 accepted any document sharing a single token, and the vector fallback returned its nearest neighbour unconditionally (a neighbour always exists). `_extract_value` then sliced a value out of whatever got selected, so an absent slot came back `status="present"` with a confident, fabricated value.

Measured against a real 12-block store with OpenAI embeddings: **13 of 13 absent slots fabricated** — e.g. `car_model` → `"My phone number is 555-0142"`, `flight_number` → `"555"` at confidence 0.905. A user who knew only an email address resolved `location` to `"The recipient is alice@example"` at 0.529, *higher* than correct answers scored.

This is the correctness fix that should land **before** `MEMORY_URL` goes live on the provider (task E3d). Without it, activating fill-from-context pre-fills users' tasks with confident garbage.

## What was rejected, and why

Calibration across three corpus sizes and 28 adversarial absent slots ruled out both obvious levers:

- **Raw BM25 score** is unusable as an absolute floor: `bm25_search.py` omits the `log()` in its IDF, so score scales with corpus size — the same true hit scored **19.1 at 12 blocks and 66.0 at 40**.
- **Vector distance does not separate at all**: present 0.708–0.866 vs absent 0.624–0.900, with some absent slots landing *closer* than present ones.

**Term coverage** is corpus-size independent by construction and separates cleanly.

## The change

- New `resolve_min_coverage()` reading `MEMORY_RESOLVE_MIN_COVERAGE` (default **1.0**; **`0.0` restores the previous accept-anything behaviour exactly** — a real escape hatch, not a claim).
- `_term_coverage()` gates both the BM25 and the vector branch.
- BM25 now takes `top_k=5` always: with a floor in place, the top-scoring hit may be a partial match while a lower-scoring one covers the whole slot name. At floor 0.0 with no scope this still picks the top hit, so old behaviour is byte-for-byte preserved.

Full coverage is the default rather than a distinctive-token variant because the provider's slot names are overwhelmingly single-token (`recipient`, `duration`, `cc`, `topic`, `timezone`), where the two rules coincide — and the variant degenerates on the one multi-token name that exists: `to_address` reduces to the distinctive token `"to"`, which matches nearly any document.

## Verification

- **A/B through the real path: fabrications 13 → 0, true positives 9 → 9.** No loss of correct answers.
- Verified against the **deployed image**, not just locally: a user holding only an email resolves `location` → `status:"missing"`, value `null` (was a fabricated string at 0.53); the true positive still resolves; per-user isolation and the 403-on-anonymous gate both still hold; and `{"min_coverage":0.0}` reproduces the old fabrication on demand.
- Suite: **125 passed, 6 skipped** (re-run on this branch today).
