author: shkhan91
body:
## Why we're merging this — in plain terms

Right now the harness can finish a change, pass every single check, and still
have no evidence that the change did anything. Every check we run asks the same
kind of question — is the code still tidy, does the suite still go green, does
the page still render. None of them asks the one question a reviewer actually
cares about: *did this change do what it said it would?*

A change that fixes nothing passes all of them. So does a change that quietly
breaks something the tests never looked at.

This adds one check that closes that gap. When a change alters behaviour, it has
to come with a test that fails on the old code and passes on the new one. That
ordering is the whole point: a test that would have passed before the change
proves nothing about the change, so the check refuses it and says so. Some
changes genuinely have nothing to test — a pure rename, a config edit — and for
those the author records a one-line reason, which is kept as part of the record
rather than silently waved through.

We already have proof it matters, from two runs of the same accessibility ticket
this week. On the first run the independent reviewer refused to sign off: it
could not confirm the fix worked, and it noted that no test covered the
behaviour. On the second run — same ticket, same unrelated infrastructure
failure elsewhere — the author wrote a test that genuinely failed on the old
code, and the reviewer approved, citing that test as its evidence. Nothing else
changed. The check turned an unverifiable change into a verified one.

**Pairs with [fiesta#156](https://github.com/Adobe-acom/fiesta/pull/156)**, which
adds the machinery this file switches on. Merge order matters: the harness side
first, then this — otherwise this file names a check the harness does not yet
know how to run.

**Nothing about how milo builds, tests, or deploys changes here.** This edits one
contract file and adds one entry to it. No source file, no build config, no
workflow, no dependency is touched.

<details><summary>Technical detail</summary>

### The gate

```yaml
behaviour-test:
  template: fail_to_pass
  name: Changed behaviour ships a fail-to-pass test
  cmd: npm run test:file -- {test_files}
  timeout_s: 600
  blocking: true
  failure_route: repair_loop
```

`fail_to_pass` runs the diff's new or changed test entries twice: once on the
candidate (must pass) and once against the base commit in a linked worktree with
those test files copied in (must fail). A base run that fails on a *collection*
error rather than an assertion is rejected — a test that cannot run on base has
not reproduced anything. `node_modules` is symlinked from the candidate worktree,
so `npm run test:file` resolves the same pinned toolchain `provision: npm ci`
installs.

Only runnable test entries reach `{test_files}` — recognised by naming
convention, never by living under `test/`. Mocks and fixtures are excluded: the
runner loads whatever path it is handed and hangs on a mock HTML page.

The abstention path is `TEST-ABSTENTION: <reason>` in the producer's output. The
gate reports the reason as evidence instead of failing; it is scoped to one round
and never becomes a standing exemption.

### Why `patch-coverage` is deliberately absent

The platform also ships a `diff_coverage` template. It is **not** declared here:
`web-test-runner.config.mjs:24`'s `coverageConfig` emits no XML report, so the
gate would have no coverage document to read and would fail every run. Add it
once the runner emits cobertura or clover XML.

### Verified live

Run `c423146d` against MWPW-198935, 9 gates, this one passing on real evidence:

```
changed_tests: ["test/scripts/accessibility.test.js"]
head_exit: 0     5 passed
base_exit: 1     3 passed, 2 failed

author: chemaclass
body:
## 📚 Description

The shipped `resources/gacela-preload.php` — the documented production performance feature — preloads almost nothing.

It names 32 files by hand. Preloaded classes are only kept if **everything they extend, implement or use was preloaded too**, and the list omits those, so PHP drops them and warns at every FPM start:

```
Can't preload unlinked class Gacela\Framework\AbstractFacade: Unknown trait Gacela\Framework\Attribute\CacheableTrait
Can't preload unlinked class Gacela\Framework\Container\Container: Unknown interface Gacela\Framework\Container\ContainerInterface
```

Thirteen classes are affected — `AbstractFacade`, `AbstractFactory`, `AbstractProvider`, `Config`, `PathFinder`, `SetupGacela`, `ClassInfo`, `ClassNameFinder`, all three resolvers, and both containers. That is essentially every class the feature exists to preload. A 33rd entry, `DocBlockResolverCache.php`, was renamed away and had been reported only as an `error_log` line nobody reads.

## 🔖 Changes

- Discover the framework rather than listing it, so the set cannot fall behind a rename
- Link through an autoloader over Gacela's runtime closure (`Gacela\Framework\`, `Gacela\Container\`, `Psr\Container\`): asking for a class pulls in whatever it extends, implements or uses, wherever that lives
- Deliberately **not** composer's autoloader — it executes every installed package's `files` entries, and the preload context forbids the I/O some do at load time (`fopen('php://stdout')` in `amphp/byte-stream` aborts the whole preload)
- Exclude `Gacela\Framework\Testing\`, which needs phpunit and is absent in production; anything else that cannot link is reported by name instead of aborting the run
- Drop `linked()`/`skippedCount()` from the result — unused surface

Before: `31 files preloaded successfully, 1 failed` + 13 unlinked warnings.
After: `Gacela Opcache Preload: 176 classes linked, 0 skipped`, no warnings.

## ✅ Verification

`OpcachePreloadTest` starts a **real preloading process** (`opcache.preload`, skipped on Windows where it is unsupported, and when opcache is absent) and asserts no class went unlinked. It was confirmed to fail against the previous script, naming all thirteen — a test that cannot fail would have been worthless here.

Mutation coverage is 100% on both new files. Three mutants are ignored with reasons: the autoloader body is only reachable in a process that has no other autoloader, which a suite running under composer's never is.

On timing I have **no defensible number to report**. Preload looks dramatic against a cold opcache (7.0 ms → 1.8 ms bootstrap) and vanishes into noise against a warm one, and CLI models neither FPM steady state. So the unverified "20-30% performance improvement" claim is removed rather than replaced with another one. The correctness finding stands on its own: thirteen classes were not being preloaded at all.

## 🧪 Tests

- `tests/Unit/Framework/Preload/PreloaderTest.php` — discovery, exclusion, sorting, psr-4 resolution, and the installed (`vendor/gacela-project/gacela`) layout, which had no coverage
- `tests/Feature/Framework/Preload/OpcachePreloadTest.php` — a real preload, plus bootstrapping on top of the resulting image

body:
## What

**Client-directed:** *"allow the users to change the pick up or drop off at anytime. Obv if pick up has past they can only change drop-off"* — plus his standing collaboration decisions: both parties edit, every edit applies instantly, no approval gate anywhere.

- **`PATCH /api/ride-requests/{id}/trip`** (contracts v0.33.0's `RideRequestTripPatch`). Windows per the client's rule: pickup from `requested`/`accepted` only — once `arrived` the 409 names the door still open ("the pickup has passed — only the drop-off can be changed"); drop-off through every live status, `enroute` included. ACL = the participant set (rider + owner; group members join it with MYR-540). Non-party 404.
- **One guarded UPDATE** carries the status window, the `tripVersion` match and the place writes (migration 0038, `IF NOT EXISTS`): a stale editor gets a 409 and refetches; a pickup edit racing a picked-up loses in the database. Places encrypt through the existing `encryptPlace` path; the unedited endpoint stays byte-identical via per-column CASE.
- **The event pair:** a `TripEdit`-marked `ride_status_changed` (unchanged status + bumped `tripVersion` — the WS refetch signal; the frame stays summary-only and the notifier deliberately stays silent for it, so moving a drop-off never re-fires "Your ride is confirmed") + internal `ride.trip_changed` for the two real consumers.
- **Dispatcher:** an edited CURRENT-leg target re-shares — pickup while `accepted`+dispatched, drop-off while `enroute` — through the sequencer's `reacquire` (MYR-527's own door: same order admitted, lower still refused) and then arms the **MYR-527 verifier** on the NEW coordinate: observe the dash converge, one more re-share, owner's "may not have the route" push on a second miss. A re-share that fails outright reports through the same seam. A drop-off edited before Start re-shares nothing (Start dispatches the new drop-off for free); a pickup edited on an undispatched reservation re-computes its MYR-535 lead automatically (the sweeper re-reads the pickup every tick).
- **Pushes:** the non-editing participants hear "«FirstName» changed the drop-off" / "Your pickup was changed" — the edited PART named, the PLACE never on a lock-screen surface. Self-ride edits wake nobody.

## Contract surface

Contracts v0.33.0 (merged + tagged): `tripVersion` on `RideRequest` + the frame (absence = 0, additive), `RideRequestTripPatch`. Migration 0038. Docs: new PATCH section under §7.8 + changelog.

## Tests

Handler: full window matrix (10 rows incl. both named refusals), the event pair (TripEdit mark, version bump, edited place on the seam, editor id), stale-version loses + publishes nothing, validation 400s never reach the store, owner-may-edit + non-party-404. Dispatcher: the re-share decision table (5 rows — aboard drop-off and dispatched pickup share; pre-dispatch, pre-start and at-kerb share nothing). Notifier: audience + copy fork by editor, the place-leak sweep, trip-edit status frames silent, self-ride silent. `golangci-lint` 0 issues; Docker-gated suites run in CI.

## iOS follow-up (same issue, separate PR)

Edit affordances on the tracking sheet + `tripVersion`-driven refetch; the route surfaces already re-render from the wire (MYR-485) and the etch legitimately re-keys on changed endpoints (MYR-390).

body:
Four packets, headlined by opt_quicksort becoming the first complex benchmark row within 1% of its C counterpart (1.00596x), plus broad spillover. Each packet independently measured on the deterministic instruction-count harness with zero-regression validation; the rebased series re-validated end-to-end (all 22 rows byte-identical, build-invariance green, both platforms' bootstrap fixpoints, 427/427 integration under opt1- and opt2-built compilers).

## Join-edge-decided compares + dead-slot-region frame elision

The dominating-comparison engine can now decide a compare over a join's phis when every reachable predecessor edge decides the per-edge-substituted compare the same way — rotated loops leave exactly this shape, and nested top-tested loops stop re-asking the enclosing guard every trip. On the backend side, a push-mode function whose only frame references were callee-save slots (which FPO push mode deletes) no longer sizes a dead slot region: recursive leaves get clang-shaped prologues — pushes in, pops out, no stack adjustment either way.

opt_quicksort −2.0% (goal-green), gvn_table −0.89%, intern/lex/peephole smaller; self-compile opt1 −0.78%.

## Recursive call-memory summaries + element-only calls in LICM

The call-memory pass resolves recursive cycles by an optimistic least-fixed-point (lattice argument documented at the define site), and LICM's store summaries stop killing descriptor-header loads across callees proven to write only element storage. Zero benchmark movement — landed for the class it opens; the binding constraint for the measured target (allocation-site provenance for &mut parameters) is documented at the gate sites with its measured refutations.

## M6-G: narrow load folded into its widening cast

When the compare-fold declines a multi-reader byte load, the load now lands directly in its widening cast's register instead of paying the extension twice. lex_source −1.59%.

## Tail-call admission in multiblock inline bodies

A tail call in an inlined body converts to a real call plus continuation jump with the same exit wiring as returns; helpers whose last act delegates to another function can finally be absorbed. lex_source −2.03%; self-compile opt1 −0.21%. The refusal test caught its own fixture being devirtualized before the inliner saw it, and was rewritten to be genuinely indirect.

## Measurements

lex_source 650.2M → 626.9M across the two lex packets; opt_quicksort 408.9M → 400.7M; ratchets in-series to exact measured values. Windows pool pins verified on the rebased tree (all four hold; ast_type_pool.macro_expand is down to 335 nodes of headroom and will need a measured re-pin on the next source growth). Self-compile vs the merge base on one host: opt1 −0.92%, opt2 −0.49%.

author: claude[bot]
body:
Auto-resolve's Python steps print to stdout and then spawn children — `mark-handoff.sh`, `status-comment.sh`, `pnpm resolve-generated`, `repair.py`, `gh` — that write to the same file descriptor. Python block-buffers stdout whenever it is not a terminal, so the parent's lines sat in its buffer until exit while each child wrote straight through, and the run log read in an order no code produced: a refusal's "Marked `<HEAD>` as handed off" line ahead of the diagnosis that caused it.

`run_inheriting` in `.github/scripts/auto-resolve/_git_io.py` is now the one definition — it flushes both streams, then spawns. Every inheriting spawn in the family goes through it: four in `_refusal.py`, two in `bundle.py`, one in `discover.py`.

The equivalence harness now drops `PYTHONUNBUFFERED` from the child's environment instead of inheriting it. That variable decides the recorded stdout ORDER; a runner has it unset and a developer's shell often exports it, so `test_the_command_reproduces_its_golden_record[leftover_markers]` reproduced locally and red on CI. Unset is the harder case, so the golden now records the order the runner sees.

## Decisions made

- The wrapper takes `check: bool = False` explicitly rather than passing it through `**kwargs`, because `ruff`'s `PLW1510` requires an explicit `check` at the `subprocess.run` call site.
- No changelog fragment: nothing here is user-facing.

<details>

**Root cause, observed.** `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1` is exported in this session's shell. With `env -u PYTHONUNBUFFERED`, the failure reproduces deterministically and matches the CI diff exactly — the handoff line moves from last to first.

**Non-vacuity.** With the two `flush()` calls deleted, `uv run pytest tests/test_auto_resolve_bundle_equivalence.py -k leftover_markers` reds *even in a shell that exports `PYTHONUNBUFFERED`* — the env pin is what makes that catch possible. Restored, green.

**Verified.** `env -u PYTHONUNBUFFERED uv run pytest tests/test_auto_resolve_bundle_equivalence.py tests/test_auto_resolve_bundle_inprocess.py tests/test_auto_resolve_discover.py -q -n auto` — 266 passed. The same equivalence file also passes with `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1` set, so the golden no longer depends on the environment.

**Also carried here.** `.github/scripts/tsc-staged-gate.sh`'s `kcov-exclude` reason, addressing a review nit on #4126: the tests do drive that script end to end, so the reason now names the one line no test can reach (`pnpm check`) rather than claiming no test runs the script. #4126 merged before this was committed, so it rides here.

**Reachable sites not converted.** `_git_io.py`, `fanout.py` and the rest of `bundle.py` capture their children's output, so they cannot interleave. Nothing outside `.github/scripts/auto-resolve/` was touched; other trees with the same shape are unaudited.

</details>

## Proposed guards

A repo-local line lint could flag `subprocess.run(` in `.github/scripts/**/*.py` whose call has neither `capture_output=` nor `stdout=` and is not `run_inheriting`. Benefit: this class is silent — it produces a plausible log in the wrong order, and only a golden-record corpus catches it. Cost: one more `checks/*.py` line lint on the existing `run-repo-lints.py` surface, no new workflow. Not shipped here per the fix-versus-guard rule.

body:
Closes #379

## Manual job change
- Clicking the Hero Statue (hover outline + distance click, mirroring the mercenary/building pattern) or the new **Change Job** button in the Hero Info tab opens "Change Job to next Crystal? Resets Hero and Pit level to 1." — or an OK-only "No crystal lined up. Please set a crystal" notice when the queue is empty.
- On Yes, the hero jumps out of the pit if inside (new `JumpOutOfPitForJobChangeAction` chains into `WalkToStatueForCrystalAction` via a new `OutsidePit` precondition), walks to the statue, and the existing crystal ceremony infuses the next queued crystal. Mercenaries follow out via the pit-intent system; the pit resets to level 1 after the ceremony.
- The outgoing crystal returns to the hero's **crystal inventory** (crystals only go to the Second Chance Shop on death); the vault is a never-lose-it fallback for a full inventory. Equipment carries onto the new hero — gear the new job can't equip falls back to bag, then vault. New hero level = max(crystal level, 1) after the tier reset, matching respawn semantics.
- `NeedsCrystal` is now the **top-priority GOAP goal**, above `StoppedAdventure`: a job change requested while the party is stopped (or while the dining service auto-stops for breakfast) goes to the statue first, and the surviving stop state sends the party to the table afterwards on its own.
- The statue walk is now **self-healing**: it repaths on any blocked step and only marks arrival on the actual statue tile. On persistent failure the manual path aborts (hero keeps its job) while the death path keeps its ceremony-in-place softlock guard. Queue-empty aborts exist at dialog-Yes, statue arrival, and mid-ceremony — the manual path never falls back to a random crystal.
- Saving stays enabled during the manual walk: the hero keeps its job/crystal/gear until the synchronous grant, and neither request flag is persisted, so a save/load mid-flow just forgets the request.
- Every job change (death or manual) clears **hero-owned skill shortcuts** (`ShortcutBar.ClearHeroSkillShortcuts`); mercenary skills and item shortcuts survive.

## Crystal fees
- Creating a crystal costs **100G** (`GameConfig.CrystalCreationFee`): "Fee: 100 Gold" under the Create Crystal title, Create button grayed/disabled when unaffordable, fee deducted only after the crystal lands in inventory.
- Forging costs **double the Second Chance Shop purchase price of the combined crystal, with the skill premium uncapped** (`CalculateBuyBackPrice(capPremium: false) × CrystalForgeFeeMultiplier`) — a 16-skill Legend combo always costs more than a lightly-skilled one at any level, and forging never undercuts the shop. "Fee: X Gold" appears next to the Forge button while both source slots are filled, updates on swaps, and disappears with fewer than 2 crystals; Forge is grayed/disabled when slots or gold are short. Shop prices themselves are unchanged (cap stays).
- Price ladder: forge > shop buy-back > sell.

## Bug fixes

author: sinhasagar01
body:
It shipped one unit ago as a single per-**study** checkbox in the Details panel, beside Template
and Category. Wrong grain and wrong place: one control for thirty images, nowhere near any of
them, and unable to say *this dashboard rewards a zoom and that decorative crop does not*.

It is now per image, rendered directly under the image in every block form.

```
Image
→ Zoomable image preview
→ Alt text
→ …
```

## One edit reaches every image in every section

`ImgSpecFields` in the studio registry is the shared form behind **every** image-bearing
case-study block — `annotatedImage`, `figureGrid`, `deviceShelf`, `featureRows`, `beforeAfter`,
`beforeAfterStory`'s three panels, `heroCover`, and `videoEmbed`'s poster. The checkbox goes in
once, between the image and its alt text. **Eleven call sites, one edit.**

`imgSpecFields()` in the schema is the matching seam — 13 case-study sites gain the field from one
change. That is what makes this consistent by construction rather than by eleven near-identical
edits, any one of which could have been missed.

⚠ **Blog opts out via a parameter rather than by sharing the field.** Blog's only use of that
helper is a `videoEmbed` **poster**, and a "zoomable preview" checkbox on a video still is a knob
with no consequence — the control-that-cannot-do-anything shape this repo deletes. Case-study
sites pass `{ preview: true }`; blog does not.

## Absent means true, in all four places that read it

Every image on disk predates the field, so a falsy read would ship the feature disabled on all 66.
The schema defaults true, the adapter takes `o.preview === false`, the studio form reads
`value.preview !== false`, and the sanitizer **writes only when false** — so an image left
previewable gains no `preview:` line and every content file stays byte-identical.

The per-study field is **removed** rather than kept alongside. Two controls for one question
leaves nobody able to say which won, and nothing had ever written it, so there is no content to
migrate.

## Proved end to end — after two false readings

Setting `preview: false` on one `deviceShelf` image took the prerendered page from **20 hosts to
19**, and that filename's hosts from **2 to 1**. Public coverage is otherwise unchanged at 44 of
66 images, which is the point: **the control moved and the default did not.**

⚠ **The first attempt flipped one of three images sharing a filename and measured a different
one** — the wrong-subject defect, in my own test. The second flipped a `heroCover` device that
this study's *web* branch never renders, so nothing could move. Both read as "the feature does not
work", and both were the instrument.

⚠ **And `--edit` refused a non-unique anchor in between**, correctly, into a `tail -1` that nearly
hid it. The build that followed was of an unmutated tree and its green reading meant nothing. Same
shape as the empty-replacement refusal two units ago: the tool told the truth and the pipe ate it.

⚠ **`data-preview-src` hosts are not previewable images.** One study reports 20 hosts against 12
images because a `DeviceImage` nests inside a `BeforeAfterStory` panel; `closest()` picks the inner
one, so the behaviour is right and the **count is a different unit**. The 44-of-66 figure is
images-whose-closest-host-exists, which is what a reader can actually click.

## What this deliberately does not change

The 22 boat-crest images inside `aria-hidden` scroll composites stay out, **by kind rather than by
flag** — an inspectable still previews, a depicted device in motion does not. They get no checkbox
because they are not `ImgSpecFields` consumers, which is the earlier ruling holding rather than a
gap. Making them previewable needs stills of their own, which is content rather than a switch.

⚠ **The studio form itself is unverified by render.** `/studio` is owner-gated in middleware and
the `/dev` harness 404s under `next start`, so the checkbox's appearance is owner-only to confirm.
What **is** verified: it typechecks, it lints, the schema field exists, and the value it writes
moves the public render.

## Gates

ralph **3137 across 87 suites**, tsc clean, eslint clean, production build clean.

⚠ The pre-push hook blocked this once and was right: a `next dev` left running several units ago
had been rewriting `.next`, so the census read a dev bundle and its denominator rows failed
correctly. Killed and rebuilt, not bypassed.

author: tyshaneoneill
body:
Closes #816.

## The gap

`pickFullScreen()` could create a cache copy of the picked file and then throw without ever returning a uri. Both import screens delete that copy in a `finally` keyed on the uri the wrapper hands back, so a copy the wrapper throws away instead of returning is one the caller can never clean up. For TV Time that copy is the export ZIP, which carries the account's auth-token / password-hash CSVs — an orphan is PII sitting in `cachesDirectory` at rest until OS cache eviction.

A second, always-live leak turned up while reading the native source: `keepLocalCopy()` creates a fresh `Caches/<UUID>/` directory per call and moves the pick into it (`ios/swift/FileOperations.swift`, `moveFiles`). The screens deleted only the file, so every successful import left an empty directory behind.

## Direction chosen

Of #816's three options, **the wrapper takes ownership of cleanup** — call sites don't grow any logic, they shrink.

- `pickFullScreen()` records the copy's containing directory the instant `keepLocalCopy()` reports success, and its `catch` best-effort deletes that directory before rethrowing. Nothing sits between the assignment and the return today, so this is guarding a future step rather than a live bug — but the gap it guards is unfixable from the call site, so ownership belongs here.
- New `releasePickedDocument(picked)` replaces the raw `FileSystem.deleteAsync(uri, …)` in both screens. The result now carries a `cleanupUri` alongside `uri`, because *what* to delete differs per path: the per-pick directory on the iOS native picker, the file itself on the legacy expo-document-picker path (its cache directory is shared across picks), and nothing at all on web. The `Platform.OS !== 'web'` check moved out of both screens into the wrapper.
- Deletes stay best-effort and silent — `idempotent: true`, errors swallowed, and never logged, since the path embeds the user's filename.

### Identifying the directory

The delete is recursive, so `containingDirectory()` returns the parent **only** when the parent's name matches the shape of the UUID the native side generates. Anything else falls back to deleting just the file. That fails closed: an unrecognized layout degrades to exactly what `main` does today, whose worst case is the empty-directory leak — never a recursive delete of a shared cache directory.

### On the `status: 'error'` path specifically

There is nothing to delete, and nothing we *could* delete. The native side creates the destination directory first and then moves the file in, so a reported error means the move failed: no file landed, and the empty directory's path is never sent to JS. #816's third option applies here — that behavior is now pinned by a test asserting no delete is attempted, with a comment pointing at the native source. If a future library version starts returning a uri on error, that expectation is what should force the cleanup.

## Constraints held

- No static import of `@react-native-documents/picker` anywhere — the lazy-require architecture is untouched.
- Web stays unreachable: no `cleanupUri` on a blob: pick, so `releasePickedDocument` never calls into expo-file-system there. Covered by a new `pick-document-web.test.ts` (web now genuinely diverges from Android, which the non-iOS suite's header previously assumed it didn't), which also carries the spy-in-the-mock-factory proving the native package is never required on web.
- No file path or name is ever logged or captured.

## Structural note

`DocumentCopyError` moved to `lib/pick-document-error.ts` and is re-exported from `pick-document`. `classify-read-error` only ever needed the class, and importing it from the picker pulled expo-document-picker and expo-file-system into its graph — both untransformed ESM, so its unit test needed empty module mocks purely to survive module load. Those are gone.

## Tests

`pick-document-ios-available.test.ts` gains a cleanup suite: a post-copy throw deletes the directory and rethrows; a failing cleanup delete doesn't mask the original error; `releasePickedDocument` targets the directory, never rejects (including when `deleteAsync` throws synchronously rather than returning a rejected promise), and no-ops on a cancel; and four non-UUID parent layouts each fall back to deleting the file alone. Mutation-checked the three load-bearing guards — removing the cleanup line, the UUID check, or the sync-throw handling each fails the test written for it.

## Runtime scope

**This PR's runtime effect ships only in binaries ≥1.6.1.** `pickFullScreen` is dead code on older runtimes — they have no `@react-native-documents/picker` native module, so `requireNativePicker()` returns null and the legacy path runs. The `releasePickedDocument` swap does apply to the legacy path on every runtime, but there it's behavior-identical to the `deleteAsync` it replaces.

## Gates

```
npm run lint      -> 0 errors, 10 warnings (all pre-existing)
npx tsc --noEmit  -> clean
npm test          -> Test Suites: 201 passed, 201 total
                     Tests:       2348 passed, 2348 total
```

author: thecodingdad-tisonk
body:
## The experimental gate asks before it flips

Turning Experimental Systems on arms **unfinished** systems on a live savegame, and it did that on a single click with nothing between the player and the consequence. It now warns and waits for a Confirm.

### Where it hooks

`SoilSettingsPanel:requestChange` is the single choke point every toggle, cycle and reset funnels through, so intercepting there means no path can flip the gate unasked. The original body moves to `_applyChange` **unchanged**; only a confirmed answer reaches it.

### The properties that matter

The point is not that a dialog appears. It is that **abort leaves the setting exactly as it was**, in both directions. A confirmation that fails open is worse than no confirmation at all, because the player now believes they declined.

- **FAIL CLOSED.** If `YesNoDialog` is unavailable the change is refused, not silently applied. A gate that cannot ask does not open.
- **Non-admins are refused BEFORE the prompt**, rather than being walked through a scary confirmation whose change we were always going to reject.
- **No prompt when the value is not actually changing** (re-selecting the current value).
- **`resetCurrentCategory` passes `skipConfirm`.** It is already a deliberate act, it runs in a loop a modal would break, and for this gate it only ever restores the LOCKED default. Nothing to warn about.

### The text

Presented as `DialogElement.TYPE_WARNING`, with direction-specific copy. Enabling says the systems are not finished, can change without warning, can affect the savegame irreversibly, and to keep a backup. Disabling says what they already wrote stays put but stops being updated. Buttons are Confirm / Abort.

`YesNoDialog.show(callback, target, text, title, yesText, noText, dialogType, ...)` per `gui/dialogs/YesNoDialog.lua:8`; the callback shape with a target set is `callback(target, value, args)` per `:82-86`.

### Verification

- Bench `experimental_confirm_test.lua`: **23 assertions** covering the ask, abort-in-both-directions, confirm applies, fail-closed, no-op, non-admin, reset-skips, and that no other setting gains a prompt.
- Full suite **2795 passed, 0 failed across 66 files**; Lua 5.1 syntax and lint clean.
- 5 l10n keys in **all 27** translation files, English fallbacks in code.
- **Not yet confirmed in-game.**

### Note on the version number

Bumped to **2.5.0.64**, deliberately past the 2.5.0.63 on `feat/SF-39-handful-panel` (PR #832), which is open in parallel. Whichever merges second will conflict on the version line in `modDesc.xml`; resolve it to 2.5.0.64.

body:
## Summary

Long text now wraps onto additional lines inside its own cell instead of spilling over empty neighbors. The whole value stays readable within its column, in both the TUI and `dump`.

Closes #33

## How it works

- A new display-width `wrap` primitive in `ui::text` breaks text char-by-char (CJK-safe; a char wider than the column still makes progress, so no pathological input can loop).
- The grid renders variable row heights: a sheet row is as tall as its tallest visible cell, with no cap (a huge cell is the source file's problem, per review). Continuation lines carry no row label, the horizontal gridline sits under a sheet row's *last* line, comment markers stay on the first, and fills / font colors / the selection highlight extend across all wrapped lines.
- Numbers never wrap — one right-aligned line, clipped with `…` — so digit groups can't split across lines (Excel-parity decision).
- Merged regions wrap at the merged width on their anchor row; wrapped tails stay inside the region's columns.
- The #21 spill-over-empty-neighbors behavior is fully retired.
- Scrolling: `follow_row_wrapped` replaces the fixed-height cursor following. Heights being ≥1 allows a coarse jump before fine-tuning, so long-distance cursor jumps stay cheap; a row taller than the window scrolls to its first line.

```

author: aymanseif
body:
## Summary

Closes the web identity/auth holes behind issue #17. The previous implementation never validated sessions: it issued an unsaved placeholder token, and multiple endpoints trusted client-supplied identity headers.

### Security fixes

1. **Real server-side sessions.** `/api/auth/login` and `/api/auth/web-login` now issue an opaque bearer token; only its SHA-256 hash is stored in a new `sessions` table (expiring, revocable). The raw token is returned once. (`services/session.js`)
2. **`x-user-id` header no longer trusted.** `/api/auth/entitlement` and `/api/auth/missions/increment` derive identity from the validated session; any client can no longer impersonate another user by setting `x-user-id`.
3. **Command Center placeholder gate removed.** `checkFounderSession` accepted any ≥32-char value in `x-founder-session` or `?session=`. It is now `sessionService.requireFounderSession`: a valid founder session is required, forged headers → 401, non-founder with a valid session → 403.
4. **Deterministic founder gate.** `identity.isFounderUser` — founder = user whose `id`/telegram id matches `TEOS_FOUNDER_TELEGRAM_ID`. Workspace member roles are no longer consulted. Also fixes a latent **web-login 500**: the old code called `repos.users.getByTelegram` which did not exist (added it).
5. **`POST /api/auth/logout`** revokes the presented session server-side.

### Data layer

- `sessions` table: `db/schema.sql`, memory `db/tables.js`, forward-only migration `db/migrations/011_add_sessions.sql` (apply via `npm run db:migrations` on deploy).
- `repos.sessions` (`create`, `getByTokenHash`, `getByUser`, `revoke`) + `repos.users.getByTelegram`.

### Config

- `SESSION_TTL_HOURS` documented in `.env.example` (default 24h).

### Tests

- New `tests/test-sessions.js` — 43 assertions: lifecycle, expiry, revocation, spoofing regression (`x-user-id`, `x-founder-session`, `?session=`), founder authz (401/403), session fixation.
- Fixed `tests/test-founder-auth.js`, which never exited (loading the server keeps the event loop alive via `app.listen`), so run-all killed it at the 120s timeout.
- Gate: **69 suites, 69 passed** (`npm test`), `eslint` clean on all changed files.

### Scope / not included

- **No merge, no deploy, no DB migration run.** The migration file is added only.
- Founders still receive the token in the response body (existing client contract). Moving to an HttpOnly cookie is a follow-up; the header-\>session store change is the security-critical fix and is deliberately minimal.
- The `/founder` static console still uses the existing `requireAuditAuth` key gate (unchanged).

author: kwoooj
body:
Closes #17

## 원인 — 서버 시각이 페이지에 박혀 나온다

같은 날 122KB 스냅샷 3건이 쌓였다. 두 파일을 실제로 비교했더니 **다른 곳이 딱 한 군데**였다.

```diff
- SERVER_NOW:"2026/08/13 16:12:42"
+ SERVER_NOW:"2026/08/13 17:02:45"
```

Nuxt SSR 페이로드(`window.__NUXT__`)에 서버 시각이 들어온다. 같은 페이로드의 `D_DAY:-220, -157, -5, 25, 81` 은 서버가 계산한 카운트다운이라 **날이 바뀌면 반드시 달라진다** — 오늘 안에서는 같았지만 내일은 다르다. 일정 값(`EXAM_DT`·`APPLY_START_DT`)은 그대로였다.

## 고친 방식

`archive()` 가 `volatile` 패턴을 받아 **해시를 뜰 때만** 적용한다. 패턴은 어댑터가 선언한다 — `store.mjs` 가 사이트별 사정을 알면 안 된다.

**저장하는 바이트는 건드리지 않는다.** 아카이브의 존재 이유가 "그날 바이트가 유일한 단서" 인데 우리가 손댄 바이트를 남기면 `--replay` 가 원본을 재현하지 못한다. 테스트로 못 박았다:

> `저장된 바이트는 원본 그대로다 — 정규화 결과를 쓰면 --replay 가 원본을 못 만든다`

곁가지 2건도 처리했다.

- 크롤 원본 확장자가 `.json` 인데 내용이 생 HTML 이었다 (`JSON.parse` 가 바로 죽는다 — 조사 중 실제로 겪었다). `.html` 로 바꾸면서 **확장자로 직전 스냅샷을 거르던 필터도 없앴다** — 그대로 두면 확장자를 바꾸는 순간 전량이 한 번 더 쌓인다
- kbs 중복 3건 삭제. 셋 다 122,195 byte 동일 페이지고 일정 값도 같아 남길 정보가 없다

## 검증 — 실측

연속 2회 수집:

```
1회차  크롤 원본 1건 저장   (kbs-korean.2026-08-13.653f250d2484.html)
2회차  크롤 원본 0건 저장
```

확장자를 바꾼 나머지 3개 소스도 재저장되지 않았다. `store.test.mjs` **12건** 추가, 전체 **210건 통과**.

## ⚠️ 검증 중에 더 심각한 것을 발견했다 — #18

2회차를 돌리다 **29종목이 조용히 사라졌다.** `meta.failed` 29건, qnet 회차 102 → 53, 그룹 11 → 8. 그런데 `qnet.health === 'ok'` · `staleCount: 0` · **종료코드 0** 이고 `ci-gate` 는 `✅ 수집 정상` 을 찍는다.

한 번 더 호출해 확인했다.

```
HTTP 429
errMsg: LIMITED_NUMBER_OF_SERVICE_REQUESTS_EXCEEDS_ERROR
returnReasonCode: 22   (일일 서비스 요청제한 횟수 초과)
```

429 응답이 `header`/`body` 가 아니라 `OpenAPI_ServiceResponse.cmmMsgHeader` 로 와서, `extractItems()` 가 빈 배열을 돌려주고 호출부가 "레코드 없음" 으로 집계한다. **정상적인 빈 응답과 요청 거절이 구분되지 않는다.**

이 PR 에서는 **고치지 않았다** — 아카이브 해시와 섞으면 되돌릴 수 없는 커밋이 된다. #18 로 분리했고, 문서에만 경고를 달았다. 함정 목록의 "응답 0건은 오류가 아니다" 가 이 구멍을 정당화하고 있었기 때문이다.

**한도 계산: 1회 수집 = 47회 호출, 개발계정 일 1,000 → 하루 21회가 상한.** 하루 1회 배치만 돌면 안전하다. 오늘 넘긴 것은 배치 1회 + 로컬 3회 + 세션 중 여러 번이 겹친 결과다.

이번 실행으로 깎인 `data/published/` 는 커밋하지 않고 되돌렸다 (11그룹·169회차·744이벤트 유지).

## 덧붙임

`npm run collect` 이 `--env-file-if-exists=.env` 를 쓴다. 셸마다 키를 앞에 붙이면 히스토리에 남는다. `--env-file` 은 파일이 없으면 죽는데 CI 에는 `.env` 가 없다.

author: bbasketballer75
body: Four independent defects found while auditing the desktop build. Each is self-contained — happy to split into separate PRs if you'd prefer. Independent of #4 (no overlapping hunks). --- ## 1. Every `settings.json` save after the first fails with a false STALE error `ConfigBackend.saveSettings` was typed `Promise` and discarded the mtime — even though the whole chain below it already returns one: | Layer | Returns mtime? | |---|---| | `save_settings` (Rust) | yes — `Result` | | `tauriSaveSettings` | yes — `Promise` | | `ConfigBackend.saveSettings` | **no — `Promise`** | With no real value available, `ConfigApp` fell back to: ```ts setSettingsMtime(Date.now()); // wall clock, never the file's mtime ``` The next save compares that against the on-disk mtime, fails the optimistic-concurrency check, and tells the user the file *"was changed on disk by another process. Reload the app…"* — which is false, and reloading discards their edits. `saveModels` 25 lines earlier already does this correctly (`const newMtime = await backend.saveModels(...); setModelsMtime(newMtime)`). This just brings settings in line by plumbing the existing return value through the interface and both backends. ## 2. Config load failures were swallowed and became an empty document `tauriLoadAll` wrapped both loads in a bare catch: ```ts } catch { models = {}; modelsMtime = 0; } ``` `load_json_at` already treats a **missing** file as success (empty object, mtime 0), so the only way these reject is a genuine failure — unreadable file or malformed JSON. The result: a user whose `models.json` had a syntax error saw a clean, apparently-empty editor with **no warning at all**; editing one field and saving replaced the real file contents. Removed both catches so the error propagates to `ConfigApp`'s loader, which surfaces it via `setError`. That loader resets each document *and* its baseline (`setOriginalModels("{}")` etc.), so nothing is dirty afterwards and the dirty-guarded save paths (`if (isDirty)`, `if (isModelsDirty)`, `if (isSettingsDirty)`) write nothing after a failed load. **Tradeoff worth flagging:** one malformed document now blocks the whole load rather than only its own section. That's the safe direction, but if you'd rather keep per-document isolation, the alternative is a per-document "failed to load" flag that refuses to save just that document. Happy to rework it that way. ## 3. Windows: every CLI is reported as not installed `check_cli_installed` shells out to `which`, which doesn't exist on Windows (the equivalent is `where`). The spawn error is mapped to `Err`, and the frontend treats that as not-installed — so every provider card shows the "Not found" badge and install instructions even for CLIs already on PATH. Verified on Windows 11 with the built app, invoking the command directly: ``` before: { node: false, git: false, gh: false, : false } after: { node: true, git: true, gh: true, : false } ``` ## 4. `list_key_statuses` panics on any non-ASCII stored value The preview built a **byte**-index slice: ```rust &v[v.len().saturating_sub(4)..] ``` When that offset lands inside a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence, Rust panics. Because this command populates the entire API Keys screen, the screen stays broken for as long as the value is stored. It was also silently *wrong* on values that didn't panic. Running the old expression against the new one: ``` "sk-ant-abc123" old="…c123" new="…c123" (same) "clé-café" old="…afé" new="…café" (old drops a char, mangles it) "キー値テスト" old=PANIC new="…値テスト" "token🔑" old="…🔑" new="…ken🔑" (old returns 1 char, not 4) "é" old="…" new="…é" ``` The panic message from the old expression, for the record: ``` start byte index 14 is not a char boundary; it is inside 'ス' (bytes 12..15) ``` Extracted `preview_suffix`, which takes the last four `char`s, plus a unit test covering CJK, accented, emoji, short and empty values. --- ## Verification - `tsc --noEmit` clean - 177/177 frontend tests pass - `cargo check --all-targets` clean (test module included) - Release bundle builds - Fixes 3 and 4 verified empirically as shown above Note: `cargo test` can't link in my environment (`export ordinal too large` from the MinGW linker building the cdylib for tests) — a pre-existing GNU-toolchain limitation unrelated to these changes, which is why fix 4 is also demonstrated standalone above. `cargo check --all-targets` does typecheck the new test. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

author: realmarcin
body:
#320's 87 records split by whether the record's CURIE carries **any structure**: 26 sit on a structureless grouping class while their own CAS is registered against a real structured term; 61 have a structured CURIE and a CAS pointing elsewhere.

## The substantive finding: neither heuristic works alone

I tried label-specificity first and it mis-sorted `Bicine` and `Aluminium sulfate`. The structureless-class split is better but still not sufficient:

- `Fructose` and `Ascorbic acid` sit on structureless classes — yet their **generic labels** make the generic term correct under §3 step 4. There the **CAS** is the over-specific field.
- `ACES`, `Bicine`, `HEPES` are **trivial names for one specific buffer**. There the **CURIE** is what moves.

Telling those apart is a chemistry judgement, not a mechanical rule. So only the unambiguous subset is changed here, and the remaining 84 stay open on #320 rather than being swept.

## Changed

```
HEPES   CHEBI:46756 -> CHEBI:42334   promotion
ACES    CHEBI:39061 -> CHEBI:39060   MERGE — target already held
Bicine  CHEBI:39065 -> CHEBI:40957   MERGE — target already held
```

Each verified before acting: the target carries a structure, the record's own `cas_rn` is registered against it in ChEBI, and for Bicine/HEPES the target carries the record's trivial name as a synonym.

## Two of the three were duplicates

Caught by the collision guard rather than assumed — a promotion would have failed outright:

- `ACES` (occ 8, on the class) was shadowing `N-(2-acetamido)-2-aminoethanesulfonic acid` (occ 1, correct term)
- `Bicine` (occ 3) was shadowing `BICINE buffer` (occ 2)

Same shape as #334's hexahydrates and #315's `Ca-pantothenate`: a term with no structure gives lexical matching nothing to distinguish records by, so the duplicate survives and the survivor lands on the class. **That is now three separate defect classes resolving into the same root cause.**

The correctly-mapped record wins in both, despite fewer occurrences — the identifier being right matters more than the traffic.

## One defect caught in review

The HEPES promotion updated the record but not its SSSOM row, and `test_sssom_currency` caught it (`expected CHEBI:42334, present CHEBI:46756`). Fixed before push. That is the third time this session that test has caught a propagation miss — it is doing more work than its name suggests.

## Problem
Selecting the `mexican` theme crashed the whole site with `Uncaught Error: Illegal value for token color: #eee` at Monaco editor mount. Since the theme id was already persisted to localStorage, every reload re-crashed until the key was manually cleared.

## Root cause
Monaco only accepts `#rrggbb` (+ optional 2 alpha digits) in theme definitions. Nine themes used 3-digit shorthand hex (`#eee`, `#333`, `#001`...).

## Fix (defense in depth)
1. **Data** — `themes.ts`: expanded all 27 shorthand hexes across 9 themes to 6-digit.
2. **Boundary** — `CodeEditor.tsx`: `normalizeHex()` expands any 3-digit hex before it reaches Monaco; `defineTheme` wrapped in try/catch so a broken theme is skipped, never fatal.
3. **Storage** — `theme.tsx`: unknown stored theme ids are dropped and fall back to default instead of re-saving forever.

## Verification
- `tsc --noEmit` and `vite build` pass
- All 192 themes validated against Monaco's actual color regex (`/^#?([0-9a-fA-F]{6})([0-9a-fA-F]{2})?$/` extracted from the shipped bundle)
- Playwright e2e of the exact repro: poisoned `mexican` in localStorage + editor mount → zero theme errors, app fully functional (control run with default theme shows identical benign headless worker noise)

author: hajisensai
body:
Windows 发布构建在 develop 上**固定红**（单独重跑 windows job，attempt 3 同样红 —— 不是并发伪红），而日志里只有两行:

```
Target dart_build failed : error : Building native assets failed.
error MSB8066: Custom build for '...' exited with code ...
```

MSBuild 把自定义生成步骤的真实报错整个折叠掉了。**连续两次重跑都拿不到根因。**

## 连锁后果

同 run 的 `Publish mirror update manifest` 报 `No files matched fushi-*-windows-setup.exe` 而挂 → `latest-beta.json` 从未写出 → `v1.4.0-beta.9473` 成了只有 ipa+zip 的半成品发布。

## 本机复现不出来（重要）

本机 `flutter build windows --release -v` **顺利通过 native assets**（`fushidicts_ffi.dll` 已产出并安装），失败在更后面的 `cmake_install.cmake:429`「Missing required Windows download runtime: fushi_torrent_ffi.dll」——那是每 worktree 需先跑 `build_windows_dll.ps1` 的本地前置条件，**与 CI 那处不是同一个**。

## 顺带查明：为什么「CI 全绿」从没暴露它

| workflow | Windows 构建命令 |
|---|---|
| `build-multiplatform.yml`（验证，绿） | `flutter build windows **--debug**` |
| `release-desktop.yml`（发布，红） | `flutter build windows **--release**` |

**根本不是同一种构建**——debug 不走 AOT。这与 #810 的 BUG-1588（TMDB key 只注入验证构建、发出去的包没有）是同一种病：**把验证构建的绿当成发布构建的绿**。

另注：`editbin /STACK` 那个 gen_snapshot 栈溢出 workaround 只存在于本机 SDK，仓库与 CI 里**一处都没有**（`grep -rn 'editbin|/STACK|gen_snapshot' .github/ tool/ ci/ docs/` 全空）。它是否是本红的成因，等 `-v` 日志确认，**不先下结论**。

## 本 PR 的范围

**只修可见性这一半**，红本身没修——根因必须等下一次 CI 跑出 `-v` 日志才能定，盲改等于赌。

- Windows 发布构建加 `-v`（本机正是靠它拿到被折叠的真错误；实测约 2500 行，远小于「红了但不知道为什么」的代价）
- 新增 `if: failure()` 步骤把 `CMakeOutput.log` / `CMakeError.log` 传成 artifact（`-v` 打的是 flutter 侧，CMake 配置期报错只在这两个文件里）

## 守卫

`release_build_diagnosability_guard_test.dart`（4 条）：发布构建必须带 `-v`；失败必须上传 CMake 日志且挂 `if: failure()`；并把「验证构建=debug / 发布构建=release」这一**当前事实**钉住——谁改动其中一边，这条会红，逼他回来确认「验证绿 ≠ 发布绿」这个前提是否还成立。

变异实测：去掉 `-v` → 红；还原 → 4 条全绿。

## 下一步需要你点头

修完可见性后要跑一次 `workflow_dispatch`（`channel=debug`）才能拿到真日志。该动作会产出一个 debug 通道预发布，属于对外动作，等你同意再发。

author: milnerrad
body:
## Summary
- invalidate `skill_view` and `read_file` dedup caches whenever proactive tool-result pruning commits
- ensure post-prune reloads return full content instead of unchanged-content stubs that point at removed tool bodies
- add focused regression coverage at the proactive-prune commit boundary

## Problem
Full context compression already resets these retrieval caches because earlier tool bodies may have been summarized away. The lighter proactive-prune path can replace the same `skill_view`/`read_file` results with compact markers, but did not perform the equivalent reset.

This creates a ghost-content state:
1. a skill or file is loaded and recorded in the per-task dedup cache;
2. proactive pruning removes its full tool-result body;
3. the agent explicitly reloads it;
4. retrieval returns `content_returned: false` and refers to the earlier result, which is no longer present.

## Fix
After the proactive prune caller accepts a new message list with a non-zero prune count, clear both per-task retrieval caches using the same best-effort semantics as full compression. No-op or failed prune attempts do not reset the caches.

## Test plan
- [x] `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/run_agent/test_proactive_prune_loop_wiring.py tests/tools/test_skill_view_dedup.py tests/tools/test_file_read_guards.py tests/agent/test_proactive_tool_result_pruning.py -q`
- [x] 61 tests passed
- [x] `git diff --check`
- [x] Python compilation of changed files

The regression test proves both caches are reset exactly once after a committed prune.

author: graylee0128
body:
Implements #28

P2 的最後一張票。紫隊唯一會被帶走的產物 —— 報告會被轉寄、被引用、被拿去要預算，所以三個欄位少一個都會誤導讀者。用**型別**把它們釘成不可省：

## 三個不可省欄位（型別強制）
1. **告警總量與 coverage 並列** —— `BlueSummary` 同時要 `action_coverage` 與 `alert_volume`，**沒有「只吐 coverage」的建構路徑**（少了會獎勵「對所有東西告警」，§3.2 陷阱②）。
2. **每個 coverage gap 標註哪一種缺口** —— `CoverageGap` 強制帶 `MissClass`，且**拒絕** hit/unknown/out_of_scope（混講會冤枉藍隊，§3.4）。
3. **unknown 的數量與原因** —— `UnknownSummary` 在 `count>0` 時強制要 `reasons`，不准只給裸數字（§3.5）。

## 其餘 AC
- **數字取自 Evaluation API 的 `metrics`，報告不重算**；`ExerciseReport` 是 frozen dataclass，產出當下複製數字，之後 metrics 再變也不動（**快照穩定**）。一條測試 mutate 來源 metrics、斷言報告不變。
- **不出現 `Detection Rate`**（ADR ⑨ 歷史別名）—— `_reject_detection_rate` 遞迴掃報告任一層，發現該 key 就爆。
- **raw 覆蓋時窗**以 `raw_coverage_windows` 標明，retention 過期時標範圍而非靜默空白（§4.2）。

## 測試分層
- **T1（本機 importlib 實跑 14 條全綠 + 進 CI）**：`tests/report/test_exercise_report.py` —— 三不可省欄位各自的 negative test（省了就爆）、缺口分類、unknown 數量+原因、快照穩定、無 Detection Rate、raw 時窗。

## blocker 說明
- #21 已 CLOSED。
- #28 的 blocker 列了 #26 —— 但 #28 需要的「缺口分類呈現契約」＝ **master 既有的 `purple.metrics.gaps.MissClass`**，本票直接沿用、**不 import #26 的 console 套件**，故獨立於 master 施工，不把兩張 canonical 票綁進同一 PR。與 #26 的一致性由共用 `MissClass` 保證。

## 刻意不在本 PR 的
- 報告的 HTML/PDF 渲染與轉寄：本 PR 是資料契約層（`as_dict()` 已 JSON-able）。
- 證據快照的 raw 抓取走既有 `retention/report.py` 的 `snapshot_report`，不在本票重造。

author: artalesadmin
body:
### Motivation
- Move the Reader UI toward a quieter, literary-first chrome by removing the user-facing Focus/fullscreen mode and surfacing only essential reading orientation and progress. 
- Consolidate secondary controls into a compact, accessible menu and add a small go‑to‑page capability that fits naturally into the toolbar without changing page slicing or reading progress semantics.

### Description
- Remove the visible Focus mode and any browser-fullscreen user flow while preserving compatibility of stored settings; the UI now uses a calm two-row toolbar (identity + title row, reading row with progress and page indicator). 
- Introduce a compact menu triggered from the toolbar that contains bookmark actions (create/update/go/clear), layout (pagedFlow / spread), theme (light / script / dark), font size, width and density controls, preview continuation and a leave-reader link. 
- Add an accessible page-jump affordance on the page indicator (click to open numeric input, Enter confirms, Escape cancels, values clamped) and wire `onGoToPage` in `ReaderClient` to compute the correct zero-based index, align spreads to their start and scroll to the target page in pagedFlow without modifying slicing. 
- Changed files: `components/reader/ReaderToolbar.tsx` (new calm toolbar, compact menu, page input), `components/reader/ReaderClient.tsx` (remove focus/fullscreen state, page-jump wiring), `components/reader/reader.css` (responsive calm chrome styles), `lib/reader/readerSettings.ts` (default `controlsCollapsed: true`), `lib/i18n/dictionaries/cs/public.ts` and `lib/i18n/dictionaries/en/public.ts` (localized labels), and docs `docs/ARTALES_READER_CALM_CHROME_GO_TO_PAGE_V0_1.md`, `docs/ARTALES_READER_PAGED_FLOW_DEFAULT_V0_1.md`, `docs/ARTALES_READER_MODE_CHROME_NOTES_REDESIGN_AUDIT_V0_1.md`; Risk: **high** (Reader critical path); Target: **develop first**; DB: **no**; Env: **no**; Rollback: revert the Phase 2 commit (branch: `codex/reader-phase-2-calm-chrome`, commit recorded during work). 

### Testing
- `git diff --check` completed successfully with no whitespace errors. 
- Targeted ESLint on the changed TS/TSX and dictionary files passed for the modified files. 
- TypeScript type-check (`npx tsc --noEmit`) completed successfully. 
- Next.js production build compiled and TypeScript passed, but collection of page-data failed in the local build step due to intentionally absent Supabase environment variables, so interactive develop-preview checks (keyboard/menu/page-jump behavior, mobile wrapping, bookmark flow and visual QA) remain manual and are listed in the Phase 2 checklist in `docs/ARTALES_READER_CALM_CHROME_GO_TO_PAGE_V0_1.md`.

author: vincentshipsit
body:
## Why

Costs sat on **Updating…** because a missing lifetime snapshot (or a missing Grok row) kicked a walk of the whole local corpus — Claude JSONL, Codex `sessions/` + `archived_sessions/` + `logs_2.sqlite`. On this machine that was ~11 GB.

Quota APIs already power the gauges. They do **not** have per-model 30-day spend, so the chart still has to read local transcripts. They cannot replace the scan. They also cannot justify reading archives from March.

## What

- **Window only.** Listing skips files whose mtime is older than `cutoff − 36h`. Grok opens `updates.jsonl` only.
- **No lifetime card.** `CostSummary.lifetime` stays optional for cache decode and is no longer filled. `lifetime == nil` no longer starts a backfill.
- **No SQLite on the default scan.** `logs_2.sqlite` (~1.8 GB here) is a recent-session fallback the 30-day rollouts already cover.
- **Progress banner.** Costs shows listed file count and bytes while a refresh runs, and warns if the *windowed* corpus is still ≥ 1 GiB.

## Local cleanup (this machine, not the PR)

author: davidtaikocha
body:
## Summary

- fetch `llvm.sh` and its signing key with bounded GET retries
- remove the hash-pinned installer repository HEAD preflight and let signed `apt-get update` validate the repository
- pre-seed the key so upstream skips its key HEAD and unbounded key GET
- test both failing HEAD probes deterministically in the arm64 LLVM CI job

## Root cause

Three arm64 jobs exposed separate network failure signatures against apt.llvm.org:

- [job 94359650498](https://github.com/taikoxyz/alethia-reth/actions/runs/31672415154/job/94359650498): the `/trixie/` HEAD preflight timed out
- [job 94366430808](https://github.com/taikoxyz/alethia-reth/actions/runs/31674635806/job/94366430808): key HEAD timed out twice and `/trixie/` HEAD timed out once
- [job 94383071812](https://github.com/taikoxyz/alethia-reth/actions/runs/31674635806/job/94383071812): the key GET stalled for 900 seconds, followed by two `/trixie/` HEAD timeouts

The pinned upstream installer treats a transient repository HEAD failure as an unsupported distribution and performs its key GET with the default 900-second wget timeout.

The wrapper now verifies the upstream script hash, disables only its redundant repository HEAD check, and relies on the signed `apt-get update` already protected by `Acquire::Retries`. It also downloads the signing key atomically using four bounded GET attempts, which eliminates both upstream key operations.

## Regression coverage

The Docker integration test runs the real wrapper in Debian Trixie and makes both repository and signing-key HEAD requests fail while bounded GETs succeed.

- before the repository-probe fix: all three installer attempts failed and the test exited 1
- after the fix: no upstream HEAD request is required and the LLVM command contract completes

## Validation

- red-green Docker regression test
- native `linux/arm64` Debian Trixie install: LLVM 22.1.8
- ShellCheck
- actionlint
- `just fmt-check`
- `just clippy`
- `just test`: 294 passed

author: benbaichmankass
body:
## Summary

**The "1d fleet cannot be graded" conclusion I posted overnight was wrong in its cause.** `train_exit_head.py` cut one walk-forward test fold per **calendar year**, which silently makes a strategy's **trade frequency** decide whether it can be graded at all. A daily-bar leg trades ~20×/year, so every year-fold landed 12–42 trades against a 50-trade floor and was skipped — while the pool held **371 trades across 19 years**. The data was always there; the slicing discarded it.

Operator-directed this morning: fix the slicing **and re-run every leg**, so the whole matrix rests on one fold scheme rather than a mixed one.

## Reproduced, both directions

On the measured shape (371 trades / 19 years):

| mode | folds | sizes | clear the 50-trade floor |
|---|--:|---|--:|
| `years` (old) | 18 | ~19–20 each | **0** |
| `trades` (new) | 6 | exactly 50 each | **6** |

The `years` row reproduces exactly what the trainer returned on both real 1d pools, which is what tells me the synthetic shape matches the real population. Projected on the real pools: donchian-1d 0 → ~6, pullback-1d 0 → ~10.

## This is not a weaker bar

What carries the statistics in a fold is the number of **trades** in it, not the calendar span they happen to cover. `--min-fold-trades` is now honoured **by construction** rather than by rejection. **Time ordering, the purge on each trade's last bar, and the embargo are unchanged** — only the block boundary moved.

## Architecture impact

- [x] **Not applicable** — research tooling. No live path, no config, no schema. (The *verdicts* it produces feed Tier-3 decisions, which stay operator-gated as always.)

## Test plan

- [x] **9 tests**, all passing; `ruff` clean; full `run_guards --base main` green
- [x] **The leakage invariant is asserted directly** — every test trade must enter at or after its fold's cutoff, so no trade can sit on both sides of its own fold. A scheme that grades more legs while leaking labels is worse than one that grades none
- [x] Folds asserted **chronological and disjoint** (walk-forward, not shuffled)
- [x] **Positive control that reproduces the DEFECT** — year-folds must yield 0 usable; if the synthetic shape drifts from what was measured, the suite says so rather than quietly testing a different population
- [x] Control that a **high-frequency pool is unaffected** — intraday legs were never the broken case and must not get worse
- [x] `test_the_check_can_fail` — a pool too small for one block yields no folds, or the block-size assertion passes vacuously on an empty list
- [ ] CI green

## Design notes

- **`--fold-mode {trades,years}`**, default `trades`. `years` reproduces any pre-2026-08-13 result *exactly* — that's what makes the coming re-run **comparable** rather than merely newer.
- **The report records `fold_mode` and `min_fold_trades`.** Trade-folds and calendar-folds are not comparable evidence, so a verdict that doesn't state which produced it invites the apples-to-oranges read this whole exercise exists to avoid.
- **A trailing partial block is excluded and *said so*** rather than silently shortening the population.

## What this doesn't fix

The 9 `vol_trail` cells have the same defect in a different place — their OOS split is a fixed **date** (2025-07-01), leaving n=3–6 on a low-frequency leg. Same reasoning, different code path; that's the next commit.

author: rattus128
body: This PR contains a new comfy model and a supporting major core feature (cuda graphs) # Minimax Music 3 native model support https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-Music-3 This is a two phase model with a non-trivial auto-regressive model feeding a smaller diffusion model. Implement core support in comfy. A text encoder node with split fields for lyrics and caption and generation settings is added. The AR model steps are proportional to the generated output and are capable of detecting short end of output therefore the AR drives latent size generation. ### Model formats and quants The original published model segmented the embedding and lm_head weights into two distinct regions for text and audio without splitting the weights. This lead to a case where the giant embedding and lm_head weights were only being partially used or in the case of lm_head padding the checkpoint with dead weight and dead computation. Comfy has repacked the models to remove these dead rows on lm_head (-1.6GB). The embedding has been split between the audio and text sections as the larger text section only needs to exist for the prefill stage of AR and should be freed from VRAM once you get the VRAM critical AR. So that is split and a new facility is added to dynamic VRAM to push that prefill only embedding down to the lowest priority and its first to go once you hit the VRAM ceiling. for the AR, bf16 and int8_convrot are tested with good results w4a8 has been briefly tested as runnable but with variable results (not shipped) for DiT, fp32 (original) fp16 and int8_convrot are tested with good results Rerformace of the AR models is often CPU bottlenecked in comfy, so now that we have this high-step-count AR model performance is unlocked with ... # Cuda Graphs Add native cuda graph support to ComfyUI interoperable with dynamic VRAM. The way it works, is a model declares its units of prefetch to the dynamic vram engine such that these units are consolidated in the aimdo VBAR. The existing block prefetcher is enabled for the model and the prefetch iterator declares the executable core for the block. The prefetch engine then aimdo faults the VRAM, and it its present in memory does nessacary one-time-prep (e.g. Lora application). The layer is then cuda graphed for replay. Each step the prefetched then only has to check if the vbar is still faulted and if so, replay the graph. The graph implementation is kept simple, with a side-effect only policy on graph IO. That is, there are no pure input and outputs to the graph by design as cuda-graphs needs static addresses for memory allocations. The models that use this engine are therefore refactored to move the critical pieces of transformer block IO to static buffers that live for the duration of inferences. This is called "cross-step-state". A registry for this is added to model_management. The most obvious piece of data that goes in cross-step-state is X (the activation that flows from one transformer block to the next). A single x buffer is allocated and then exists for the lifetime of inference and each graph reads from and write to this singular buffer. This avoids D2D copies and per graph allocations for IO buffers (which cost a lot of VRAM too). The main code pattern to use this is this (from llama in this PR): ``` for i, layer in enumerate(self.layers): ... def core(): _, current_kv = layer( x=x, attention_mask=mask, freqs_cis=freqs_cis, optimized_attention=optimized_attention, past_key_value=past_kv, ) ... comfy.model_prefetch.prefetch_queue_pop(prefetch_queue, x.device, layer, x.dtype, core=core, enable_graph=enable_graph) ``` Graphs can be disabled with `--disable-cuda-graphs` at comfy startup. ### LLama and KV Cache Attention The llama model as used by minimax uses a growing KV cache. The original code does cpu management of the constantly growing-by-one KV cache artifacts however the logical CPU control is incompatible with cuda graphs. This requires a sequence length controllable attention. Comfy-kitchen v 0.2.31 introduces a minimal generic flash attention for bf16 that implments this. The attention length are GPU controlled buffers and their increments are single element tensor ops that are just part of the graph. The fully migrates the geometry control to the GPU and gets the CPU out of the way enabling cuda graphs. ### Minimax AR use of Graphs and layer priorities Minimax AR is a demanding model for AR generation on two levels. The main transformer is a high-layer-rate model in its own right so this is graphed on a block-by-block basis. There is also and audio processing transfomer that runs 7 times per main AR step (so ultimately these layers are 7x the step state). The audio transformer is therefore place at the ultimate priority for the dynamic VRAM engine to load (the new api for declaring prefetch blocks also lets you declare priority). This transformer is prefetched and graphed monolitically as its only 2GB of weights but maximizing layer-rate is critical through this section. # Test results 120s generation (long prompt to overflow AR) https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15570#top `minimax_music3_text_encoder_int8_convrot_pruned.safetensors` `minimax_music3_dit_int8_convrot.safetensors` `minimax_music3_dav.safetensors` ``` System CUDA graphs Total AR DiT DAV ---------------------------------- ----------- ------- ------- ------- ------- RTX 5090 (96 GB RAM) — Linux enabled 87.7s 39.6s 46.0s 2.1s RTX 5090 (96 GB RAM) — Linux disabled 287.5s 238.7s 45.6s 2.0s RTX 5090 (96 GB RAM) — Windows enabled 137.0s 45.3s 86.8s 3.3s RTX 5090 (96 GB RAM) — Windows disabled 562.0s 471.2s 86.1s 3.2s RTX 3060 (48 GB RAM) — Windows enabled 538.8s 142.7s 143.6s 251.9s RTX 3060 (48 GB RAM) — Windows disabled 700.6s 307.1s 143.0s 249.8s RTX 5060 (48 GB RAM) — Windows enabled 1096.2s 913.3s 110.1s 71.8s RTX 5060 (48 GB RAM) — Windows disabled 1090.1s 921.1s 99.4s 68.5s ``` NOTE: the RTX5090 system is also underclocked to 2GHz to emulate slower CPU. _NOTE: The DAV performance on 3060 is under investigation_ Preformance regression tests ``` Platform Workload Current Baseline Change -------- --------- ------- -------- ------ Linux Z-Image 2.75s 2.78s -1.0% Linux Ideogram 10.03s 9.68s +3.6% Windows Z-Image 2.88s 2.98s -3.4% Windows Ideogram 14.62s 14.71s -0.6% ``` General regression tests: Linux, RTX5090, 96GB, 2GHz underclock ``` - MiniMax H3 — completed in 79.09s ✅ - WAN 2.2 — completed in 51.57s ✅ - Stable Cascade → Flux2 — completed in 69.81s ✅ - Ace step turbo 1.5 XL ✅ - LTX2.3 ✅ ``` All outputs human checked ✅

author: olivrg
body:
**Deploy this before the matching data-repo PR.** Widens the loader so both the current dataset and the new one load, which means neither repo's deploy can break the other.

`pnpm build` clean, `pnpm test` 82/82, plus a build against the fixture.

## Why the ordering matters

`lib/incidents.ts` throws on an unusable payload — deliberately, so a bad dataset fails the build rather than deploying an empty page. The revalidation webhook validates upstream before purging and keeps serving stale on failure. So if the data repo shipped first, the site would reject the new payload, the publish step would report the rejection, and `helio.so` would serve the old entries until this landed.

Widening the consumer first removes that window entirely.

## `reversible` becomes a string

The log needs to be able to say **nobody knows**. The inbox-deletion entry has no source addressing whether the deleted mail was recoverable, and recording that as `false` asserts something no one checked. `harm_bearer` and `prevented_by_action_governance` already carry `unclear` for exactly this reason.

**It's a string, not `boolean | "unclear"`, and that's the important call.** `"unclear"` is truthy. This was live in `incident-meta.tsx`:

```tsx
<Row term="Reversible">{incident.reversible ? "Yes" : "No"}</Row>
```

A union would have rendered an unknown as a confident **"Yes"**, and the filter would have folded it in with the genuinely reversible ones — a silently wrong answer in the field that tells a reader how much to trust the entry.

`normalizeReversible` maps `true`/`false` → `yes`/`no` and writes the result back on the entry, so the union lives in one function instead of leaking into every consumer. Unrecognised strings pass through, matching the open-vocabulary contract the other fields already have.

## `tools` may be empty

On an `infrastructure` entry no agent invokes anything. The current data only satisfies the old `minItems: 1` by recording what an RCE *grants*, which was always a stretch.

The site does **not** duplicate the `surface: infrastructure` condition — whether empty is permitted is the log's rule, and re-encoding it here would just be a build failure the next time upstream refines it. Empty renders as an explicit "None — no agent invoked a tool" rather than a blank cell.

## Verification

The fixture now **mixes both encodings on purpose** — strings on three entries, booleans on the rest — because the two repos deploy separately and both shapes have to load. A build against it exercises all four cases at once, and I checked what each actually renders:

| Fixture case | Renders |
| --- | --- |
| `reversible: "unclear"` | Unclear |
| `reversible: true` (legacy) | Yes |
| `reversible: "not_yet_invented_reversible"` | Not yet invented reversible |
| `tools: []` | None — no agent invoked a tool |

The filter facet picks up `Unclear` as its own option rather than collapsing it.

The fixtures README now warns against "tidying" the mixture into one shape, and notes that a boolean-only fixture would pass while still reporting unknowns as Yes.

## Follow-up

Once the data repo has shipped and the dataset carries only strings, the boolean branch in `normalizeReversible` can go — but not before, and there's no hurry.

author: sanele-khoza
body:
Summary
-------
Fixes three related bugs discovered while testing the ratings feature and investigating why new Service Provider accounts couldn't see assigned jobs.

Bug 1: Service Provider registrations never linked to service_providers ------------------------------------------------------------------- Registration only ever inserted into the `users` table. The `service_providers` table (which job assignment and routing actually read from) never got a matching row, so any newly registered provider could log in but would never see jobs — even ones assigned directly to them.

Fix: register() now also creates a service_providers row when role === 'SERVICE_PROVIDER', linked by matching email (the same mechanism resolveProviderId() already used to look providers up in tickets.controller.js).

Added companyName and specialisations as required fields on the registration form, but only when Service Provider is selected as the role, plus matching backend validation in auth.validation.js.

Bug 2: JSON.stringify() used on a native Postgres array column ---------------------------------------------------------------- technicians.repository.js's create() function JSON-stringified the specialisations array before inserting it, producing JSON syntax (["Plumbing"]) instead of Postgres's native array syntax ({Plumbing}). This caused every service_providers insert to fail with "malformed array literal" the moment real data was pushed through it — a pre-existing bug that had never been triggered before because nothing previously called this function with live data.

Fix: pass the array directly; the pg driver handles native array columns correctly without JSON encoding.

Bug 3: Number(id) breaking every admin user-management action ---------------------------------------------------------------- admin.service.js wrapped every user ID in Number(id) before passing it to the database — leftover from before the project migrated user IDs from integers to UUIDs. Number() on a UUID string produces NaN, so approveUser, deactivateUser, reactivateUser, changeRole, and unlockUser were all silently broken.

Fix: removed the Number() conversions; IDs are passed through as-is.

Testing
-------
- Registered a new Service Provider through the real UI end-to-end
- Verified matching rows created in both users and service_providers
- Activated the account, had a Property Manager assign it a ticket
- Confirmed the new provider could see the assigned job (previously impossible — this was the original symptom that led to the investigation)

author: zsombra
body:
Two changes, both archived through the pipeline. The first is the substantial one.

---

## 1. `the-connection-asks-who-it-is` — the delegated OAuth path completes for the first time

**Track `full` · production gate PASS · 22/22 tasks**

BattleGrid is plain OAuth 2.1 — `/.well-known/openid-configuration` is 404 and its authorization-server metadata advertises no `userinfo_endpoint` — so its token response carries no `sub`. `tokenRequest` required one and threw without it, which means **every grant this product was ever issued was refused, and no delegated connection had ever completed** (#203). The throw was a bare `Error`, so it escaped the callback's `catch` and reached the user as a framework error page *after* they had consented.

### What changed

- Identity is established by an **authenticated read performed with the newly granted authority**, not read off the grant.
- `TokenGrant.subject` is **removed**, not made optional — optionality would preserve the false claim that a grant is a plausible identity source, and the next reader would wire to it again.
- A connection whose account cannot be named is refused, stores nothing, and **releases the grant it was just given**. The tokens are live at that moment; dropping them locally is precisely what `DisconnectCommand` exists to refuse. A failed release is a distinct outcome, hedged accurately: the authorization *may* still stand, because a failed revoke is not proof it survived.
- `AccountPort.subjectFor` reports *why* it could not answer instead of flattening every failure to `null`. `OwnerOnlyUser` collapses that at its own call site, where the tolerance actually applies — personal mode is unchanged, including its caching of an unknown.

### The walk found a second defect, and it was ours

The first two live authorizations both refused. The identity read had **never reached BattleGrid** — zero audit rows, and `callTool` audits *before* it attempts.

`callTool` measures authority via `heldScopes.forUser(userId)`, which on a delegated deployment reads the caller's **stored connection**. The identity read runs at the one moment no connection can exist — that is its purpose — so the lookup answered "no authority at all" and the guard refused a call whose grant was holding exactly the scope it wanted. Same key, same tool, one variable:

```
ConnectionScopes (no connection row) -> unreadable: "requires mcp:read authority"
DeclaredScopes(['mcp:read'])         -> subject: 0eccbf37-…
```

`ConnectionScopes` was correct. The scope guard was correct. The call was correct. The defect was in the **composition** — a pre-identity call routed through a post-identity guard.

Fixed with `ToolCallRequest.grantedScopes`: the authority to measure against, for the one call with nowhere to look it up. **Not a bypass** — with an *empty* grant the call is still refused, so a narrower-than-requested grant still fails, which is what the spec requires. Contained by `tests/architecture/granted-scopes.test.ts`, holding that exactly one call site may declare its own authority.

**Nothing offline could have found it.** 2,257 unit tests fake the port; both live probes wire the personal path, whose scopes come from configuration.

### Proven live

```
GET /api/auth/battlegrid/callback?code=…&state=…  307 in 7610ms
GET /agents                                       200
```

Verified in the database rather than from the redirect: `users.battlegrid_subject` = the same account the personal key resolves to, `users.id` a separate local token, connection `active`, scopes `["mcp:read"]`, tokens stored **encrypted**.

---

## 2. `the-two-records-describe-one-server` — two guards that compared the wrong thing

**Track `standard` · 15/15 tasks**

`docs/battlegrid-mcp-capabilities.json` sat at **v17.2.0** while the surface record said **v18.2.0** — a major version apart, hiding **188 output-schema leaves across 11 tools** (#198).

Two guards should have caught it and both read the wrong field:

- The offline check already compared the surface record to the **vocabulary** record, reasoning written out — and hard-coded that pair, so a third record was never covered.
- `refresh_declared` refused only when the files disagreed about *which tools exist*. **v18 added no tools.** The count held at 114, none added, none removed, and it derived a v18 artifact's declared fields from a v17.2.0 dump while both files agreed perfectly about the tool set.

A guard written against *"a count that has not moved proves nothing"* concluded currency from a matching set of names.

Now: a **derived** sweep over every `docs/*.json` that declares a server, reading either `server` or `serverInfo`; `refresh_declared` compares versions before deriving; and the spec's tool-identity rule widened from "the number of tools agreeing with the live server" to any tool-identity comparison against anything. `CLAUDE.md` and `HANDOFF.md` now state what *"nothing a count could see moved"* was scoped to — **inputs** — and that outputs grew unseen.

**The verifier caught the same defect inside the fix**: the new sweep's own failure path had no permanent test, proven only by a mutation run by hand and reverted. `records()` now takes a directory, and four tests drive the refusal against synthetic fixtures — including identical tool sets at different versions.

---

## Gates

`typecheck` · `lint` · **2,264** vitest (172 files) · **255** Python harness · `build` · drizzle schema clean · **85** db tests. `openspec validate --all`: **0 errors**.

Every new guard was mutation-checked — six mutations across the two changes, each confirmed to fail the intended assertion and only it. That mattered here more than usual: the suite these replace was green for the entire life of both defects.

## Issues

**Closed**: #203 (the bug), #91 (keep the delegated path — decided), #206 (a refreshed grant is for the same account — observed), #198 (the record drift).

**Filed and open**: #207 (three live probes can no longer find an evaluation — proven by reachability *not* to be these changes' doing), #208 (`test:db` truncation strands a live grant upstream), #209 (the archiver writes CRLF specs on Windows).

## Two live-environment caveats

- **An orphaned grant is standing at BattleGrid.** A connection created during verification was truncated by `npm run test:db` during the re-audit; its tokens went with the row, so it can no longer be revoked through the product. It needs revoking from the account's own settings. That is #208.
- A delegated connection is deliberately left standing in `grid_commander_test`, with rotated tokens written back.
