author: clubanderson
body:
## Problem

`SweepQueuedAutoMerges` exists on v4 (`v2/pkg/github/automerge_sweep.go`, tests intact) but has **no caller** — the label-queued merge queue silently never runs. v2 drains it every minute from the governor eval loop via `runAutoMergeSweepIfDue` and emits the `automerge-sweep-merged` dashboard audit event; that string is absent from all of v4. v4 only starts the separate `StartSelfAuthoredAutoMergeSweep`, so PRs queued by a human "Approved ... for Hive auto-merge" review + queue label are approved but never landed by the hive.

## Fix (port from v2)

- Add `autoMergeSweepInterval` (1 minute floor) + `runAutoMergeSweepIfDue` to `cmd/hive/main.go` and call it after both `runEvalCycle` sites in the governor loop (startup eval and the ticker tick), matching v2's placement.
- Restore the `automerge-sweep-merged` dashboard audit event emitted for every merge the sweep lands (repo, pr, author, queued_by, label, head_sha, merge_sha).
- Restore `normalizedAutoMergeLabel` and the `cmd/hive/automerge_label_test.go` test deleted in the sync: a blank configured label now resolves eagerly to `github.AutoMergeQueuedLabel` at the `SetAutoMergeLabel` call sites, belt-and-suspenders over the existing config normalization and the `Client.AutoMergeLabel` read-side fallback (which are unchanged), so a partially-populated config can never propagate an unnamed label to a fresh client.

## Security scope

v4's merge-eligibility gating inside the sweep — queue-approval trust (App-authored review, forged-approval rejection, head-SHA binding), check verification, and tier gates — is **untouched**. `pkg/github` has zero edits; this PR only adds the scheduler call and the label normalization in `cmd/hive`.

author: gigurra
body:
## Background / Purpose

The dashboard footer's **Open PRs** indicator (#2215, #2216) hides itself whenever the authored-open count is zero. That makes the one glanceable "what am I waiting on" affordance appear and disappear as the last PR merges, so it is not a fixed place to look. The operator asked for it to be permanent, behind a feature flag (config file + Config tab, default on), and for the popover to also surface recently merged/closed PRs — under their own filter so they never interfere with the open list, and bounded to the last few days rather than all history.

## Implementation

- `dashboard.always_show_open_prs` (`*bool`, default **true**) keeps the indicator mounted at zero open PRs, rendered muted rather than as a live counter; an explicit `false` restores the previous show-only-when-non-empty behaviour. Either way it stays hidden until the daemon has resolved a GitHub identity — a permanent "Open PRs 0" would be a lie with no `gh` login.
- `dashboard.recent_pr_window_days` (`int`, default **3**, max 30, `0` = off) drives a new **Closed Nd** filter listing PRs you merged or closed inside the window. It is a separate list end to end: recent PRs never enter the open list, the footer count, or the attention/unattached tallies, and they are dotted by terminal state (purple merged, red closed) instead of CI state.
- The closed search rides the **same** GraphQL request as the open one via a second aliased `search`, and deliberately asks for no `statusCheckRollup` (CI state on a landed PR is noise and the rollup is the expensive half of the response), so a poll still costs one `gh` call.
- Both knobs resolve when the **snapshot** is built rather than when the cache is written, so toggling them lands on the next 2s dashboard poll instead of the next GitHub search. Narrowing the window applies immediately (the snapshot re-filters to the exact instant); widening it waits for the next poll, and the snapshot advertises the narrower of the two until then.
- Config tab controls (checkbox + days field) with the usual omit-the-default persistence, and `docs/dashboard.md`.

## Tests / verification

- `go test ./pkg/claude/agentd -run 'PR|Config|Dashboard|Snapshot'` — new coverage for the recent-PR decode (terminal state, newest-first, issue-URL rejection, open list untouched), the exact-instant window filter, snapshot-time config resolution, and Config-tab load/save wiring for both knobs.
- `node --test pkg/claude/agentd/jstest/shell-model.test.mjs pkg/claude/agentd/jstest/shell-island.test.mjs` — recent PRs excluded from open tallies, stale `recent` selection falling back when the window is off, the indicator staying mounted (and muted) at zero, and the opt-out hiding it.
- `go test ./pkg/claude/common/config`, `go build ./...`.

body:
## Summary
- Real WSI viewer for whole-slide review in-app (issue #549), backed by a real (not guessed) storage/serving design per KB-17's own named open question.
- Since no `apps/web` UI existed anywhere in the M13 Anatomic Pathology epic, this also ships the minimal case/slide UI needed to actually reach the viewer: `/cases` list, `/cases/:caseId` detail (parts → blocks → slides), per-slide upload/view affordances.
- Scoped to pre-tiled DZI zip upload only (no raw scanner-format decoding — that needs OpenSlide, real infra no scanner/vendor exists yet to size against), synchronous in-request unzip-to-object-storage (no job queue exists yet), a dedicated `whole_slide_image` table (not `image_attachment`'s polymorphic shape), and tile serving via an authenticated-redirect chain (`apps/api` 302 → a new `apps/web` proxy route → a short-lived presigned MinIO URL) — never bytes proxied through either server, never a public bucket.

See `docs/plans/feat-067-wsi-viewer.md` (Status: APPROVED) and both ADRs (lis-engineering repo) for the full reasoning, including alternatives rejected.

- `cases/[caseId]` vs a flat `cases/[id]`: Next.js requires the same dynamic-segment name across sibling routes at the same path depth — crashed the dev server outright at boot.

author: hugo-ccabral
body: Closes #184 ## Problem `window.__parity_vitals` was read in exactly one place in the codebase: inside `capturePage()`, immediately after its own `page.goto()`. Since `inp` only ever populates from real user interactions (never from navigation), and every read happened right after a fresh navigation, `inp` was structurally always `null` — not just in the validation spike, in every command that captures vitals (`audit`, `check`, `e2e`, `journey`, `run`, `vitals`). Parity's own interactive flows (`login.ts`, `cart-interactions.ts`, `purchase-journey.ts`, `spa-navigation.ts`) genuinely click real elements (add-to-cart, minicart open, SPA nav links, login submit) — the collector itself would correctly record those as INP samples — but nothing ever read `window.__parity_vitals` back out before the next `capturePage()` navigated and wiped it. ## Fix - `src/engine/collect.ts`: added `readVitalsSnapshot(page)` — reads `window.__parity_vitals` with no navigation, safe to call mid-flow. `capturePage()`'s own read now calls this too (DRY). Added `mergeInpSnapshot(vitals, snapshot)` — merges only `inp` (taking the max), leaving `lcp`/`cls`/`fcp`/`ttfb` untouched since those are tied to the specific document `capturePage` already read at goto-time; re-reading them later (after an SPA nav swap or reload reinstalled the collector on a new document) would risk misattributing them to the wrong page. - `src/engine/flows/shared.ts`: added `captureInpSnapshot(page, cap)` — the one-liner flow steps call after a real interaction to merge the sampled INP into an already-pushed `PageCapture`. - Wired into the 4 interactive flows at points confirmed safe (a real click happened, with no intervening navigation before the merge): - `spa-navigation.ts` — after the SPA nav click, before the F5-of-destination capture navigates away. - `login.ts` — after `submit-invalid` (steps 2-3 don't navigate away), before `submit-valid`'s expected redirect. - `purchase-journey.ts` — after `open-minicart` (steps 4-7: variant select, add-to-cart, minicart open), before the checkout click risks navigating. - `cart-interactions.ts` — before the persistence-check `page.reload()`, and again at flow end (covers qty +/-, coupon, remove-item, all on the same post-reload document). ## Tests New `tests/engine/collect-vitals-snapshot.test.ts` covers `mergeInpSnapshot` (adopts/keeps/max-wins/never-regresses/only-touches-inp) and `readVitalsSnapshot` (reads via `page.evaluate` without calling `page.goto`, returns `null` on evaluate rejection or missing collector) — all fail without the fix (the exports don't exist yet) and pass with it. ## Checks - `bun run check` (tsc --noEmit): clean - `bun run test` (vitest run): 1001 passed, 3 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change (Windows path-separator mismatches in `baselines.test.ts`, `visual-prompt-builder.test.ts`, `interactive-selector-prompt.test.ts` — none touch vitals/collect/flows) - `bun run lint` (biome): clean --- ## Summary by cubic Samples INP mid-flow and merges it into the current `PageCapture`. Previously INP was always null because we only read `window.__parity_vitals` right after `capturePage()`’s `page.goto`; now flows snapshot after real interactions and merge so INP reflects user input without misattributing other vitals. - Adds `readVitalsSnapshot(page)` and `mergeInpSnapshot(vitals, snapshot)` in `src/engine/collect.ts`; `capturePage()` now uses `readVitalsSnapshot`. - Adds `captureInpSnapshot(page, cap)` in `src/engine/flows/shared.ts` and wires it into `spa-navigation.ts`, `login.ts`, `purchase-journey.ts`, and `cart-interactions.ts` immediately after safe post-click points. - Merges only INP (max-wins). LCP/CLS/FCP/TTFB remain from the original document capture to avoid cross-document attribution. - Adds `tests/engine/collect-vitals-snapshot.test.ts` for snapshot reading and merge behavior. **Rollout** - No public API or config changes. - When adding new interactive flow steps, call `captureInpSnapshot(page, cap)` right after the interaction and before any navigation. Written for commit d8222bd01fdee266164b64c84f4c6b7e0889d030. Summary will update on new commits.

body:
## Summary

Docs only, and narrow: **the justification prose for `docs/38` §7's placement, in the two files that carry it.** The placement itself is correct and does not move; no arc definition, no section ordering and no gate changed.

This corrects prose merged by #773. **No `Closes` keyword** — it closes no issue.

## The defect: a citation with an expiry date

#773 filed `docs/38` §7 — the studio-cleanup boundary — as a new section after §6, and justified that placement partly on **§6 being marked SUPERSEDED**: a current coordination boundary filed inside a superseded section would read as superseded too. That is true today.

**#759 retires it.** That PR re-cuts `docs/38` (its own summary: title, §1 step 3, Arc 4, §6) — it retitles §6, drops the superseded framing, and removes the marker from the doc header. The hunks do not overlap, so **git merges both cleanly and no gate fails.** The prose simply goes on asserting a condition the document no longer supports, with nothing downstream to flag it — the defect class this repo has spent the week eliminating. Cheaper to catch before #759 lands than after.

## The fix: durable ground

> **§6 covers dependencies; §7 covers scope boundaries. Different questions, so different sections.**

That holds regardless of §6's title, framing or supersession status, so #759 can land without disturbing it.

**`docs/38-arcs.md` §7 opener**

- before — `**Current as of 2026-08-13, and outside §6's supersession.**`
- after — `**Current as of 2026-08-13.** §6 covers dependencies; this section covers scope boundaries. Different questions, so different sections.`

**`docs/00-progress.md`, #773's entry, "Placement note for §7"** — the more load-bearing of the two, since the log is what a future reader trusts for reasoning a diff cannot show.

- before — *"It could not go inside §6: the header marks §6 SUPERSEDED as of 2026-08-12, and a current coordination boundary filed inside a superseded section reads as superseded too, which is why §7 opens by saying it is not."*
- after — *"§6 is about **dependencies**; §7 is about **scope boundaries**. Different questions, so different sections — and adjacent ones, so a reader working through what the plan depends on meets what it does not cross next."*

## Four instances, not one

The first pass fixed the named claim and then **reproduced it one gloss over**, which is the part worth reading:

1. **The named defect** — the supersession stamp in §7's opener. Fixed.
2. **The same claim in the progress note**, which additionally quoted §6 *by its current title* (*"the doc's 'what this plan waits on' section"*). #759 changes that too.
3. **The replacement clause itself.** It read *"§6 covers dependencies — what this plan waits on"*. #759 retitles §6 to *"What this plan no longer waits on"* and concludes #252 was never a blocker — so that gloss would not merely go stale, it would be **wrong**, which is worse than the claim it replaced. Both em-dash glosses dropped; the distinction carries itself without them.
4. **A clause about a reader arriving at §6 *"with the blocking question in hand"***, which presumes §6 is about blockers — precisely what #759 changes. **Rephrased rather than cut**, to the plan's dependencies: the adjacency reason is real placement archaeology worth keeping, and #759 removes the blocker, not the dependency question.

The transferable lesson is now recorded in the progress entry: **naming a section by its subject survives a retitle; quoting its title does not.**

## Two judgement calls, made deliberately

**The §6/§7 relationship goes in the doc**, not only in the log. §7's opener already carried a §6 clause (the supersession stamp), so the minimal fix would delete the answer rather than correct it — and `docs/38` is the file a lane reads before picking up an arc, whereas the progress log is not. The placement *record* (why not §2's table, why not an arc body) stays in the log alone.

**Not rebased.** #759 also inserts at the top of `docs/00-progress.md`, so whichever PR merges second takes the top-slot conflict. That resolution is being held on #759; rebasing here would duplicate it.

## Left alone deliberately

- **#773's commit message** repeats the same reasoning. It is immutable history; rewriting merged history to correct a justification is a worse trade than the defect.
- **The `SUPERSEDED` markers** in `docs/38`'s header and §6 are #759's to remove, not this PR's.
- `packages/engine/` and `packages/engine/components/` untouched — component arcs are running there concurrently.

## Gates

All 28 of `ci.yml`'s gate steps run in full — re-run from scratch after the review pass — rather than trimmed on the grounds that this is a docs change. Four of them read prose, and `lint-layout-claims.ts` polices exactly the kind of path claim these files carry. Fresh worktree off `b85d91f` with a real `npm ci`. Working tree clean after the run, apart from the two intended edits.

body:
PR Summary by Qodo

Improve MCP retrieval fallback, add MCP settings UI, and refresh docs 🐞 Bug fix ✨ Enhancement 📝 Documentation 🧪 Tests ⚙️ Configuration changes 🕐 40+ Minutes
AI Description

>
>• Fix passive context retrieval to fall back to keyword search when embeddings fail.
>• Add UI + API to persist MCP retrieval settings and restart MCP with new env.
>• Refresh Olive MCP docs/examples and add Docker + setup guidance for semantic search.
>
Diagram

```mermaid graph TD UI(["SettingsMenu (UI)"]) --> API(["POST /api/mcp/settings"]) --> CFG["Studio config (mcpSettings)"] --> RECON(["reconnectMcpClient()"]) --> MCP(["Olive MCP Server (Python)"]) --> KB[("KB indexes + embeddings")] MCP --> CTX(["get_context_for_pipeline"]) --> KB subgraph Legend direction LR _ui(["UI"]) ~~~ _api(["API route"]) ~~~ _svc(["Service/process"]) ~~~ _db[("Data/index")] end ```
High-Level Assessment

>The following are alternative approaches to this PR:
1. Runtime settings via MCP control endpoint (no restart)
- ➕ Avoids restarting MCP process (no transient unavailable window) - ➕ Settings can be changed more frequently without respawn overhead - ➖ Requires adding a new MCP-side control API and maintaining in-process mutable config - ➖ Harder to guarantee consistent behavior across tools that currently read env at startup
2. Only expose retrieval mode (omit preload toggle)
- ➕ Simpler UI and less restart churn - ➕ Fewer combinations to test/support - ➖ Users can’t address first-query latency without setting env manually - ➖ Less operational flexibility for containerized deployments
3. Treat semantic failures as hard errors (no keyword fallback)
- ➕ Makes retrieval failures explicit and simplifies ranking logic - ➕ Avoids silent semantic-to-keyword quality changes - ➖ Worse UX and breaks callers relying on context injection - ➖ Inconsistent with existing docs/troubleshooting tools that already degrade
>**Recommendation:** The PR’s approach (persist settings, restart MCP with new env, and degrade to keyword on semantic failure) is the best tradeoff for reliability and consistency. Env-driven configuration keeps the MCP server stateless and predictable, while the explicit `status=degraded` + `retrieval` metadata makes quality degradation observable to clients.

## Summary
- add a provider-neutral blind trigger evaluation runner with deterministic opaque suites, strict selector protocol, scoring, and reports
- include trigger corpora and the runner in release artifacts and validate suite preparation in CI
- document the workflow, add 5 focused runner tests, and prepare release v0.6.0

## Validation
- `python scripts/validate_skills.py`
- `python scripts/trigger_evals.py prepare --output .trigger-evals/suite.json`
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` (38 passed)
- `npx skills@1.5.22 add . --list`
- deterministic v0.6.0 release build and checksum verification

## Blind model observations
Two independent Codex selector runs received only the public suite (41 cases; no labels, author reasons, source eval files, or prior reports):
- run A: 35/41, accuracy 85.37%, precision 82.61%, recall 90.48%
- run B: 36/41, accuracy 87.80%, precision 86.36%, recall 90.48%

This PR records those observations without tuning descriptions against the same evaluation sample.

author: marmar9615-cloud
body:
Related: #92884
Focused replacement for #120332 — see *Why This Change Was Made*.

## What Problem This Solves

An operator installs a channel plugin that replaces another one. The Gateway activates the replacement, and `openclaw config validate` then rejects that replacement's own `channels.<id>` config keys. The operator sees a working channel reported as invalid configuration, with no way to satisfy both surfaces at once.

The cause is that two surfaces answered "which plugin owns this channel?" differently. Plugin activation answers it in `shouldSkipPreferredPluginAutoEnable`, which drops any claimant another configured claimant lists in `preferOver`. Channel schema metadata answered it by install origin alone, breaking ties by whichever record the registry happened to iterate last.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair is to make schema ownership resolve the way activation does, rather than to add a special case where the two were observed to differ.

`collectChannelSchemaMetadataWithOwnership` now selects an owner through one explicit priority order, in `decideChannelSchemaOwnership`:

1. **Operator policy.** A plugin that is denied, entry-disabled, or disabled through its channel config never takes a channel from an active claimant, and never keeps one once an active claimant appears.
2. **The declared replacement.** A claimant loses if another active claimant declares it in `preferOver`. Displacement is indexed across the whole registry before any schema is chosen, so a chain of declarations resolves the same way in any registry order.
3. **Install origin.** The closest origin wins once policy and the declaration leave claimants tied.
4. **Registry order**, only when nothing else separates them.

Both the schema pass and the presentation pass call that function, so a channel's label and its fields cannot come from different plugins.

Two callers supply the config-dependent half of that policy through `createConfiguredChannelOwnershipPolicy`: `config validate` and `loadGatewayRuntimeConfigSchema`, which builds the operator-facing Control UI schema. Docs and generated baselines keep the config-independent default, since they describe every declared replacement rather than one operator's setup.

Preference resolution is shared rather than duplicated. `resolveChannelPreferOverIds` reads the installed manifest, then the built-in channel registration, then an external plugin catalog — the same order activation uses — and both candidate discovery and schema ownership call it. Channel-level sources name a channel rather than a plugin, so their declarations are attributed to the claimant that owns the entry instead of to every claimant of that channel.

**Deliberate scope boundaries.**

- Mutual declarations keep the existing last-writer behavior. Two plugins naming each other is a manifest authoring conflict, and inventing a tie-break for it is not needed here.
- An explicitly selected plugin is never displaced. Auto-enable deliberately leaves such a plugin enabled, so both claimants stay active and the runtime falls back to registration order; ownership follows.
- A record that does not list the channel in `record.channels` decides nothing, because activation and the read-only channel facade build claimants from that list alone.

**Relationship to #120332.** That PR fixes this same bug but grew to span Gateway startup, registry lifecycle, alias migration, and doctor work. Review feedback there asked for a narrowed repair. This is that repair, rebuilt on current `main` rather than trimmed down, so it can be judged on its own. #120332 is left open as the integrated version; whichever shape maintainers prefer, the other can be closed.

## User Impact

An operator running a replacement channel plugin gets a `config validate` result that agrees with what the Gateway loaded, and a Control UI config form that offers the fields the active plugin actually reads. Their channel config stops being rejected.

Nothing changes for a setup where one plugin claims a channel, which is every default install.

## Evidence

**Production delta is +1564/−282, net +1282, with tests counted separately at +2392/−15.** That is far above what a bug fix should cost, and `AGENTS.md` defaults bug fixes to net ≤0, so it needs an argument rather than a footnote. The figure grew through review; earlier revisions of this section quoted +593/−136, accurate when written and stale now.

| File | +/− | What it buys |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `channel-config-metadata.ts` | +313/−27 | the displacement rule, and the two claimant gates that share it |
| `plugin-auto-enable.prefer-over.ts` | +257/−36 | shared preference resolution, declaration attribution, catalog snapshot |
| `channel-ownership-policy.ts` | +148/−0 | one place where the two config-aware callers assemble their policy |
| `channel-activation-candidates.ts` | +137/−0 | candidate discovery, split out of the auto-enable module |
| `loader-shared.ts` | +128/−6 | the ceded-channel carrier, its scope and activity filters, the unowned-channel diagnostic |
| `plugin-replacement-eligibility.ts` | +121/−0 | operator-policy predicates, moved out of `plugin-auto-enable.shared.ts` |
| `manifest-plugin-alias.ts` | +69/−0 | alias table extracted from `plugin-registry-id-normalizer.ts` (−48 there) |
| `plugin-auto-enable.shared.ts` | +57/−159 | net negative: predicates and a duplicated precedence chain removed |

`registry-registrars-network.ts` ends at +7/−0. An earlier revision of this branch added a ~50-line arbitration block there and this one deletes it again, so the file the bug lived in is nearly untouched.

Where the growth goes: extractions that are net-neutral across two files, the selection rule itself, and the plumbing that lets validation and the runtime schema share it. I could not find a way to make the two surfaces agree without expressing the agreement somewhere.

**Real behavior proof — two competing channel plugins, real CLI, no mocks.** Two plugin packages are installed through `plugins.load.paths`, both claiming channel `zzproofchat` with mutually exclusive strict schemas. `zzproof-plus` declares `preferOver: ["zzproof-core"]`. Load order puts the replacement first, which is the order that reproduces the bug. The operator config sets the replacement's key:

```json
{ "channels": { "zzproofchat": { "plusToken": "operator-supplied-value" } } }
```

Before, on the merge-base `baf85e6868`:

```
$ openclaw config validate --json
{
  "valid": false,
  "issues": [
    {
      "path": "channels.zzproofchat",
      "message": "invalid config for plugin zzproof-core: must not have additional properties: \"plusToken\""
    }
  ]
}
exit 1

$ openclaw config schema   # channels.zzproofchat token properties
[]
```

After, on this branch:

```
$ openclaw config validate --json
{ "valid": true, ... }
exit 0

$ openclaw config schema   # channels.zzproofchat token properties
{ "plusToken": { "type": "string" } }
```

Validation accepts the active plugin's key, and the Control UI schema offers that same key.

**Control UI, before and after.** The transcript above shows the schema the Control UI consumes; these show the form an operator actually sees. Same gateway config, same route, same clicks, only the head differs.

Setup: a local gateway on an isolated state dir and its own port, with the two plugins installed through `plugins.load.paths`. Each registers a minimal channel using the shape in `src/plugins/loader.test-harness.ts` (`registerChannel`, `listAccountIds`, `resolveAccount`, `outbound.deliveryMode: "direct"`); neither ships a real transport, so nothing is sent anywhere. The channel config is left empty so the same file is valid on both heads. Route: **Settings -> Channels -> ZZProof Chat -> Show advanced**.

Before, on merge-base `baf85e6868` — the form offers **Core Token**, the displaced plugin's field:

![Control UI before: Core Token](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3f409f0f-d380-4cfa-876b-dc220c506d77)

After,

author: cabezadalila
body:
El shop pasa de "coordinamos el pago" a cobrar con tarjeta dentro del sitio, sin redirección.

> **⚠️ Este PR mueve plata.** Abajo están los tres bugs críticos que encontré revisando mi propio código antes de abrirlo, y lo que queda sin cubrir. Léelo antes que el diff.

## Decisión de fondo: Orders API, no `/v1/payments`

Primero elegí `/v1/payments` con el argumento de que combinar Bricks con Orders no estaba documentado. **Ese argumento era falso** — la documentación de Orders dice explícitamente que acepta el token de los bricks. Verificarlo dio vuelta la decisión.

Se usa `POST /v1/orders` porque MP marca `/v1/payments` como **legacy en su propio panel de webhooks**, y no había razón técnica para construir sobre lo viejo. La migración salió barata solo porque no había nada encima todavía.

En el panel de MP el topic a marcar es **Order**, no "Pagos (legacy)".

## Arquitectura: el resto del sistema no habla el idioma de Mercado Pago

```
tipos.ts                vocabulario propio + contrato ProveedorPago
mercadopago-estados.ts  traducción de estados      (puro, testeable)
mercadopago-firma.ts    validación HMAC del webhook (puro, testeable)
mercadopago.ts          cliente HTTP                (plomería)
```

Sumar Mobbex o MODO es implementar `ProveedorPago` en un archivo nuevo. Los mensajes al comprador se escriben una sola vez.

## Los tres bugs que encontré revisando

Los tres habían pasado `tsc`, `eslint`, `next build` y 95 tests.

**1. Un contracargo nunca desmarcaba el pedido.** `esReversion` compara contra estados de MP, pero el webhook le pasaba nuestro vocabulario ya traducido. Siempre daba `false`, así que la plata se iba y el pedido quedaba cobrado para siempre — anulando exactamente la protección escrita para eso.

**2. El reintento con otra tarjeta no podía funcionar.** La clave de idempotencia era constante por pedido. En MP eso significa "te devuelvo la respuesta cacheada", así que un rechazo por fondos quedaba pegado y el botón "Probar de nuevo" era decorativo.

**3. Carrera entre notificaciones simultáneas.** `registrarCobro` leía y escribía sin lock. Si la acreditación y el contracargo llegan juntos, el pedido podía terminar `pagado` con la plata ya devuelta. Se agregó `for update`.

Que 95 tests no atraparan nada de esto es tan grave como los bugs. Se agregaron 12 tests de regresión.

## Reglas que sostienen todo

- **El monto sale del pedido persistido**, nunca del browser.
- **El webhook es la única fuente de verdad.** La URL de retorno se puede escribir a mano en la barra.
- **Nunca se confía en el payload**: trae un id, y el estado se le vuelve a preguntar a MP.
- **Solo `processed` marca cobrado.** Cualquier estado nuevo de MP cae en *pendiente*, nunca en fallido: dar por perdido un pago en curso es cancelarle la compra a alguien que sí pagó.

## El webhook no llegaba al handler

El gate de "Próximamente" devuelve la página con **200** para cualquier ruta. MP habría recibido HTML, lo habría dado por entregado, y ningún pago se habría confirmado — sin error en ningún lado.

Se agregó `RUTAS_PUBLICAS` en `proxy.ts`, evaluada antes del gate y de Clerk. Es una lista explícita, no un patrón: abrir `/api/pagos/*` habría expuesto la ruta de cobro.

## Manejo de rechazos

No se mapean códigos de MP a texto, sino `código → motivo interno → mensaje`. Los motivos son las categorías que cambian **qué le decimos al cliente que haga**.

El botón de reintentar aparece **solo** si conviene: invitar a reintentar con la misma tarjeta cuando el banco pide una llamada solo suma rechazos y baja la tasa de aprobación de la cuenta.

El mensaje de `riesgo` no explica el motivo real — detallar el antifraude es darle un mapa a quien prueba tarjetas robadas. Hay un test que lo verifica.

## Verificación

- **107 tests.** Mutación probada: reintroduciendo los bugs a propósito caen exactamente los tests correspondientes.
- **Webhook end-to-end en el navegador, con el gate activo**: firma válida calculada con el secreto real → 200; la misma alterada en un carácter → 401; `/api/pedidos` sigue detrás del gate.
- **El brick monta** en React 19.2.4 + Next 16.2.9 (riesgo del plan, descartado), en español rioplatense, y trae su propio iframe de fingerprinting — o sea que el device ID para el antifraude no hay que agregarlo a mano.

## Lo que NO entra, y no es olvido

**Dinero en cuenta de Mercado Pago.** Los tipos del SDK dicen que el `amount` del brick aplica a todo *"with exception of Mercado Pago Wallet, which has its processing value determined in backend through the preferenceId"*. Ofrecerlo requiere crear una **preferencia** — otra API distinta de Orders, con su propia forma de notificación. Es una decisión de alcance.

**3DS: falta cerrar el círculo en la UI.** El desafío se renderiza con Status Screen Brick, pero cuando el comprador lo completa la pantalla del checkout no avanza sola — el estado se corrige por webhook. Funciona, pero la experiencia queda a medias.

**Dos pestañas con tarjetas distintas** podrían generar dos cobros: la idempotencia deduplica por token, no por pedido.

**Ubicación de `three_ds_info`** en la respuesta de Orders: asumida en `transactions.payments[0]`, no confirmada en la documentación. El extractor tolera que falte.

## Antes de mergear

- Aplicar la migración `0007` en producción
- Cargar `MP_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_MP_PUBLIC_KEY` y `MP_WEBHOOK_SECRET` de **producción** (hoy solo hay de prueba, y solo en preview)
- Probar con las tarjetas de prueba de MP forzando cada rechazo
- Revisar Deployment Protection en preview: si está activa, MP recibe 401 y el pago queda colgado

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: dea0030
body:
## Description

Closes #1678

The lake access audit trail (the `LakeAccessEvent` model and its `record()` write path) existed but nothing called it - every surface that reads lake content wrote zero audit rows. This PR wires the write path into every retrieval surface: the data-lake API routes (semantic search, articles browse, public browse, sync-delta, single-file fetch), the chat `search_knowledge_base` and `retrieve_knowledge_content` tools, and forced retrieval.

Each write records who read the lake, which lake(s), which files/chunks, and via which surface - never the retrieved content itself. Writes are always best-effort: an audit-write failure never affects the caller's actual search/chat response. The 6 API routes await the write before responding (so it can't be silently dropped by a serverless freeze right after the response is sent); the chat tools and forced retrieval fire it without awaiting, since those run in a long-lived process where the freeze risk doesn't apply and awaiting would only add latency to a response the model/user is actively waiting on.

## Changes

**Shared helpers**

- `attributeAccessedLakeIds` - maps a returned file's tags back to the lake(s) whose `datalake:<slug>` meta-tag it carries. Can optionally fall back to the full authorized/searched scope when nothing in the result set carries a recoverable tag, so a lake is never silently dropped from its own audit trail just because attribution was inconclusive - but only where that's actually sound. The fallback is opt-out (`allowFullScopeFallback: false`) on every surface whose search corpus is mixed (owned + shared + org-shared + lake content together, not lake-only): there, a result with no recoverable tag might be the caller's own private file, and falling back would falsely claim a lake was read. Those surfaces record nothing at all when nothing is attributable, rather than over-claim.
- `recordLakeAccessEvent` - a best-effort wrapper around `record()` (which throws on failure): resolves the platform-configured retention centrally so every call site gets it correctly without having to ask, and logs/swallows any write error rather than propagating it. Returns a promise so a caller can `await` it (see above); the promise itself never rejects.

**New surface values**

- Added `data-lake-articles`, `data-lake-public-browse`, `data-lake-sync-delta`, and `data-lake-file-fallback` to the audit event's surface vocabulary, for the API routes that had no prior surface to record under. `data-lake-file-fallback` is its own value (not reused from `data-lake-articles`) so the two entry points to the same kind of single-file read stay distinguishable in the audit trail.

**Dependency wiring**

- Added an optional `lakeAccessEvents` adapter to the tool/chat `db` context types and wired the real repository into all 5 places that construct that context (the default chat-completion options, the quest and Slack-quest queue handlers, and both the top-level and delegated-subagent paths in the agent executor).

**Instrumented surfaces**

- `POST /api/data-lakes/semantic-search`
- `GET /api/data-lakes/articles` and `GET /api/data-lakes/:id/articles`
- `GET /api/files/:id`'s lake-authorized fallback (serves a curated/shared lake file that isn't directly owned by the caller)
- `GET /api/data-lakes/public`
- `POST /api/data-lakes/compute-sync-delta` (a hash match reveals a file's existence regardless of which conflict-resolution policy then classifies it, so every matched hash is recorded)
- The `search_knowledge_base` chat tool, both its semantic and keyword-fallback arms, and both unscoped and agent-scoped modes
- The `retrieve_knowledge_content` chat tool
- Forced retrieval (the always-on grounding path), attributed to the files actually injected into context, not the wider scanned candidate pool

Every write site skips recording when nothing was actually returned - a zero-hit search or empty browse reflects no lake content read, so no event. A mixed-corpus surface (see `attributeAccessedLakeIds` above) also skips recording when something WAS returned but none of it is attributable to a specific lake - that result may be the caller's own file, not lake content, so there is nothing to record a lake read for.

`rlm-answer`'s own endpoint is not separately instrumented: its retrieval is an HTTP loopback through the now-instrumented semantic-search and articles routes, so recording there too would double-count one user-visible read as two events.

**Also fixed in passing:** the articles browse/search route (`GET /api/data-lakes/articles`) was passing a repeated `?search=` query parameter (which Express hands back as an array) straight into the real search call unnarrowed, corrupting the actual search behavior for that edge case, not just its audit log. Fixed at the source so both the search and its audit entry narrow the same way.

## Guide for Testers

This is a backend-only change with no UI surface of its own, and no in-app view of the resulting data exists yet - this PR writes the audit trail, it does not display it. QA's role here is confirming that normal functionality is unaffected, since the write is a side effect with no visible output to check directly.

1. On your PR preview env, go to `/data-lakes`, open a lake with some indexed content, and use its search box to look up something you expect to match. Expected: results return exactly as before, with no change in behavior, wording, or latency.
2. Start a new chat and ask a question that would draw on that lake's content. Expected: the assistant responds normally, citing sources as before.
3. Ask a follow-up question requesting the full text of one of the cited documents. Expected: the document content is returned as before.
4. Repeat step 1 and 2 with a query that matches nothing in the lake. Expected: a normal "no results" response in both cases, no error.
5. From `/data-lakes`, click **Discover** in the manager panel's footer bar. Expected: the public-lake catalog opens and browsing works exactly as before.

### Regression Checks

- Existing search/chat/retrieval behavior and response payloads are unchanged - this PR only adds a side-effect write, never alters what's returned to the caller.
- Triggering a search/chat call still succeeds normally even if the audit write were to fail - the write is best-effort and must never surface as an error to the end user.
- No new latency or errors on any of the touched surfaces (semantic search, article browse, public browse, sync-delta, chat knowledge-base search/retrieve, forced retrieval).

### What NOT to test

Retrieval ranking, chunking, and citation behavior are unchanged. The correctness of the audit-event content itself (who, which lake, which files/chunks) has no in-app view yet and is covered by the automated test suite, not manual QA in this PR.

## Additional Information

There is currently no way to inspect the written audit events from within the app - that view is separate, planned follow-on work. Until it lands, correctness of the written data is verified by the automated test suite listed below; if a reviewer needs to eyeball a real row, that requires direct database access.

Typecheck clean across the affected packages, lint clean, and ASCII/smart-punctuation guards pass on the full diff. Full test suites pass for the touched packages, including new coverage for every instrumented surface (event shape, attribution/fallback behavior, empty-result no-op, and audit-write-failure resilience).

## Checklist

- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings

an ambiguous one is a question the admin has to answer. Pseudonym-only people are
flagged as unmatchable rather than guessed at. Progress polls while the import runs.

The Type column now says which accounts the directory owns. It keyed off `sso_sub`,
which only exists once someone has signed in, so imported accounts read as "aula"
until their owner first logged in.

Messages for the error codes the backend can return, including cancelling at the
provider and a school already connected to another instance. Several had no message at

author: genestjc
body:
Follow-up to #190, which is already merged — this branch was rebased onto it, so the diff here is the recency work alone.

## The miss

Asked what trading cards Daniel Arsham has done, the agent surfaced a years-old Pokémon collaboration and never mentioned the current Contemporary100 project.

The cause is ranking, not retrieval. Tavily orders by keyword relevance, which has no sense of time — the older project wins because more was written about it — and nothing downstream re-ordered or dated the results, so the model served the top hit as *the* answer.

## Why this isn't a filter

Tavily's `time_range` **excludes** everything outside the window. A "prefer recent" filter would have erased the Pokémon collab before the model ever saw it, when the point is that both belong in front of the reader. So recency is handled as ranking guidance, and the default sends no window at all.

## What changed

- **Dates on every result.** `published_date` is surfaced when Tavily gives it, and explicitly marked `date not given by the source` when it doesn't — an undated old page must never read as current. Unparseable dates are dropped rather than rendered as `Invalid Date`, which the model would treat as a real value.
- **Ordering guidance in the tool result.** Results are ordered by relevance, not date; re-order before answering; lead with the newest thing that answers the question unless the reader pointed at a specific project or era.
- **Disambiguation.** When two genuinely different things match, lead with the recent one, name the other in a clause, and ask which — with the two options as the suggested follow-ups, so it's a tap rather than a typed reply. That hooks into the existing suggestion-chip UI.
- **Optional hard window** (`recency`: `week` / `month` / `year`) for cases where old material is actively wrong — "is the pop-up open this week". Off by default. Since the model fills this argument, an off-enum value falls back to unfiltered instead of forwarding a bogus `time_range` to Tavily.
- **Fixed a formatting bug from #190:** `.filter(Boolean)` was stripping the intentional blank lines between sections, so the block arrived as one wall of text. Sections are now built as discrete blocks.

`max_results` also goes 5 → 6, so competing projects actually have room to appear rather than five links about the same drop.

## Testing

`npm test` — 40/40 pass, 6 new here, built around the Arsham case:

- both eras survive the search, dated, with the lead-and-offer instructions present
- no `time_range` sent by default
- an explicit window is passed through and disclosed in the header
- an off-enum `recency` never reaches Tavily
- undated and unparseable-date results render honestly

Typecheck holds at the same 80 pre-existing errors as `main`, none in touched files.

## One thing I could not verify

Tavily populates `published_date` reliably for `topic: "news"` but only sporadically for general search. The undated path is handled honestly either way, but if dates turn out to be missing too often in real traffic, the next lever is a `topic: "news"` pass for time-sensitive queries. Worth checking against live runs before building it.

author: obenland
body:
## Summary

Spun out of #777: the exactly-once consumption of security scan callbacks, independent of any release-blocking policy. Splitting it out lets #795 (and other consumers of scan results) be based on trunk without carrying #777's policy change.

### What it does

- Consumed callbacks are recorded per `scan_id` under a canonical (key-order-insensitive) digest: an identical scanner retry — including one that re-marshals the same body with a different key order — is acknowledged without repeating effects, where previously a retry arriving after the pending entry was cleared was rejected as an unknown scan.
- A different body for an already-consumed scan is rejected as a conflict (HTTP 409) and recorded for operators.
- A completed verdict supersedes an earlier failure report for the same scan: a failure report keeps the pending entry alive for exactly that reason, and only a completed callback clears it.
- A short per-plugin lock (released even if processing throws) serializes callback processing, so a scanner retry racing a slow first delivery can't double-process or clobber the consumed record. Consumption is recorded after the effects, failing closed: a crash mid-processing makes the retry re-apply the idempotent effects rather than acknowledge effects that never happened.
- Consumed records are pruned after a week; the existing advisory behavior (Slack alert on findings, error recording on failure) is unchanged.

### Testing

`tests/Security_Scan_Consumption_Test.php` (7 tests) covers the identical replay acknowledged without re-running effects, conflict rejection, a re-marshalled retry with different key order, a completed verdict superseding a failure report, the failure report keeping the pending entry, a mismatched version leaving no consumed record, and the per-plugin lock rejecting a concurrent callback without consuming anything. Full plugin-directory suite passes (206 tests); both files lint clean.

author: gjtorikian
body:
The device authorization grant (RFC 8628) was partially implemented, leaving CLIs that follow the spec unable to test it against the emulator (#62).

## What changed

- **Form-encoded bodies now accepted on both endpoints, for every grant.** `/user_management/authorize/device` and `/user_management/authenticate` previously called `parseJsonBody` and rejected `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, which RFC 8628 §3.1/§3.2 require and which is what CLIs send. A new `parseOAuthBody` helper dispatches on `Content-Type` — JSON goes through the existing `parseJsonBody`, form-encoded through `c.req.parseBody()` — and returns the same `Record<string, unknown>` the handlers already index into.
  - This mirrors production, verified against the WorkOS API source: `/user_management/authenticate` accepts both media types on **every** grant (Nest's default `urlencoded` parser is active, and the edge proxy documents both content types for that path), not just `device_code` — even though the docs only show form-encoded for the `device_code` example. Scoping form-encoded to `device_code` alone would be *more restrictive* than production and produce false failures, so the emulator accepts form-encoded everywhere production does.
- **`verification_uri` is now resolvable.** It was hardcoded to the unreachable `http://localhost:0/user_management/authorize/device/verify`. The emulator's `baseUrl` is now threaded into `formatDeviceAuthorization`, so the URL points at the running instance.
- **Verify page served.** Added `GET /user_management/authorize/device/verify` returning a styled HTML confirmation page. Because the emulator auto-approves device authorization with the first seeded user, the page confirms rather than collects a `user_code`, so a CLI that opens `verification_uri` in a browser no longer hits a 404. It is registered as a public path (like the `/user_management/authorize` login page), since a browser cannot send a bearer token.

## Why

Device authorization is the standard grant for CLIs and other input-constrained devices. Without form-encoded support, a spec-compliant CLI couldn't even start the flow against the emulator; and the returned `verification_uri` was both unresolvable and pointed at a route that didn't exist.

Closes #62

author: hobbyiq
body:
> "we aren't using the catalog to search from… it came back with duplicates - leaking from sold comps, we want to show all the potential options in that checklist with auto"
> "we want to search for the checklist and see the comps attached to it. So the checklist feeds the search"

Four defects, all found by running your exact query against prod.

## Before / after

`"2026 bowman Justin gonzalez auto"`

**Before** — four `cardhedge::` vendor rows at the top, every one `comps=0`, duplicates, one auto option.

**After:**
```
0.77  Justin Gonzales  Green Refractor  /99   auto=true   comps=  0
0.77  Justin Gonzales  Base             /250  auto=true   comps=  0
0.57  Justin Gonzales  Base             /-    auto=true   comps= 56  med=$64.66
0.57  Justin Gonzales  Base             /-    auto=false  comps=110  med=$2.13
```

## 1. Selectivity — the root cause

The candidate query ORs every token and takes `TOP 500` **with no ORDER BY**. "bowman" alone matches millions of rows, so the 500 returned are an *arbitrary sample*. Both the vendor-row flood and a later zero-hit result came from this, not from scoring. Same sampling trap as the pricing lookup's `TOP 60`.

Queries now **anchor on the longest alphabetic token** — the surname in essentially every real query — and require it.

## 2. Fuzzy names

You searched "Justin gonzale**z**"; the checklist spells him "Justin Gonzale**s**". The player token is the strongest signal in the scorer, so a one-letter variant dropped his cards below noise.

The SQL anchor matches by prefix with the last two characters dropped (`gonzal`), reaching both spellings; `fuzzyIncludes()` then does bounded edit-distance scoring in memory at **2.5 vs 3.0**, so correct spellings still outrank variants. Diacritics fold first, so `Peña`/`Pena` costs nothing against the edit budget. Tolerance scales with length — a 1-edit window on a 4-letter token would make "Cruz" match "Ruiz".

## 3. Vendor rows were the "duplicates"

`cardhedge::…` rows are mirrors of cards we already hold canonically. They carry the *vendor's* setKey, so they never collapse into their canonical twin — and they outscored it. Canonical `hiq:` rows now win whenever any matched; vendor rows survive only when nothing canonical did, so a card known only through a vendor stays findable.

## 4. Comps never attached

`salesSummary` is written by a batch job, so every freshly-ingested checklist row read `comps=0` — the right cards with no market data behind them. `sold_comps` partitions on `/cardId`, so counting a card's comps is a single-partition query; attaching live for the returned page makes a brand-new checklist card correct immediately.

## Dedup

Collapses to one row per physical identity, built from **fields** rather than ids. Grade variants carry identical identity fields, so a `:psa-10` row could win the tie on score and return the right card with an **empty** market panel — the tie-break prefers ungraded, then canonical, then score.

## Also in this branch

`fix(catalog)` — the checklist ingest hardcoded `parallel="Base"` for every category, so all three of Justin Gonzales's auto sections (plain, Gold Ink, Packfractor) slugged to one id and overwrote each other. Sections are now distinct cards; CPA-JG has its full ladder (SuperFractor /1 … Refractor /499).

It also adds `authoritativeSetKey`: a published checklist knows its own product, so the cardNumber-prefix repair for *untrusted vendor text* must not fire on it. `CPA-AG` is **Adrian Gil** in 2026 Bowman and **Angeibel Gomez** in 2026 Bowman Chrome — forcing both to `bowman-chrome` collapses two players onto one slug. Vendor paths keep the repair that fixed 92,362 mis-slugged rows.

## Known remaining

- Some rows show `parallel: "Base"` with a print run (`/125`, `/250`) — older ingest generations that lost the parallel name. Not addressed here.
- A few `playerName` values carry a trailing comma from an earlier converter pass.

`tsc --noEmit` clean.

body:
## Outcome

Add the first supported synchronous application boundary for adopting an ordinary existing v0.2 SQLite workspace as exact managed generation zero.

This replaces fixture-only bootstrap assumptions with an explicit, versioned, operator-supplied manifest; complete vault and source evidence; read-only legacy-index attestation; immutable receipts; and restart-safe SQLite authority initialization.

## Included scope

- Add `ChangeControlApplication.bootstrap()` and immutable/query-only `get_status()`.
- Add a stable five-part application error taxonomy: usage, review-required, conflict/stale authority, integrity failure, and unsupported operation.
- Bind exact managed SourceNote identity, temporal/authority metadata, governing source bytes, and opaque provenance through a versioned YAML/JSON manifest.
- Adopt explicitly bound external source roots without copying or rerendering the governing source or SourceNote, and without persisting runtime absolute root locators.
- Derive a bounded, closed inventory of every indexable vault note separately from the managed subset; reject all indexing skips.
- Reopen exact PDF source assets and parsed artifacts through the normal projection verifier.
- Attest the existing SQLite index read-only across file identity, schema/migration ledger, embedding configuration, documents, records, FTS, vectors, and deterministic logical contents.
- Add migration 005 for immutable bootstrap intent/inventory/index-readiness receipts, generic generation-zero authority, and typed non-authoritative operator navigation.
- Extract shared generation-resolution logic used by activation and serving.
- Preserve fixture-seeded generation zero and existing managed-review/activation compatibility.

## Safety and recovery properties

- No mutation, rebuild, copy, or rerender of the legacy vault, SourceNotes, raw sources, assets, parsed artifacts, or index.
- Descriptor-pinned no-follow reads; owner/single-link/permission checks; symlink, hardlink, sidecar, inode and path-substitution rejection.
- Live, non-serializable evidence capability retained and revalidated across the authority transaction.
- Exact retry returns identical immutable receipts and authority; different-input operation reuse fails.
- Crashes and lost acknowledgements after every durable stage reconcile synchronously without deletion or rollback.
- Concurrent threads/processes converge on exactly one authority.
- PostgreSQL and unsupported platforms are rejected before managed filesystem or authority effects.
- Operator-run links are navigation only and cannot confer authority.

## Verification

Local verification on exact head `15ab364c6889ed13dc0ca4920294076ad121cc41`:

- CI-matched unit remainder: **1,457 passed, 2 skipped**.
- Integration suite: **131 passed, 66 skipped**.
- Post-refactor affected-consumer/bootstrap suite: **80 passed, 2 skipped**.

- Package/wheel/sdist and migrations 001-005 checks passed.
- Ruff passed.
- mypy passed across 142 source files.
- compileall passed.
- `uv lock --check` and Git diff integrity checks passed.
- Independent scope and safety reviews found no remaining P0/P1 findings.
- A production `run_ingest` integration test proves external source adoption, exact replay, preserved provenance, and unchanged source/vault/manifest/index bytes and inodes.

## Review focus and known risk

This is a large but bounded security-sensitive change. Please focus review on:

- POSIX descriptor/no-follow and inode-stability contracts;
- the migration 004→005 transition and foreign-key restoration;
- legacy-index completeness/fingerprint semantics;
- evidence lifetime across `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` authority initialization;
- exact retry, crash reconciliation, and concurrent initialization.

Authoritative GitHub CI still needs to validate Linux behavior, aggregate coverage, PostgreSQL rejection/compatibility contracts, package artifacts, and evaluation/provenance gates before this leaves draft status.

## Explicitly excluded

- Public change-control/operator CLI.
- Wiring ordinary `search` or `ask` to generation-aware serving.
- Regression-query execution/scoring and final JSON/Markdown audit reports.
- Managed `EDIT` execution.
- PostgreSQL managed bootstrap/generation parity.
- LangGraph expansion and multi-event operation.
- Retention/cleanup, OCR, UI, or background workers.
- Public README marketing, version bump, keyless demo, release, tag, publish, or deployment.

## Delivery impact

Library-level SQLite application/bootstrap capability only. This PR does not release or deploy v0.3.

This pull request adds support for estimating the memory usage of an index (both static and dynamic Vamana) based on the builder configuration and number of vectors, and implements the necessary logic and API functions in the C bindings. It introduces new estimation methods in the C API, adds implementations for memory estimation in the builder and dispatcher classes, and updates data builders to support size estimation for various data types.

**API Additions:**

* Added two new C API functions: `svs_index_builder_estimate_memory` and `svs_index_builder_estimate_memory_dynamic` to estimate the memory usage of an index and a dynamic index, respectively, based on the builder configuration and number of vectors.

**Core Logic and Implementation:**

* Implemented `estimate_memory_breakdown` and `estimate_memory_breakdown_dynamic` methods in the `IndexBuilder` class to provide memory usage estimates for static and dynamic Vamana indexes.
* Added dispatcher functions `dispatch_vamana_memory_estimate` and `dispatch_dynamic_vamana_memory_estimate` to calculate the memory breakdown for static and dynamic Vamana indexes, including graph, data, and metadata sizes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4d0f273362e0b22bbf59bbd72315c7e68b9205b002495c4d063412be95cd1555R132-R154) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f73875f8bbc75a8b601362b974c3ad46ac52582c2b47e5a7ee51538cf2e80933R168-R213)

[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f3ba11abdd57c387a19589945930e35c4fd7593343cd74ce1538771f07228d87R62-R70) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-71f42890738a05fa27b2b395a74c294ed8f00801ed65f35b6e43ca973b53da29R55-R66) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-71f42890738a05fa27b2b395a74c294ed8f00801ed65f35b6e43ca973b53da29R83-R128) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-811943a906bc2b6d50496a4ccb2d9e6ecda932c1b5aba09246bf0e1e0dd36dfeR79-R114) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-610950847add2fb9ebb89679db6f18c3f1d1faa946d98a17bc0e49a972e953d7R60-R71)

[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2a806c2239ebfd77eed3295a2743eb29dc6a0cfcc2fbf20869b308e5fef09f8aR22-R29) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-811943a906bc2b6d50496a4ccb2d9e6ecda932c1b5aba09246bf0e1e0dd36dfeR22) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-037b3945d8fbb9964a2256d45e1ec3b2e30094386fced7aa1b0a5221a0ebbe37R52-R60) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-01f5ea0310e9f6043dab966b4c54aa16248bd69ca55e155a22ef800b45211aa9R47-R54) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-6fb5101eb6123f74dd77171edbe4a686fa1fd9f963c9d450f100538ec07f6ac8R21) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-6fb5101eb6123f74dd77171edbe4a686fa1fd9f963c9d450f100538ec07f6ac8R33-R34)

These changes collectively provide a robust mechanism for clients to estimate index memory requirements before actually building an index, improving usability and resource planning.

author: davidscotttufts
body:
I wrote that the four remaining open RFCs were *"gated on external parties — none is mine to close."* **That was wrong for 0038.**

Three of its five acceptance criteria were **unticked repo work needing no external party**:

| Criterion | Reality |
|---|---|
| `docs/working-group/` directory created | **genuinely missing** |
| `GOVERNANCE.md` forward-pointer | **done, but unticked** |
| CHANGELOG entry | **done, but unticked** |

**An RFC parked on an external condition and an RFC parked on unfinished work look identical from the outside.** This one looked like the second while being the first.

## The new directory

`docs/working-group/README.md` says in its **first line** that nothing in it is operative. It records the three tripwire conditions against their status today and names **condition 1 — three independent organizations with a maintainer — as the binding one**, since lazy consensus among one person is not consensus.

It also states what it is **not**: evidence of a working group, a steering committee, or multi-organization governance. That would be exactly the class of claim **RFC 0147 §A bans**.

## All five criteria met, and the status stays `Draft`

Not a contradiction. **§E ties promotion to an external tripwire, not to this checklist** — and `Active` would suggest a governance model somebody is following, when there is nobody to follow it yet.

What was closable here was the *work*. What remains is a count of independent organizations, which no amount of repository work produces.

## A bare box misleads in both directions

RFC 0111 carries a **ticked** box whose prose says "not yet." These carried **unticked** boxes whose work was done. Both cost a reader the same re-derivation. The same fix landed on RFC 0035's `Spec text merged (this file)`, unticked since 2026-05-21 while self-evidently true.

- `npm run openwop:check` green.

**Thirteenth check; seventh defect in a claim of my own** — this time the claim that there was nothing left of mine to do.

🟡 **Live preview: [pr-16096.preview.langfuse.com](https://pr-16096.preview.langfuse.com)** ## What does this PR do? > Stacked on the two PRs below it. The one directly beneath makes the worker record *why* a PostHog export was disabled; this one shows it. When a configuration fault auto-disables the PostHog export, the worker records the reason. Nothing rendered it. The settings page read only the sync timestamp, and that block was gated on the integration being enabled — which it no longer is once the fault disables it. So the section disappeared exactly when it finally had something to say, leaving a one-time email as the admin's only explanation. Adds a status section mirroring the blob storage one: - A destructive alert carrying the recorded fault and its timestamp, shown whether or not the integration is still enabled. - The status badge now reads as an error rather than merely inactive. - The sync line is no longer gated on `enabled` (matching blob storage), so a manually disabled integration doesn't render an empty status section. **On the alert title.** A fault is usually terminal and the integration is off, so the copy asks for action. But a fault can also be recorded *without* disabling — when the host changed under a running job, the disable is skipped after the error was already persisted — and there the export is still live. A single "export disabled" title would misinform in that case, so the title distinguishes the two states. Extracted as a component rather than inlined in the page, matching the blob storage layout and making it testable from plain props; there are no page-level client tests in this area to extend. Full parity with blob's status model is not attempted. Its six-state derivation depends on `nextSyncAt`/`runStartedAt` columns that the PostHog integration deliberately doesn't have. ## Type of change - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) ## Mandatory Tasks - [x] Make sure you have self-reviewed the code. body:
### Motivation

- Define a reusable, versioned CSV contract and validation for hydrology inputs so downstream components can rely on canonical columns and QC rules.
- Improve scientific training plumbing by adding chronological train/validation/test splits and explicit normalization/scaling that is fitted on the training partition.
- Make standalone physics-only runs explicit and safer by introducing a dedicated `PINNWrapper` and clearer physics residual APIs. 
- Add small utilities and tests to verify units, dataset loading, scaling, metrics, and core scientific helpers.

### Description

- Introduce a dataset contract and validator via `Hydro/dataset/hydro_dataset_contract.{h,cpp}` with `HydroDatasetContract` profiles `rainfallRunoffV1` and `waterBalanceV1` and `HydroDatasetValidator::validateCsv`.
- Implement CSV observation loader `DDRRLoader` (`ddrr_loader.{h,cpp}`) that validates the CSV, parses canonical UTC timestamps, computes per-catchment elapsed hours, converts discharge to depth-rate using `hydro_units.h`, and preserves optional `storage`.
- Add deterministic chronological partitioning with `chronological_split.h` and use it to reserve a validation fraction in the wrappers; expose `validation_split_ratio` in `HydroRunConfig`.
- Add `TensorScaler` (`tensor_scaler.h`) and integrate training-only normalization into `FFNWrapper`, `LSTMNetworkWrapper`, and `FFNPINNWrapper` with inverse transforms for test/plotting outputs.
- Add hydrology-specific evaluation helpers in `evaluation/hydro_metrics.h` and compute/store more metrics (`validation_mse`, `rmse`, `mae`, `nse`, `pbias`, `physics_loss`) in `HydroRunResult`.
- Add explicit physics-only `PINNWrapper` and update UI/dispatch to use it; update `FFNPINNWrapper` and LSTM PINN logic to reject normalization for physics-informed residuals until appropriate inverse-transform plumbing is available.
- Extend physics API in `rr_physics` with `waterBalanceResidualAtTimes` and ensure timestamps are strictly increasing when used.
- Update UI text and GA logging in `hydropinnwindow.cpp` to reflect the chronological split, validation reporting, PINN backend change, and validation-mse selection for GA.
- Add documentation files: `DATASET_CONTRACT.md` and `GISTOOHQ_PIPELINE.md`, plus small README updates and project file (`HydroPINN.pro`) entries for the new sources/headers.
- Add unit tests and run scripts under `Hydro/tests/` for dataset contract, loader, units, tensor scaler, and scientific core checks.

### Testing

- Added test binaries and shell runners: `run_dataset_contract_test.sh`, `run_ddrr_loader_test.sh`, `run_hydro_units_test.sh`, `run_tensor_scaler_test.sh`, and `run_scientific_core_test.sh` that compile and exercise the new components.
- Executed `dataset_contract_test`, `ddrr_loader_test`, `hydro_units_test`, and `scientific_core_test` and they passed (validate/parse/chronological-split/metrics behaviors).
- `tensor_scaler_test` is included and runs where LibTorch headers/libraries are available; the test is skipped when LibTorch is not present and passes when executed in an environment with `LIBTORCH_PATH` configured.

author: jimmy058910
body:
fix(scan): stop per_tool flags overriding the flags JMo must own

Closes #822

`per_tool.<tool>.flags` was spliced into the argv **after** JMo's own flags, and
a scalar flag is last-one-wins. So a config entry could take over the flags the
adapter contract depends on -- where the tool writes, and in what format:

    per_tool:
      trivy:
        flags: ["-f", "table"]

trivy then wrote a *table* into `trivy.json`. The file existed, so the tool
graded `success`; the adapter could not read it; the run exited 0. Measured on
one target, same tool, only the flag differing:

    without the flag:  2 findings, rc=0
    with the flag:     0 findings, rc=0, zero errors logged

Now, on the same reproduction, both configurations report **2 findings**, and the
second says what it ignored:

    WARN  Ignoring 2 flag(s) for trivy that JMo must control -- they decide
          where it writes and in what format, and the report phase cannot read
          the output otherwise: -f table

## Chosen approach, and what was rejected

Warn-and-drop, matching the precedent `filter_trivy_flags` already set in this
module. Considered and rejected:

- **Reordering so JMo's flags come last.** Cheapest, but it converts silent
  *destruction* into a silent *no-op* -- still silent, the #807 class. And flag
  position is not uniformly safe to change: several invocations put the target
  as a trailing positional.
- **Hard-erroring.** Breaks working configs on upgrade and conveys nothing a
  warning does not.

The reserved set is **derived from what the scanners actually pass**, not
guessed:

    git grep -oE '"(-o|--output|-f|--format|...)"' scripts/cli/scan_jobs/

and is deliberately narrow: only the flags that decide whether the output is
readable at all. Repeatable flags are **not** policed -- `--scanners` unions
rather than replaces (measured against trivy 0.70.0), and dropping a legitimate
repeated `--exclude` would break working configs.

**A dropped flag takes its value with it.** Reducing `["-f", "table"]` to
`["table"]` would leave a bare word in the argv, and trivy reads a bare word as a
scan target -- strictly worse than the collision being fixed. `--format=table`
is handled too, where the value is not a separate token.

## Consolidating five copies, which found a second bug

`get_tool_flags` and `get_tool_timeout` existed as **five identical copies**, one
per scanner. A filter added without consolidating would have had five homes and
got none -- the #808 shape, and why #803/#807 existed.

Moving them to `scan_utils.py` exposed a real divergence: only
`repository_scanner`'s `get_tool_timeout` applied the `TOOL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULTS`
floor, because that table was **defined in that module** and the other four could
not see it. `zap` carries a 900 s floor and also runs on `url` targets:

    balanced URL scan:  zap got 600 s, floor says 900 s   <- 300 s short
    balanced repo scan: zap got 900 s

A third of its budget, on a DAST tool, depending only on which target type it
was attached to. `TOOL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULTS` now lives in `scan_utils.py` and is
re-exported from `repository_scanner` for readers that use that name.

The call sites are untouched: the local closure names stay and delegate, so the
diff is the definitions rather than ~30 invocations.

## Guards

`tests/unit/test_per_tool_flag_policy.py`. The one worth calling out asserts a
**property, not a name**: any `get_tool_flags`/`get_tool_timeout` under
`scan_jobs/` that reads `per_tool_config` directly has grown its own copy again.
It also asserts it inspected at least 8 helpers, so it cannot quietly stop
covering anything -- the "assert the property, not the pattern" lesson from the
encoding drift guard, which was walked around twice by exactly that failure.

Every guard mutation-tested against file backups.

author: nmorabowen
body:
## The defect

A plane-strain model built from `LadrunoLST` — the fork's recommended quadratic triangle for near-incompressible plane-strain plasticity, i.e. exactly where σ_zz carries the most weight — rendered wrong von Mises, principal, and mean stresses **with no warning**. `results/_plane_recovery.py` recognized only `LadrunoQuad` and `LadrunoCST`, so `plane="auto"` failed to classify the model, σ_zz fell back to `0` instead of `ν(σ_xx + σ_yy)`, and the contour path exposed no `plane=` override to correct it downstream.

Reported from the Cerro Lindo SSI program (ADR-0005 rung M4), whose `m4_render.py` works around it by computing plane-strain von Mises by hand. The defect specifically punishes users following the fork's own element guidance.

## The fix

**1 — The missing tokens.** `LadrunoLST` joins the flag-style 2-D set (its arg layout is byte-identical to `LadrunoCST`). Audit of the rest:

| token | verdict |
|---|---|
| `tri6n` / `SixNodeTri`, `BezierTri6` | already covered by `_POSITIONAL_PLANE_ELEMENTS` |
| `SSPquad` | not applicable — no typed primitive emits it (deferred, `element/solid.py:37`) |
| **`LadrunoUP`** | **one more real gap.** Its 2-D shapes are plane strain by construction (no `-type` flag exists). The token spans 2-D and 3-D, so the per-axis permeability count (`-perm` / `-permH`) is read as its dimensional witness. Same silent-wrong-answer for effective-stress geotech. |

**2 — Silence was the actual defect.** An element the recovery cannot classify — or one whose material Poisson's ratio it cannot read — now raises `OutOfPlaneRecoveryWarning`, exported from `apeGmsh.results` so it is filterable, naming the offending `type_token` and the fix. An element correctly recovered as zero (plane stress for σ, plane strain for ε) is **not** reported: that zero is exact. Deduped per situation, because the viewer re-reads every frame.

Critically it fires *before* the `if not pmap: return False` bail-out — an all-`LadrunoLST` model resolves an empty map, which was precisely the case that said nothing.

**3 — Auto-detection is no longer the only word.** `ContourStyle` gains `plane=` / `nu=` (honored on `topology="gauss"`, mirroring the pair `PrincipalGlyphStyle` already had), and `results.plot.contour(...)` gains the same — both already existed on `results.elements.gauss.get`.

One trap worth naming: the viewer's visual store caches a float16 slab **and** the global colour range per `(stage, component)`, shared across diagrams, read with the default recovery. An overriding contour therefore bypasses the store on all three surfaces (pre-warm, per-step subslab, initial clim) and re-reads per step — otherwise you'd set `plane="strain"` and get auto-plane pixels back.

## Tests

8 new: LST classification both ways, `LadrunoUP` 2-D vs 3-D, the warning naming the token, the ν-unreadable warning, no-warning-when-zero-is-exact, once-per-situation dedup, plus an end-to-end contour check (uniaxial σ_xx: auto gives `|S|`, `plane="strain", nu=0.3` gives `|S|·√0.79`) and the store bypass.

author: wittjosiah
body:
## Problem

Follow-up to #12565, one layer down. `Obj/atoms.ts` documents *"Uses object reference as key — same object returns same atom"* but keys through `Atom.family`, i.e. a `MutableHashMap` keyed by Effect's `Hash`/`Equal`. Only `Ref` implemented the traits ([`ref.ts:636`](https://github.com/dxos/dxos/blob/main/packages/core/echo/echo/src/internal/Ref/ref.ts#L636)); entities did not, so Effect fell back to `Hash.structure`:

```js
// Hash.hash — no trait → structural
const h = withVisitedTracking(self, () => structure(self))
hashCache.set(self, h)                       // ← cached by reference, forever
```

Two consequences for an entity:

1. **Every hash deep-reads the record** — own keys, then each nested record, array and ref, recursively.
2. **The digest is cached and then goes stale.** Effect's own docstring says as much: *"For mutable objects, implement a custom `Hash` interface that hashes the object reference rather than its content."* An ECHO object is mutable by definition, so the family's key stops describing the object after the first `Obj.update`.

Nested records were worse than stale — they were *conflated*. `compareRecords` is not prototype-gated, so two structurally identical sub-records of two unrelated objects compared equal.

## Fix

`Hash`/`Equal` accessors on `TypedObjectPrototype`, keyed by entity `id`. Objects and relations both route through that prototype, so one insertion point covers both, and the file's own comment already places the ECHO system surface there "rather than as branches in the `get` trap". Entities are Proxies, so these are accessors returning functions, not plain methods.

**Keyed by the bare `id`, not the DXN.** `getObjectEchoUri` throws on a malformed id — a hash trait that can throw reinstates the class of bug #12565 fixed. `id` is a plain data property with no invariant behind it. ECHO ids are ULIDs, so DXN's cross-space precision buys nothing, and collisions are legal anyway — `Equal` decides.

**Both traits ship together.** A `Hash` that disagrees with `Equal` silently breaks every `MutableHashMap` lookup.

Nested records carry no `id` and fall back to reference identity (`Hash.random` / raw-target comparison) rather than to structural comparison.

## Id identity is the entity invariant, spelled cheaply

An entity has exactly one live proxy: `createProxy` caches by target, `EchoDatabase.getObjectById` hands back `core.rootProxy`, and `initEchoReactiveObjectRootProxy` asserts `!core.rootProxy`. **Two live proxies over one entity is a bug**, not a supported way to hold two views.

So id identity and reference identity coincide in normal use, and keying by `id` is simply the throw-free, mutation-stable way to write the invariant down. The two only diverge once the invariant is already broken — and there the pair keeps both proxies as a single hash-map entry instead of letting two atoms race over one entity. `clone(…, { retainId: true })` yields such a duplicate only because the copy is destined for a *different* database; the tests use it to fabricate the forbidden state deliberately.

## Behaviour change

`Equal.equals` on an in-memory entity is now id identity, process-wide:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Distinct entities, identical contents | `false` (`id` is an own key, so the structural digests differed) | `false` |
| Nested records of two different objects, identical contents | **`true`** | `false` |
| Any entity, after mutation | digest cached from first read | unchanged — `id` is immutable |
| Duplicate proxies over one entity (invariant violation) | `false` once contents diverge | `true` — one hash-map entry |

No fallout in the suites below; nothing relied on the structural comparison.

## Scope

**In:** in-memory objects and relations.

**Out — already handled:** database-backed roots. `initEchoReactiveObjectRootProxy` marks every root proxy `Equal.byReferenceUnsafe`, which short-circuits ahead of `isHash` in both `Hash.hash` and `Equal.equals`. Traits on `EchoRoot` would be dead code. Reference identity there enforces the same one-proxy-per-entity rule from the other direction, and `proxy-identity.test.ts` pins the case that motivated it: a branch binding and the live object must stay distinct atom-family keys.

**Out — needs its own mechanism:** types/schemas. `getObjectEchoUri` rejects them outright, `Entity.Unknown` is objects + relations only, and class-declaration type entities are functions.

## Test plan

New `entity-hash.test.ts`. **6 of its 11 cases fail without the change** — the direct contract (`Hash.isHash` false → `Hash.hash(obj) !== Hash.hash(obj.id)`), the nested-record conflation, relations, and the duplicate-proxy cases:

```
× objects implement both traits
× hash is derived from the id, not the contents
× a duplicate proxy (invariant violation) still resolves to one entity
× relations implement both traits
× nested records fall back to reference identity
× a family keyed directly by an entity round-trips
  Tests  6 failed | 5 passed (11)
```

With the change:

```
echo              569 passed |  9 skipped (34 files)
echo-client       522 passed |  7 expected fail | 12 skipped | 2 todo
app-graph         151 passed
plugin-space       54 passed |  3 todo
plugin-client      15 passed |  2 skipped | 2 todo
echo:build        clean       echo:lint  clean       oxfmt  clean
```

Not stacked on #12565 in the end — zero file overlap, and this branch is already past that PR's base on `main`.

Changeset: `@dxos/echo` `minor` (Group A) — the `Equal` change is consumer-breaking, and pre-1.0 breaking rides the minor.
