author: smdurgan
body:
## Summary

Rehearsing card 18 on the pilot 2026-08-12 produced a good demand draft: specials traced, the settlement figure reserved behind `{{FILL}}` markers, a privilege wall around the firm-prepared chronology built unasked. **It was filed as a `.txt`, because there was nowhere else for it to go.**

`render_docx_template` is the only .docx path and it is a **template** renderer. Its gate refuses case content for a sound reason — *"content that reaches a template reaches every future matter the template is filled for"* — and a filled demand letter is case content top to bottom. So the one artifact the firm most needs in Word was the one artifact that could not be rendered.

## The sibling, with the gate inverted

Same docx builder, same two-stage upload.

| rule | template | draft |
| --- | --- | --- |
| case content (dates, figures, identifiers) | refused | **required — it is the letter** |
| `{{FILL:}}` / `{{NOT IN RECORD:}}` / `{{ATTORNEY:}}` | refused | **preserved, rendered visibly** |
| malformed marker syntax | refused | refused |
| em dash | refused | refused **outside quoted passages** |
| HTML comment | refused | refused |

Case content is not refused here because refusing it would not add a control. Every figure is already bound to trace to a source by rules enforced elsewhere: the drafting discipline's ten mechanical gates, the A1 identifier provenance gate, and the skill's own *"name the source in the same sentence"*.

## The em-dash carve-out is decided, not discovered

House style bans em dashes; the drafting checker requires quotations to appear **verbatim** in a source. A medical record whose quoted words contain an em dash can satisfy only one of those, and the two ways out are to misquote the record or drop the quote. Both are worse than a dash. **The quote wins: house style governs our prose, never the record's words.**

Bounded to closed quotation spans, straight and curly. An unterminated quote exempts nothing — the same fail-toward-refusing choice the marker scanner already makes.

## 27 tests, and most are pairs

The same input accepted by one gate and refused by the other. That pairing is the contract: **if the two gates ever agree about case content, one of them is wrong**, and `test_the_same_draft_is_refused_by_the_TEMPLATE_gate` is what says so.

Marker preservation is verified by reading the rendered .docx back through `extract._docx_text` — the same extractor `read_document` uses — so it asserts what the attorney would actually see, not what the renderer intended.

## The conformance oracle did its job

It caught the unclassified tool immediately: *"live tools ['render_docx_draft'] are neither classified nor listed as expected-unclassified — they would fall through to the fail-closed default at runtime."* `manifest.toml` `tool_classes` and the conformance expectations now carry the entry.

## Test plan

- [x] Smokeball connector suite **221 passed** in the CI-shaped per-connector venv
- [x] `npm run verify` exit 0
- [x] Overlay half **merged**: hermes-smd-overlay#266 maps `mcp_smokeball_render_docx_draft` → `INTERNAL_WRITE`, mutation-tested
- [ ] **(runtime)** The tool is UNREACHABLE on any seat until an `OVERLAY_REF` bump + reprovision — the fail-closed direction. Card 18 on the pre-suit matter is the proof, and it goes on #2258 with its verify id.

Refs #2258

author: n-drobyshevski
body:
## Why

`gas_ai` already queried `issuesV2`, but the step was built from an older, **project-scoped** capture (`exemples/toxic_combos_request.js`). Measured against the console's own **Risk Issues** view — *Wiz for Risk Assessment → AI Security*, tenant-wide, **98 issues** (0 critical / 0 high / 88 medium / 10 low) — the register was under-reporting in three independent ways, none of which left a mark on the page.

That capture is now archived as `exemples/risk_issues_{request,response}.js` and is the ground truth for this step.

## The three under-counts

**1. Wrong category filter.** `riskEqualsAny: [wct-id-1998]` → `frameworkCategory: [wct-id-1998]`. `wct-id-1998` is a *framework-category* id, and the sibling `aiConfigFindingsVariables` already passed it that way. Both filters work against this tenant — different axes that happen to accept the same id — but only one matches what an analyst sees.

**2. `IN_PROGRESS` was collected and never counted.** The query has always asked for `OPEN` *and* `IN_PROGRESS`; **seven** readers then discarded the second with `status === "OPEN"` (`api.openIssues`, `comboSummary`, `comboDigest`, `graphEnrich` ×2, `graphApiParams`, `syncStore`). Those issues reached `ai_issues` and were counted by nothing. Now one `UNRESOLVED_ISSUE_STATUSES` in `config.ts`, used by all of them. (`normalizeConfigFindingsPage` keeps its own filter — findings have no in-progress state.)

**3. The issue-type filter hid a whole class — caught during review of this PR.** The first pass replaced one narrow filter with a slightly wider one: `type: ["CLOUD_CONFIGURATION", "TOXIC_COMBINATION"]`. That matched **91** of the tenant's 98. The 7 it dropped were every **threat detection** in the category, and the shortfall was visible only because it landed entirely on one severity:

| | Wiz (Type chip inactive) | with the type filter |
|---|---|---|
| Medium | 88 | 88 ✓ |
| Low | 10 | 3 |

A dropped-row bug scatters across severities; an excluded *class* lands on one. **The type filter is now gone entirely** — the category is the scope, and the issue type is Wiz's taxonomy of *how* an issue was produced, which this register has no business asserting on. The console's own 98 isn't type-filtered either.

**Unmodelled rules also vanished.** `comboSummary` did `if (!bucket) continue`, so an issue whose source rule isn't one of the four was dropped — as would every issue in a group someone renamed. They now fall back to **Other AI risk**, and `sum(counts) === unresolved issues` is an invariant with a test. `comboDigest` separately built its cards from `COMBO_GROUPS` rather than the summaries it had just computed, so a fifth bucket would have been counted and then never rendered.

## Design notes worth reviewing

- **Other AI risk lives *outside* `COMBO_GROUPS`, deliberately.** `syncJobs.syncSteps()` maps that array into per-rule `ISSUES_<ruleId>` fallback steps via `Q_RULE_ASSETS`; a member there would generate a step querying `ruleIds: [""]`. Exported separately, joined in `REGISTER_GROUPS`.
- **It declares no amplifier**, so its card shows the severity mix it actually *holds* rather than a shift badge, and states that Wiz's rating is carried through unchanged. `comboSummary` computes its severity from content — a declared `UNKNOWN` would bury a genuinely critical unclassified issue at the bottom of a page ranked worst-first.
- **`Q_ISSUES` spreads `... on CloudEventRule`.** That's the shape a threat detection's source rule takes; without it the element returns `{}` and those issues arrive real, counted, and **nameless**. The issue sheet also falls back to the issue-type label for a heading, so a rule shape no fragment covers still gets a title instead of a blank one — without inventing a rule name.
- **The thin `GNode` stays minimal, and that is load-bearing.** `mergeParts` merges field-wise on any truthy value and `ISSUES_TOXIC` runs *after* `INVENTORY_AI`, so `entitySnapshot.tags`/`status` set there would overwrite fresher inventory data with a point-in-time snapshot. Both ride on the `IssueRow` instead.
- **The ignore expiry is read off `rejectionExpiredAt`.** The `Ignored until: Feb 1, 2026` inside the note prose is deliberately not parsed — that note is free text a human typed.
- **`filterBy.type` is editable but not `required`**: with no default to empty, `[]` and absent both mean "every type", so rejecting one would be incoherent. It remains available as a *narrowing* knob, with help text saying that narrowing is exactly what hid the threat detections. **`filterBy.frameworkCategory` is locked**, reason shown in the panel: nothing in a response says an issue is an AI issue, so the category filter *is* that claim, and widening it would relabel the register rather than extend it. A test asserts a stored override can't displace it.

## Lifecycle fields

The capture proves a set of fields the register never selected — what lets it talk about *remediation* rather than only exposure: `resolvedAt` / `resolutionReason` / `resolvedBy`, the accepted-risk note and its expiry, `serviceTickets`, `assignee`, `environments`, `validatedAsExploitable`, entity `status` / `subscriptionId`, and Wiz's own `aiRemediationAnalysis` verdict.

These land on `IssueRow`, on **16 appended `ai_issues` columns**, and in the issue sheet. No `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump: `ensureHeaders` appends declared-but-missing headers on the next write, so existing ledgers self-heal with no migration — and the constant has zero readers today. `rowToIssue` maps a legacy `combo_group: ""` to the Other bucket so pre-existing rows stop being invisible.

## Numbers that move — all verified, none guessed

- Seed **29 → 32** issues (3 in Other AI risk, 1 in progress) so the dry-run demo isn't an empty card
- `digest.totalOpen` **29 → 32**; new `unclassified` and `inProgress` totals
- `reRated` is now a real **29-of-32** ratio; it used to equal the total because every counted issue was a modelled pattern
- `agent-e` AARS **62 → 66** from the multi-issue factor — the only asset that moves
- **The AARS severity distribution does not move**, so `SEED_TREND`'s last point still lands exactly on the estate the seed produces (checked, not assumed)
- **Pillar B is untouched**: unmodelled issues carry no framework codes, so no asset is re-priced through a path this PR can't account for
- Dropping the type filter moves **no snapshot but `Q_ISSUES`** — the seed is unchanged and the filter only governs a live sync

## Verification

`npm run check` green — **670 tests**, typecheck clean, build through both the middlebox and `entry.js` drift guards. The `apiGolden` snapshot diff was reviewed line by line and is fully attributable to the above.

Driven in a browser against the dev harness (no console errors): the KPI reads **32 — 29 re-rated · 3 outside the four patterns · 1 in progress**; the Other card renders its mix badge and no amplifier claim; the issue sheet shows Accepted risk / Tickets / Wiz AI analysis on the rows that carry them; the Wiz Scans panel shows the effective filter as `status` + `frameworkCategory` and nothing else.

## What to expect on the first live sync

The register should land on **98**, with the 7 threat detections appearing in Other AI risk at their Wiz severity. If it lands on 91, then `THREAT_DETECTION` wasn't the whole story and the remaining gap is `normalizeIssuesPage` skipping rows with no `entitySnapshot.id` — the Scans page test run separates those two cleanly via `totalCount` vs `normalized.issues`.

## Follow-up, deliberately not in this PR

`aiRemediationAnalysis` is an AI-analysis join and `ISSUES_TOXIC` is an `optional` step, so a timeout would **skip the whole register silently** rather than fail loudly. It's commented as the first line to delete, and the first live sync should confirm via `wizDiagnostic()` that the step isn't in the skipped list. A degraded-query fallback ladder is the obvious next step.

body:
Closes #199.

Formalizes CLRS fourth-edition §32.5 (suffix arrays) as a native section.

- `suffixAt` / `suffixLe`: the suffix order (lexicographic with ties broken by starting index), proved decidable, total, and transitive.
- `SuffixArrayValid`: the validity predicate — a permutation of the positions sorted by suffix order.
- `suffixArray` + `suffixArray_valid`: an executable construction (insertion sort) proved to be a sorted permutation of the positions.
- `suffixArraySearch` + `suffixArraySearch_mem_iff`: suffix-array pattern search proved sound and complete.

The construction is honestly `O(n³)` (insertion sort with `O(n)` suffix comparisons); the textbook `O(n log n)` construction and `O(|p| log n)` range query are recorded as remaining optimization, per the issue's honest-complexity requirement.

Headline theorems (`suffixArray_valid`, `suffixArraySearch_mem_iff`) are axiom-clean (`propext`/`Classical.choice`/`Quot.sound` only). Registers the section in the facade, literate.toml, interface test, and syncs the edition map / progress ledger / proof-map / Status. `python3 scripts/check_repository.py` passes.

author: luvkapur
body:
## Proposed Changes

- Make capsule optimization dependency-aware: a component can use its published package only when its entire dependency subtree is also safe to consume as packages.
- Keep package-only subtrees optimized while retaining mixed-generation dependency paths as capsules.
- Add a registry-backed constructor-identity regression and strengthen `bit ci pr --keep-lane` coverage for unchanged components.

Closes #10583.

## Problem

Capsule optimization, introduced in #9820, avoids creating capsules for exported, built, and unmodified dependencies by installing their published packages instead.

The previous decision was made independently for each component:

> If this component is published and unmodified, use its package.

That establishes package availability, but not whether the resulting dependency graph is safe.

A dependency still needs a capsule when it is:

- new or not exported;
- modified locally, even when an older version was published;
- a seeder or original seeder that is part of the current build;
- exported without a successful build;
- not configured as an installable package; or
- a snap that built successfully but was never published.

This allowed a graph such as:

```
A (registry package) ──> B (published package copy)
                             +
                         B (current capsule copy)
```

If `B` had to remain a capsule, the published `A` could still resolve its recorded package copy of `B`, while another path loaded the current `B` capsule. JavaScript classes and module state are identified by runtime instance, not package name or semantic version. Two copies can therefore break `instanceof`, Harmony singletons, shared remotes, caches, and error recovery based on constructors.

`bit ci pr --keep-lane` exposed this consistently because a reused lane can preserve artifacts from an earlier run while later runs rebuild only changed components.

## Fix

The package side of the optimized graph is now required to be **dependency-closed**:

> If `A` is installed as a package, every transitive dependency of `A` must also be safe to install as a package.

The isolator now:

1. Applies the existing eligibility rules:
   - seeders, modified components, and non-installable components start in the capsule set;
   - published, built, unmodified, installable components start as package candidates.
2. Walks dependency edges backwards from the capsule set.
3. Promotes any package candidate that depends on a capsule into the capsule set.
4. Repeats until no package-to-capsule edge remains.

For example:

```
A ──> B ──> C
            ^
       must be a capsule
```

`C` causes `B` to remain a capsule, which causes `A` to remain a capsule. Conversely, a subtree that is fully resolvable from the registry remains optimized:

```
A (package) ──> B (package) ──> C (package)
```

The closure is computed in `O(V + E)` time using a reverse dependency map and a work queue.

## Behavioral Impact

- Mixed graphs may create more capsules than before. This is the correctness cost of keeping one coherent module generation.
- Registry-only dependency subtrees keep the original optimization.
- Capsule optimization remains enabled globally.
- Lane reuse remains enabled; this does not force every component on a reused lane to rebuild.
- Capsule selection gains linear graph traversal and `O(V + E)` temporary bookkeeping.

## Regression Coverage

The registry-backed regression constructs:

```
comp1 -(dev)-> comp2 -(prod)-> comp3 -(prod)-> comp4
  |                                              ^
  `--------------------(dev)---------------------'
```

`comp4` is modified and must remain a capsule. Before the fix, registry-installed `comp3` loaded its package copy of `comp4`, while `comp1` loaded the current capsule. Constructor identity failed with:

```
Expected constructor: SharedClass
Received constructor: SharedClass
```

After the fix, the capsule requirement propagates through `comp3` and `comp2`, and the test passes. The existing optimization test also proves that a registry-only subtree is still pruned.

The keep-lane regression now verifies that a second PR run reuses the remote lane while preserving the exact head of an unchanged component.

## Validation

- Identity regression: fails before the fix and passes after it.

author: ywy50
body:
Ten rows of transcript was too much to give up for decoration. Now five, and half the width, so it reads as a companion in the corner rather than a second pane. Minimum terminal drops from 23x18 to **12x13**.

## Halving the grid alone would have cost it its face

Each cell now covers 4x the source area, and the sampler averaged that area *before* quantizing. An average of "mostly grey head with a small cyan eye" is grey — so the eye, the chest patch and most of the dust vanished in one step, leaving a grey blob. The eye is most of what makes the thing read as a robot.

So the sampler is inverted: **quantize at full resolution, then let the source pixels behind each half-cell vote**, weighted per colour. A small feature can then win a cell it does not dominate by area. Only the small load-bearing colours are boosted — the three body greys still compete on raw area, or the silhouette distorts.

The eye weight was swept, not guessed, and it is sharp on both sides:

| weight | result |
| --- | --- |
| 2.0 | eye missing in 4 of 11 frames |
| **2.5** | **exactly one cyan cell, inside the head, in 9 of 11 frames** |
| 3.0 | spills to two cells, reads as a visor poking past the head |

The two frames that miss at 2.5 land as a blink.

## A documentation bug this surfaced

`fits` takes the height of the **transcript region**, but the `--mascot` help and `config.toml` quote a **terminal** size. The two differ by the status row plus the three-row input box plus one. The text shipped in #221 said "13 rows" where the real figure for the old size was 18 — wrong before this change, and it would have stayed wrong.

Both now say 12x13, derived by driving a real pty at 12/13/14 rows rather than on paper, and pinned by a test that fails if `rows` or the layout changes without the docs following.

## Verification

Gate, from the repo root in order, in a worktree:

- `zig build` clean
- `zig build tools` clean
- `zig build test --summary all` -> `169/169 steps succeeded; 884/886 tests passed (2 skipped)` (the 2 skips are the expected worktree pair)

Driven live over a real pty, screen read back with pyte:

- `loop`: claims 5 rows, travels and wraps (`0 -> 91 -> 1 -> 93`)
- `type`: 25 characters typed puts the robot at column 25
- boundary swept directly: 11 cols and 12 rows are refused, 12 cols and 13 rows draw — matching the documented minimum exactly
- live turn on deepseek-v4-flash: `PONG` back, turn stats rendered, transcript intact, robot animating throughout

**Still not verified end to end: the kitty-graphics path**, same as #221 — this terminal has no kitty support, so every live run exercised the half-block fallback. The pngs are byte-identical here (they are generated at a fixed 192px and scaled by the terminal), so only the placement's row/col count changed, but that path still wants a manual look in Ghostty.

  * Improved mascot visibility when partially clipped at the terminal edge.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Lowered the minimum supported terminal width to 12 columns.

author: ermakov-oleg
body:
## Summary

A MessagePack header states how many entries a container holds, but the parser dropped that number — `enter_array_known` returned only "has a first element", so `ArrayEncoder::load_format` walked the regrowth ladder (8 → 16 → … → 1024 for a 1000-element list) and `DictionaryEncoder::load_format` let CPython resize the dict table on the way. JSON has no such number (it only shows up at the closing bracket), so the hint is `Option` and JSON keeps the old behaviour.

The length now reaches the four places that build a Python container: `ArrayEncoder::load_format`, `DictionaryEncoder::load_format`, and both containers in `bridge::parse_any`. Map needed its own entry point (`enter_map_known_sized`) because the borrowed first key rules out asking the parser a second time.

## Measurements

Cachegrind on the x86 verification VM, `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`, 20 000 iterations per driver (numbers include ~0.47e9 instructions of CPython startup in both columns):

| load | base | head | Ir |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `dict[str, int]`, 1000 pairs | 22,928,849,250 | 21,579,269,095 | **−5.89%** |
| `Any` (list of 500 + dict of 200) | 6,881,086,000 | 6,584,765,992 | **−4.31%** |
| `list[int]`, 1000 | 6,363,931,271 | 6,280,911,475 | **−1.30%** |

`cg_annotate --diff` attributes the list delta to the malloc subsystem (−60.2M across `_int_malloc`/`_int_realloc`/`realloc`/`_int_free*`), `__memcpy_avx_unaligned_erms` (−12.1M) and the Rust ladder itself (`RawVecInner::finish_grow` −6.2M, `RawVec::grow_one` −3.4M). `ArrayEncoder::load_format` pays 160K more for asking the hint.

The dict delta is larger by an order of magnitude because a 1000-key table is rebuilt ~7 times without a presize: `__memcpy_avx_unaligned_erms` −242.7M and `__memset_avx2_unaligned_erms` −174.6M disappear.

## Why the count is clamped

The stated count feeds an allocation, and `array32`/`map32` can claim 2^32-1 entries in five bytes. The bytes left cap it: an array entry costs at least one byte, a map pair at least two. Without the clamp those five bytes are enough to kill the process — on Linux with 3 GiB RAM and `overcommit_memory=0`:

```
Fatal Python error: Aborted
  File "python/serpyco_rs/_main.py", line 168 in load
  File "tests/test_codec_msgpack.py", line 140 in test_msgpack_oversized_container_header_is_not_preallocated
```

Worth knowing for anyone touching that test: it cannot fail on macOS, where reserving 34 GiB succeeds virtually and the pages are never touched. It only guards on Linux.

author: ipv1337
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1597. I had an independent (Opus) review of that PR's `go_test_with_retry` wrapper after merging, since I'd already caught one subtle bash bug in it via testing and wanted a second pass. It found two more real issues, plus one I found myself while fixing one of them:

1. **SIGPIPE under `pipefail`**: `printf "$out" | grep -q PATTERN` — `grep -q` exits the instant it matches, and on output larger than the pipe buffer that can SIGPIPE the still-writing `printf`. Under `pipefail` the pipeline then reports 141, so the retry check read **false even on a genuine match** (verified: 200KB of matching output → exit 141, not a match). Fixed by having `grep` read a file directly instead of a pipe.

2. **Regex gaps**: missed common proxy transients — 5xx responses, `Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers`, DNS `server misbehaving`, HTTP/2 `GOAWAY`, `context deadline exceeded`. Widened it; verified none of these substrings currently appear anywhere in infra test source, so this doesn't risk masking a real failure as a retry. Deliberately **not** matching bare `EOF` — `io.EOF` is routine in legitimate non-network test failures.

3. **Output loss on hang/timeout**: buffering each attempt's output into a variable and only printing it on return meant a module that hung lost its output entirely if `timeout-minutes` killed the job — exactly when the log matters most.

My first attempt at fixing (3) — `tee /dev/stderr` inside the capturing subshell — was itself broken and arguably worse: reopening `/dev/stderr` fresh on every retry attempt doesn't reliably append, it can overwrite. Caught this myself by testing it and watching two full attempts' worth of output vanish down to just the final line. Replaced with `tee` to a real temp file instead: streams live via the pipeline's own stdout, the grep-for-retry check reads the file, and `PIPESTATUS[0]` (not `$?`, which on that line is `tee`'s status, not `go test`'s) gets the real exit code regardless of `pipefail`.

## Test plan
- [x] Re-extracted the function from the YAML and re-ran the full scenario matrix against faked `go` binaries: immediate success, transient-recovers-on-retry, deterministic hard-failure-does-not-retry, the 200KB SIGPIPE reproduction, a new-regex-pattern match (`GOAWAY`), and bare-`EOF`-does-not-retry — all correct (exit codes, retry counts, and backoff timing all verified).
- [x] Explicitly confirmed every attempt's output survives intact in order (not just the last one) — the exact case the `/dev/stderr` version silently broke.
- [x] Real end-to-end run against two actual modules (`tabula/infra/app`, `infrastructure/pulumi/foundation/gcp-app-infra/modules`) — passes, output streams correctly.
- [ ] `go-test-infra` itself green on this PR.

## Not in scope here

The review also surfaced three pre-existing, unrelated gaps I'm deliberately not bundling into this fix: no tripwire if the module-discovery `find` comes up empty (silent "ran go test in 0 modules" green), the root `infrastructure/pulumi` module gets counted as "has tests" via a nested module and runs a no-op `go test`, and a real failure leaves `::endgroup::` unclosed in the log. Flagging in case they're worth their own follow-up.

author: noahklimczuk
body:
Ontario's AODA (O. Reg. 191/11 s. 14) makes WCAG 2.0 Level AA a legal obligation for these businesses' public websites. We hand them a site — an inaccessible one is a liability we created for them, quietly, in exchange for money.

Nothing about the design changed. The type scale, the frosted nav, the aurora art panels, the scroll-driven reveals and the dark sections are all intact.

## The two structural changes

**`.on-night` re-points the colour tokens** instead of restating colours per component. A dark section sets `--ink`, `--muted`, `--surface`, `--accent-ink` and `--focus` to their night equivalents, so anything placed inside resolves correctly without a new rule. The old shape — one `.on-night .thing { color: … }` override per component — is right until someone moves a component into a dark section nobody wrote an override for, and it fails silently. Eight override rules deleted; the behaviour got broader.

**`design.audit()` now enumerates every pair the templates actually put together**, including the ones that only exist in a dark section and the one behind the frosted bars. That last one found a real failure: the bars are translucent, so with a night section scrolling under them the nav renders around `#e7e7e9`, where the muted grey measures **4.11:1**. Fixed with a darker grey for text on chrome, `CHROME_ALPHA` templated into the CSS so the stylesheet and the contrast check cannot drift apart, and `accent_ink` darkened against that composite so accent text is safe wherever it is put rather than safe until someone moves it. Cost: about one step of lightness on the worst hue.

## Real defects fixed

- The **"why call us" section had no heading at all** — anyone moving by headings met three cards with nothing saying what they were. The eyebrow is now the `h2`: same words, same place, nothing changes on screen.
- The generated artwork announced itself as `aria-label="<name> artwork"`. It is decoration and now says so — which made the page *quieter*, not merely conformant.
- `<main>` gained `tabindex="-1"`. Without it WebKit scrolls but leaves focus on the skip link, and the next Tab goes straight back into the nav being skipped.
- The focus ring was `--accent-ink`, i.e. invisible on a black section.
- `[hidden]` lost to `.pill { display: inline-flex }`, so the open/closed pill flashed "Hours" before the script ran.
- Services and reasons are now `<ul>`; the stats strip is a `<dl>`. A number and its label are a pair and a screen reader had no way to know.
- Links are underlined unless they carry a second signal (button shape, chevron, nav position). The footer phone and the big phone number were marked by colour alone.
- The build **refuses a photo with no alt text**, or alt text that reads "image" or the filename. A failure, not a warning — an operator working through forty sites scrolls past warnings. `"decorative": true` is the explicit escape hatch.

## Two failures that only testing found

Neither would have come out of reading the code. At **200% text on a 390px phone**:

- the display headline overflowed and was clipped by `overflow-x: clip` — a headline the visitor cannot read at all. Every display clamp floor is now capped against the viewport (`min(2.75rem, 11vw)`), because a rem floor does not know how wide the screen is.
- the fixed call bar **covered the footer's address and phone number**. It is `sticky` now: pins to the bottom of the viewport exactly the same way, and reserves its own height at the end of the document — so it cannot cover anything at any text size, without anyone having to guess how tall it will be.

## Measured, not asserted

| | |
|---|---|
| axe-core, `wcag2a` + `wcag2aa` tags only (what AODA cites) | **56 audits, 0 violations** |
| Lighthouse, launched page over HTTP | **a11y 100** · perf 100 · best practices 100 · SEO 100 |
| Page weight | under 30KB |
| Tests | **409 passing** (93 new in `tests/test_a11y.py`) |

The axe sweep covers 3 templates × preview and launched × 390px and 1440px × reduced motion and full motion × top-of-page and fully-scrolled. Auditing happens *after* the page settles — axe reads composited pixels, so a run during the first frames measures a fade in progress and reports every animating heading as a contrast failure. Worth knowing before it turns up in someone's inbox.

## What's added

- `tests/test_a11y.py` — 93 tests, each naming its success criterion, parsing the HTML rather than grepping it. Criteria that don't apply are listed with the reason, so the gaps are deliberate.
- `tools/audit_a11y.py` — re-runs the axe pass on demand, for when a client or a client's lawyer wants a report from a tool they recognise. Same footing as `tools/calibrate.py`: nothing imports it, no new dependency, deleting it breaks nothing.
- `ACCESSIBILITY.md` — what is enforced where, what has been measured, and the two things a machine cannot check: whether alt text is *accurate* rather than merely present, and whether the copy reads plainly. Both stay the operator's job, and now that is a decision rather than an oversight.

author: srujan-rai
body:
`publish.yml` was OIDC-only, so an API token in the repo secrets would never have been read — the run would fail with no credentials at all.

`pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` treats an **empty** `password` as "use Trusted Publishing", so passing the secret unconditionally supports both: token now, OIDC the moment a pending publisher exists, with no further edit.

Two separate secrets, since the registries don't share credentials:

- `PYPI_API_TOKEN` → pypi.org
- `TEST_PYPI_API_TOKEN` → test.pypi.org

## Security note

The token needed for the *first* upload must be **account-wide** ("Entire account"), because project-scoped tokens can only target a project that already exists. That token can publish any project the account owns, so it should be deleted as soon as either a project-scoped token or Trusted Publishing replaces it.

body: ## Qué se hizo Se agrega `indexbanca.html`: el mismo tablero de Speech Analytics de `Speech Analytics Promerica.html`, armado como un único archivo HTML autocontenido y con toda la marca eliminada. El tablero se armó a partir de las fuentes reales del archivo original (`speech-app/app.css` y los seis módulos JSX que carga `speech-app/index.html`), así que conserva el mismo sistema de diseño, las mismas pantallas y los mismos datos de negocio bancario. ## Estructura (igual que el original) - Tabs: Resumen, Comercial, Caja, Interacciones, Performance de usuarios, Agencias. - Resumen: KPIs, frecuencia de atenciones (heatmap), ratio de escucha, sentimiento en el tiempo, top ejecutivos y temas del período. - Comercial y Caja: indicadores comerciales, servicio, SLA, tipo de consulta, operativo y motivos de no resolución. - Interacciones con panel de filtros, tira de "requieren revisión", tabla y drawer de detalle (reproductor, transcripción con detecciones, métricas, cumplimiento de protocolo y coaching). - Performance de usuarios y Agencias con ranking, gráfico configurable, exportación CSV y paginación. - Vista previa de exportación (Excel/CSV) por tab. ## Referencias de marca eliminadas - No queda ninguna mención a la marca del banco original ni a sus agencias: las agencias pasan a ser genéricas (Agencia Centro, Norte, Sur, Oriente, Poniente y una red ampliada con nombres neutros). - Los nombres de ejecutivos del despliegue original se reemplazaron por nombres genéricos. - Se quitó la marca del proveedor de analítica: el logo del sidebar es una marca neutra de barras y el asistente se llama "Asistente de analítica". - El cliente se identifica solo como "Banca" en el chip de la barra superior. - Se neutralizaron datos locales (documento de identidad en la transcripción, nombres de zonas, escalación a atención al cliente) y los comentarios internos que citaban el archivo original. ## Adaptaciones para que funcione como archivo suelto - React, ReactDOM, Babel, Inter y Phosphor se cargan por CDN; el CSS del sistema de diseño queda embebido (sin las fuentes empaquetadas en base64). - El modal de insights ya no carga un `informe.html` externo: ahora es un informe del período autocontenido, con KPIs, temas, productos mencionados y próximos pasos, imprimible a PDF. - El panel de tweaks del entorno de prototipado se reemplazó por un panel de demostración propio (estado del tablero, ranking público, nube de palabras, lista vacía, datos insuficientes). - Se activaron piezas que en el original quedaban definidas pero sin usar: sidebar, asistente, nube de palabras, detalle de tema (con próximos pasos), checklist de cumplimiento de protocolo con salto al minuto de la grabación, exportaciones CSV del ranking y gráfico configurable de conversión por agencia. Se eliminó el resto del código que quedaba sin uso. - Se unificaron las fechas de la interacción de ejemplo con las del listado y el período se expresa como "últimos 30 días" en todo el tablero. ## Verificación - Los seis bloques JSX compilan con Babel y no hay componentes usados sin declarar. - Recorrido en navegador headless: los seis tabs, el drawer de interacción, el drawer de tema, el informe del período, la vista previa de exportación, el panel de demostración y los tres tipos de gráfico, sin errores de consola ni de red. - Sin desborde horizontal en viewport móvil (390 px).

body:
## 背景

以 `architecture-coordinator` skill 身份做例行 review 时发现：`SKILL.md` 三处仍写协调权威在 **coord-service（D1）**、归因 ADR-009，但代码早已在 2026-07-18（ADR-017）割接到 **coord-gateway（RepoHub DO）**——ADR-017 只换载体，不改 ADR-009 定的 claim/heartbeat/TTL/fail-closed 语义。

**实测证据**（动态事实，非读注释）：本会话在无 `COORD_GATEWAY_URL`/`COORD_API_TOKEN` 的环境下跑 `pnpm harness module-lock-status --module architecture`，报错原文就是"coord-gateway（RepoHub DO，ADR-017）是协调租约的唯一权威……旧 COORD_SERVICE_URL/COORD_SERVICE_TOKEN 已随 coord-service 退役（ADR-017），配了也不会被读取"。同时 [`module-lock.ts`](.harness/scripts/module-lock.ts) / [`coord-client.ts`](.harness/scripts/lib/coord-client.ts) 印证代码已完全跑在 coord-gateway 上。

L100-104 还有一处明显拼接痕迹：凭据名已经是 ADR-017 换的新名字（`COORD_GATEWAY_URL`/`COORD_API_TOKEN`），却被文字归到 ADR-009 头上，前后对不上。

## 改动
只订正 `.agents/skills/architecture-coordinator/SKILL.md` 的四处措辞（顶部说明、启动仪式、跨平台设计原则、领域知识小节），把权威载体更新为 coord-gateway/ADR-017，凭据名与出处对齐，并补充一句「这份 skill 自己就是漂移的反例」。

## 范围说明（有意收窄）
同样的 ADR-009→ADR-017 措辞滞留在十几份其他文档里（`multi-agent-coordination.md`、`coordinator-sop.md`、`agent-onboarding-checklist.md` 等），本 PR **有意不动**，避免一次改动铺太大面。这批文档的漂移部分已有 backlog 追踪：
- #381（范围仅 `cycle-report.ts` + `docs/coordination-protocol.md`，不含这批 instructions）
- #384（大审计，backlog/out-of-scope，尚未点名这批文件）

后续是否要开新 issue 扩大到这批文档，留给 coord-main / 人类决定优先级。

## 验证
- 纯文档改动，无代码/schema 影响；`turbo` affected 检查 0 任务，pre-push 通过。
- 无独立合并权，等 review + coord-main 合并。

author: douglasmun
body:
## Why

Every CDR verdict in this repo is confirmed against **pikepdf, python-docx, openpyxl and Pillow** — never against Acrobat or Word. That matters more than it sounds: the bug class we keep finding (pitfalls #49, #54, #55) *is* parser disagreement — a real consumer resolving a part differently than the test parser does. Verifying only against Python parsers means the test oracle shares a blind spot with the thing being tested.

This adds the tooling to close that gap the only way it can be closed: a human opens the sanitised files in the real viewers.

## What's here

- `build_corpus.py` — 14 cases through the real `cdr_dispatch`, saving inputs and sanitised outputs (honours `EXT_REMAP`, so `.docm` → `.docx`).
- `build_realistic.py` — `p55_realistic.docx`, the highest-value artefact: a genuine python-docx document (heading, styled runs, 2×2 table) whose main part was relocated to `word/doc.dat` and declared solely by `<Default Extension="dat">`. The #55 vector, carried by a file Word should render normally.
- `CHECKLIST.md` — priority-ordered (P1 the #54/#55 bypasses, P2 Office fidelity, P3 Acrobat, P4 the container-layer sweep), with pass/fail criteria that separate **fidelity** failures from **security** failures, and a red-flag list.

## What is deliberately not here

The binaries. `originals/` holds **live malicious payloads** (DDE field codes, PDF JavaScript) and must never reach the public repo; `sanitised/` is large and regenerable. Both are gitignored, following the existing `docs/test-corpus/` precedent — verified with `git check-ignore`.

## Two things worth flagging

**Expected residue, not a finding.** Scrubbed fields read `DDEAUTO _CDR_REMOVED_ "/c calc.exe"`. The executable path is replaced; the inert string survives inside the quoted argument (pitfall #13). Seeing `calc.exe` in the XML is expected — being *prompted* to update remote data is not. The checklist says so explicitly, so the reviewer doesn't raise a false alarm.

**Four fixtures excluded, in the generator rather than by hand.** `docx_dde_field`, `docx_autoopen_field`, `docx_multithreat` and `docx_vba_macro` are synthetic packages with no `officeDocument` relationship — python-docx cannot open the *inputs* either, so Word would reject them for reasons unrelated to CDR. Excluding them in code means a rebuild can't quietly reintroduce them. `p55_realistic.docx` covers what they cannot.

## Verification

436 tests pass; all five repo guards green (lambda-requirements, IaC parity, cap defaults, pitfalls index, test count). Corpus regenerated from clean to prove the committed generators reproduce it — 15 files, no manual step.

Docs and scripts only; no change to `lambda_function.py`.

## Outcome

If everything passes, the Python-parser verdicts in `docs/cdr-gap-analysis-stevens.md` and the pitfalls doc are corroborated by the shipping viewers and the stated limit there can be narrowed. A security failure would be a real bypass the whole suite is currently blind to.

body:
Documentation only — the actual post edits were applied directly to Typefully (social set 278688). This records them so the queue file and the live schedule don't drift.

## Why

Recovering the verified X handles the sweep had been discarding (#30) took `twitter_handle` from **43,704 → 1,070,442** (1,070,137 owner-attested). Every post citing the old ~41k figure was wrong by ~25x.

## Corrected

| Post | When | Change |
|---|---|---|
| **Milestone thread, T4** | **Sat Aug 15** | Said "about 41k wallets" *and* "attested onchain" — the second wrong independently of the count, since the dominant source is now a Farcaster verified account, not an ENS record. Other four tweets untouched. |
| Post 47, attested Twitter | Sep 14 | "1M you can trust than 10M you have to hope about" — argument unchanged, scale corrected |
| Post 37, sources | Sep 8 | Added "X accounts owners verified on Farcaster"; it listed only ENS text records |
| Post 43, month close | Sep 11 | Added "1M+ X handles, every one owner-verified"; video media preserved |

The Aug 15 thread was the urgent one — it publishes in two days.

## Left alone on purpose

Posts 14/16/22/24 cite 14,773 wallets / 11.5% / 1,692 reachable. Those are accurate measurements of a real run, framed as "we ran", and the 2026-08-13 re-measure put Robinhood index-only Farcaster at **11.3%** — consistent. Older, not stale.

## Audit lesson worth keeping

My first pass scanned the `preview` field and **missed the Aug 15 thread entirely**, because `preview` contains only the *first* tweet. A queue audit has to fetch each draft's full `platforms.x.posts[]` or multi-tweet threads are invisible to it. Second pass read full thread text across all 47 drafts.

## Verification

Re-read from the API after patching: 47 scheduled, zero collisions, Aug 13 → Sep 14 unchanged, video media intact on post 43, and a final full-text sweep for surviving stale figures returns **none**.

author: oratis
body:
## 做了什么

把 DeepSeek Harness（`dsh`，MIT，2026-08-13 开源）的一手调研引入本仓，并逐项对着当前树（v0.23.0 / `9cfe2a3`）审计出 LISA 侧的真实差距与取舍。

| 文件 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `docs/RESEARCH_DEEPSEEK_HARNESS.md` | 原文照收（来自 DouDouAI 仓），加引入说明。**§5 是源项目的结论而非 LISA 的**，指向源仓的相对链接已改纯文本 |
| `docs/PLAN_HARNESS_ALIGNMENT_v1.0.md` | LISA 侧的逐项对照、取舍、排期与验收清单（新写） |

## 核心结论

**dsh 对 LISA 不是引擎候选，是体检报告。**

dsh 花大力气建的生态兼容层，LISA 已经追平或更全 —— 20+ provider 预设且是 `apiKeyEnv` 引用制、Claude Code `hooks.json` 同形状、`SKILL.md`、`mcp__server__tool` 命名、PTY/managed 已能把 claude+codex CLI 当受控子代理。这一层照抄零增量。反过来 dsh 完全没有 soul/desire/mood/KB/Reve 这层持久身份。

**真差距只有三处**，每处恰好卡在 1.0 的一条主线上：

1. **H1 能力 seam** — `ToolContext` 只有 `{cwd, signal, log, onObjection}`，工具各自 `import fs`/`spawn`；Cloud 多租户只能靠 `cloudSafeSubset` 白名单硬砍 fs/shell 工具（白名单是补丁，seam 才是解）
2. **H2 权限沙箱三个洞** — `wrapForSandbox` 唯一调用点是 `bash.ts:34`，`write`/`edit`/`apply_patch` 完全绕过；非 macOS **静默降级**成无沙箱；默认全关
3. **H3 会话日志不是真源** — `tool_use`/`tool_result` 其实都在，但**系统提示词一个字节都不进日志**且会话中途热重载 → 拿一条历史会话重建不出当时模型看到的 persona，drift/coherence 无法离线复算

唯一值得写代码接入的：把 `dsh` 加成 `src/integrations/` 的第 11 个 observer + `dispatch_agent` 后端。

**明确不做**：不 fork、不当执行引擎、不引 Cordis、Code Mode 缓到 seam+沙箱落地后再评估（理由见计划 §6）。

## 后续 PR

本 PR 只含文档。实现按计划 §7 的优先级拆成独立 PR 跟进（H3 → H1 → H2 → dsh observer → 生态小补）。

## 验证

- 两个文档里的全部相对链接（含 `../src/*.ts` 与 `./PLAN_*.md`）均已脚本校验可解析
- 计划中的每条现状断言都带 `file:line`，取自当前树

author: marius-cetanas
body:
## What this fixes

`cli/feedback.test.mjs` was filed in session 13 as leaking a temp directory per run. It does — and so
do five other suites. **23 unregistered `mkdtempSync` sites across six files leaked 78 directories per
run**, against 43,986 already sitting in `os.tmpdir()` on the maintainer's machine.

Each site now registers on its suite's scratch list, swept at process exit — the idiom eleven suites
here already carry, and the rationale in each is the existing one (node's ten-listener limit), restored
rather than replaced.

**Measured, before and after:** `78 → 0`.

## The instrument had to be replaced before the fix could be checked

The task arrived with a verification recipe: count `portulan-*` directories in `os.tmpdir()` before and
after a run, assert a delta of 0. **That instrument can see 46 of the 78 — 59%.** It is blind to
`skills-set-*`, `recipe-set-*`, `compile-*`, `index-*` and `vendor-bothroots-*`, so a delta of 0 under
it would have been reported as a fix while **32 directories per run kept accruing** — and the report
would have been *true about what it measured*.

An instrument keyed on a naming convention measures the convention, not the phenomenon. The prefix was
never the thing; *a directory this suite created and did not remove* was. The replacement snapshots
every directory in `os.tmpdir()`, runs the suite, and diffs the name sets: it cannot miss a prefix
because it never enumerates one, and it attributes any hit **by name**. That paid for itself — one run
came back `1`, immediately legible as `MSBuildTemp…` from an unrelated process, confirmed foreign by a
clean re-run.

## A second defect, found while fixing the first

Every sweeper in `cli/` was a naked `for (const dir of SCRATCH) fs.rmSync(dir, {recursive:true, force:true})`.
**`force: true` suppresses ENOENT, not EACCES.** Eight suites chmod a scratch directory and restore it
in `finally`; a case dying before its `finally` leaves one `rmSync` cannot enter — and inside a
`process.on("exit")` handler that throw **aborts the loop and abandons every directory after it**.

Demonstrated rather than argued — three directories, the first locked:

| sweeper | left behind |
|---|---|
| naked loop | **3 of 3** |
| per-directory `try` | **1 of 3** (the locked one only) |

Which locks bite was measured too: an **empty** directory blocks only if *unreadable*; a **non-empty**
one also needs write and search. The errno follows readability, not position — an unreadable root gives
EACCES, everything else ENOTEMPTY. Two cases an earlier draft cited as hazards turned out not to be,
and each comment now says so: **a hazard claimed where none exists is the same defect as one missed.**

`collisions.test.mjs` keeps its bare `rmSync` and now says why — its handler already unlocks the one
path it ever locks.

## Scope

Six files for the registrations, eight for the hardening — not the one file named. Per the ruling of
2026-07-27 (#43) and [`0020`](.portulan/proposals/0020-a-fix-is-not-done-at-the-site-it-was-found.md):
*the defect class sets a fix's scope, not the task's literal boundary.* Fixing only `feedback` would
have left 32 directories per run and its own siblings knowingly unswept.

## Verification

- **Leak delta: 0** directories, prefix-blind, across a full eleven-recipe run.
- **Suite 1557 pass / 0 fail.** No test weakened, skipped, deleted, or loosened — the diff deletes
  exactly 10 lines: 7 naked sweeper loops, 2 `mkdtempSync` rebindings, 1 generated index count.
- **Eleven recipes green.**
- Seam scan clean across diff, file paths, commit message and branch.

## Checkpoints

Session-open **A-W-A (13)**; pre-commit **five times** — REQUEST-CHANGES (5), (7), (6), (5), then
**A-W-A (7)** once the mechanism was confirmed correct and complete with only prose outstanding. Every
adjustment folded, optional included.

**Every one of the five folds introduced a fresh defect inside itself** — three on a number, one on a
file mode, one deleting rationale that three other files cite. None was reachable by re-reading; each
was consistent with the reasoning that produced it and false about the tree. That is the session's
carried lesson, and it is in the handoff: **a fold is a change and needs grading like one.**

## Not done here

- **No rail stops the 24th unregistered site.** Nothing goes red when a new `mkdtempSync` is left
  unswept; these 23 were found by census. A check could enumerate call sites, or a run could assert its
  own delta — deliberately not smuggled into a cleanup, since five sites clean up correctly in four
  different vocabularies and the false-positive surface is real.
- **The abort path is exercised by no test.** A green run reports 0 with or without the per-directory
  `try`; it rests on the standalone demonstration above.
- **The ~44,000-directory backlog is untouched** — they are empty directories, some predating this
  session, and clearing them is the maintainer's call.

Rebased onto `d9be6e3` after #237 merged mid-session; all four predicted conflicts resolved by keeping
both sides, which compose — the hermetic guard neutralises the host, the scratch list sweeps the tree.

author: auerlian
body:
## Summary

- **Follow-up correction to #179**, per explicit owner feedback the same day: #179 fixed a dead-end navigation loop by routing the Overview CTA through `nextOnboardingStep(state)`, but `state` was still computed from the GLOBAL `student_profiles.confirmed_at` — so once a student confirmed on *any* application, every future application's onboarding silently skipped Reflections, Achievements, and Review & Confirm entirely and jumped straight into report generation. Reported: *"this is wrong. We want them to go through the normal reflections and application UI again... but for the flow to always be the same."*
- **New migration** `supabase-per-application-onboarding.sql` adds `personal_summary_reviewed_at` / `achievements_reviewed_at` / `candidate_confirmed_at` to `course_applications` (plus a nullable `application_id` on `confirmed_candidate_snapshots`, tagging each confirmation with the application it belongs to).
- `fetchOnboardingState` now reads these three columns instead of the global `student_profiles` ones — restoring #179's CTA fix to actually work as intended (`nextOnboardingStep` correctly resolves to `'personal-summary'` for every new application again). `apply/page.tsx`'s `fetchStrategyReadiness` (My Portal's "ready" vs "continue applying" label) had the identical global-flag bug independently and got the same fix.
- The underlying **shared candidate profile is unchanged** — only the *review/confirmation state* is now tracked per application. `PATCH /api/reflection`'s lock and `POST /api/candidate-information/confirm`'s idempotency both moved from `student_profiles.confirmed_at` to `course_applications.candidate_confirmed_at` for the application in question, verified server-side via a new shared `verifiedApplicationId` helper — `applicationId` arrives from the client already derived from an untrusted `?return=` URL (via the existing `applicationIdFromPath`, the same pattern `ApplicationNavFromReturn` already used), and every route independently re-checks ownership.
- Per explicit owner direction (confirmed via `AskUserQuestion`): the flow order is always Reflections → Achievements → Review & Confirm → Analysis, for every application, never silently skipped by the system — but each of the first two pages gained a one-click **"Skip — my answers/achievements are still correct"** button for a returning student who doesn't need to retype anything.
- Every entry point with no application context (the legacy `/ai-strategy/report` generation) keeps today's exact global-fallback behavior, unchanged.
- Full incident writeup in `docs/known-issues.md` §5p.

## ⚠️ Action required in production before/at deploy

**Run `supabase-per-application-onboarding.sql` in the Supabase SQL editor.** Reads degrade gracefully without it, but the write side does not fully: without it, `course_applications.candidate_confirmed_at` never gets set no matter how many times a student confirms, so `nextOnboardingStep` never advances past `'confirm'` — a student would repeatedly reach Review & Confirm, submit successfully (a new snapshot row each time — safe, append-only, but duplicated), and land right back on the same page instead of reaching report generation.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — 0 errors
- [x] `npx tsc -p tsconfig.strict.json --noEmit` — 0 errors
- [x] `npx eslint .` — 0 errors, 23 pre-existing warnings unrelated to this change
- [x] `npx vitest run` — 1979 passed, 2 todo, 192 files, 1 pre-existing failure unrelated to this PR (confirmed failing identically on a clean `origin/main` checkout via `git stash`, not touched here). New/updated: `onboarding-status.test.ts` (incl. a regression test that one application's review state never leaks onto a different, brand-new application), `reflection/route.test.ts` and `confirm/route.test.ts` (per-application lock/idempotency/stamping alongside the existing global-fallback paths), `verified-application-id.test.ts` (new), `apply-page-logo-performance.test.ts` (updated to check the still-parallel `applicant_analyses` read)
- [x] `node scripts/check-i18n.mjs` — 0 missing keys
- [ ] Browser click-through: confirm application A → open new application B → verify B starts fully editable at Reflections, Skip works, Confirm is independent of A → open a still-newer application C → verify C also starts fresh after B locks (not run in this sandbox — no `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`)

author: afinetooth
body:
## Problem

The `build-linux` job has been failing since ~May 2026. The last green build was `v0.6.17` (Sept 2025).

**This blocks releases entirely.** The `release` job is `needs: [build-windows, build-linux]`, so a tag push right now would publish **no release assets at all**. (`continue-on-error: true` on `release` does not help — `needs` gates on success, so the job is skipped, not failed.)

## Root cause

The failure is in the `macos-packages` Docker stage. `scripts/homebrew-downloader.cr` declared:

```crystal
@bottle : {stable: {files: {arm64_monterey: BottleFile?, monterey: BottleFile?}}}
```

a strict Crystal `NamedTuple` requiring a `stable` key — and it deserialized the **entire** Homebrew formula index (8,546 formulas), so one non-conforming formula anywhere in the index kills the build.

Homebrew has since added five formulas with `"bottle": {}` and no `stable` key — `portable-libffi`, `portable-libxcrypt`, `portable-libyaml`, `portable-openssl`, `portable-zlib` — producing:

```
Missing json attribute: stable at line 5960, column 675 (JSON::ParseException)
```

Fixing only the JSON shape would have exposed a **second** problem: Homebrew has dropped `arm64_monterey` bottles for 9 of the 11 requested packages now that macOS 12 is EOL (only `gmp` and `libyaml` still have them). The stage would have produced an incomplete dependency set regardless.

## Why removal is the right fix

None of it was load-bearing. As the Dockerfile already documented:

> We are not using this script to cross-compile for MacOS at this time (you'll notice we have no accompanying target in our Makefile for a MacOS build).

Confirmed: the Makefile only cross-compiles `x86_64-linux-musl` and `aarch64-linux-musl`, and `v0.6.17`'s assets are Linux and Windows only. MacOS users install via the [Homebrew tap](https://github.com/coverallsapp/homebrew-coveralls). This was speculative scaffolding for a path we never wired up, and it could only ever break.

## Changes

- Remove the `macos-packages` stage and its `COPY --from`
- Remove the MacOS SDK download
- Delete `scripts/homebrew-downloader.cr` (no remaining consumers)
- Remove `aarch64-apple-darwin` from `scripts/xbuild.sh`, so the container no longer advertises a target it cannot build
- Correct the stale `libz.a` comment, which referenced the now-removed darwin path (it is copied explicitly because `zlib-static` installs it into `/lib` rather than `/usr/lib`)

Net: **-208 / +18**.

## Verification

Ran the full `build-linux` pipeline locally (Docker, aarch64 host):

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `make build-xbuild-container` | passes (previously failed here) |
| `make compile-and-strip-all` | both targets compile, link, strip |
| `make package` | all 6 artifacts, matching `v0.6.17`'s asset list |
| `coveralls-linux-aarch64 --version` | `0.6.17` (native arm64 container) |
| `coveralls-linux-x86_64 --version` | `0.6.17` (emulated amd64 container) |

Linking picks up the expected libraries including `-lunwind`, so the musl path is unaffected.

## Note

body:
This PR addresses the following issue in `multi_stream_pkg/multi_stream_pkg/multi_stream_class.py`: close label file handles with with statements.

## Changes
- `multi_stream_pkg/multi_stream_pkg/multi_stream_class.py`: close label file handles with with statements.

## Details
```diff
--- a/multi_stream_pkg/multi_stream_pkg/multi_stream_class.py
+++ b/multi_stream_pkg/multi_stream_pkg/multi_stream_class.py
@@ -1,7 +1,11 @@
-class_obj = (open(location+'object_labels.txt').readline().rstrip('\n')).split(';')
-
-class_color = (open(location+'color_labels.txt').readline().rstrip('\n')).split(';')
-
-class_make = (open(location+'make_labels.txt').readline().rstrip('\n')).split(';')
-
-class_type = (open(location+'type_labels.txt').readline().rstrip('\n')).split(';')
+with open(location+'object_labels.txt') as _f:
+    class_obj = (_f.readline().rstrip('\n')).split(';')
+
+with open(location+'color_labels.txt') as _f:
+    class_color = (_f.readline().rstrip('\n')).split(';')
+
+with open(location+'make_labels.txt') as _f:
+    class_make = (_f.readline().rstrip('\n')).split(';')
+
+with open(location+'type_labels.txt') as _f:
+    class_type = (_f.readline().rstrip('\n')).split(';')
```

## Tests
- `tests/test_multi_stream_class.py`

```diff
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_multi_stream_class.py
@@ -0,0 +1,44 @@
+import ast
+import os
+import unittest
+
+
+class TestLabelFileHandles(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_label_files_loaded_via_with_statement(self):
+        """Each label file must be opened with a context manager so the
+        handle is closed right after reading.
+        """
+        module_path = os.path.abspath(
+            os.path.join(
+                os.path.dirname(__file__),
+                '..',
+                'multi_stream_pkg',
+                'multi_stream_pkg',
+                'multi_stream_class.py',
+            )
+        )
+        with open(module_path) as f:
+            tree = ast.parse(f.read())
+
+        opened_inside_with = set()
+        for node in ast.walk(tree):
+            if not isinstance(node, ast.With):
+                continue
+            for item in node.items:
+                call = item.context_expr
+                if (
+                    isinstance(call, ast.Call)
+                    and isinstance(call.func, ast.Name)
+                    and call.func.id == 'open'
+                ):
+                    for arg in call.args:
+                        if isinstance(arg, ast.Constant) and isinstance(arg.value, str):
+                            opened_inside_with.add(arg.value)
+                        elif isinstance(arg, ast.BinOp) and isinstance(arg.right, ast.Constant):
+                            opened_inside_with.add(arg.right.value)
+
+        for label in (
+            'object_labels.txt',
+            'color_labels.txt',
+            'make_labels.txt',
+            'type_labels.txt',
+        ):
+            self.assertTrue(
+                any(label in opened for opened in opened_inside_with),
+                f'{label} is not loaded inside a with statement',
+            )
```

author: cmloegcmluin
body:
This repo already says the branch preview is part of delivering a user-facing
change, because he judges mergability by clicking through the real app. It
never said WHEN, and the Landing section directly below reads as a complete
recipe ending in "merges it when green" — so an agent follows both, opens the
PR and hands over the preview in one message, and auto-merge.yml lands the
change about twenty minutes later while he is still clicking. That is #33
(2026-08-13): merged before the preview link had been opened, which is exactly
the "just guessing at whether it's mergable" this section exists to prevent,
arrived at by obeying the page.

State the ordering where both halves can see it: preview → his word → PR, with
the reason (opening a non-draft PR here is not proposing the change, it is
landing it) and the escape hatch for wanting the branch visible sooner —
--draft, which auto-merge.yml exempts on purpose, then gh pr ready on his word.

fun_time's CLAUDE.md already carries this rule ("Get his eyes on the branch
before the PR"); the global engineering law has required review before a merge
to a shared main since the sagittal-app revert. This repo was the odd one out.

Also record that merged branches now prune themselves — every haglio repo has
GitHub's "automatically delete head branches" on as of today, so the only
branch left for an agent to remove is one it abandons without merging.

author: jeankadang
body:
Refs #210. Delivers acceptance criteria 1 and 2 — the inventory and the decomposition. The migration itself is the sub-issues, not this PR.

## Why a script rather than a one-off count

The first count I took was a naive bullet count: 1,884 legacy bullets. It was wrong in both directions, because the catalogue's certification sections are not uniform:

- **97 roles** carry a flat list *and* `**Complementary Certifications:**` subheads naming the same credentials again — double counting.
- **24 roles** write `Complementary certifications:` as a bullet rather than a subhead — a non-credential counted as one.
- **172 roles** pack several credentials into one comma-joined bullet — undercounting.

Counting credential-shaped *claims* instead gives **2,166**, of which **524** are families, topics, or vague "or other …" text that can never become registry records. Batch sizes come straight from these numbers, so getting them right had to come before filing anything.

Keeping the script in the repo makes the criterion-1 evidence re-runnable after each batch, so rollout progress is measured rather than asserted.

## What it reports

```
Legacy credential entries: 2166   migrated: 25
Distinct credentials after alias grouping: 1100

Entries by kind:
  credential  1642   auditable as an individual credential
  family       398   a group, not one credential
  topic         94   a subject, not a credential
  vague         32   "or other ..." -- unverifiable as written

Certification section shapes:
  grouped  121   subheads only
  mixed     97   flat list AND subheads -- duplicated recommendations
  flat       8   no subheads
  none       1   no certification section
```

Plus legacy entries per domain, and the cross-cutting credentials with their alias groups — `FinOps Certified Practitioner` alone appears in 14 spellings.

The script reports and never edits a role file.

## Test

Nine tests written first, each pinning a shape found in the real catalogue: BOM/CRLF handling, learning-resource exclusion, bullet-as-subhead, comma-joined splitting, and the case that must *not* split (`Oracle Certified Master, Java Architect` is one credential, not two). Also `aliasKey` grouping and the family/topic/vague classification.

A parser bug is exactly what these guard: the first version used a `$` end-anchor under the `/m` flag, where `$` matches a *line* end, and silently captured an empty section for every role — reporting 0 bullets across 227 files.

## Decomposition

19 native sub-issues on #210, each with a milestone, labels, and assignee. The first three are prerequisites — structure normalisation (#227), family/topic policy (#228), and the cross-cutting credential audit (#229) — because without them every domain batch re-audits shared credentials and guesses at duplicated lists.

## Verification

- `npm test` — 312/312 pass (was 303)
- `npm run validate` — 0 errors; 199 KPI warnings unchanged (#140)
- `node scripts/credential-inventory.js` — output above

## Scope

No role file, registry record, or `audited_roles` entry changes here. #210 stays open until its batches land.

## Summary
`SyncService._syncPendingData` casts every local PoD column *outside* the per-row `try`/`catch`: `pod['stop_id'] as String`, `pod['trip_display_id'] as String`, `pod['id'] as int`, etc. Local PoD rows are written by multiple app generations, so any missing or mistyped column throws a `TypeError` before the try block — aborting the entire sync batch instead of skipping the single bad row.

- Move all column reads inside the per-row `try`, guarding each cast with `is` checks and safe fallbacks (`null`/empty string/`-1`).

- The catch/retry path re-derives values defensively instead of referencing possibly-uninitialized locals.

## Impact
- A single malformed row is skipped without killing the rest of the batch.
- Behavior for well-formed rows is identical.

Fixes #12275

author: warp-agent-staging[bot]
body:
## Description
`GlobalBufferModel::resolve_conflict` accepted the client's content during sync-conflict resolution by calling `Buffer::replace_all`, which discards the whole buffer and rebuilds it from scratch. That means two full-buffer allocations on every conflict resolution, regardless of how small the actual divergence is:
1. The buffer's own text storage (`Buffer::edit` -> `push_text_fragments_to_block`/`update_content_with_text_fragments` -> `BufferText::append_str` -> `SumTree::extend` -> `Arc<Node<BufferText>>::new`).
2. The resulting `EditDelta`'s styled-content materialization (`styled_blocks_in_range`, same underlying mechanism as APP-5353's diff-triggered layout path).

This is confirmed directly by two Sentry heap profiles on issue 7259255054 (this is a follow-up to APP-5353, tracked as [APP-5357](https://linear.app/warpdotdev/issue/APP-5357/memory-globalbuffermodelresolve-conflict-full-buffer-replace-all)):
- Event `76699a1f5b35444a85423bb607a310b2`: 13.38GB sampled, with a single 6.88GB stack whose frames explicitly name `GlobalBufferModel::resolve_conflict` -> `Buffer::replace_all` -> `apply_core_edit_actions` -> `Buffer::edit` -> `update_content_with_text_fragments`/`push_text_fragments_to_block` -> `BufferText::append_str` -> `SumTree::extend` -> `Arc<Node<BufferText>>::new`.
- Event `1366e96e4af14f79b7466dc272f24dbe`: 12.30GB sampled, with a 0.62GB stack through the same `resolve_conflict`/`replace_all` call chain.

A sync conflict's client content almost always diverges from the server's only in the ranges edited during the conflict window (both sides share recent common history) -- unlike, say, a first-ever file load where there's nothing to diff against.

## Linked Issue
[APP-5357](https://linear.app/warpdotdev/issue/APP-5357/memory-globalbuffermodelresolve-conflict-full-buffer-replace-all) (follow-up to APP-5353). Sentry issue: https://sentry.io/organizations/warpdotdev/issues/7259255054/

- [x] Filed via the internal Sentry memory-triage bot; not `ready-to-spec`/`ready-to-implement` labeled since this is a factory-originated fix, not a GitHub issue flow.
- [x] No UI change, no screenshots applicable.

## Changes
- `GlobalBufferModel::resolve_conflict` now diffs the client's content against the buffer's current content and applies the result as a scoped, anchor-preserving edit via the existing `insert_at_char_offset_ranges` (the same mechanism already used for incremental auto-reload), instead of `Buffer::replace_all`.
- Added `text_diff_sync` to `crates/editor/src/content/diff.rs`, a synchronous counterpart to the existing async `text_diff`, sharing the same diff core (extracted into `edits_from_diff`) so both compute identical results. `resolve_conflict`'s conflict-resolution flow doesn't need the cooperative-yield/cancellation machinery that auto-reload's background task uses (that task can be superseded rapidly by file-watcher events; conflict resolution is a one-shot, user-initiated action).

### `replace_all`'s other callers -- deliberately not touched
- **Initial file load** (`populate_buffer_with_read_content`'s `is_initial_load` branch): no prior content exists to diff against; a full materialization is unavoidable and correct here.
- **Non-incremental auto-reload fallback** (same function, `FeatureFlag::IncrementalAutoReload` disabled): this scenario already has a diff-based alternative gated behind that flag; enabling it more broadly is a rollout decision, not a code gap.
- **Remote `OpenBuffer` response / force-reload** (`apply_open_buffer_response`, `force_reload_server_local`): both are explicit "discard in-memory state, take the server's/disk's truth" operations. A full `ContentReplaced` is the intentionally correct signal there (matches "discard any in-memory edits" semantics), not just an incidental cost. Flagging as a candidate follow-up if their allocation profile becomes evidenced, but out of scope here since it wasn't the evidenced site and changing it changes the observable "discard" semantics.

## Testing
- `crates/editor/src/content/diff_tests.rs` (new): pins that `text_diff_sync` matches the async `text_diff` byte-for-byte, that its edits correctly reconstruct the new text from the old, and specifically that a single-line change in a 200-line buffer produces one small diff hunk rather than touching the whole buffer.
- `app/src/code/buffer_location_tests.rs::resolve_conflict_applies_scoped_diff_not_full_buffer_replace` (new): drives the actual `resolve_conflict` -> diff -> apply pipeline end to end against a real `GlobalBufferModel`/`Buffer`, asserts the final content is correct, and -- the invariant that actually matters -- asserts no `BufferEvent::ContentReplaced` fires and the `BufferEvent::ContentChanged` delta's replaced range is far smaller than the full buffer.
- Ran `./script/format` (clean), `cargo clippy -p warp --all-targets --tests -- -D warnings` and `-p warp_editor` (both clean, exit 0), `cargo nextest run -p warp -E 'test(code::buffer_location)' -E 'test(code::global_buffer_model)'` (23/23 pass, including the pre-existing `resolve_conflict_updates_content_and_clock` correctness test), and `cargo nextest run -p warp_editor` (488/488 pass).
- I could not reproduce the original multi-GB macOS heap profile in this environment (no macOS runner, no way to generate a real multi-GB conflict-resolution workload here) -- the regression tests above are the best available proof that the fix produces a scoped edit instead of a full-buffer replace; I have not verified the actual peak-memory delta on a real large file.

- [x] Not manually tested with `./script/run` -- this is a daemon-side (`remote_server`) buffer-sync code path with no direct UI surface to exercise; automated tests above exercise the actual code path instead.

### Screenshots / Videos
Not applicable -- no UI change.

## Agent Mode
- [x] Warp Agent Mode - This PR was created via Warp's AI Agent Mode

CHANGELOG-BUG-FIX: Fixed a memory leak where resolving a file sync conflict could allocate memory proportional to the entire file instead of just the changed portion.

author: cemoso
body:
## What

A vendor-admin machine endpoint `POST /api/admin/merge-orgs` (guarded by the shared `ADMIN_API_SECRET` bearer, inert on self-host) that consolidates one organization into another, plus the core logic in `lib/merge-orgs.ts`.

Driven over loopback by octopus-deploy's `merge-orgs-wdc.yml` (backup → dry-run → apply), mirroring `seed-docs-wdc`.

## Behavior

- **Single Postgres interactive transaction** re-points every org-scoped table from source → target. `dryRun` (the default) executes every statement then **rolls back**, returning exact affected-row counts — a zero-risk preview against live data. Callers must pass `dryRun:false` to commit.
- **Balances** summed onto the target; **survivor renamed** (optional); **source API tokens revoked** by default (so they can't silently reach the target's repos); **source org soft-deleted** (`deletedAt`) — never hard-deleted, so no destructive FK cascade (matches `deleteOrganization` in `actions.ts`).
- **Compound-unique tables** (`organization_members`, `day_summaries`, `incident_comms`, `coupon_redemptions`, `user_presences`) drop colliding source rows before moving; members demote a moved `owner` to `admin` and keep the target's own owner.
- **Qdrant**: on apply (after commit) rewrites the `orgId` payload across `knowledge_chunks`, `review_chunks`, `chat_chunks`, `flowchart_chunks`, `feedback_patterns` (code_chunks is `repoId`-keyed, untouched) — otherwise those vectors silently orphan.

## Safety

- Table classification verified against `packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma` (every `organizationId`-bearing table enumerated; compound uniques handled).
- Preconditions: source/target exist, neither already deleted, new slug not taken.
- No schema change. `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- The real acceptance check is the production **dry-run** (rollback) row counts, run before any apply.

author: supertokens-agent-runner[bot]
body:
## Problem

`activity_log.payload` shipped as `TEXT`. The table is dormant today (every current
`AuditLogEvent` writes `payload = null`, and nothing reads the column), but it is about to
carry structured lifecycle-event JSON. A `TEXT` column accepts malformed JSON silently; the
column should be `JSONB` so bad payloads are rejected at write time. This is the (dormant,
therefore non-breaking-now) schema fix called out in the plan.

## Fix

- **Fresh install** — `getQueryToCreateActivityLogTable` now declares `payload JSONB`. Monthly
  partitions are created with `PARTITION OF`, which copies the parent's column definitions
  verbatim, so every new partition inherits `JSONB` automatically — no per-partition DDL to keep
  in sync.
- **Insert path** — `createActivityLogEntry` binds the payload with `?::jsonb`. The JDBC driver
  sends the parameter as text and text is *not* implicitly coercible to `JSONB`, so without the
  cast a non-null payload insert would fail (and `AuditLog.emit` swallows the error, so it would
  fail *silently*). A null payload casts to SQL `NULL` unchanged. This keeps the column correct
  once non-null payloads start flowing.
- **Existing deployments** — startup detects a pre-existing non-`JSONB` payload column
  (`isActivityLogPayloadColumnNotJsonb`, probed via `::regclass` so it honours the configured
  schema/table prefix) and adds `ALTER TABLE activity_log ALTER COLUMN payload TYPE JSONB USING
  payload::jsonb` to the DDL. Applied to the partitioned parent, Postgres rewrites every child
  partition with the same cast. It is:
  - **idempotent** — guarded on the column not already being `JSONB`, so it never re-runs;
  - **fail-loud** — placed in the *transactional* startup DDL batch, **not** the best-effort
    index backfill (which logs-and-skips failures). An old row holding non-JSON text aborts the
    cast (`invalid_text_representation`), rolls back the batch, and stops the core from starting
    against a half-migrated schema, exactly as the issue requires.

## Tests added

`ActivityLogPayloadTypeTest` (3 tests):
- `freshInstallHasJsonbPayloadOnParentAndPartitionsAndAcceptsJson` — parent and this-month
  partition are `jsonb`; a JSON payload written through the production insert path reads back via
  a JSONB-only operator (`payload->>'k'`).
- `existingTextPayloadColumnMigratesPreservingNullAndValidJson` — reconstructs the legacy
  `TEXT`-partitioned table with a NULL row and a valid-JSON-string row, re-runs
  `createTablesIfNotExists`, and asserts the column becomes `jsonb` with both rows intact (the
  JSON row now queryable as real JSONB).
- `invalidJsonInOldRowFailsMigrationLoudly` — a legacy row holding non-JSON text makes startup
  throw, and the rolled-back column stays `TEXT` (not half-migrated), so a fixed re-run can retry.

## What I ran locally

- `./gradlew :supertokens-postgresql-plugin:test --tests "io.supertokens.storage.postgresql.test.ActivityLog*"`
  against PostgreSQL 16 — **6/6 pass** (the 3 new tests plus the existing `ActivityLogPartitionTest`
  and `ActivityLogUserLastActiveTest`, the latter exercising the `?::jsonb` insert path via the
  last-active mirror).
- Full plugin build via the pre-commit hook (`runBuild`) — success.

## What I did NOT verify

- The full plugin test suite (left to CI).
- Rewrite behaviour / lock duration on a large, many-partition `activity_log` — the table is
  dormant and 31-day-retained so this is small in practice; the CHANGELOG documents the
  `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock and the manual pre-apply option for large deployments.

## Cross-SDK note

This is a PostgreSQL-plugin change. The same `activity_log` DDL and insert path exist in the
sibling storage layers — the MySQL plugin (which would use the `JSON` type and its own text→JSON
cast) and core's in-memory SQLite — and PLAN-010 unit 6 already tracks in-memory parity. Those
ports are **flagged, not made here**.

Part of PLAN-010.

Fixes #378

author: nicknikolakakis
body:
## What

Stage 1 of #190: when a non-empty `.choragos/memory.md` exists, the orchestrator's boot context gains a "Project memory" section pointing at it. Decisions, gotchas, and conventions written there carry into every session instead of being relearned run after run.

## How

- `internal/deck/memory.go`: `memoryNote()`, same shape as `handoffNote()`; empty string when the file is missing or empty.
- `injectBoot` appends it after the recap and handoff notes, so on a resume the order is recap, handoff, memory; on a fresh session it stands alone.
- Docs: "Project memory" section in `docs/long-running-sessions.md` (hand-written today, dated headings suggested, delete/empty to boot stateless).

No config key: absence of the file is the off switch, matching how the handoff document behaves. Works identically with the gateway on or off.

## Verification

- `make test` green (race detector), `golangci-lint` 0 issues.
- Unit test mirrors the handoff-note test: no file / empty file produce no note, content produces the pointer, and `injectBoot` lands it in `orchestrator-context.md`.
- Live verify: headless `serve --detach` with a cat team and a hand-written `memory.md`; the generated `.choragos/orchestrator-context.md` contains the section and the read line.

## Out of scope (follow-up on #190)

Orchestrator-appended entries at deliberate session end, and the injection size cap that only matters once agents write entries.

Refs #190
