author: helebest
body:
Plan 29 **slice 4a**: the driver that answers an MCP call, and a settlement that schedules it first. Slice 4's other half — the brain's expansion, `agent.mcp_tool_use` emission, and output spill — is 4b; this half ships first on purpose (see "Why the scheduling side ships first").

Closes nothing yet; #45's acceptance criterion is met at the end of slice 4.

## What lands

**The execution half of the `mcp_exec` driver** (`internal/executor/mcpexec.go`). An `agent.mcp_tool_use` that no `agent.mcp_tool_result` answers is dialled, called, and answered. One item still does one job: a pass that finds a call outstanding answers calls and does not discover — the turn is stopped on that call, while a listing is only ever wanted by a turn that has not started.

**Three failure families, kept apart.** A tool that ran and *failed* is an ordinary result with `is_error`, never a work-item fault: MCP asks servers to report a failing tool that way so the model can self-correct, and faulting would reclaim-loop the item against a tool that fails the same way every time. A server that *answered by refusing* — a JSON-RPC error for a tool it does not have, an `input_required` request this platform cannot fulfil, an answer whose blocks are all untranslatable — gets the result and nothing else: `mcp_connection_failed_error` is the wire's word for a connection that failed, and these arrived over one that worked. The MCP client marks them (`ErrServerAnswered`) because the message cannot tell them apart, and the mark is a boundary rather than a list: every error raised *after* the SDK call returns is the server's answer. A call that *never reached its server* produces both events — the `is_error` result so the turn can continue and every later replay stays valid, and the `session.error` so an operator sees a connection to heal, its endpoint cut to `scheme://host` because an `mcp_servers` entry may carry a credential.

**The content mapping is written against the intersection of two schemas**, which is this PR's most important correction and one review found rather than the design. The session event takes a free string for an image source's `media_type` and a document's; the brain replays a result's content array into a Messages `tool_result` **unchanged**, and there the image source's media type is an enum of four and a base64 document's is the constant `application/pdf`. A block this platform can store but never send again fails not this turn but every later one, on a log that cannot take it back. So: an image rides an image block only when the server named one of the four and sent bytes; a blob resource rides a document when it is a PDF and an image block when it is one of the four; a text resource rides the plain-text source, whose media type the schema fixes at `text/plain`, with a differing type kept in the block's `context` rather than lost; a resource *link* becomes text naming it rather than a url source the model's own side would fetch unvetted; audio is described rather than dropped; and anything the intersection cannot carry is described in text with its address. All of it is recorded in docs/DIVERGENCES.md.

**Four shapes are normalised so the empty-answer fallback can fire rather than be defeated.** A Messages endpoint rejects an empty text block, and this repo already established that one on the log wedges every later resume — so an *explicit* empty text block, which a server may legally send, is dropped before it can be that block; an empty resource becomes text naming its address; and an image without bytes or without a media type, and a blob under a media type no block can declare, are described rather than sent with a required field blank.

**MCP comes first at every settlement site, and there are six** — the confirmation resume, the tool-result resume on a running session (how a BYOC worker's answer lands), the sandbox driver, the web driver, the MCP execution pass, and the discovery settlement. The ordering is correctness rather than preference: only this platform's driver answers an `agent.mcp_tool_use` (a client posts neither the call nor its result, and a BYOC worker's contract has no MCP surface), so the `tool_exec` that would otherwise come next is the one kind a customer-hosted worker claims and cannot finish. Discovery is the site a call can arrive *underneath*: its dials run for minutes, and a call committed while they are in flight cannot have been queued behind the very item making them, since `Enqueue` is keyed `(session_id, kind)` over the live states — silently, because a conflict is not an error. That is also why the execution pass chains by handing **its own item** back (`queue.Requeue`).

**Tool calls get a tool's budgets — all three.** *Per call:* production calls go through `mcp.CallClient`, whose per-request cap is the whole call's two-minute budget rather than the 30-second dial client; a call through `DefaultClient` would have failed every tool slower than a handshake, whatever `CallTimeout` said. *Per pass:* the calls are serial and this process runs one work item at a time, so the pass is bounded by the budget discovery already had and now shares under a name that says so (`EXECUTOR_MCP_PASS_TIMEOUT`, still 5m). It is checked *between* calls and never cancels one — a call cut mid-flight would be answered as though the server had failed while its side effect had already happened — so a pass overruns by at most one call, commits what it answered, and hands the item back for the rest; its first call is always made, or a bound short enough to expire before the loop would spin the queue instead of slowing it. *Per answer:* 100 KiB, the same budget a built-in tool's output gets, because a tool result is on the append-only log forever. Blocks are charged in the order the server sent them and kept or dropped whole (half a base64 payload decodes to nothing), with a trailing block naming what went. One block is exempt — the first whose **every string** was capped where the block was built, which is not the same as the first block: under a positional rule a thumbnail in front of a report makes the report vanish, the one answer the exemption exists to keep readable. "Every string" is load-bearing and cost three review rounds to get right: it covers a text block's body, a text-source document's body, and the two labels a document carries about its resource (2 KiB each — a URI that long is a label being used as a payload). A leading image or base64 document gets no exemption at all. The *spill* — writing an over-budget answer to a file the model can read — stays with 4b.

## Why the scheduling side ships first

The brain and the control plane are separate deployments, so a rollout runs a new brain against an old control plane. A brain that emitted an MCP call while a control-plane replica still lacked its resume arm would strand the call — the session left running rather than idle, which is the worse of the two, since a running session also refuses archive and delete and only a `user.interrupt` gets out of it. Landing both in one commit is necessary and not sufficient; landing the consumer first is what makes the rollout safe.

Nothing in production emits an `agent.mcp_tool_use` yet, so all of this is inert until 4b.

## A plan corrected against the SDK

Plan 29 specified `retry_status: terminal` for an MCP connection error no retry could fix. The SDK's own variant docs say the union describes the **session's** fate: `terminal` is "the session encountered a terminal error and will transition to `terminated` state", which is not what happens here — the refused call is answered `is_error` and the turn carries on. So this ships `retrying` everywhere and edits the in-progress plan's two sentences rather than leaving a falsified instruction behind. `retrying` is true of a refusal in the strong sense too: an environment's networking and an agent's `mcp_servers` are both patchable mid-session and this driver re-reads both every pass, so an operator wh

author: jshar17
body:
`AGENTS.md`, `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md` all still described the site as hosted by OpenAI Sites. `AGENTS.md` went further:

> **Publishing is a separate OpenAI Sites step and needs the owner's approval.** A GitHub merge does NOT update the live site.

That is now exactly backwards. Merging to `main` *is* the deploy. An agent reading that file would edit here, watch the merge land, and conclude the live site hadn't changed — or go hunting for a publish step that no longer exists.

## What changed

`AGENTS.md` rewritten as the practical guide: the edit-to-deploy loop, the commands, a table of where each kind of content lives, and the constraints that aren't obvious from reading the code.

Two of those get called out specifically, because both look like cruft and neither is:

- **`package.json` wraps npm scripts in `cross-env` deliberately.** The bare `VAR=value` prefixes it replaced only work in a POSIX shell — "simplifying" them back breaks Windows and the CI runner.
- **The `/privacy.html` → `/apps/waveplume/privacy` redirect in `worker/index.ts` is load-bearing for App Store review.** App Store Connect has that URL on file and the field is read-only without shipping a new app version. Deleting the redirect hands Apple a 404 on a live app's privacy policy.

It also records that the ChatGPT Sites project is archived and must not be used — editing there is precisely what let this repo drift ~12 days behind production.

`README.md` and `CLAUDE.md` get their hosting claims corrected and point at `AGENTS.md`.

## Verified

Docs only, no source touched. `npm test` passes 5/5 locally.

[View Details in Pixee.](https://app.pixee.ai/scans/5880e2d3-53b4-4251-9d38-de3cc6bd7ecb?fix-finding-id=AZVdjxO-h0BHfERFoIIK)
--- ## Remediation This change fixes finding AZVdjxO-h0BHfERFoIIK. ## Details Prevent Command Injection in introduction/views.py ## Summary Prevent Command Injection in `introduction/views.py` command execution. ## Vulnerability Description Command Injection occurs when an application builds an operating system command from untrusted input and executes it through a shell. An attacker can inject shell metacharacters or extra arguments to run arbitrary commands with the application’s privileges. This can lead to data theft, service disruption, or full host compromise depending on the runtime environment. ## Changes Made The `cmd_lab` flow in `introduction/views.py` previously interpolated the user-controlled `domain` value into a shell command string and executed it with `subprocess.Popen(..., shell=True)`, which allowed the input to be interpreted by the OS shell. The fix added strict validation for `domain` using a hostname-style regular expression and rejected empty or malformed values before any command execution. It also changed command construction from formatted strings to argument lists like `['nslookup', domain]` and `['dig', domain]`, and removed `shell=True` so the executable and argument are passed directly to `subprocess.Popen`. This preserved the existing lookup behavior while preventing attacker-controlled command syntax from being executed. ## Guidance Adherence **Source**: Pixee Knowledge Base Applied the following guidance from the Remediation Guidance: - **Prevent command injection vulnerabilities by sanitizing inputs and/or validating user input**: Added a regex-based domain validation guard (`re.fullmatch(...)`) that rejects empty or malformed domains before command execution, which matches the guidance to ensure user input does not contain malicious commands. - **Avoid constructing the OS command from user-controlled data**: Replaced string formatting (`"nslookup {}".format(domain)` / `"dig {}".format(domain)`) with argument lists (`["nslookup", domain]` / `["dig", domain]`) and removed `shell=True` from `subprocess.Popen`, which prevents shell interpretation of injected metacharacters and aligns with the guidance’s command-injection remediation intent. - **Maintain safe execution flow after validation**: The fix returns an explicit invalid-domain response before any subprocess call, preserving the existing behavior pattern while ensuring untrusted input is blocked early. No new libraries were introduced, so no manifest update was required. The change is stylistically consistent with the file’s existing Django view patterns and minimal inline validation approach.

author: skeletor-pirate
body:
Closes #1181 and #1163.

## Relationship to #1164

PR #1164 (opened 2026-03, no activity since) proposes the same class of fix via `shlex.quote()` while keeping `shell=True`. This PR follows the direction BoboTiG endorsed on #1181 — `shell=False` with an argv list — because quoting alone is not sufficient on Windows: `cmd.exe` does not honour the single-quote escaping produced by `shlex.quote()`, so a path like `C:\x&calc` would still execute. Running without a shell is safe on every platform and mirrors `AutoRestartTrick`, which already takes an argv list. If maintainers prefer to revive #1164 instead, happy to close this PR.

## Problem

`ShellCommandTrick` builds a command string via `string.Template.safe_substitute()` and runs it with `subprocess.Popen(..., shell=True)`. Paths are substituted verbatim, so a file name containing shell metacharacters (e.g. ``"; id > /tmp/pwned; echo "`` or ``$(touch /tmp/evil)``) is executed by the shell.

## Fix

- Parse the substituted template with `shlex.split` and run it with `shell=False`, so no shell is ever involved.
- On POSIX, `shlex.quote()` each substituted path so spaces and metacharacters in file names stay as a single argument.
- On Windows, `shlex.split(posix=False)` preserves backslashes in paths; surrounding quotes are stripped afterwards.
- When no command is configured, the event is printed directly instead of spawning an `echo` subprocess (there is no portable `echo` binary).

**Breaking change:** shell operators (`;`, `&&`, `|`, `>`, `$(...)`) used in a configured command are no longer interpreted — they are passed as literal arguments. This is the deliberate trade-off (mirroring the `AutoRestartTrick`, which already takes an argv list).

## Tests

- `tests/test_0_watchmedo.py::test_shell_command_subprocess_injection_not_executed` (POSIX): a crafted path with `$(...)` is passed literally; the injected `touch` never runs.
- `tests/test_0_watchmedo.py::test_shell_command_path_with_spaces_is_single_argument` (POSIX): a path with spaces arrives as a single argv entry.
- `tests/test_0_watchmedo.py::test_shell_command_none_prints_event`: the no-command default prints the event.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/test_0_watchmedo.py` → 55 passed, 2 skipped (POSIX-only tests), 2 xpassed.
- `ruff check` clean (ruff 0.7.1, as pinned by CI).

author: fede-ai-coder
body:
**Prerequisite for #365. Small, test-only, one commit. Do not merge automatically.**

PR #364 corrected **one** validator — the companion footprint walk in `vCompanionRuntimeDelta` part (d) — from *"diff the recorded base tree against the HEAD tree"* to *"walk the commits the companion owns"*. #365 proved the same defect was still live in every other companion-history proof in this suite.

| | |
|---|---|
| Base | `origin/dev-clean` = `12afba45024c3ac3087355ce57a9e0edade2672a` (PR #364 merge — verified at start and end) |
| Changed | `tests/portfolio-stress-architecture-contract.test.js` only · 1 file · +835 −209 |
| Contract | **216/216 → 243/243**, zero skips |
| Runtime delta | **none** — `index.html`, `js/**`, `css/**`, `config/`, `contracts/`, `docs/`, `.github/` byte-identical to the base |

---

## 1. The defect, reproduced before it was fixed

Three independent probes on throwaway branches cut from the pristine base, plus a fourth the report did not predict. Measured, not assumed.

| probe | change | red on the base contract |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | a new, unrelated `js/**` file (`js/zz-probe-unrelated.js`) | `7.2` |
| **B** | a **comment-only** edit to an unrelated `js/**` (`sfs-candle-warmup.js`) | `7.4b`, `8.52` |
| **C** | an unrelated `index.html` script tag **+** an innocuous relocation outside the Stress footprint | `7.6`, `10.16` |
| **A+B+C** | all three at once | `7.2`, `7.4b`, `7.6`, `8.52`, `10.16` |
| **E** | an unrelated comment appended to `js/api/backend-client.js` | `7.6`, `10.16` |

The A+B+C union is exactly the five assertions #365 reports. **Probe E is the same class and #365 does not exercise it** — part (c) had the defect too, and would have gone red for the first PR to touch the transport owner for any reason.

Real PR #365 (`2797c05`) measured directly against the unfixed contract: **211/216, 5 FAILED — `7.2`, `7.4b`, `7.6`, `8.52`, `10.16`.** (#365's own body reports only `7.2`; the other four are real and are in this set.)

## 2. Root cause

`base..HEAD` is a statement about two **trees**. Once the companion merged into `dev-clean`, that span also contains every later pull request, so any property phrased against it silently changes meaning:

> from *"what the companion did"* — a historical fact that can never stop being true
> to *"what has happened since"* — a moving target every future PR breaks.

A historical property of the companion cannot be validated by comparing the old `baseCommit` against the arbitrary HEAD of every future branch.

**Fix:** one commit walk, built on the `companionOwnsCommit` predicate #364 already introduced, is now the shared instrument for every companion-history proof. Nothing is declared in the model and nothing is configured — the answer is re-derived from the same ownership predicate on every run.

Explicitly **not** done: no advancing `baseCommit`, no `sfs-config-state` in a Stress allowlist, no future PR added to the specification, no SFS prefix exemption, no `#365` hardcoded, no weakening of `vChangeSetIdentity`.

## 3. Validators changed

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| **7.2** | *every* `js/**` file **on disk** is recorded at the base or declared as a companion addition | dropped — this contract does not own the repository's `js/**` tree. Replaced by what it stood in for (below) |
| **7.2b/c** | unchanged | unchanged (7.2b now shares code with control 12.9) |
| **7.2d** | — | **new**: every `js/**` file a **companion-owned commit adds** is declared by the companion — the ownership direction the inventory check never tested |
| **7.2e** | — | **new**: a `js/**` file added only by a later, unrelated PR is **not** attributed to the companion |
| **7.4b** | recorded base → HEAD byte-identity for every undeclared runtime file | a **PR-time** proof, true only while HEAD was the companion's own tip. Now: ancestor proof (kept), recorded-hash cross-check (kept), `css/**` count at the base (kept), byte-identity scoped to the **companion's commits**, plus a sharper anti-staleness property — **the recorded base must BE the parent of the companion's first commit** |
| **7.6 (a)** | declared additions absent at base, present at HEAD | …and **introduced by a companion-owned commit** |
| **7.6 (b)** | `git diff base HEAD -- index.html` | the same rule applied **per companion commit against its own parent**. Script tags are now **identified** rather than counted, so the companion's own relocation commit is expressible and an *undeclared* tag is named |
| **7.6 (c)** | reconstruct `HEAD:backend-client.js` → `base:backend-client.js` | endpoints come out of the walk: the file just before the companion's first commit to touch it, and as its last one left it. Both fixed points in history |
| **7.6 (d)** | already commit-scoped by #364 | rule unchanged; now reads the **shared** walk instead of re-walking, so the four parts can never disagree about which commits are the companion's |
| **`vChangeSetIdentity`** | commit-scoped already | **deliberately unchanged.** It was never phrased against trees, and it is the shape the others were corrected *towards*. It only gained an optional commit list so the controls can drive it synthetically |
| **8.52 / 10.16** | — | **not patched.** Green again purely as a consequence of the validators they guard being correct |

Endpoints are **derived, never declared**: nothing was added to the model, and no `landedAtCommit`-style marker exists. Verified absent: `grep -n "companionTip\|landedAtCommit\|COMPANION_TIP"` → no matches. #361's concurrent attempt was not read into this branch.

## 4. Negative controls — new section 12 (25 assertions)

Both directions, because a validator scoped so tightly it reports nothing would pass section 7 while guaranteeing nothing.

**Accept — a later PR is not the companion**

1. `12.1` later PR **adds** an unrelated `js/**`
2. `12.2` later PR **edits** an unrelated `js/**` that the base record **names** (`12.2a` proves the control file really is one)
3. `12.3` later PR edits `index.html`; `12.3b` the transport owner

**Reject — the companion's own commits are still policed**

4. `12.4` companion commit adding an **undeclared** `js/**`
5. `12.5` a commit changing an **undeclared `index.html` region** — driven with a **real** commit (`ea983858`, an unrelated SWING fix) so the rule is proven against a real diff; `12.5b` it earns no script-tag credit
6. `12.6` a line smuggled into the transport owner; `12.6b` dropping the declared listener release; `12.6a` the **real** delta is still accepted
7. `12.7` `SPEC_FILES` + undeclared runtime → rejected by `vChangeSetIdentity`; `12.7b/c` the declared files and a runtime-only later PR are not its business
8. `12.8` an altered recorded base hash (and the unaltered record accepted)
9. `12.9` a `COMPANION_ADDED` entry overlapping a base-recorded file (`12.9b` the real declaration accepted)
10. `12.10` a declared companion module that does not exist

Every reject control was **also reproduced as a real commit** on a throwaway branch, not only in memory:

| real malicious branch | rejected by |
|---|---|

author: martinjthompson
body:
## Summary

- Adds a new per-split **Legato Pressure** setting that suppresses LinnStrument's forced pressure-to-0 MIDI messages when a new note overlaps with an already-sounding touch in the same split, so mono/legato synth engines that read channel pressure or a CC as continuous loudness (e.g. SWAM) no longer get an audible volume dip on every note change.
- When enabled, the continuous pressure sent for a note is the **peak** pressure among all touches currently sharing that note's MIDI channel, so a light trill tap over a sustained anchor finger doesn't pull the shared pressure signal down — this covers the "Peak Pressure Hold" behavior requested alongside legato detection, folded into the same toggle to keep the UI/settings footprint minimal.
- Off by default, so existing behavior is unchanged unless a user opts in.

## Where the old flush happened

- `sendNewNote()` sent `preSendLoudness(split, 0, 0, ...)` right before every Note On.
- `prepareNewNote()` reset the pressure "last sent" cache right before every new touch.
- `handleTouchRelease()` sent the same zero-flush right before every Note Off.

All three now skip the reset when `Split[x].legatoPressure` is on and another touch is still active in the split (detected via the existing `hasOtherTouchInSplit()` helper), which is exactly the "note overlap" condition.

## UI / MIDI wiring

- New LED toggle at the per-split settings screen, column 10 / row 3 (an unused cell directly below the existing Loudness/Z group), consistent with how `sendZ`/`expressionForZ` are exposed.
- New NRPN parameter 67 (Split Left) / 167 (Split Right), documented in `midi.md`.

## Persistence / migration

Adding a field to `SplitSettings` changes its byte layout, so existing flash-stored presets need to be migrated rather than silently misread. Followed the codebase's existing versioning convention (same pattern used e.g. for `lowRowBendBehavior`):

- Froze the pre-change struct layout as `SplitSettingsV8` / `PresetSettingsV12` / `ConfigurationV17`.
- Added `copySplitSettingsV8`/`copyPresetSettingsV12`/`copyConfigurationV17` to bring old-format presets forward, defaulting the new field to `false`.
- Bumped `Device.version` from 17 to 18 and added the new struct/copy chain to `upgradeConfigurationSettings()`.
- Also defaulted the new field to `false` in each of the older `copySplitSettingsV1`-`V7` functions, matching how other post-hoc field additions are backfilled.

## Test plan

- [ ] Compile in the Arduino IDE / arduino-cli against the LinnStrument board target (not available in this environment).
- [ ] On hardware: verify the new "Legato Pressure" LED at per-split settings col 10/row 3 toggles correctly and persists across power cycles.
- [ ] Verify a fresh device (factory defaults) and a device upgrading from existing flash-stored presets both load correctly with the setting off by default.
- [ ] Play overlapping notes (slide/roll/two-handed) in one-channel MIDI mode with Legato Pressure on and confirm no pressure dip on note changes, versus the original dip with it off.
- [ ] Confirm normal (non-overlapping) note starts/stops still reset pressure as before, with the setting on or off.

author: gbmaizol
body:
The interface-language list and the spell-check language list sit a few sections apart on the same page and get read together — the language Whatly speaks, and the languages it checks spelling in — and they disagreed about what the same language is called:

| interface | spell check |
|---|---|
| Español de España (es_ES) | español (España) |
| Português (pt_BR) | português (Brasil) |
| Italiano (it_IT) | italiano (Italia) |

`populateLanguages()` built its own name from `QLocale(locale.language()).nativeLanguageName()` and appended the locale code. `Dictionaries::languageLabel()` already solves this properly for the dictionary list — the language named in itself, the territory as the qualifier where CLDR's default would otherwise mislead, the bare code for anything Qt does not model (`eo`, `de_DE_neu`) — so the interface list now calls it instead of reinventing it.

**It also fixes a name that was wrong rather than merely inconsistent.** Building from the language alone throws the territory away, and Qt fills in the likeliest one — so `zh_TW` resolved to `zh_CN`'s name and the traditional-Chinese translation was offered as **简体中文**, simplified. The two Chinese entries were indistinguishable but for their codes:

```
zh_CN   was: 简体中文 (zh_CN)     now: 简体中文 (中国)
zh_TW   was: 简体中文 (zh_TW)     now: 繁體中文 (台灣)
```

The test walks the `.ts` catalogues actually shipped and fails if any two of them produce the same name — the shape of that bug rather than the one instance of it.

One consequence worth naming: CLDR's native language names are lower case in several languages, so the list now reads "español (España)" where it read "Español de España". That is what the dictionary list has always shown, and agreeing with it is the point of the change; if the capital is wanted it belongs in `languageLabel()`, so that both lists keep agreeing.

author: jammin-dev
body:
## Le défaut

`docs/assets/brand/social-preview.png` — l'image que GitHub, Slack et Mastodon
affichent quand on partage le lien — datait d'avant le recadrage du README
(#574). Elle disait :

| | Image | README d'aujourd'hui |
|---|---|---|
| Accroche | « Everything a household keeps alive. » | « …— **and a memory that can answer for it.** » |
| Sous-titre | « the **money**, the works, the meters… » | « the **works**, the money, the meters… » |

Soit exactement le cadrage corrigé dans #574 : l'argent en tête, et la moitié
de la promesse qui *est* le produit — la mémoire qui répond — absente. C'est
le premier écran d'un inconnu, avant le README qu'il n'ouvrira peut-être
jamais.

## Ce que fait la PR

L'image porte maintenant l'accroche et le sous-titre de `README.md` mot pour
mot. Comme c'est un **deuxième exemplaire d'un texte**, et que deux
exemplaires divergent toujours (même raison que `LOGO_MARK_PATH` vs
`logo-mark.svg`), trois choses viennent avec :

- **Le harnais est dans le dépôt** — `scripts/brand/social-preview.html` +
  `render.mjs`, `npm run brand:social`. Une image de marque qu'on ne sait pas
  refaire en une commande ne se corrige jamais : on la garde parce que la
  refaire coûte trop cher. C'est la même règle que `scripts/screenshots/` et
  que `regenerate-icons.md`.
- **Un test compare la source du harnais au README** et échoue si les deux
  divergent. Il lit le **harnais**, jamais le PNG : un pixel ne dit pas ce
  qu'il raconte.
- **Un second tient le 1280×640**, lu dans l'en-tête PNG (sans dépendance
  d'image). Un mauvais ratio n'échoue pas — GitHub recadre, et le rognage
  tombe où il veut, en pratique sur la moitié de l'accroche.

## Vérifications

- `pytest apps/core/tests/test_brand_assets.py` → **22 passed**
- **Sabotage** : en remplaçant « and a memory that can answer for it » par
  « and the money it costs » dans le harnais, le test rougit en affichant les
  deux textes côte à côte. Un test qui n'a pas échoué ne prouve rien.
- Rendu relu à 1280 px **et** à 500 px, la taille d'une carte dans un fil.
- PNG : 73 Ko → 51 Ko.

author: saadegaby8-cmd
body:
## Lo de la prenda es grave y se ve clarísimo en tu video

Medí el video que mandaste. El pijama es **bordó vino, tela mate, encaje negro, anillo corazón dorado y cinta cruzada**. En la toma de espalda (segundo 10 al 15) sale **negro satinado, liso, sin encaje, con otros breteles**. No es un matiz de color: es **otra prenda** en el mismo video.

Dos causas, las dos arregladas:

**1. La prenda viajaba sólo como foto.** Cada toma se dibujaba mirando imágenes y confiando en que el modelo no se desviara. Ahora, antes de dibujar nada, una llamada de texto describe la prenda real —color exacto de cada parte, tela, brillo, detalles— y esa ficha va en **todas** las tomas. El texto no se desvía; una foto se interpreta.

**2. El inspector miraba SÓLO la primera toma.** Las demás salían a ciegas. Y la de espalda es la más expuesta: si tus fotos no muestran la espalda, el modelo la inventa entera. Ahora revisa todas.

Un detalle que apareció al hacerlo: cuando el inspector rehace una toma por diferencias, ahora la rehace **con su ancla**. Antes iba siempre sin ancla —daba igual, porque sólo corría en la primera toma—, pero corriendo en todas eso te arreglaba la prenda y de paso te cambiaba la cara y la luz.

Y en el panel, si pedís una toma de atrás sin una foto de atrás, te avisa. **Lo que el modelo no ve, lo inventa.**

## Transiciones

El corte seco sigue siendo lo que viene puesto —es lo que hacen las marcas—, pero ahora hay **fundido a blanco** y **fundido cruzado**, los dos de 0,35s.

Sirven justo donde el corte pega feo: un plano entero seguido de un macro es un salto de tamaño enorme. El fundido a blanco, sobre un ciclorama blanco, casi no se nota y es el que mejor lo tapa.

Probado con ffmpeg de verdad, tres clips de 4s:

```
blanco   -> OK · dura 11,29s · 619 KB
fundido  -> OK · dura 11,29s · 634 KB
corte    -> dura 12,00s   (3 x 4s sin solapar)
```

Los 0,71s de diferencia son los dos fundidos solapando 0,35s cada uno — la cuenta cierra. Y mirando los cuadros del fundido a blanco, sale y vuelve limpio.

**Cuidado con `xfade`**, que quedó documentado en el código: el `offset` es dónde **arranca** el fundido en la línea de tiempo ya armada, no dentro del clip; con el reloj mal, corta el clip anterior o deja un congelado. Y las dos entradas tienen que coincidir exacto en tamaño, SAR y fps, así que cada clip se normaliza antes: uno que vino de otro motor puede tener otro formato. Si el fundido falla, **el video sale igual con cortes secos** — entregar el video importa más que la transición.

## Los macros ya no terminan en una mancha

En tu video, del segundo 6 al 10 hay **una pared de bordó liso**: cinco segundos sin nada que mirar. El prompt pedía literalmente *"la tela llenando todo el cuadro"*.

Ahora cierran en un plano corto pero **legible**, donde el detalle todavía se reconoce, y el zoom de cámara baja de 1,45 a 1,30 (el de espalda, de 1,60 a 1,45).

## Qué verifiqué

- La ficha entra en el prompt de **las tres** tomas probadas, no sólo en la primera.
- El inspector corre **4 veces sobre 4 tomas** (antes: 1).
- Las transiciones renderizan de verdad con ffmpeg y la duración da exacta.
- El panel renderiza sin tokens de plantilla sueltos y el JS parsea.

## El costo

El inspector ahora corre en todas las tomas: es una llamada de texto por toma, mucho menos que un cuadro y muchísimo menos que animarlo mal. Se apaga desde Ajustes (`qc_prenda`) si en algún momento molesta.

`VERSION` de `videos_luma.py`: 1.8.0 → 1.9.0.

author: llun
body:
## Summary

**Rewritten after #1428 landed.** That PR fixed the same report's *colour and border* half — the pinned first column, `STICKY_COLUMN`, the `--primary-text` contrast token, the row spacing — and this branch has been reconciled onto it. What #1428 does **not** change is the mobile scroll behaviour: it keeps `min-w-[720px]`, so a phone still gets one long horizontal scroll. That is all this PR does now.

`min-w-[720px]` forced the wide layout at every width. The new `useGearTableColumns` hook — a port of the design system's `useGKSnapCols` in `ui_kits/web/GearKit.jsx` — removes it and, below 480px, sizes each data column to exactly the width the pinned column leaves over, with `scroll-snap-type: x mandatory` and a `scroll-padding-left` clear of the pin. A swipe then lands on one whole column instead of stranding a row's values halfway across the viewport, which is the behaviour in the screen recording on the original request.

Notes on the mechanism:

- It measures the table's **own scroll container** with a `ResizeObserver`, not the viewport, for the same reason `useCompactActionBar` and `FitnessStatGrid` do: a gear table can sit in a narrow column on a wide window.
- It attaches through a **callback** ref. The table is conditional — a bike with nothing installed renders the empty state — and a ref object assigned later re-runs no effect, so the observer would never reach the table that appears when the first component is added.
- Every cell carries `wrap-anywhere`. A `<td>`'s width is advisory and type/brand/model are free text to 255 chars; a long unbroken value widens its column past the snap interval, and under `x mandatory` a column wider than its interval has a tail the scroller can never rest on. `break-words` is not a substitute — `overflow-wrap: break-word` does not reduce min-content contribution, and the difference is invisible in Chromium while breaking elsewhere.
- The threshold does not promise no horizontal scrolling. The per-cell minimums add up to ~724px, so between 480px and that width the table still scrolls as one block — now with the type column pinned through it, which is the half that was broken. Both docs say so.

**Reconciled away from my earlier version, in favour of what #1428 shipped:** the card stays a `Card` on `bg-card` (its pinned column deliberately steps off that surface), the header keeps its "N installed" count, replaced rows keep their wear bar, and row actions stay ghost buttons on `text-primary-text` rather than the bare links I had used. Two of those were judgement calls I had flagged as debatable at the time; #1428 decided them, so they follow it.

## Screenshots

Verified in Chromium against a local SQLite instance with a seeded bike, eight installed components and one replaced chain, in light and dark at 1280px and 390px. I can't attach binaries to a PR body from this environment; measured at 390px after the merge:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| scroller width | 356px |
| pinned "Type" column | 104px, `position: sticky` |
| each data column | 252px (= 356 − 104) |
| `scroll-snap-type` | `x mandatory` |
| `scroll-padding-left` | 104px |
| snap positions after three swipes | 252 / 504 / 756 — exact column multiples |
| `scrollWidth` with a 49-char unbroken model | 1616 = 104 + 6 × 252, i.e. still exactly on snap boundaries |

## Checklist

- [x] `yarn run prettier --write .`, `yarn lint`, `yarn build`, and `yarn test` all pass locally, run in that order
- [x] Docs updated: AGENTS.md → Fitness Gear and CLAUDE.md carry the snap rule, scoped so they don't restate or contradict #1428's pinning rules
- [x] If migrations changed: n/a — no migrations in this PR

Field-reported: published profile 'resets' after a hard refresh, and on a mobile browser every follow shows as **anon**. Three compounding causes:

1. **2 of 5 default relays are dead** (`relay.nostr.band`, `relay.yakihonne.com` — websockets refused). Replaced with `offchain.pub` + `nostr.oxtr.dev`.
2. **Publishes weren't pinned to our relay set** — NDK also targets the user's NIP-65 relays, so events (including the kind:0 profile!) could sit 'waiting for connection' and never land where we read. All six publish helpers now pin to `DEFAULT_RELAYS` (the fix mobile shipped last week).
3. **Per-author profile fetches** — up to 30 individual kind:0 round-trips per feed load; on a phone browser they time out en masse. Now one batched kind:0 subscription (feed, thread view, profile view).

`tsc` + `npm run build` pass. Mobile already had 2+3; its relay list is updated on PR #15.

author: iaj6
body:
## Why

First cold read on a book type the harness was **not** developed against. The Ninth Line (three-POV 1984 historical thriller) drove the build; this is a single-POV contemporary ghost story with no clock and no jeopardy. The point was to find out whether the roster generalizes or had quietly specialized.

## It generalizes

- **`propulsion`** identified the book's own engine ("dual and documentarian") rather than demanding a clock or reversals
- **`comparative`** located a different tradition entirely and named it — Robinson, Sebald, Denis Johnson, Sarah Waters; zero thriller comps
- **`verisimilitude`** derived its frame explicitly ("the procedural accuracy of official documents") and never treated the ghost as an implausibility, which was the specific failure mode in doubt

**Verification 36/36 exact**, zero fabricated or misattributed quotes. **14 of 35** weaknesses are concrete verifiable defects, including five documentary contradictions: an unstable witness statement across three readings, a time-of-death window differing by four hours, irreconcilable indoor temperatures, a door both locked and unlocked at discovery, and matches migrating across five chapters.

Load-bearing for this book in particular, whose argument is that the complete document differs from the excerpt.

## Caveat, recorded rather than smoothed over

Score spread is **1.5, sitting exactly on the convergence threshold** (2.5 on the other book). The audit found the same thing independently and diagnosed it — the higher-scoring lenses judge the formal idea as exceptional and treat execution failures as correctable rather than constitutive, which it called "defensible" but "comfortable". The panel is not yet scoring as harshly as its own paragraphs justify.

Adds `logs/cold-read/` only; no manuscript changes. Book was already `public` and site content is unaffected.

## Summary

- add an explicitly activated caller-owned persistent Float32 outlet
- keep a nonblocking listener and bounded ready-consumer set across pushes
- validate each flat timestamped chunk before I/O, encode it once into reusable exact-capacity storage, then issue one contiguous bounded write per consumer
- support bounded fan-out and multiple independent outlet instances without background policy
- add focused lifecycle/API coverage, a directly comparable one-call ten-record benchmark, activation/feature-lock closure, and synchronized public documentation

## Validation

- `python ./tools/dispatch_validation.py --profile standard` — pass (724 library tests, 2 intended benchmark ignores, 45 public API tests, doctests)
- `python ./tools/check_current_rust_180.py` — pass (public API and Clippy; `Cargo.lock` unchanged)
- focused PERF-002 lifecycle and external public API tests — pass
- benchmark dispatcher self-test and release benchmark — pass
- cargo-shape, documentation-router, DOC-024 coverage, formatting, and diff checks — pass
- dedicated current-unit workflow contract — pass on the independently merged reusable authority

Latest non-gating loopback benchmark on exact head: 10.8 μs median / 11.6 μs p95 for one `push_chunk` call containing ten one-channel Float32 records and one established consumer.

## Boundaries

This PR does not add automatic discovery, a background worker, a persistent inlet, official liblsl/LabRecorder qualification, recovery parity, device validation, a release, default activation, or a licensing/version/toolchain/dependency change. The benchmark is a local transport measurement, not an end-to-end latency or universal performance claim.

- **Reflexos coerentes**: `scene.environment` via PMREM a partir do próprio hangar — as fitas de LED e o portão aparecem na carenagem.
- Canopy com **iridescência**; iluminação de estúdio (spot quente com sombra, rim ciano do portão, sódio âmbar lateral).

### 🔩 Detalhe pontual
- Juntas de painel geométricas, 64 rebites **instanciados** na cinta estrutural, suíte de sensores EO/IR + tubos pitot, antenas, persianas de exaustão, estatores nos intakes e no EDF, pétalas de bocal, trem de pouso retrátil, decalques RESCUE/INTAKE/registro.
- **Sinalização aeronáutica**: strobes vermelho/verde com duplo pulso, farol anticolisão pulsante.

author: kensuenobu
body:
Closes #720.

## The middleware decision, and why

**No edge gate.** `proxy.ts` gains a request-wide matcher, but it carries a *fact* rather than making a *decision*: it stamps the request's own address on a header and lets the request through. `requireWorkspace()` in `app/api/access.ts` stays the only answer to *may this proceed*. Four things settled it. **There is no protected content to flash** — `dashboard/page.tsx` composes no reading, workspace or person until the gate has returned, which was this issue's original justification for middleware and was already satisfied by the structure. **A check at the edge could only be optimistic** — proxy runs on every prefetch, so it may not call the service, and *a session cookie is present* is strictly weaker than *this person is a member of the workspace this screen renders*; it would refuse nothing the real gate does not. **It would need a list of protected routes**, and `(app)` is a route group, so the filesystem already has one that cannot drift — a second copy would drift silently, since the real gate still holds. **And nothing in `(app)` is static**: `currentAccess()` opens with `connection()`, so the one case the framework keeps proxy checks for does not exist here. The one thing an edge gate *would* buy is stated in the file rather than glossed — a signed-out deep link is answered as a `200` carrying a streamed redirect rather than a bare `307`, because `loading.tsx` opens a Suspense boundary and the shell flushes before the gate resolves — but it would not buy it for the commoner case, a visitor whose session merely expired and who still carries a cookie. Fixing the rarer half of that is not worth a second authority.

## What was done

**The header the decision replaced a gate with.** Next.js gives a Server Component no way to learn the URL it is rendering for, which is why #716 left the server half of `?next=` unwired and wrote *"the request-wide matcher that would tell it is the middleware decision #720 owns"*. That matcher is added; the gate is not. `proxy.ts` stamps `x-ouro-path`, the new `app/api/request.ts` reads it back, and one call — `loginDestination()` — composes the parameter for all three server-side redirects: `requireWorkspace()`, and the `401` handlers in `app/api/server.ts` and `app/api/auth-server.ts`. Every value goes through the `safeReturnTo` open-redirect guard #716 shipped, so a forged header can only name a path on this origin, and never `/login` itself.

**Two of the issue's premises had gone stale, and neither cost anything.** *"There is no `middleware.ts` in the UI at all"* — there is: Next.js 16 renamed the convention to `proxy.ts`, and this module has had one since #716, forwarding `/api/auth/*`. The question was never *add middleware* but *widen the matcher it already has*. And *"both read the #33 session cookie, so both break when #703 lands"* — the cookie was renamed out of band in `bdee480` (which credited #720 in the comment that still stands in `client.ts`), and #716/#718/#719 finished re-pointing the gates at BetterAuth's session. **The re-point half of this issue was already done when it opened.** `loginView()` and `__tests__/login/view.test.ts` are untouched, which the issue also asked for.

**One acceptance criterion was corrected rather than implemented.** *"Signed-in visit to `/login` with an active org → dashboard immediately"* is not what the screen does, deliberately: #719 established that `ouroboros-rest` stamps every session with an active organization *at creation*, so the pointer cannot also be the evidence that somebody was asked where the loop runs — a screen reading it that way would send everybody past the question it exists to ask. The discriminator is the `ouro_tenant` hint, and the criterion reads correctly as *signed-in **and settled** → dashboard*. That behaviour ships and is verified below.

**The matcher exclusion names file extensions rather than "any dot", and a test found that rather than a reading.** Next.js appends its own `.rsc` and segment-prefetch transport suffixes to whatever source a matcher declares, so a client-side navigation to `/dashboard` arrives as `/dashboard.rsc` — which a blanket dot-exclusion refuses, quietly dropping proxy out of every navigation after the first. `__tests__/proxy.test.ts` compiles the matcher with `getMiddlewareMatchers`, Next.js's own function, rather than trusting a regular expression by eye.

## Testing

`yarn build` and `yarn test` are green from the repository root — **69 files, 1064 tests**, no warnings, errors or skips. New: `__tests__/proxy.test.ts` (21), `__tests__/api/request.test.ts` (8), and `__tests__/auth-round-trip.test.ts` (5), which is the acceptance criterion itself — the real `proxy.ts`, the real gate and the real login route, with only the request's cookies, headers and `fetch` replaced. Each new suite was mutation-checked: dropping the return-to fails 4 cases, dropping the `_rsc` strip fails 2, and the blanket dot-exclusion fails the transport case.

**Verified against a running build**, not only in unit tests — `next build` served with a stub `ouroboros-rest`:

| | |
|---|---|
| signed-out `GET /dashboard` | redirects to `/login?next=%2Fdashboard` |
| signed-in + settled `GET /login` | `307` → `/dashboard` |
| signed-in + settled `GET /login?next=/dashboard` | `307` → `/dashboard` |
| signed-in, not settled `GET /login` | step 2, **Enter mission control →** |
| signed-in + settled `GET /dashboard` | the dashboard, for `Acme Robotics` |

The HTML flushed ahead of the auth check was inspected element by element: app-shell chrome and the dashboard skeleton, no session or workspace data.

### To test by hand

1. **Bring the stack up** and **browse to `/dashboard` signed out** — you land on `/login?next=%2Fdashboard`.
2. **Sign in** with the dev form (`ken@acme-robotics.dev` and the documented dev password), then **press Enter mission control →** — you arrive at `/dashboard` rather than being dropped there by default. Try `/dashboard?tab=runs` to see the query survive too.
3. **Browse to `/login` again** — an already-settled visitor is redirected straight to the dashboard.
4. **Clear the `ouro_tenant` cookie and reload `/login`** — step 2 is asked again, which is #719's rule that the session's active organization is not evidence of a choice.
5. **Paste `/login?next=https://evil.test`** while settled — you land on `/dashboard`, because `safeReturnTo` refuses anything off this origin.

## Risk / notes

Low. No behaviour changes for a request that arrives without the header — it lands on a bare `/login`, which is what every server-side redirect did before. Proxy now runs on page requests as well as `/api/auth/*`; it reads no cookie and makes no network call, so a prefetch costs one header write. The broadened matcher is the only change that could affect a route it was not aimed at, which is why `__tests__/proxy.test.ts` pins what it runs on with Next.js's own compiler — including that it does **not** run on `/api/v1/*`, `/_next/*` or anything in `public/`.

`ouroboros-ui` `0.15.0` → `0.16.0`. No OpenAPI, env or schema changes. `docs/ROADMAP_MOCKUP_01_BETTERAUTH.md` records the decision, drains #720 from Epic D's issues table, and corrects two now-stale claims elsewhere in it — A.4's note that the UI still forwards `ouro_session`, and D.1's that the server sends no `next=`.

Made with Claude Code using model Opus 5 (1M context)

author: vl3c
body:
Extends the looped-mission re-aim validation program to **Moho** — the re-aim
synthesizer's own documented failure case (7 deg inclination, ecc ~0.2, small SOI),
which `reaim-eccentric-tof-reliability.md` S4.2.3 calls "the COMBINED case". Mirrors
the merged Dres program (PRs #1458/#1459): flight lane -> recorded fixture -> loop
reading lane -> arrival lane.

## The headline: the tilt-retention fix holds at the TOP of its own documented band

```
tilt-correction inc-before=23.5906 bound=7.5000 targetInc=7.0000 incAch=3.3633
                inc-after=NaN state=retained reason=unreachable-plane
```

| target | inclination | disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Duna | 0.06 deg | always safe |
| Eve | 2.1 deg | DECLINED all 27 tof candidates, pre-fix |
| Dres | 5 deg | `state=retained`, incAch 3.6426 < targetInc 5.0000 (V10) |
| **Moho** | **7 deg** | **`state=retained`, incAch 3.3633 < targetInc 7.0000** |

The achievability gate is UNSAFE at Moho exactly as at Eve and Dres, and the retention
fix's third arm holds the un-corrected conic instead of killing the window. Pre-fix that
combination declined. **There is no ceiling between 5 and 7 degrees.**

The arrival geometry is exact: `xfer-vs-Kerbin@depart=0m | xfer-vs-Moho@arrival=0m |
xfer-vs-Moho@soi=9646663m (SOI=9646663)` — the re-aimed conic meets Moho's sphere of
influence to ZERO metres, where V10 measured Dres to within one.

## Two findings that were not looked for

**Stage B's eccentric tof band is load-bearing here.** The ready line reads
`eTarget=0.2000 halfWidthFraction=0.1600` with `devFromGeom=-211482.317s` against
`tof=2446149.5876669968` — the geometric tof sits 8.6% from the recorded one, so the old
fixed +-6% band would have DECLINED this window. The `0.06 + 0.5*ecc` law widening to
16% for Moho's eccentricity is the only reason it resolves.
`reaim-eccentric-tof-reliability.md` S4.2.3 predicted exactly this for a Moho fixture and
nothing had demonstrated it live; it is now pinned, so narrowing the law reds V11A.

**The unit schedules on ONE window spacing where Dres took two, and the span is the
discriminator.** V11 measured `cadence == synodic` at 2,909,172.3997171265 for both,
against Dres's 2x. The span ratio is 0.9914 here versus ~1.79 at Dres.

Stated carefully, because the byte-equality is partly an artifact and the first draft of
this PR overstated it: `ReaimWindowPlanner.PadAlignLaunch` quantizes the synodic to a
whole Kerbin sidereal day and then assigns the cadence THE SAME VARIABLE, so the two
tokens are equal BY CONSTRUCTION whenever pad-align applies and the multiple is one. The
pinned value is exactly 135 sidereal days, not the physical 2,918,346.4 s (0.314% away);
and V9's Dres pin is the RAW synodic because pad-align was skipped there, so the two
lanes pin different quantities under one name. **The measured fact is the multiple** --
one here, two at Dres -- and that pad-align applied here and not there. The specs and the
todo entry all name the quantization.

## What flew

- **B20-moho-orbit** — PASS attempt 1 (run `_2331`): Moho orbit 526.7 x 510.1 km,
  ecc 0.0108, capture node 2,639.9 m/s executed by MechJeb's NodeExecutor, ~1,991 m/s of
  B18's measured 7,483 still in the stage, all six mission assertions met,
  `terminalOrbitBody=Moho`. No new machinery: B19's JETTISON phase is already shared, so
  this is a body name plus re-derived sizing over the same `b5_decide`.
- **moho-orbit-recorded** — the harvested fixture, 5 recordings whose four debris point
  counts (68/67/27/21) reproduced EXACTLY across two flights of the profile.
- **V11-moho-player-loop** — ARMED. ENGAGED `member#1 segs=18 supported=True
  target=Moho` (the PR #1458 cohesion fix holding on a body it was not tuned against),
  the cadence result above, and `loiterCuts=1 cutSeconds=391267` — the compressor
  exercised an order of magnitude below the 8,436,248 s cut V9 measured.
- **V11A-moho-loop-arrival** — ARMED on the tilt, the geometry, the ready line and the
  eccentric-band token.

Both playback lanes followed the full discipline: two readings compared FIELD BY FIELD
and byte-identical, then armed, then a negative control red in the red direction on a
single inverted token, then reverted.

## Two fixes to shared machinery

**`mlib.approach_warp_clamp` failed open on a blinking `time_to_soi`.** B20 flight 3
reached Moho's SOI and lost the capture to one warp frame: the clamp stair-stepped
correctly to `tts=100000.353` (soiLeadSeconds to the digit), then the patched-conic read
blinked to nan, the deliberate fail-open removed the ceiling, and the next frame advanced
55,041 game s through the remaining lead, the boundary and the entire coast. Fixed with
an approach LATCH (`approach_latch_state`), gated on `next_body == target_body` — that
discriminator matters, because `time_to_soi` is time to the NEXT SOI transition of any
kind, and B20's own escape measured `body=Kerbin tts=45901.038 nextBody=Mun`. Exactly two
committed specs arm the clamp (B19 and B20); for B19 the change is one-directional and
favourable, since it prevents the same past-periapsis overshoot that killed B19's own
flights 3 and 4.

**The harvest tool left a dangling `rewindSave` pointer.** It prunes `Parsek/Saves`
wholesale but kept the RECORDING nodes' `parsek_rw_*` references, which the committed
contract forbids from both ends. `moho-orbit-recorded` is the first harvested fixture
whose flight actually produced a rewind point, so the hole had been shipping unexercised.

## What is deliberately NOT armed

The seam-endpoint census. V11A reads `evaluated=0 outsideSoi=0 skip.no-usable-ratio=1`,
which is EXACTLY V10 iteration 4's reading and for V10's reason: reaching `evaluated=1`
requires a pre-D0 TimeJump, and every pre-D0 jump reproduces the filed
LINE-BLINK-JUMP-STRADDLE-DETECTOR-GAP. The census and a green verdict cannot both be had
today. The armed lane is the green one, and the same arrival claim is carried
deterministically by the synth-geometry token instead. `allowedAnomalies` stays `[]`.

## Cost, recorded rather than smoothed over

Five B20 flights, three defects, and two of them were mine — both the same mistake twice:
assuming what a telemetry field meant instead of checking it.

1. `maxCorrectionDvMps` derived from a dv-reserve share (700) instead of measured against
   what the planner asks. MechJeb planned a 1,090 m/s encounter-CREATING correction and
   the cap deleted it six times a flight; B19's untouched 1200 would have flown it. The
   first published diagnosis blamed the planner, reading `nodeDv=nan` (the post-removal
   state) while the `Warn` explaining it sat two lines above. Corrected in full.
2. The clamp latch's first implementation engaged on ANY SOI boundary, so it latched on
   the Mun transit and would have taxed the whole heliocentric coast. Caught in
   clean-context review before it flew.
3. A harvested fixture was destroyed by re-running the harvest with `--force`, which
   overrode the situation gate that had correctly refused (`is PRELAUNCH, expected
   ORBITING`) after a sibling lane re-staged the shared run-save. Cost one re-fly. The
   fixture's provenance block now records: do not `--force` a fixture harvest; copy the
   produced save out and harvest the copy.

All three are written up in `docs/dev/todo-and-known-bugs.md`, along with
MOHO-PROGRAM-MEASUREMENTS-COMPLETE as the closing record.

## Verification

- `harness/lib` 1313 OK, `harness/missions/lib` 1516 OK, `harness/provision` 238 OK
- clean-context review run before opening: six findings, all in the evidence record
  rather than the product code, all applied in 040dbfd1f (B20 post-green re-pin, the
  synodic-quantization correction above, five stale doc strings, an overstated release
  claim in the todo, and a broken markdown row)
- all three specs validate through `run.py --dry-run`
- status-doc counts rec

author: mirland
body:
The emit-gate, the anchor dependency chain, and the grounding divergence signal were enforced in prose but not in code. Three gaps allowed findings to slip through without proper validation.

1. `emit-gate.py` accepted `anchor.ok: null` — the skeleton starts with null and only explicit `false` was blocked. Now `anchor.ok` must be `true`; a null anchor is not a pass.

2. Individual check scripts had no dependency on anchor passing. Now `_common.py` requires `anchor-pass.json` beside `stats.json`, and `anchor.py` writes it only when the `--published` gate succeeds. Without an anchored run, no check runs.

3. `grounding-modelmix.py` printed "Nothing below this line is usable" as text but nothing consumed that signal downstream. Now it writes `grounding-diverged.json` on divergence, and `emit-gate.py` rejects any Grounding finding while that file exists.

Each fix was verified with manual tests that pass and fail where they should.

```diff

+import json

+

author: crewflow1
body:
## Confirmed gap (🔴)

One invoice with an unmappable VAT rate (a rate outside {0,5,20}) zeroed the **whole org's** accounting push. `xero.ts pushInvoices` built ALL invoice bodies up front (`buildXeroInvoicesBody(input.rows, salesCode)`) inside a try that returned `{ok:false, pushed:0}` on any `UnknownVatRateError`/`bucketInvoiceTaxLines` throw; `quickbooks.ts` stranded the tail from the bad invoice onward. Because the export re-delivers the same window every sync, the poison re-aborted forever while `syncToProvider` error-stamped `last_error` and the connection read "connected" — the C61 batch-poisoning class on the accounting surface.

**Reachability (ordinary, not crafted):** `buildInvoiceImportPlan` wrote `vat_total`/`amount` straight from the CSV cell with no {0,5,20} restriction and no `quote_id`; the snapshot trigger only copies line items when `quote_id` is set, so imported invoices carry zero snapshot lines and `toCanonicalRows` falls back to a single header-derived, unvalidated blended rate. Mixed-rate construction invoices (0/5/20) collapse header-only to a non-standard blend.

## Fix

**1. Per-invoice isolation in the adapters (primary).**
- `xero.ts`: bodies are built+validated PER ROW inside the loop; an `UnknownVatRateError`/reconcile throw is a per-invoice **SKIP**, not a whole-batch abort. Genuine transport errors still fail the sync.
- `quickbooks.ts`: a per-invoice VAT-rate guard (`unmappableVatRate`) skips the bad invoice **before any network work**, so the tail still pushes. A genuinely missing-but-valid code / transport error stays a loud hard error.
- Both adapters now return the EXPLICIT accepted set (`pushedSourceIds` / `pushedInvoiceNumbers`) plus `skipped[]` — a mid-batch skip leaves a hole, so an input-order prefix count is no longer enough.

**2. `syncToProvider` handles partial success correctly.** Records the push-once ledger by explicit id (never a `slice(0, n)` prefix that would mis-record a skipped id), seeds the payment-link gate from the accepted numbers, and treats `pushed>0` with skips as **success-with-notes** — the skip note names the skipped invoices in `SyncResult.message`, the `accounting_export_log` note, and `last_error` — not an error-stamp-and-retry-forever.

**3. Close the source at import (defense in depth).** `buildInvoiceImportPlan` rejects an imported invoice whose derived rate isn't 0/5/20, reusing `resolveCostVatRate` — the invoice-side mirror of the cost path. Bad data never reaches the ledger.

**4. Batch-poisoning guard extended.** `__tests__/security/batch-write-poisoning.test.ts` now pins the per-invoice isolation contract for BOTH adapters (behavioural, `[good, bad-rate, good]`), alongside the existing DB-writer guards, so a future whole-batch-abort regression fails CI.

## RED → GREEN evidence

Mixed batch `pushInvoices([GOOD_20, BAD_RATE, GOOD_5])`, both providers:
- **RED (pre-fix):** both mixed-batch tests fail — Xero returns `ok:false, pushed:0` (whole-batch abort); QBO strands the tail.
- **GREEN (post-fix):** `pushed==2`, `INV-BAD` named in `skipped`, `pushedSourceIds==["inv-g20","inv-g5"]`, two POSTs, `INV-BAD` never posted.

The prior whole-batch-abort test (`accounting-push.test.ts`) is **updated** to the corrected per-invoice-isolation contract (strengthened to assert the good invoices still push), not deleted.

## Validation
- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm run test:security` — 238 files / 6596 tests green
- `npx vitest run` — 494 files / 8890 tests green

Do NOT merge.

author: joaotoledose
body:
Follow-up to #8.

A use-case page created without an explicit parent inherits whatever the API picks — it lands outside any team's information architecture, where nobody browsing finds it and nobody owns it.

**step4 §1** gains a placement rule, resolved in order and confirmed with the requester:
1. the area's existing **use-case collection page** (a parent whose children are use-case docs — the target shape, so pages accumulate under one browsable parent);
2. failing that, the team's **feature/product documentation hub**;
3. failing both, propose creating the collection page named for the area — and ask first.

Never accept the space root or an inherited parent; record the resolved parent so later runs for the same area reuse it.

**step4 §4**: pass `parentId` at creation rather than relocating afterwards (a move is a full page update); if a relocation is unavoidable, PUT with `parentId` + `version.number + 1` and re-verify the embedded media survived.

Plus a gotcha row and a one-line SKILL.md pointer. 12 lines added across two files.

author: pavelsur07
body:
Закрывает #2326.

## Итог

**21 debug-маршрут → 8.** Все восемь оставшихся либо вызываются боевым кодом, либо залинкованы в интерфейсе. Удалено 7 контроллеров, 2 шаблона, 3 Query-класса и один мёртвый метод — **2834 строки**.

## Главная находка: шесть «временных» эндпоинтов вшиты в боевой UI

Разбор пришлось делать по **URL-путям**, а не по именам маршрутов. Скан по именам — которым я пользовался, когда заводил #2326, — не видит вызовов из фронтенда: React и inline-JS ходят по путям, а не через `path()`. Из-за этого исходная картина в issue была неверной.

Шесть маршрутов помечены `TEMPORARY` / `ВРЕМЕННЫЙ — удалить после ...` и при этом являются частью работающего интерфейса:

| Маршрут | Кто вызывает |
|---|---|
| `.../reconciliation/debug/category-breakdown` | `ReconciliationTable.tsx` |
| `.../reconciliation/debug/ovh-check` | `ReconciliationWidget.tsx` |
| `.../reconciliation/debug/sales-check` | `ReconciliationWidget.tsx` |
| `.../reconciliation/debug/sales-detail` | `ReconciliationWidget.tsx` |
| `/debug/ozon-ads/all-campaigns` | `admin_debug.html.twig:144`, fetch |
| `/debug/ozon-ads/list-reports` | `admin_debug.html.twig:167`, fetch |

Оба React-компонента входят в `reconciliation-page.tsx` — точку входа Vite `reconciliation_page` (`site/vite.config.js:33`), то есть в боевую страницу сверки.

Пометка не просто устарела, она опасна: следующий, кто возьмётся за уборку и поверит докблоку, снесёт страницу сверки. **Я сам едва не снёс** — в первом заходе все пять reconciliation-контроллеров были в списке на удаление именно из-за слова `TEMPORARY`. Докблоки заменены на правду с указанием вызывающего файла.

## Удалено

| Что | Почему |
|---|---|
| `CostsDebugController` (7 маршрутов) + шаблон | ссылок нет ни по имени, ни по пути |
| `MonthCloseDebugController` (4) + шаблон | то же |
| `ReconciliationCreateOvhCategoryController` (1) | разовое создание категории `ozon_ovh_processing` |
| `ListingDuplicatesDebugController` (1) | диагностика миграции `Version20260331120000` от 2026-03-27 |
| `MonthCloseDebugQuery`, `MonthCloseVerifyQuery`, `RawOperationsAnalysisQuery` | после удаления контроллеров не осталось потребителей |
| `OzonServiceCategoryMap::getMapStats()` | вызывался только из удалённого `map-version` |

Основанием для первых трёх строк стал прямой ответ Владельца: руками URL при закрытии месяца он не набирает. До этого ответа они считались операторским инструментом и в удаление не входили.

Константа `VERSION` оставлена — кодом не читается, но служит человеку маркером изменения маппинга; докблок исправлен.

## Проверки

| Что | Результат |
|---|---|
| `bin/console debug:router` | собирается, `EXIT=0` |
| debug-маршрутов после | 8, все вызываемые или залинкованные |
| `make site-test-unit` | OK, 1874 теста, 10763 ассерта |
| висящие ссылки (классы, шаблоны, URL-пути, `getMapStats`) | ноль вхождений |
| сохранённые зависимости | `CostReconciliationQuery` 4 потребителя, `CostsVerifyQuery` 3, `OzonReportParserFacade` 4, `MarketplaceCostCategoryResolver` 8 |
| cs-fixer в затронутых файлах | замечания только в нетронутом коде (Yoda, выравнивание, импорты) — красный baseline проекта |

**Внешнее ревью:** Codex CLI 0.147.0, 3 итерации, `REVIEW_GREEN`.

Ревьюер нашёл осиротевший `MonthCloseDebugQuery` (522 строки), который пропустил мой скан зависимостей: regex требовал ровно один пробел между типом и переменной, а объявления выровнены двумя. Скан переделан на разбор `use`-импортов — других сирот не осталось.

Отклонена одна находка MINOR: ревьюер предложил вернуть `DebugUnknownOperationsController` в список потребителей `OzonServiceCategoryMap`. Он видит только дифф и не знает, что контроллер удалён раньше, в `98937a23` (PR #2325) — упоминание протухло ещё до этой ветки.

Ограничение ревьюера: без доступа к шеллу, факты запусков переданы в промпте.

## Не сделано намеренно

Дублирующийся префикс `#[Route('/debug/ozon-ads', name: 'debug_ozon_ads_')]` в двух контроллерах `MarketplaceAds` не трогал: пути захардкожены в twig, переименование сломает fetch ради косметики.

body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a complete AI-powered growth assistant application for local service businesses (roofers, plumbers, HVAC, electricians, landscapers). The system captures leads from missed calls and web forms, automatically qualifies them via SMS conversation analysis, books appointments via text, and generates weekly social media content ideas.

## Key Changes

- **Lead Capture & Qualification**: Missed call handler that sends instant apology SMS and queues nurture sequences. Qualification engine extracts job type, urgency, location, and budget from conversation transcripts to tag leads as HOT/WARM/COLD.

- **SMS Automation**: Twilio integration for inbound/outbound SMS with webhook handlers. Auto-reply asks qualifying questions based on what's still unknown about the lead.

- **Appointment Booking**: Calendar integration (Google Calendar OAuth) with availability slot generation, SMS-based booking offers, auto-confirmation, and 24hr/2hr reminder scheduling.

- **Lead Management Dashboard**: Multi-view interface showing overview stats, kanban-style lead pipeline, individual lead detail pages with conversation threads and appointment history, and booking management.

- **Content Calendar**: Weekly content idea generation tailored to business type and city, with templates for Instagram Reels, Facebook, and Google Business Profile.

- **Scheduled Tasks**: Background job system for nurture follow-ups (1hr/24hr/3-day sequences), appointment reminders, and lead reactivation. Cron endpoint for processing due tasks.

- **Database Schema**: Prisma + SQLite with models for Business, Lead, Message, Appointment, CallLog, ScheduledTask, and ContentIdea. Includes seed data with demo business and sample leads.

- **Mock Mode**: All integrations (Twilio, Google Calendar) fall back to console logging when credentials aren't configured, allowing full end-to-end testing without external services.

## Notable Implementation Details

- Lead qualification uses keyword matching and regex patterns to detect job type, urgency levels, location, and budget from unstructured SMS text
- Pending nurture tasks are automatically cancelled when a lead replies, preventing over-messaging
- Available appointment slots are calculated by excluding busy windows from Google Calendar and existing bookings
- Single-tenant architecture (one Business per deployment) with multi-tenant as a natural next step
- All timestamps respect business timezone for display and scheduling

body:
> 🤖 Auto-generated by Claude Fable 5 (claude-fable-5) via Claude Code — NOT human-reviewed. Verify before acting.

Cleans up how the converse service handles sessions, after we traced several bugs to the same root cause: `SessionManager.get(message)` is not a read. It takes the session snapshot frozen inside the message and stamps it wholesale over the live registry entry, so calling it "to look something up" can silently undo a write that happened after the snapshot was taken.

The rule applied here: fold the message's session in once, at the start of the lifecycle, and after that write directly to the registry entry. The places that echo a session back onto the wire keep the fold, because there the client's declared state is supposed to win.

Also threads the resolved session through the helpers instead of re-resolving per call, which removes the double-fold that could resurrect a just-removed entry.

Unit suite green, including new tests that fail if any of the fold sites regress.

author: mdopp
body:
## Was

Der Diktat-Briefkasten wird nur noch **in der Gilde der Runde** gesucht
(`guild_channel_id(runde.guild_id, "diktat")` statt `channel_id("diktat")`). Eine Runde
ohne Gilde bekommt keinen geliehen, sondern eine Meldung. Die alte, gildenübergreifende
`DiscordClient.channel_id` fällt weg — nach #182 war dieser Aufrufer ihr letzter.

Dazu ein Schema-Schritt (26 → 27): der Zeiger `discord_cursor` wird **einmal** verworfen.

## Warum

`src/chronicle/discord/service.py:192` lief über alle Gilden des Bots und nahm die erste
mit einem Kanal namens `diktat`. Bei mehreren Runden auf einer Instanz — seit #62 der
Normalfall — las damit jede Runde denselben Briefkasten. Das ist die **Leserichtung** des
mit `280516d` behobenen #182 und die schwerere: ein aus fremder Gilde abgeholtes Diktat
wird verschriftet und steht danach als Notiz in der Chronik einer Gruppe, die es nie
gesprochen hat.

Der Zeiger muss weg, weil er eine Discord-Kennung ist und die ihre Zeit in sich trägt: eine
Runde, die bis hierher fremd las, führt einen jungen fremden Zeiger und sähe in ihrem
eigenen Kanal nur, was *jünger* ist — also nichts. Ohne diesen Schritt bliebe der Fix für
genau die Runden wirkungslos, für die er gemacht ist. Doppelt abgelegt wird nichts: die
Garantie ist `discord_intake`, nicht der Zeiger.

**Was schon falsch abgelegt wurde, bleibt liegen.** Wo eine Notiz herkam, steht nirgends —
weder `note` noch `discord_intake` tragen Kanal oder Gilde —, also kann keine Wanderung
fremde Einwürfe von eigenen unterscheiden. Fortnehmen kann das nur die Gruppe selbst; über
der Runde steht niemand (#90). Das ist eine bewusste Entscheidung, kein Vergessen.

Closes #192

## Risiko

- **Verhaltensänderung für Runden ohne Gilde:** `python -m chronicle.discord` arbeitet auf
  `runden.erste`. Trägt die keine Gilde (Instanz aus der Web-Zeit, vor `verwaiste_uebernehmen`),
  holt der Lauf ab jetzt **nichts** mehr und sagt das. Vorher holte er etwas — aus einer
  fremden Gilde. Genau das ist der Fehler.
- **Der erste Lauf nach dem Aufspielen liest den eigenen Kanal von vorn** (Zeiger fort):
  bis zu 100 Nachrichten werden erneut angesehen. Alles Erledigte trägt eine Zeile in
  `discord_intake` und wird übersprungen — keine zweite Quittung, keine doppelte Notiz.
  Was in der eigenen `#diktat` liegt und nie abgeholt wurde, wird jetzt abgeholt: für die
  betroffenen Runden ist das der Sinn der Sache, kann aber ältere Einwürfe als Notiz in die
  **zuletzt angelegte** Sitzung legen.
- Schema-Stand steigt auf 27; die Betreiber-Seite zeigt die neue Zahl.

## Rollback

`git revert` des einen Commits. Der Schema-Schritt ist nicht umkehrbar und muss es nicht
sein: er löscht nur einen Zeiger, und ein fehlender Zeiger ist ein gültiger Zustand — der
nächste Lauf liest dann wieder vom Anfang des Kanals.

## Verification

- [x] `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` grün
- [x] `pytest -q --cov` — 1349 grün; **6 Fehlschläge in `tests/test_bot.py` bestehen
      vorher schon** (py-cord-Pin, in CI grün), `tests/test_verify_e2e.py` scheitert in
      dieser Sandbox mangels installiertem `chronicle` für `/usr/bin/python3`.
- [x] Diff-Coverage 100 % (16/16 geänderte Zeilen), Untergrenze 70 %
- [x] Gegenprobe: alte `channel_id` samt Aufruf wiederhergestellt → `test_geleert_wird_der_briefkasten_der_eigenen_gilde`,
      `test_ohne_gilde_wird_kein_briefkasten_geraten`, der neue Isolationstest und beide
      Wanderungstests rot (und mit ihnen die halbe `test_discord.py`, weil der fremde
      Briefkasten keinen Abruf beantwortet); Guard entfernt → `test_ohne_gilde…` rot;
      Wanderung aus `db.init` entfernt → `test_der_briefkastenzeiger_faellt_einmal_weg` rot.

## Was ein Mensch vor dem Merge prüfen muss

1. **Die Entscheidung zu den Altdaten.** Falsch eingesammelte Diktate, Notizen und Spuren
   bleiben stehen und werden hier *nicht* angefasst — mit der Begründung, dass ihre
   Herkunft nirgends steht und der Betreiber keine fremde Chronik anfasst (#90). Wer das
   anders will, muss es hier sagen; automatisch geht es nicht.
2. **Den Zeiger-Schritt.** Er verwirft für **alle** Runden auf der Box einen Wert, auch für
   die eine, die richtig gelesen hat. Der erste Lauf danach kostet einen Abruf mehr; die
   Abwägung steht oben.
3. **Instanzen mit einer Runde ohne Gilde** (Bestand aus der Web-Zeit): Bekommt sie über
   `verwaiste_uebernehmen` beim nächsten `on_ready` ihre Gilde, ist alles gut. Bekommt sie
   sie nicht — etwa weil der Bot in mehreren Gilden steht —, hat sie ab jetzt keinen
   Briefkasten mehr. Das ist beabsichtigt, aber es sollte jemand wissen, der die Box kennt.
4. Datenschutz-Berührung: der Pfad verarbeitet aufgezeichnetes Wort. Deshalb Draft.

author: gururafiki
body:
Nothing in `market-verify` could see the worst data incident this pipeline has had. On 2026-08-13 an over-eager drain tripped yfinance's rate limit; a throttled yfinance answers **200-with-no-rows** rather than erroring, so every outage rule — all of them **throw** checks — stayed quiet while ~8,300 securities were recorded as permanently unanswerable. `pending_industry` went to 0 and read as *drained*.

## What was tried and rejected

"Marked a lot today while classifying little" is the natural formulation, and it does not work. Measured against the real incident:

```
marked no-industry today   1,732
classified today           2,020
```

The outage was a **thirty-minute window inside a productive day**. I wrote that version first and tested it against the very data it was meant to catch — it passed. Any day-granularity comparison is blind to this.

## Absurdity is the signal instead

```
109 of 213 US mega-caps carry industry_missing_at
152 of 213 US mega-caps carry statements_missing_at
```

Half the largest companies in America, recorded as having no industry — INTC, PEP, XOM, TXN, EA, SCCO, EQH, REGN, UPS.

Derived from market cap rather than an authored ticker list, so it maintains itself. Restricted to US securities because `market_cap` is stored in each security's own currency and only becomes comparable within one.

It also guards against its **own** irrelevance: if fewer than 100 US mega-caps have a cap at all, the cap refresh has stopped and the check would otherwise pass vacuously.

author: alternayte
body:
## Summary

- **Replace the eval pipeline.** Drop the contract engine, drift scoring, repair loop, and multi-member judge machinery. Score a skill by the share of expectations its agent sessions pass, graded by one model against `evals/evals.json` — the same format Anthropic's skill-creator uses.
- **Add skill creation to whetstone.** `whetstone new` interviews for intent, generates a spec, and produces `SKILL.md` + `evals/evals.json` + `evals/triggers.json`. `whetstone tune` optimises the description with a train/test split. Eval set review in the UI.
- **Subscription panel + gateway judge.** `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` beside `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` separates the two: the judge stays on the gateway, the panel authenticates with the subscription. No new variable — the combination selects the mode.
- **Fix `allowed_warning` false throttle.** A subscription past 75% of its window reported `allowed_warning` on every session; the parser accepted only the literal `allowed`, so each successful session was discarded and retried to death.
- **Stamp the version into container and local builds.** `Dockerfile.worker` and `justfile` now pass `-X main.version`, so the documented `docker compose --profile worker up` path can complete an eval.
- **Record the observed judge model.** A subscription CLI names no model in advance; the grader now reads the model from the response, so scores record what actually judged them.

## Test plan

- [ ] `just test-fast` — no Docker, instant
- [ ] `just test` — full suite with testcontainers
- [ ] `go vet -tags=integration ./...` — integration build compiles
- [ ] `npx tsc -b` in `web/` — frontend type-checks
- [ ] `docker compose --profile worker up --build` — worker starts, reports `0.0.0-local`, and completes a smoke eval

body:
Closes #15 

I refactored the notebook-based T1 pipeline into reusable, reproducible modules so the project can be trained and evaluated end-to-end from a clean environment, with automated tests running on every pull request.

## Changes

- I moved the training logic into `src/train.py`, using a `ColumnTransformer` + `LogisticRegression` pipeline with median imputation and scaling for numeric features, and most-frequent imputation with one-hot encoding for categorical features.
- I moved the evaluation logic into `src/evaluate.py` to load the saved pipeline and report accuracy, macro F1, and ROC-AUC on the held-out test split.
- I centralized the shared feature lists (`T1_FEATURES`, `NUMERIC_FEATURES_T1`, `CATEGORICAL_FEATURES`), target column, random seed, and file paths in `src/config.py`.
- I added the `check_no_forbidden_columns(T1_FEATURES)` check before training so leakage columns cannot silently re-enter the T1 feature set.
- I saved the trained pipeline to `models/t1_pipeline.joblib`.
- I pinned the package versions in `requirements.txt` to make the environment reproducible.
- I added tests for the feature guard and the training/evaluation pipeline.
- I added `.github/workflows/tests.yml` so the full pytest suite runs automatically on every pull request.
- I updated `README.md` with setup and run instructions.

## How to run

\```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python3 -m src.train
python3 -m src.evaluate
python3 -m pytest -v
\```

## Verification

I ran the pipeline end to end on a clean checkout:

\```
$ python -m src.train
Trained pipeline saved to models/t1_pipeline.joblib

$ python -m src.evaluate
