author: trueeyu
body:
## Why I'm doing:

`order_by_types` is a dead constructor parameter on both sort context factories, and it has never actually been read:

- It was introduced with partition topn (#6118) as `_order_by_types` on `LocalPartitionTopnContextFactory` / `LocalPartitionTopnContext`, but was only stored and forwarded — `ChunksSorterTopn` never took it, so it never affected behavior.
- #12812 ("Fix clang complains 3") removed the dead members, and removed the parameter from `LocalPartitionTopnContext`, but left it in `LocalPartitionTopnContextFactory`'s signature.
- #18551 unified both factory signatures so `TopNNode::_decompose_to_pipeline` could dispatch over them as a template parameter, which copied the already-dead `order_by_types` into `SortContextFactory` as well. It is unused there too — note the sibling parameters in that constructor already carry `[[maybe_unused]]`, and `order_by_types` was simply missed.

Unlike `is_merging`, this parameter is not needed to keep the two factories signature-compatible for the templated dispatch, since neither side uses it.

## What I'm doing:

Removing `const std::vector<OrderByType>& order_by_types` from the constructors of `SortContextFactory` and `LocalPartitionTopnContextFactory`, and dropping the corresponding argument at the single construction site in `TopNNode::_decompose_to_pipeline`.

`TopNNode::_order_by_types` itself is kept: it is still initialized in `TopNNode::init()` and passed to the sink operator factories (`PartitionSortSinkOperatorFactory` / `LocalPartitionTopnSinkOperatorFactory`), which do use it to build the sorters.

While here, `SortContextFactory`'s `has_outer_join_child` is marked `[[maybe_unused]]` for consistency with the sibling parameters in the same constructor. That one must stay in the signature: `LocalPartitionTopnContextFactory` really does use it (it drives `_has_nullable_key` for the partitioner, added by #56432), and both factories go through the same template instantiation.

No behavior change — this only removes parameters that were never read. `python3 build-support/check_be_module_boundaries.py --mode full` is clean.

body:
Closes BAK-40

Tenant bazlı girişin (BAK-36) 1. fazı: şema, migration ve giriş çekirdeği. UI yok — bu faz bittiğinde e-postasız bir kullanıcı **API/servis katmanında** giriş yapabiliyor.

## ⚠️ Migration etkisi

`prisma/migrations/20260813120000_tenant_login_identity`

| Değişiklik | Etki |
|---|---|
| `Workshop.loginCode` (NOT NULL, unique) | Kolon önce nullable eklenir, **mevcut tüm atölyeler için isimden slug üretilir**, sonra NOT NULL + unique index konur. Çakışmada `-2`, `-3` soneki. |
| `User.email` → nullable | Mevcut e-postalar aynen kalır; `User_email_key` korunur (Postgres çoklu NULL'a izin verir). **Kimse giriş kaybetmez.** |
| `User.username` + `@@unique([workshopId, username])` | Yeni, nullable. Kullanıcı adları global değil, tenant içinde benzersiz. |
| `User.mustChangePassword` | Yeni, `DEFAULT false` — mevcut satırlara dokunmaz. |
| CHECK `User_identity_present` | Her kullanıcının `email` veya `username`'i dolu olmalı. Mevcut veri zaten uyumlu. |
| CHECK `User_privileged_role_requires_email` | `owner`/`manager` e-postasız olamaz — **rol yükseltme yolunu da kapatır**. |

**Geri alma:** CHECK kısıtları + index'ler düşürülüp yeni kolonlar DROP edilir. `User.email` tekrar NOT NULL yapılacaksa önce e-postasız kullanıcılar temizlenmelidir — yani tek yönlü güvenli değil.

**Doğrulama (gerçek Postgres 16 üzerinde çalıştırıldı):** temiz DB'ye tüm migration'lar uygulandı; ayrıca migration ÖNCESİ veriyle (Türkçe adlar, aynı isimli atölyeler, yalnız emoji, rezerve kelime, 20+ karakter ad) doldurulmuş bir DB'ye uygulanıp backfill sonucu incelendi:

```
Şahin Oto Servis          → sahin-oto-servis
Şahin Oto Servis          → sahin-oto-servis-2
ŞAHİN OTO SERVİS          → sahin-oto-servis-3
🚗🚙                       → atolye
demo                      → atolye-2        (rezerve kelime)
Anadolu Yakası Profesyo…  → anadolu-yakasi-profe
Anadolu Yakası Profesyo…  → anadolu-yakasi-pro-2
---Öz-Güven---            → oz-guven
AB                        → atolye-3
Çiğdem & Işık Otomotiv!   → cigdem-isik-otomotiv
```

Üretilen 10 kodun tamamı uygulama tarafındaki `isValidWorkshopCode()` doğrulamasından geçiyor (SQL slug'ı ile TS slug'ı uyumlu). `prisma migrate diff` → **No difference detected** (şema ile migration birebir). CHECK kısıtları tek tek denendi: kimliksiz kullanıcı, e-postasız `manager`, e-postasız `usta`'nın `manager`'a terfisi ve aynı tenant'ta tekrarlanan kullanıcı adı reddedildi; e-posta eklendikten sonra terfi geçti.

## Giriş çekirdeği (`src/lib/auth-login.ts`)

- `verifyCredentials({ identifier, password, workshopId })` — girdi `@` içeriyorsa **bugünkü e-posta akışı birebir aynı**; içermiyorsa `(workshopId, username)` ile çözülür, yani çağıran taraf iş yeri kodunu çözmüş olmalı (`resolveWorkshopIdByLoginCode`).
- Bilinmeyen kullanıcı adında da sahte bcrypt karşılaştırması korunuyor (zamanlama sızıntısı yok), hata mesajı jenerik (kullanıcı adı enumerasyonu yok). Bilinmeyen iş yeri kodu da aynı jenerik hataya düşer.
- `isActive`, `approvalStatus`, plan kilidi kontrolleri hiç değişmeden aynı yoldan geçiyor.

## Rate limit

Bugün yalnız IP bazlıydı ve dakikada 8 denemede kesiyordu: tek atölye wifi'sinden giren 6 usta aynı kovayı paylaşıyor, biri şifresini yanlış girince hepsi kilitleniyordu. Artık:

- IP kovası **8 → 40/dk** (paylaşımlı NAT'ı taşır)
- yanına `(workshopId, kullanıcı adı)` bazlı **8/dk** kova — asıl kaba kuvvet freni bu, ve bir ustanın hatası ekibi etkilemiyor.

## İş yeri kodu üretimi

Tek modül (`src/lib/workshop-code.ts`): üretim + format doğrulama + rezerve kelime listesi (`login`, `api`, `app`, `admin`, `www`, `demo`, `invite`, `payment`, `s`, `p`). Format küçük harf `a-z0-9-`, 3–20 karakter. Üç çağrı yerinin hepsi kullanıyor — `api/checkout`, `api/auth/register`, `prisma/seed.ts` — ve çakışmada `P2002` yakalanıp sınırlı sayıda yeniden deneniyor (`generateOrderReference()` deseninin aynısı). Kod v1'de uygulama içinden değiştirilemez.

## Null-safe hâle getirilen `user.email` kullanımları

`src/lib/admin.ts` (`requireAdmin` artık `AdminUser` döner, `email: string`), `api/auth/forgot-password` (**e-postasız kullanıcı bu akışta hiç eşleşmez** — `canReceivePasswordReset` kapısı), `settings/team/actions.ts`, `settings/page.tsx`, `dashboard/page.tsx`, `components/settings/security-info.tsx`. Ek olarak e-postasız kullanıcı yüzünden bilgi kaybı doğacak üç yer düzeltildi: denetim kaydında actor artık "sistem" diye görünmüyor, ekip/admin listelerinde kullanıcı adı gösteriliyor, admin listesindeki "iletişim e-postası" sütunu e-postası olan üyeyi seçiyor.

## Kapsam dışı

Ekip paneli UI (P1), `/w/<kod>` giriş ekranı ve wizard'daki kod alanı (P2), `Technician` bağı (P3). Giriş formu hâlâ `email` alanı gönderiyor; rotalar `identifier`'a düşerek geriye dönük uyumlu kalıyor.

## Testler

Yeni: `src/lib/workshop-code.test.ts`, `src/lib/user-identity.test.ts`, `src/lib/auth-login.test.ts` (prisma sahte istemciyle değiştirilip `verifyCredentials`'ın gerçek kodu çalıştırılıyor) — kullanıcı adıyla doğru/yanlış şifre, tenant izolasyonu, kod olmadan eşleşmeme, pasif koltuk, e-posta yolunun değişmemesi, e-postasız kullanıcının şifre sıfırlamada eşleşmemesi, owner/manager e-posta zorunluluğu ve hesap bazlı rate limit.

`bun run typecheck` ✅ · `bun run lint` ✅ (0 error) · `bun test` ✅ 1042 test · `bun run build` ✅

## Manuel QA

1. `bun run db:seed` — demo atölyenin kodu `demo-oto-servis`, e-postasız `usta` hesabı açılır (şifre `admin123456`).
2. `POST /api/auth/login` → `identifier=usta`, `workshopCode=demo-oto-servis`, `password=admin123456` → `{ success: true, mustChangePassword: false }`.
3. Aynı istek yanlış şifreyle → jenerik hata; `workshopCode` olmadan → "iş yeri kodu gereklidir".
4. Mevcut e-postalı giriş (`admin@bakimx.com`) hiç değişmemiş olmalı.

author: julius-babies
body:
Closes #43

Devices standing close together used to draw their pins on top of each other. They are now grouped into one bundle that shows their images side by side, each still opening its own device.

## How the grouping is decided

In screen space, not in coordinates — two devices a street apart cover each other at city zoom and stand clearly apart a few zoom levels in, so the answer is recomputed on every camera move.

Two pins are bundled when their overlap covers more than 65% of the smaller one **in both dimensions**. Both, not either: pins at the same height share their whole vertical range however far apart they stand, so "one dimension is enough" bundles pins that merely touch at the edges. In practice they now bundle at roughly 20 px horizontally and 23 px vertically. Overlap is transitive (union-find), and merging repeats until nothing changes, because a bundle is drawn wider than the pin it grew out of and can reach a neighbour neither member did alone.

The web app's threshold lives in one constant, `BUNDLE_COVERAGE` in `web/src/lib/app/shell/map/pin_bundling.ts`; the app takes it as a parameter with the same default.

## The spread circle

Zoomed far enough out, a bundle can stand for devices that are nowhere near each other. Past 10 km apart the map draws the circle they lie in — full border, translucent body, in a blue of its own — and the bundle is anchored at the top of it instead of hiding its middle. Real geodesy (widest pair sets the circle, then widened until nothing sticks out) and real distances, so the circle keeps covering the same ground at every zoom.

## Android

The grouping and the circle live in `commonMain/utils/` free of Mapbox and Compose, so iOS can pick them up later. Only the drawing is platform code.

Everything drawn is derived from the devices and the camera on every composition: one annotation per device for as long as that device exists, bundling only decides what it shows and where it sits; bundles are anchored geographically rather than at a projected pixel; no animation touches opacity, so a marker can come out slightly small but never invisible.

## Not verified in the running app

The web app was checked against a live dev server. The Android side is compile-checked only (`:app:shared:compileAndroidMain`, `compileCommonMainKotlinMetadata`) — worth a run before merging, in particular opening a device out of a bundle and navigating back.

author: jcfs
body: Ten of the thirteen unconditional sleeps under `tests/office` were hand-rolled API poll loops; each one burned wall-clock when the backend was fast and gave up early when it was slow. They are now `expect.poll`, and the three that genuinely cannot be event-driven are labelled with why. ## Important Changes - **Ten `while (Date.now() < deadline) { …; setTimeout(500) }` loops became `expect.poll`** — same polling, but with Playwright's timeout handling and a real failure message instead of a silent fall-through to a bare assertion. Where a loop captured a value for later assertions (route attempts, agent comment, routing profile) the capture is preserved and commented, so the assertions still read the last observed value without an extra request. - **Three are labelled rather than converted**, each with the reason it cannot be event-based: - `onboarding-task-launch` asserts an invariant on **every** iteration (the session must never reach FAILED/CANCELLED before launch). `expect.poll` would drop that per-iteration guard, so the loop keeps sampling. Marked `poll-interval`. - `realtime-dashboard` waits past the window in which a cross-workspace event could trigger a refetch, then asserts none occurred. Marked `negative-assertion`. - `agent-run-detail` injects 800 ms into a mocked paginated-runs response so the pending UI is observable. This is not a wait at all — the delay is the stimulus under test. Marked provisionally; it becomes an `injectLatency(…)` call once that helper lands. Owners can upload their own mark, replacing the emoji.

**Precedence — uploaded logo → emoji icon → nothing** — lives in one `RestaurantMark` component rather than at each of the three places a mark appears, so a restaurant can't end up showing its logo on the menu and an emoji in the navbar.

`logo_url` and its anon grant are **already on production and dev**, applied before this branch could merge. Merging code that selects a column production lacks is exactly what took the customer menu down twice.

pnpm prod:check

It diffs dev against production — columns, **anon grants**, tables, functions, policies — then fetches a real customer menu from production and fails if it's showing its error page.

`ordering-data.ts` selects an explicit column list, so the logo appeared in the navbar (which uses `select("*")`) but **not** on the customer menu. Third time that list has been the gap — the check above now covers the grant half of it, and the query half is why the list is worth watching.

## Summary

Introduces a compositional session identity model. Sessions have a **role** (what they are) and **capabilities** (additive grants).

### Roles
| Role | Tools | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `master_orchestrator` | 24 | Primary session or `allowMainTools` — full access |
| `session_owner` | 13 | Spawned session with its own thread — the work unit |
| `factory_builder` | 6 | Restricted — born to build, report done, defend review |
| `protocol_guest` | 8 | Restricted — visitor in another session's thread |

### Capabilities (additive on `session_owner`)
| Capability | Adds |
|---|---|
| `protocol_context` | `advance`, `extend_phase` |
| `factory` | `factory_build/retry/accept/abandon/status/review` + `spawn_session`, `kill_session`, `create_thread` |

### Key changes
- `SessionRole` and `SessionCapability` types exported from `bridge-tools.ts`
- `computeToolsForSession` builds tool set from role + capabilities, not "all minus exclusions"
- Factory tools are a **capability grant**, not a default — plain `session_owner` can't call `factory_build`
- Backwards compatible: legacy booleans (`isGuest`, `allowMainTools`, `scopedToolOverrides`) infer the correct role

### What's NOT in this PR
- `SessionRole`/`SessionCapability` are not yet stored on `SessionInfo` — role is inferred at tool-computation time from legacy booleans. Step 2: declare at spawn time, replace booleans.

## Files
- `daemon/bridge-tools.ts` — identity model, tool sets, rewritten `computeToolsForSession`
- `daemon/__tests__/protocol-scenarios.test.ts` — tests updated to match new semantics

author: adrianjiga
body:
`http://localhost:3000/qa` served the **portfolio homepage** instead of the QA section — with a 200, which is worse than a 404 because nothing looks wrong.

## Cause

Two settings combine:

- `rollupOptions.input` contains only `./index.html`
- Vite's default `appType: "spa"` rewrites any extensionless request that misses a file to `/index.html`

So `/qa` matched no file and fell through to the portfolio. Production never had this problem — GitHub Pages answers `/qa` with a `301` to `/qa/`. This was a dev-only divergence, which is the annoying kind: a link written without a trailing slash works when deployed and silently shows the wrong page locally.

## Fix

A `pagesStyleDirectoryRedirects` plugin issuing the same 301 Pages does. It's registered inside `configureServer`, which Vite runs **before** its own middlewares, so the redirect happens ahead of the SPA fallback. It only fires when the directory actually contains an `index.html`, and it resolves the candidate path before touching the filesystem so `..` can't escape the project root.

## Verified against a running dev server

| Request | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `/qa` | 200, portfolio homepage | 301 → `/qa/` → QA Resources |
| `/qa/helpers` | 200, portfolio | 301 → QA Helpers |
| `/qa/helpers/webtables` | 200, portfolio | 301 → Web Tables |
| `/qa?x=1` | 200, portfolio | 301 → `/qa/?x=1` — query preserved |
| `/` | portfolio | unchanged |
| `/js/main.js` | 200 | unchanged |

## Deliberately not changed

`/doesNotExist` still returns the homepage with a 200, because the SPA fallback is untouched. Making genuine misses 404 means `appType: "mpa"`, which changes behaviour for every unmatched path — a separate decision from fixing directory URLs, so I left it alone and documented it in CLAUDE.md.

author: nickyleach
body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is the open source app people use to manage AI agents for work
> - The server provides issue APIs and the database stores issue child rows
> - The issue delete endpoint removes the parent issue before dependent rows
> - Several issue foreign keys had no delete policy, so PostgreSQL returned a foreign-key error
> - This pull request adds safe cascade and set-null policies and a clear conflict response
> - The benefit is reliable issue deletion with a useful error when a restricted audit row still blocks deletion

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

Fixes #7728
Fixes #4660
Fixes #7991
Fixes #4627
Fixes #5086

**What happened?**

`DELETE /api/issues/:id` returned HTTP 500 when dependent comments, thread interactions, read states, inbox archives, feedback votes, or ledger rows referenced the issue. The database raised SQLSTATE 23503 because several foreign keys had no delete policy.

**Expected behavior**

The endpoint must remove dependent rows that have no meaning without the issue. It must keep ledger rows with a null issue reference. It must return HTTP 409 when a restricted decision audit row still references the issue.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Create an issue.
2. Add a comment or thread interaction that references the issue.
3. Send `DELETE /api/issues/:id`.
4. Observe the HTTP 500 response.

**Paperclip version or commit**

Commit `1f8f456f8340823fe2bd891ae8933d942f190b7b`.

**Deployment mode**

Local dev with embedded PGlite or external PostgreSQL.

## What Changed

- Add `CASCADE` to five issue child foreign keys.
- Add `SET NULL` to the finance and cost event issue foreign keys.
- Keep decision audit references restricted.
- Map SQLSTATE 23503 from the issue delete service to HTTP 409.
- Add migration 0217 for the seven changed tables.
- Add regression tests for cascade deletion and restricted decision references.

## Verification

- Run `pnpm --filter @paperclipai/db typecheck`.
- Run `pnpm --filter @paperclipai/server typecheck`.
- Run `npx vitest run src/__tests__/issue-remove-cascade.test.ts` from `server/`.
- The regression test applies migration 0217 to a fresh embedded PostgreSQL database.

## Risks

- Migration 0217 changes only seven foreign keys that reference `issues.id`.
- Cascade deletion removes child rows that cannot exist without the parent issue.
- Set-null preserves finance and cost ledger rows.
- Decision audit rows remain protected, so the endpoint can return HTTP 409.

## Model Used

Codex, based on GPT-5, with tool use and code-review support. The implementation author used an AI coding agent. This PR handoff uses the same model family to validate the commit and manage the pull request.

author: alexefimov
body:
## Summary

A document dropped by the post-LLM dedup was neither `processed` nor `skipped`, so `failed_count = total - processed - skipped` collected it **by remainder**. Eight working sources therefore sat in a permanent false `degraded` with a four-digit `fail_count` and a `last_error` describing a failure that never happened. That misreading already cost time once: during the R8 deploy the signal was read aloud as "content processing has been stuck for a while", and only a direct query to `processed_documents` disproved it.

- **The drop now has its own counter** (`_batch_post_llm_dedup` → `deduplicated_count`) and is excluded from `failed_count`. It deliberately does **not** join the two existing "not a failure" buckets (cooldown-skipped, pre-LLM deferred): those documents never entered processing, whereas a duplicate went through it and succeeded.
- **The B1 denominator is a decision, not leftovers.** `attempted` keeps counting duplicates, so `fail_ratio` still reads "share of processing attempts that failed". The `scheduler_degraded_failure_ratio` threshold is untouched.
- **Visibility:** `source_tick_deduplicated` (INFO, at the tick where the false alarm lived), `total_deduplicated` in the tick summary, `deduplicated_count` in `source_attempts.details_json`, in the CLI and in the API job result. Deliberately **not** added to `get_pipeline_status` — that surface reads current state from `sources` and would need a new column whose only consumer is the R11 cost question, which the existing metric already answers with history.
- **Two invariants the suite never stated:** a deduplicated document does not raise `failed_count`, and a dedup-only tick is not `degraded`. The second feeds the scheduler the stats a real `run_processing` produces rather than a hand-written dict, since the whole change lives upstream of the scheduler.

## Measured on prod (read-only), and it reframed half (b)

Half (b) — ordering relative to the LLM call — is **not** in this PR (it is R11). But the baseline measurement taken here changed its shape: over 41 hours the attempts recorded as failures processed 1108 documents and burned **1 495 164 tokens** against 10 documents and 20 416 tokens on the successful ones. The volume is not the story — in the surviving log window those 81 dedup events belong to **27 distinct documents, each seen exactly three times**. The drop persists nothing and work is selected by `NOT EXISTS` against `processed_documents`, so every tick pays for the same summary again, indefinitely. Recording the drop is what stops the loop; moving the check only ever saves the first call per document. Details in BUG-097; the plan and its queue are updated accordingly (R11 pulled ahead of R1 by owner decision).

## Test plan

- [x] Red/green: 7 of 9 new tests fail on the pre-fix code, for the right reasons (`failed_count` = 3 on a tick with no failures; scheduler writing `fail_ratio=1.0`, the same line visible on prod)
- [x] default suite: **3848 passed**
- [x] PR standard (`TEST_POSTGRES=1`): **4260 passed**, 22 skipped, 2 deselected
- [x] ruff clean
- [ ] After deploy: a source whose tick contained only duplicates is not `degraded`, its `fail_count` = 0 and `last_error` = NULL (baseline before deploy: 8 sources at 1079 / 1005 / 1004 / 945 / 866 / 642 / 473 / 144)

author: kelvinuknowhu
body:
**Title:** Registration form ingestion pipeline

---

Ingests registration forms from the third-party provider, transforms them to the target schema, geocodes the postcode, and makes them available to the FORM-BOT — handling duplicate deliveries, provider schema drift, and downstream API outages.

📹 [Loom walkthrough](https://www.loom.com/share/e7da384a28594383b818232298bb100d)

## Design

`/ingest` stores the raw payload **verbatim** and returns `202` immediately. Nothing is parsed on the request path, so a delivery succeeds even while the geocoder is down — a form is never dropped because a downstream API is unavailable. All processing happens in background workers.

The three "never" requirements are enforced by database constraints rather than application logic, which is far harder to get right under concurrency, crashes and replays:

| Requirement | Guarantee |
|---|---|
| Duplicate deliveries are harmless | `UNIQUE(session_id)`, written via `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING` — no read-then-write race |
| FORM-BOT never sees a form twice | `UNIQUE(form_id)` on `transformed_forms` + atomic claim: `SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, then stamp `delivered_to_bot_at`, in one transaction |
| The email is guaranteed | Transactional outbox: `UNIQUE(form_id)` on `email_outbox`, inserted in the *same transaction* as the transform |
| Failures are replayable | The raw payload is stored before anything parses it, so any form can be re-run from scratch after a code fix |

## Failure handling

- **Permanent failures** (schema drift, invalid DOB) → `FAILED_VALIDATION`, parked for a code fix, then replayable via `/retry`
- **Transient failures** (5xx, 429 from the geocoder) → `PENDING` with exponential backoff + jitter; `DEAD_LETTER` once attempts are exhausted
- **Crashed workers** → rows stuck in `PROCESSING` past their lease are reclaimed as `PENDING`
- **Sweeper** → periodically retries dead-lettered and validation-failed forms, so a deployed schema fix heals the failed forms unattended

## Stack

Postgres via Drizzle, docker-compose for local dev, 84 tests covering the transform, validation, and the full pipeline (including duplicate delivery, outage and crash-recovery paths).

See the [README](https://github.com/kelvinuknowhu/healthtech1-take-home/blob/main/README.md) for setup and the full architecture diagram. The original brief is preserved as `BRIEF.md`.

author: jaapstronks
body:
## What

A7.19-nazorg, C3 stragglers (brief § Nazorg): the last eight hand-rolled env parsers move onto the `envStr`/`envBool`/`envInt` accessor family, making "one accessor family" actually true.

## The deliberate part: envBool semantics

`envBool` now treats an **unrecognized value as unset** (→ fallback) instead of as false. Recognized tokens are unchanged: `1/true/yes/on` → true, `0/false/no/off` → false. This is the linchpin for the two default-ON flags on the list:

- **`AUTH_ENABLED`** (default-on, was `=== 'false'`): a naive envBool would have made `AUTH_ENABLED=fasle` disable auth — silent anonymous-admin fail-open. With the new rule a typo leaves auth ON; only an explicit falsy token disables. Behaviour change: `0/no/off` now also count as explicit disables (previously only the literal `false` did). Pinned in `tests/auth-config-guard.test.js` **before** the conversion, documented in `.env.example`.
- **`PDF_EXPORT_IMAGE_COMPRESSION`** (default-on falsy-set): identical truth table as before via `envBool(name, true)` — the "inverse semantics" flagged in review are now just the fallback direction.

Family contract itself pinned in new `tests/config-env-accessors.test.js`.

## Converted sites

- `auth/auth.js` — `truthyEnv` (SANDBOX_MODE/DEMO_MODE/AUTH_ALLOW_WEAK_SECRET), the three `=== 'false'` AUTH_ENABLED reads, and the raw `String(process.env.X||'').trim()` reads (AUTH_SECRET, AUTH_ADMIN_EMAIL, COOKIE_DOMAIN, AUTH_DEV_BYPASS, NODE_ENV)
- `utils/debug-log.js` — byte-identical `truthy()` clone
- `render/thumbnail-warm-queue.js` — tri-state parser (vocabulary now includes `on/off`)
- `export/image-compress.js` + `export/image-measure.js` — falsy-set toggle and int parsers; the injected-`env` parameters are dropped (the family reads `process.env`, tests set it scoped). Behaviour change per the envInt contract: out-of-range values now **fall back to the default instead of clamping** (`QUALITY=999` → 80, was 100; `RETINA_SCALE=100` → 2, was 4) — documented in `.env.example`

body:
## Mise en page des e-mails

Les trois messages adressés aux clientes — confirmation, déplacement, rappel — partagent désormais un gabarit unique (`api/_lib/email-template.js`) plutôt que trois variantes qui auraient divergé.

Bandeau de date en tête, car c'est l'information qu'on cherche des mois plus tard en rouvrant le message : jour de la semaine, date en grand, horaire. Puis séance, tarif avec la mention « à régler sur place », et adresse cliquable vers la carte.

Contraintes du courrier électronique respectées et vérifiées automatiquement : mise en page en tableaux, styles en ligne uniquement, polices système, aucune ressource externe, aucune balise `<style>` ni classe CSS. Outlook ignore `flex` et `grid`, et la plupart des messageries retirent les feuilles de style.

## Rappel de la veille

Tâche planifiée quotidienne à 16h00 UTC — 18h00 à Bruxelles en été, 17h00 en hiver. SMS via Brevo quand un numéro est disponible, e-mail sinon : le téléphone étant facultatif à la réservation, s'en tenir au SMS priverait de rappel une partie des clientes.

Le texte du SMS est **écrit sans accent**, et ce n'est pas un oubli. Un seul caractère hors alphabet GSM-7 fait basculer le message entier en Unicode, où un SMS ne compte plus que 70 caractères au lieu de 160 : le rappel accentué partirait en trois segments facturés au lieu d'un. Mesuré à 147 caractères, un segment.

La colonne `reminder_sent_at` empêche le double envoi. Un échec ne l'horodate pas : le rendez-vous est repris au passage suivant, un rappel en retard valant mieux qu'aucun rappel.

## Vérifications

Normalisation des numéros belges sous toutes leurs formes — `0470 11 22 33`, `+32…`, `0032…`, `04/70.11.22.33` — et rejet des numéros inutilisables.

Sélection des rendez-vous : demain seulement, ni annulés ni déjà rappelés ; aucun doublon si la tâche se rejoue ; un échec laisse le rendez-vous disponible pour la tentative suivante ; secret de cron exigé.

Migration v3 → v4 sur une base déjà en service : colonne et index ajoutés, réservations conservées.

## À configurer après la fusion

`BREVO_API_KEY` dans Vercel, et éventuellement `BREVO_SMS_SENDER` (11 caractères maximum). Sans clé, le rappel part par e-mail et le manque est journalisé — jamais d'échec silencieux.

> L'API SMS de Brevo n'a pas pu être appelée depuis l'environnement de développement, dont le proxy bloque le domaine. En cas de refus, la réponse complète de Brevo part dans les journaux Vercel.

> Le projet déclare maintenant **deux tâches planifiées**, ce qui est la limite du plan Hobby de Vercel.

> ​<!-- roomote:pr-attribution:start -->Created by Roomote.<!-- roomote:pr-attribution:end --> Follow up by mentioning @roomote, in [the web UI](https://community.roomote.ai/task/2vm8h4adlj2e1?utm_source=github-comment&utm_medium=link&utm_campaign=snapshot_resume), or in [Discord](https://discord.com/channels/1332146336664915968/1527716172924195047/1537562366613524520).

## What changed

Removed the startup-only Goal Mode policy from the agent developer prompt and moved the complete policy into trusted per-turn goal context. Goal turns explicitly signal that Goal Mode is enabled while carrying the objective, generation, continuation budget, and lifecycle rules without including the `/goal` command.

All follow-up delivery paths now resolve and attach the latest active goal before sending or steering a turn, including Slack, Discord, Teams, Telegram, Linear, snapshot replay, deferred resume prompts, setup notifications, and direct API relays. Worker delivery fails closed and preserves queued messages when goal lookup or harness delivery cannot complete.

## Why this change was made

Goal Mode can be enabled after a runtime starts, so startup-only instructions are not a reliable signal. Keeping the policy with every goal-aware turn makes the mechanism explicit to the agent without leaking command syntax into the user-visible transcript or allowing integration follow-ups to bypass lifecycle guidance.

## Impact

Agents receive consistent Goal Mode instructions for initial, integration-delivered, and steered follow-up turns, including generation-safe completion and blocking behavior. Users continue to see only their own message content in the transcript.

author: zia-
body:
## Summary

- Self-hosts Inter (Latin subset, OFL-1.1 — `apps/web/src/assets/fonts/LICENSE.txt`) instead of the legacy site's `http://` Google Fonts dependency, via a real imported `fonts.css` so Vite copies each `.woff2` into the build as a same-origin, content-hashed asset.
- Adds a cookie consent banner (`packages/ui`'s `CookieBanner`) gating non-essential (analytics) cookies behind explicit accept/reject, backed by `apps/web/src/scripts/consent.ts` (`hasConsent`/`setConsent`/`hasStoredConsent` — the typed gate any future non-essential script must check first).
- Fulfils FR-WEB-07 / NFR-04 per `docs/plan/05-execution-plan.md` TASK 1.2.3.

## Design note: no client:* island

The banner is deliberately **not** hydrated via a `client:*` directive. Astro's island runtime needs its own inline bootstrap `<script>`, which the CloudFront `ResponseHeadersPolicy` CSP's `script-src` (falls back to `default-src 'self'`, no `'unsafe-inline'`) would silently block — confirmed by inspecting a real `astro build` output before choosing this shape. Instead:
- `CookieBanner.tsx` renders static markup (zero framework JS shipped, per ADR-0017), with `data-cookie-action="accept"/"reject"` as the real production hook.
- `BaseLayout.astro` wires it up with a plain `<script>` that Astro bundles as an external, same-origin file.
- `astro.config.mjs` sets `vite.build.assetsInlineLimit: 0` — otherwise Astro/Vite's default 4096-byte threshold would inline that small hoisted script right back into every page's HTML, defeating the point.

## Two pre-existing gaps fixed along the way

Both were exposed by this being the first task to add a real `<script>` tag / a `hidden`-toggling class to the codebase:

1. **`packages/eslint-plugin-i18n`'s `no-hardcoded-strings` rule** flagged every `<script>`/`<style>` tag's code and comments as hard-coded copy, since `astro-eslint-parser` emits their body as opaque `AstroRawText` — the same node type real template text gets. Added a targeted exemption (script/style bodies only), plus a new `RuleTester` suite using the *real* `astro-eslint-parser` (the existing suite deliberately uses plain JSX via espree, which has no `AstroRawText` node type to exercise this against).
2. **`.ndn-cookie-banner`'s own `display: flex`** silently defeated the native `hidden` attribute — author-stylesheet rules always beat the user-agent stylesheet's `[hidden] { display: none }`, even at equal specificity. The banner stayed visible after accept/reject until an explicit `.ndn-cookie-banner[hidden] { display: none }` override was added. This was caught by driving a real headless Chromium against a local `astro preview` build, not by unit tests — jsdom-based component tests never exercise a real UA stylesheet.

## Test evidence

- `pnpm run lint` — pass (all 12 workspace projects + no-disable-comments check)
- `pnpm run typecheck` — pass (all 12 workspace projects)
- `pnpm run test` (builds `apps/web` first, then all unit/e2e suites) — pass: 598+ tests across every package, including new suites:
  - `apps/web/src/scripts/consent.test.ts` (5 tests)
  - `packages/ui/src/components/CookieBanner.test.tsx` (5 tests)
  - `packages/eslint-plugin-i18n/src/no-hardcoded-strings.test.js` (new real-`.astro`-parser suite, 2 tests total in file)
- Manual verification: drove a real headless Chromium (`@playwright/test`'s bundled chromium) against a local `astro preview` build — confirmed: banner visible on first load; reject/accept buttons keyboard-focusable and Enter-activatable; banner hides correctly after each and stays hidden across reload; consent cookie recorded correctly (`essential` only on reject, `essential,analytics` on accept); zero console errors; fonts load same-origin only; `body`'s computed `font-family` resolves to `Inter`.
- `tests/pr-env/*` (cookie-consent.test.ts, plus updated keyboard.test.ts/a11y-full.test.ts) run against a live ephemeral stack in CI's `pr-environment` job (informational-only per TASK 0.6.3, not yet gating) — not runnable locally, no AWS deploy in this session.

## Rollback

Revert the branch. No infra/data changes; nothing destructive.

## Cost delta

£0.00 — no new AWS resources (CSS/JS/font assets served from the existing CloudFront distribution).

## Test plan

- [ ] CI `quality` gate green (lint/typecheck/unit tests)
- [ ] CI `pr-environment` job's Playwright suite (including new `cookie-consent.test.ts`) passes against the live ephemeral stack
- [ ] Manually load the PR's ephemeral URL, confirm banner appears, self-hosted fonts render, no external network requests to `fonts.googleapis.com`/`fonts.gstatic.com`

author: tysjosh
body:
The dev-split protocol spends 40% of each seed's benchmark fitting the escalation policy, leaving arms scored on the other ~94 of 156 examples. OCMR's published Table III is scored on all 156. The split is category-stratified and so a fair sample -- B0 landed at 80.00, 80.32, 79.68 across three runs against a published 77.20 -- but a row measured on a subset is not strictly comparable to the rows already in that table.

fit_policy_across_seeds pools routing cases from the other seeds and evaluates every arm on the held-out seed's full benchmark. Seeds sample different names, projects, and tasks, so the fitted policy has not seen the held-out trajectories. Selected with --fit leave-one-seed-out, now the default; --fit dev-split keeps the existing numbers reproducible as a robustness check. Both modes share one _fit_from_cases core so the labelling rule and threshold selection cannot drift.

Two hazards found while building it, both handled rather than assumed away.

The six hand-authored anchors are injected verbatim and are byte-identical in every seed, so a naive pool would fit on the exact trajectories it later scores. They are excluded from the fitting pool and kept in evaluation, so the evaluation set stays the published 156.

Example ids collide across seeds -- longitudinal-000 exists in every seed with different content -- so leakage cannot be audited by id. It is measured on session text and reported: 11% of held-out session text also appears in the pool at two seeds, arising from the generator's small vocabularies. Surfaced by the summarizer as a new section 0 alongside the fit mode and the number of examples scored.

Cases are collected once per seed and reused across folds, since a seed's cases do not depend on which seed is held out.

894 tests pass with -m "not slow".

author: aborrego24
body:
The magic number answered the wrong question. `G + 1 - my_wins - rival_losses` is the baseball two-team formula: "can this one rival pass me". It cannot answer "do I finish in a playoff seat", which needs a count of how many teams can finish above you, and the points tiebreaker.

At `R=0` -- the season-end state stage 4 always reaches -- the formula reduces to `clinch_MN = R + 1 - (wins - first_team_out.wins)`, which is unconditionally <= 0 for anyone in the "in" bucket. So the rule collapsed to "your win total beats 5th place, therefore you clinched", uncapped by the number of seats. Measured: more teams were reported clinched than there were seats in 47.4% of permutations, up to 9 of 10 for 5 spots. It exited 0, so it was silently wrong.

New s`cenario_engine/playoff_math.py` decides it by definition instead: a team has clinched iff it holds a seat in every completion of the remaining schedule, and is eliminated iff in none, ordered by wins then total points (ESPN `playoffSeedingRule = TOTAL_POINTS_SCORED`).

It does not enumerate completions. For each team it searches for a counterexample and stops at the first one, which makes the exponent disappear:

  weeks left 3 (2^15 completions)  0.9 ms
  weeks left 4 (2^20)              0.6 ms
  weeks left 5 (2^25)              0.4 ms
  weeks left 6 (2^30)              0.5 ms

Two things keep it small. Dominance: to prove a team CAN miss it is always optimal for it to lose out, since its own wins only help it and each loss also hands a rival a win -- so its games are fixed, not branched. And bounds pruning: a rival that cannot reach the team win total even by winning out can never finish above it, collapsing whole branches. A node budget raises rather than returning a guess.

Verified against brute force: 52 random 6- and 8-team leagues where every completion is enumerated and compared. They agree in all cases.

Also removes the both-locked matchup filter. It froze those teams records while everyone else played on, moving them relative to teams they should have stayed ahead of, and corrupting the standings the verdict is computed from. Its pruning is worthless now.

Magic numbers stay as display values for teams still alive. Stage 2 now also emits remaining_matchups, since deciding a full-season question needs the full remaining schedule, not just next week.

On the week13 fixture: clinched goes 8 -> 4 of 5 seats. Momma Gus was printed as "Clinches a playoff spot with: a WIN" and is in fact eliminated -- it cannot reach a seat under any completion.

The strict xfail is promoted to a real assertion across all three fixtures, plus a wiring cross-check that the pipeline verdict matches the math module called directly.

author: pavp
body:
## The bug

Selecting an author chip near either end of the row left it clipped against the screen edge. The `ScrollView` had no ref and never called `scrollTo`, so nothing repositioned anything — the active filter sat half off screen, and looked like the last option available.

Reproduced on device before fixing: scrolled the row until "Chelsey Dietrich" was flush against the right edge, tapped it, and the list did not move.

## The fix

The row measures its own viewport via `onLayout` and each chip's position, then centres whichever chip is selected.

```ts
export const centreOffset = ({ x, width }: ChipLayout, viewport: number) =>
  Math.max(0, x + width / 2 - viewport / 2);
```

The clamp matters: centring a chip near the start resolves to a negative offset, which would ask the list to scroll before its own beginning.

Centring rather than merely revealing is deliberate — it also shows there are more options on both sides, which a chip pinned to the edge hides.

## On the tests

`centreOffset` is exported and tested directly. That is not only for convenience: three consecutive `renderWithProviders` calls in one file hit an isolation problem in this setup where the third render's tree is not queryable, and I spent longer than I would like discovering that. Pulling the arithmetic out made the clamp properly testable and left the component test covering what only a render can show — that selecting a chip triggers the scroll at all.

**Mutation-verified.** Removing `Math.max(0, …)` fails exactly the two clamp tests and nothing else.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npx jest` (full suite) — 16/16 suites, 60/60 tests (baseline 15/55; one suite and five tests added)
- `npx eslint .` — 0 errors, 5 pre-existing warnings
- Verified on device: the same chip that used to clip now lands centred, with the neighbours visible either side

author: alpcaner
body:
Closes #725.

`_bash_available()` bounded its probe with `timeout=10` and caught only `OSError`. **`subprocess.TimeoutExpired` derives from `SubprocessError`, not `OSError`** — so the one failure mode the budget existed to bound was the one the handler did not absorb.

The probe runs at **module scope** (the `@pytest.mark.skipif(...)` decorators call it at import time), so the escaping exception did not fail a test. It aborted **collection**:

```
tests\commands\test_completion_command.py:479: in <module>
    not _bash_available(), reason="no real bash on this host ..."
E   subprocess.TimeoutExpired: Command '['bash', '-c', 'echo tan-bash-ok']' timed out after 10 seconds
!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Interrupted: 1 error during collection !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
```

pytest then exits **2** having run nothing, printing zero `FAILED` lines — so a branch-vs-baseline failure diff reads every known failure as **newly passing**. Measured while doing exactly that: a comparison that should have read `37 failures, 0 regressions` instead read `0 failures, 37 newly passing`, from a run that executed no tests.

Nothing is wrong with `bash` — it resolves to Git Bash and works. It is cold process start-up under load: **10.6 s** cold against the 10 s budget, **0.10 s** warm.

## Two commits, because the first fix was not enough

**1. Absorb the timeout.** `except (OSError, TimeoutExpired)` in `_bash_available`, and the same in `_noexec_probe` (`timeout=15`, `except OSError`, also called at module scope by `noexec_capable`) — one guard per probe, not just the site that happened to bite. Two neighbours were checked and are already correct: `_bash_setlocale_warning_probe` catches `subprocess.SubprocessError`, and `conftest.py`'s `_git()` catches `(OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError, UnicodeDecodeError)`.

**2. Retry once — and this is the part the numbers forced.** With only the handler in place the suite went `37 failed / 307 skipped` → `20 failed / 325 skipped`. Seventeen failures "disappeared" with zero regressions, which looks like an improvement and is not one: **skips rose by 18**. The 15 bash-completion tests had moved from FAILED to SKIPPED, because the probe timed out and the new handler answered "this host cannot". A loud collection abort had been traded for quietly untested code, on exactly the loaded hosts that provoke the bug. Since the sole observed cause is cold start-up, `_bash_available` now makes a second attempt: the first spawn pays the cold cost, the second is warm. `_noexec_probe` deliberately does **not** retry — an `unshare` namespace probe that times out is reporting a genuinely restricted host, not a warm-up cost.

## Why `TimeoutExpired` and not `SubprocessError`

Narrowed deliberately. For a **host-capability probe** a timeout is a legitimate answer: "bash did not respond within the budget" means the same as "no bash on `PATH`" — this host cannot usefully run these tests, so skip. That is the opposite of the rule for production code, where `test_diff_command.py::test_sdk_validator_timeout_refuses_instead_of_reporting_clean` records a blanket `except ... SubprocessError` swallowing a timeout as a **MAJOR** defect: a wedged validator must refuse, never fall back to a clean result. The narrower catch keeps that distinction visible at the seam.

## Tests

`python/tests/gates/test_capability_probes_absorb_timeouts.py`, hermetic (patches `subprocess.run`, runs nothing slow):

- a timed-out probe returns `False` instead of raising — both probes
- a missing tool still returns `False` — the pre-existing contract must survive
- a working host still returns `True` — a fix that made every host look incapable would skip these suites everywhere and hide real breakage
- the retry is pinned by **counting spawns** (`calls["n"] == 2`), so collapsing back to one attempt fails the test rather than silently restoring the skip

Verified it can fail: against the pre-fix probes the new file cannot even be **collected** — importing `test_completion_command` runs the module-scope probe, which raises `TimeoutExpired`. That is the defect reproducing itself. With the fix, 7 passed.

One trap worth recording: `_bash_available` is `@lru_cache(maxsize=1)` and already called at import time, so the first cut of these tests read that one cached verdict and exercised none of the code they named — two passed against a cached `False`. They now clear the cache before each call, and an autouse fixture clears it afterwards so a verdict computed against a faked `subprocess` cannot leak into the rest of the session.

## Gate

```
35 failed, 4090 passed, 309 skipped, 1 xfailed in 606.53s
regressions vs baseline: none
```

The 15 completion tests are back **in the failure list** — running again, not skipped, which is the point of commit 2. Against the 37-failure `dev` baseline the only two absent are `test_faultdecode.py` / `test_faultdecode_command.py`, which moved to skipped (`307 -> 309`) because the sibling `alp-sdk` checkout on this host was rebased during unrelated work; they behave identically on other branches measured today and have nothing to do with this change.

This host does not meet the repo's "zero failures" bar for pre-existing environment reasons, so the claim here is **no regressions**, not green.

author: jasonmanuel-cmd
body:
Addresses the mobile PageSpeed report from Aug 13 (Performance **59**, Accessibility **96**).

## What was actually wrong

The headline number was almost entirely the **brand intro video**. `index.html` preloaded a 1.4 MB MP4 at high priority and autoplayed it full-screen over the page for up to 10 seconds. Lighthouse always audits a cold session, so it played on every single run — which is why Speed Index was 5.2s and LCP was 6.1s.

Everything else was ordinary critical-path bloat: four render-blocking stylesheets, and ~90 KB of chat/analytics/HubSpot JavaScript shipped with the document.

## Performance changes

- **Intro video is desktop-only now.** Also skipped for `prefers-reduced-motion`, Save-Data and 2g. The `<source>` is attached from JS rather than markup, so a skipped intro downloads **zero** video bytes. `MOBILE_MAX` in the inline gate turns it back on everywhere.
- Dropped the `as=video` and poster preloads that were competing with the hero image.
- **gtag.js, the chat assistant bundle and HubSpot moved off the critical path** — they load on first engagement, with a floor timer so analytics still fires for visitors who never interact. The gtag queue stub stays inline so no early `gtag()` calls are lost.
- `reviews.js` loads when the reviews section comes into range instead of with the document.
- `reviews.css`, `project-assistant.css` and the Google Fonts sheet are non-blocking; `styles.min.css` is now the only render-blocking stylesheet. Added preconnects for the font origins.
- `/data/*.js` gets an hour of caching with a day of stale-while-revalidate; it was falling through to the `must-revalidate` catch-all.

## Accessibility changes

Found along the way: **`index.html` was the only page still on the old brand red.** Its inline critical CSS pinned `--metal: #C41E3A`, which overrode the site stylesheet — so the earlier "brighten red to #E63946 throughout site" change never actually reached the home page.

Fixing that exposed the real issue: **#E63946 does not pass AA as small text** — 4.16:1 on white, and 4.16:1 again with white text on it. It is fine as a fill behind large text, and fine on near-black. So small text now uses `--color-brand-hover` (#D62828), which passes both ways at ~4.96:1:

- `.eyebrow` and the two section-heading eyebrow rules on white / #f5f5f5
- the mobile call FAB label and the chat launcher label (white-on-red)
- chat launcher hover moves to `--color-brand-focus` so the hover shift stays visible

Eyebrows inside `.section-ink` move the *other* direction — from `--metal-light` (#D62828, 3.95:1 on #0a0a0a) to `--metal` (#E63946, 4.75:1). On dark, the brighter red is the legible one.

## Verification

Local Lighthouse, mobile preset, simulated throttling:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Performance | 86 | **92** |
| Accessibility | 96 | **100** |
| SEO | 100 | 100 |
| Speed Index | 20.1s | **1.5s** |
| FCP | 1.8s | **1.5s** |
| TBT | 0ms | 0ms |
| CLS | 0 | 0 |

The local baseline reads higher than the live 59 because there is no network latency and third parties are blocked, but the deltas hold. Speed Index 20.1s → 1.5s is the intro video.

Also verified in Chromium at both sizes: mobile requests no video and no third-party JS on load, desktop still plays the intro once per session, the chat launcher appears after interaction, and the reviews strip still renders.

## Not in this PR

The two image swaps that were requested with this work — the new commercial-building hero and the edited hospital-door photo — are **not** included. The photos came through as inline images rather than files, so they are not on disk to commit. They need to be re-sent as file attachments.

Worth knowing for the hero swap: the current `Homehero.webp` is 2400×658 in a hero box that is ~1350px tall on a phone, so `object-fit: cover` upscales it about 4× — mobile visitors see a blurry crop today, and Lighthouse flags 194 KiB of wasted image bytes. The replacement building photo is much closer to the right shape, and I will generate properly-sized `.webp`/`-sm.webp` variants when the file arrives.

## What kind of change does this PR introduce?

Bug fix

## What is the current behavior?

Client can disconnect after the request body has already completed but it's not an abort anymore either. In that case, request db handle will stay alive.

Register finish (normal) and close (disconnect after upload) once. Whichever fires, disarm and call dispose.

body:
## Sammanfattning

Åtgärdar en regression från #12 som drabbar alla återvändande användare: instruktionsraden visade den bokstavliga texten **"undefined"** i formuläret och skrevs dessutom ut på själva bladet.

`normalizeState` i `state/storage.ts` fyllde på `clock`/`fraction` för äldre sparade tillstånd, men skickade vidare hela `document` rakt av. Ett tillstånd sparat innan `header.instructions`/`exampleFirst` fanns kom därför tillbaka med fälten som `undefined`, vilket i tur och ordning gav:

- `instructionsEl.value = undefined` → texten "undefined" i inmatningsfältet
- `params.set('instr', undefined)` → `instr=undefined` i den delade länken, så strängen blev klistrig vid nästa avkodning
- `config.header.instructions.trim()` i `headerExtraLineCount` → `TypeError` för ett tillstånd som ännu inte gått via URL:en

### Ändringar
- `document` och dess `header` slås nu ihop med standardvärdena i stället för att skickas vidare orörda. `STORAGE_KEY` bumpas medvetet **inte** — sammanslagningen bevarar användarens sparade inställningar i stället för att kasta bort dem.
- `sheetType`-vitlistan bygger nu på en delad `SHEET_TYPES`-konstant, så nya bladtyper inte glöms bort.
- Länkar som redan delats med `instr=undefined` städas upp vid avkodning (en instruktion som bara råkar innehålla ordet påverkas inte).

author: dcasati
body:
Hi, 

MCPTool._ensure_connected() used a periodic `ping` as a connection health check. 

When the server rejected `ping` with an McpError, the code only treated error code -32601 ("Method not found", the JSON-RPC-spec-correct code for an unimplemented method) as "ping unsupported, keep using this connection". Any other error code fell through to a reconnect attempt.

It seems like some real-world MCP servers (like the Microsoft Fabric's Data Agent MCP endpoint) reject an unsupported `ping` with a different code (-32600 "Invalid Request") instead. Since that server only implements initialize, notifications/initialized, tools/list, and tools/call, every single tool call triggered this same failed-ping path, and instead of just disabling future pings, the client attempted an unnecessary reconnect. That reconnect can itself fail in ways unrelated to the original (harmless) ping rejection, breaking an otherwise fully working MCP tool.

Any well-formed JSON-RPC error response to ping - regardless of its specific error code - already proves the connection is alive: the server received the request and replied. It just means the server doesn't support (or accept) the optional ping method. 

This change treats any McpError from send_ping() the same way: disable future pings and continue using the existing connection, without attempting a reconnect. Only non-McpError exceptions (timeouts, transport/connection failures) -- where we genuinely don't know if the server is still reachable -- still trigger a reconnect, unchanged from before.

Added a regression test (nonstandard error code -32600) alongside the existing -32601 test to cover this.

author: evanphx
body:
Getting a shell in a running instance had an annoying preamble. You'd run `miren sandbox list`, scan the table for a row belonging to your app that was actually RUNNING, copy the ID, and only then get to the thing you wanted to do. That's a lookup the CLI has everything it needs to do itself, so now it does: `miren sandbox exec --app myapp -- ls -la` picks one for you.

The selection happens entirely in the CLI. It picks an ID and hands it to the exec RPC through the path that already existed, so there's no server or protocol change in here at all. The proxy still resolves the target's app from the sandbox itself and re-checks access, which is the guard that was actually load-bearing.

The interesting decision was how a sandbox gets connected back to its app. The obvious route is `spec.version` to the app version to the app, which is what `sandbox list` uses for its APP column. I went through the pool instead, since the pool carries the indexed app ref and, more importantly, ephemeral sandboxes don't have one. `miren app run` creates those for console sessions, and picking one would drop you into somebody else's shell.

Among what's left, service is a requirement and version is a preference, in that order, and the asymmetry is the interesting part. Which service you get is the difference between a web process and a background worker, so substituting one for the other is never a kindness: without `--service` you get web, and if web has nothing running you get told that rather than quietly handed a worker. Which version you get is the difference between newer and older code for the same job, where insisting is what hurts, since a failed deploy leaves the current version pointing at something that never came up while the previous instances keep serving traffic. Refusing those would lock you out of a shell exactly when a deploy has just broken.

That ordering matters more than it sounds. Web has to bind its declared port to go ready and workers don't, so a rolling deploy routinely has the worker on the new version while web is still on the old one. Taking version first would hand you a worker there, and silently, since only one candidate survives and the "which one did I pick" notice stays quiet at one. Taking service first gives you old web instead. An app with no web service at all is exempt, since there's nothing to substitute. Whatever survives, we pick from at random, and name the choice on stderr when there was more than one to choose from (on a terminal only, since stdout there belongs to the sandbox).

`sandbox list` picked up matching `--app` and `--service` flags along the way. That started as a nicety and turned out to be load-bearing for the error messages: when exec can't find anything running, "go look at `miren sandbox list --app foo`" is a useful thing to say, and "go look at every sandbox on the cluster" isn't. Those filters match the values shown in the APP and SERVICE columns, so what you filter on is what you see.

Closes MIR-1577

author: rubensaucedo
body:
Answers the host-behaviour questions that gate the pack split (#29), using a
harness built from the **live roster** rather than toy fixtures. **Nothing in
the shipped plugin moves** — `kai` stays monolithic and authoritative.

## Test matrix (real host, Windows CLI)

| # | Test | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | Core present, contract 1 | Preflight fired, resolved **across the plugin boundary**, agent proceeded |
| B | **Core absent** | A real agent with full tool grants, asked `teach me binary search`, **refused** with the exact token and did nothing else |
| C | Core present, contract **2** | **Refused** — version skew detected |
| D | Legacy `kai` + `kai-core-preview`, both providing `team-operating-rules` | Bound to **`kai:`** (legacy) while the preflight **passed** |
| D2 | Same set, core listed first | Bound to `kai-core-preview:` |
| E | Roster enumeration | Listed exact qualified IDs; answered **NO** for an agent that was not installed |

## What this changes

**D is a newly discovered blocking hazard, not a confirmation.** Skill binding
is load-order dependent, and the preflight cannot catch it: core *is* present
and answering correctly while a different plugin silently supplies the rules —
the failure is invisible from inside the agent. Ordering luck is not a
mitigation, so **core skills must carry contract-versioned names**
(`kai-core-team-operating-rules-v1`); renaming removes the ambiguity outright.

**B and C are the reassuring half.** The earlier evidence for a fail-closed
preflight was a single-tool probe, which proved little. B is the hard case — an
agent that could trivially have answered, refusing instead.

**E clears directors to stay in core**, conditional on resolving availability
*before* claiming work. `director-chief-of-staff` currently **leases before it
dispatches**, so it needs fixing before any pack split lands.

Also measured: core is bigger than the six universal contracts — a 9-agent pack
pulls **10** skills from it, because shared *utilities* cross departments too.

## Not verified

- E was tested at **9 agents, not 56** — truncation under a full roster is unproven.
- Collision was tested only across `--plugin-dir` order; **install order,
  marketplace-vs-direct, and fresh sessions are untested**.
- Everything here is **Windows CLI**. macOS and the cloud host are untested.

## Verification

`npm test` passes; the harness self-test (10 checks) is wired into it, since an
unrun self-test is decoration. Release hygiene: 0.52.0 across all three
manifests, dated changelog entry plus compare link, README stamp rewritten.

author: coachtui
body:
## What

The site's CTA has rendered a dead **"Coming soon to the App Store"** badge since web went marketing-only. Build 5 is now approved and live to external testers, so the site can collect beta signups instead of nothing.

`TESTFLIGHT_URL` → `https://testflight.apple.com/join/Ys1CRVxy` (verified live — resolves to the join page for "Offload: Location Reminders", not full/closed/expired).

## Why not just set APP_STORE_URL

The old comment in `appStore.ts` suggested a TestFlight URL could go straight into `APP_STORE_URL`. It can't, cleanly — the label was hardcoded:

```tsx
const label = APP_STORE_URL ? 'Download on the App Store' : 'Coming soon to the App Store';
```

That would have put a TestFlight beta-install destination behind Apple's "Download on the App Store" badge — misleading about where the button goes, and against Apple's badge guidelines.

So the two links are separate constants and the CTA labels itself from whichever it has:

| `APP_STORE_URL` | `TESTFLIGHT_URL` | Renders |
|---|---|---|
| set | anything | "Download on the App Store" → App Store |
| null | set | "Join the beta on TestFlight" → TestFlight |
| null | null | "Coming soon to the App Store" (non-interactive) |

**App Store always wins**, so public launch stays a real one-liner: set `APP_STORE_URL` and every CTA upgrades itself — no need to remember to remove the beta link. Same visual slot in all three states, so no layout shift.

## Note

This makes the beta joinable by anyone with the site URL, up to TestFlight's 10,000-tester cap. That's the intent here, but it is a widening of who can get in.

## Testing

`tsc --noEmit` clean. Worth eyeballing the Vercel preview to confirm the button reads "Join the beta on TestFlight" and links correctly.

## Summary

Completes the buffered CCR transport fix across both Anthropic Messages and OpenAI Responses. This supersedes the partial alternatives in #2959 and #2968 for review: it preserves real upstream error status/headers and also rejects malformed successful responses instead of forwarding a broken HTTP 200 stream.

- Waits for the buffered operation before committing ASGI response headers, preserving real 429/5xx status and retry headers.
- Applies the lifecycle correction to both Anthropic and OpenAI Responses paths.
- Preserves valid JSON-to-SSE resynthesis and the existing valid upstream-SSE adaptation/relay behavior.
- Converts a non-JSON, non-SSE upstream 200 into a sanitized 502 `upstream_protocol_error` rather than a malformed successful turn.
- Initializes the OpenAI parsed-response state explicitly and contains JSON decoding at the usage boundary, so malformed input reaches the protocol guard rather than the generic exception wrapper.
- Semantically rebased onto current `main`, including the MCP SDK v1 compatibility cap and newer buffered-CCR fixes already merged there.

author: teng-lin
body:
Closes #2232

## The defect

All four `PROBE_THEN_CREATE` paths snapshot the resource list *before* the create so their probe can tell "the row I just made" from "one that was already there". Three of them degrade a **failed** snapshot to `None` — the "baseline unavailable" sentinel — and their probes then refuse to attribute any match.

`notebooks.create` degraded to an empty `set()` instead. An empty set reads as *"nothing existed"*, so the filter `nb.id not in baseline_ids` matched everything:

| pre-existing notebooks with this title | pre-fix result |
|---|---|
| exactly one | returned as `PROBED` — the caller gets **someone else's notebook** as if `create` had just made it. No signal, nothing to act on. |
| two or more | hard `Cannot disambiguate` failure on a create that had nothing to do with them |

The first row is the #2204 failure mode verbatim, and it is unbounded: every subsequent `sources.add_*` / `chat.ask` in that session targets the wrong notebook. It was documented in place as an *accepted known limitation*, predating the sentinel the source paths adopted in #2113 / #2204 — leaving `notebooks.create` the only one of the four that guessed.

## The change

Adopt the sentinel, mirroring `add_url`'s shape exactly (`_source/add.py:299-419`):

- `baseline_ids: set[str] | None`, `None` on failure; the WARNING now says the probe is disarmed rather than "falling back to an empty baseline".
- `baseline_error` is retained so the raise can name what broke the snapshot — the caller sees "baseline unavailable" long after that line ran.
- `_probe()` filters by title first, subtracts the baseline **only when it has one**, and otherwise raises a marked-`unconfirmed` `RPCError` naming the ambiguous rows (`_describe_notebooks`, the twin of `_describe_sources`).

The guard is on *matches*, not on the sentinel itself: a probe that lists cleanly and finds no notebook with this title has answered the question the baseline was only needed to disambiguate, so the retry still proceeds. An unavailable baseline never fails a create that would otherwise succeed.

## The tradeoff — please engage with this, not just the diff

**Silent wrong identity vs. a louder duplicate create.**

Today's failure is that a caller *silently receives a pre-existing notebook believing it is new*. That is the harder bug to ever notice: nothing is raised, nothing is logged above DEBUG, and the damage shows up later as sources and chats attached to a notebook nobody meant to touch.

Refusing to guess trades that for a different risk: when the probe cannot attribute a match, we raise instead of adopting, and the caller may end up issuing a duplicate create. A duplicate is loud — it is visible in the notebook list, it is diagnosable, and the error tells the caller exactly which rows to look at and why. The maintainer's call is that **duplicate-loudly beats silent wrong identity**, which is the same call #2113 and #2204 already made for the three source paths.

It takes three things at once to reach either outcome (a failed baseline `list()`, a commit-lost create, and a successful probe `list()`), so this is narrow — but `notebooks.create` is retried by exactly the callers most likely to hit a flaky window.

## Tests

- `test_create_baseline_failure_makes_a_match_ambiguous` (unit, parametrised over a decode `RPCError` and a transport `ServerError` baseline failure) — asserts the pre-existing id is named, `__cause__` is the baseline failure, `__context__` is the create's transport error, `unconfirmed` is set, and exactly one create attempt fired.
- `test_notebooks_create_baseline_failure_refuses_to_adopt_a_pre_existing_notebook` (wire-level, `MockTransport`) — the #2232 scenario end to end. The load-bearing assertion is negative: the call must not *return* the pre-existing notebook.
- `test_notebooks_create_baseline_failure_still_retries_when_probe_finds_nothing` — pins that the sentinel gates on matches, catching a blanket `if baseline_ids is None: raise` regression.

**Mutation-tested.** Reverting the source fix (`baseline_ids = set()` + the old unconditional filter) turns the three new tests red and leaves the other 55 in those files green. Separately, mutating `elif matches:` → `else:` turns only the "still retries" test red.

## Docs

- `CHANGELOG.md`: new `Unreleased / Fixed` entry, and the #2220 paragraph that read *"what changed there is only the log level"* is scoped to its own release — that sentence described exactly what this PR changes.

- ADR-0005 named this as the one gap the #2220 probe-failure rule left open. It now records the closed rule, and states the trade explicitly.
- `docs/python-api.md` idempotency table: the `notebooks.create` row now carries the non-unique-title caveat, matching the `add_url` row.

## Verification

```
uv run pytest -n auto --dist loadgroup --cov=src/notebooklm --cov-fail-under=90
  -> 16511 passed, 64 skipped, 1 xfailed; coverage 96.80%
uv run mypy src/notebooklm --ignore-missing-imports  -> Success, 353 files
uv run pre-commit run --all-files                    -> exit 0
```

Full 6-extra install (`browser dev markdown mcp server impersonate`).

## Live-API probe: run, with a pre-fix/post-fix contrast

This changes real idempotency behaviour on the wire, so it was probed against the real backend. Same script, same account, same injected conditions (unavailable baseline + lost create response), run on `origin/main` and on this branch:

- **pre-fix** — `create()` returned `0acef09e-…`, the *pre-existing* row, with no error raised
- **post-fix** — `RPCError: Cannot disambiguate notebook with title …` naming that row, `unconfirmed=True`, and exactly one row carrying the title afterwards (the ambiguity aborted the loop rather than firing a second create)

Also confirmed live: two `create()` calls with an identical title yield two distinct notebooks, so a title genuinely is not an identity on this backend. Full output, the script, and what the probe cannot show are in the [probe comment](https://github.com/teng-lin/notebooklm-py/pull/2235#issuecomment-5286293681).

author: jwh3times
body:
## Summary

ApexRacers used **Race**, **Session**, **Subsession**, **Split** and **Event** across ingestion, results, telemetry and the race-detail UI without an agreed meaning for any of them, and code comments treated several of them as interchangeable. This runs the domain-modeling session and records the result.

The captured results payload settles the hierarchy. Subsession `86109311` carries one `session_id` and a `session_splits` list naming two subsessions, so a Race Session divides into Splits and **each Split is exactly one Subsession** — a Subsession never *contains* Splits. The same payload's `session_results` holds three simsessions (practice at `-2`, qualifying at `-1`, race at `0`), so what a Subsession does contain is **Sim Sessions**.

```
Race Week → Race Session (1) → Split (1..n) → Subsession (exactly 1 per Split)
                                                  ↓
                                            Sim Session (1..n, sequential; race = 0)
                                                  ↓
                                            Race Result (1 per Driver)
```

`CONTEXT.md` gains a **Race Sessions** section recording that hierarchy and its cardinalities, plus eleven terms: Race Session, Split, Split Index, Subsession, Event Type, Sim Session, Sim Session Type, Race, Official Subsession, Race Result, and Strength of Field. **Session** and **Event** are recorded as terms to avoid — each names more than one level. **Race** is confirmed as the word for URLs and driver-facing copy, which is what `/races/:subsessionId` and "Race History" already use.

Two pieces of contributor guidance contradicted this and are corrected: `AGENTS.md` and the `postgres-specialist` agent both described a Subsession as "one race session" rather than as one Split of one.

**No ADR.** The one hard-to-reverse-looking choice underneath this — iRacing's `session_id` is discarded, leaving Splits unreassociable after ingest — was evaluated and judged a gap rather than a decision, so it is tracked as #191 instead of recorded as a trade-off.

### Follow-up issues filed

The modeling surfaced five contradictions between the recorded language and the code:

| Issue | Contradiction |
| --- | --- |
| #191 | iRacing's `session_id` is never persisted, so Splits of one Race Session cannot be reassociated |
| #192 | `SplitNum = 0` conflates "top split", "no splits" and "not found" — and is written but never read |
| #193 | `LapSessionType` mixes Event Type, Sim Session Type, and a simsession *subtype* name |
| #194 | `WeekNumber` / `RaceWeekNum` say *Number* but hold a zero-based Index |
| #195 | The race-detail DTO promises a "full classified field" but silently drops team entries |

author: julpo2000
body:
## Symptom

You could barely look around on Windows — mouse-look felt almost dead.

## Cause

`Game::advance` runs a fixed 60 Hz sim from an uncapped render loop. Mouse motion
is accumulated into `self.look_delta` by `mouse_look`, and `advance` sampled it
into an `InputFrame` **and cleared it on every call** — but only *applied* it when
the accumulator had a full tick's worth of time.

On a fast machine the render loop runs at thousands of FPS, so ~59 of every 60
`advance` calls are shorter than one tick and run **zero** ticks. Each of those
calls still sampled-and-cleared `look_delta`, throwing that frame's motion away
before any tick could consume it. Net effect: ~98% of mouse motion silently
dropped. At/near 60 FPS every frame runs a tick, so nothing is lost — which is
why this only bit on the fast RTX 4060 Windows box, not a 60 Hz-ish machine.

The same drop hit the `jump` / `toggle_fly` key edges.

## Fix

Accumulate time first, then **return before touching the one-shot inputs when
there isn't a tick's worth of time yet**, so they survive until a tick consumes
them. `move_axes` is a held continuous state re-read on the frame that does tick,
so returning early loses nothing.

Also clear `look_delta` after the *first* tick of a catch-up burst (as `jump`/
`toggle_fly` already were): it's a one-shot accumulated total, not a held state,
so a multi-tick burst must apply it **once**, not once per tick. This subsumes
the earlier `fix/mouse-look-catch-up-tick` branch — its test is included here,
so that branch can be dropped.

## Tests

- `mouse_look_across_sub_tick_frames_is_not_dropped` — 500 px of motion spread
  over sub-tick frames turns the player by the same total as 500 px in one frame
  (the drop bug; **fails on `main`**, where the spread version turns 0).
- `a_multi_tick_catch_up_burst_applies_mouse_look_only_once` — a 3-tick burst
  applies one delta exactly once, not ×3 (the multiply bug).

Existing timing tests (`sub_tick_dt_does_not_run_a_tick_yet`,
`frame_rate_independent_movement_reaches_the_same_state`) still pass. `cargo fmt`,
`clippy`, and `cargo test -p cubara` all green locally.

﻿## Summary

Completes the Admin Web portion of the single-location menu experience. Merchants with exactly one active accessible location now see a neutral menu-management workflow without redundant `All Locations`, `Global`, base, or override framing.

## Why

The dashboard already resolved single-location menu edits through the merchant-level base records, but several menu, item, category, modifier, recipe, scheduling, and pricing surfaces still exposed multi-location terminology and controls. This made a one-store merchant look like a multi-location account and allowed ambiguous scope choices.

## Changes

- Removes redundant global/location framing for single-location merchants across menus, items, categories, modifiers, recipes, schedules, and menu settings.
- Keeps multi-location selectors, badges, and override behavior unchanged.
- Forces single-location bulk base-price and delivery-price edits to use `location_id = NULL`.
- Enables modifier library group reordering for the single-location base library.
- Keeps inherently location-specific stock and merchandising controls scoped to the sole physical location.
- Neutralizes assignment and deletion copy that previously referenced global or location scope.
- Adds a focused modifier-library scope helper and unit coverage.
- Adds the implementation/QA document and updates the menu feature and ticket indexes.

## Scope boundaries

- Website/Admin Web only.
- No POS/mobile files changed.
- No database migration added or executed.
- No package or lockfile changes.
- The companion POS ticket remains for the Dexa-POS repository.

## Validation

- `npm run build` passed on Next.js 16.2.12.
- `npm test -- lib/menu/__tests__/modifier-library-scope.test.ts` passed: 3/3 tests.
- `git diff --check` passed after normalization.
- Manual primary acceptance check passed: a single-location merchant shows neither Global framing nor a location selector.

## Remaining QA

- Verify single-location create/edit/reorder persistence for menus, items, categories, modifiers, and recipes.
- Verify bulk base-price and delivery-price changes persist after reload.
- Run a multi-location regression check confirming global and per-location override controls remain available and isolated.

## Documentation

See `docs/features/menu-management/PLAN-2026-08-13-SINGLE-LOCATION-MENU-WEBSITE.md` for scope, implementation notes, and the complete manual QA matrix.
